Pros:
- The story is quite good imo (although it would make more sense if you played SR1 but you can still pick up the pieces by various references in this game or google the plot of saints row 1) You face 3 brand new rival gangs that control stillwater each with their own disturbing leaders and brutal executions for all of them.
- The character customisation is amazing (although nowhere near on the level of saints row 4 this is one of the only redeeming qualities i'll give SR4) it is still quite good and you can change a lot on your character and you can change your character by visiting a plastic surgeon if you don't like your characer or just feel like a change and you can change your clothing (there is a lot to choose from, not to mention you can change the colour and pattern and such). There are 6 voices for your character (3 for male and 3 for female) each with a different accent and they each have their own unique dialouge. You can create really attractive characters or just do what most real saints row players do and just mess around and make the most ugly abomination the world has ever seen. (let's face it, a lot of saints row players are fat 19 year old weaboos who have no taste)
- Stilwater is a really fun city. I'm guessing it's based on san francisco because it has a lot of similarities. Each neighbourhood is completely unique. From a huge university to a huge mountain with a horror movie-like village near it to a secret underground facility researching unknown things to a red light district full of dirty projects populated with hookers, pimps and homeless people and a Prison on an island far away from the city (*cough cough* alcatraz anyone?). Saints Row has changed into the complete opposite of what it was in saints row 1 now being a huge paradise for the rich with a massive skyscraper where the construction site was in saints row 1. There's even a large underground western town which was buried due to an earthquake (this making stilwater even more similar to san fran) There are also many easter eggs in the city and it's super fun to explore.
- The gangs in stilwater don't feel like real gangs but they are definately really cool. You get great rewards for defeating each of them. The Brotherhood are the first you encounter and are probably your worst enemy they wear red and cover themselves in tribal tattoos and piercings and ride around in monster trucks. They control rough neighbourds like ghettos and such.
Controlling Downtown and the museum is The Ronin which are merciless yakuza who wear motercycle jackets wield katanas and ride motorbikes and have a harsh a**hole dad and an annoying son as their leaders. The last and probably least important is a gang of Jamaicans and Africans who use voodoo called the Sons of Samedi, They are dressed in green and control the university, the red light district and the trailer park. Their second in command is unkillable, literally. Pay attention to what the pedestrians sometimes say after you kill him.
- There are a lot of weapons in the game and you can customise your vehicles and what the saints look like.
- The AI in this game is really awesome. Every single ped feels like a real person and in every district the people there change in voice and clothing to better suit the style of person who would live there. If a major thing happens in the story the pedestrians will sometimes comment on it when they see you. You can also give compliments and taunts to people and I find the reactions really funny or just cute. It's a lot better than GTA 4's AI imo.
- You can have homies following you who will fight with you and have some pretty cool dialouge.
Cons:
- You die pretty easily
- Thanks to gamespy shutting down, multiplayer is completely defunct and unplayable unless you mod your game.
- Sadly I don't quite recommend starting saints row with saints row 2. Start with the third if only just to see how much the series has changed.
- Unecceasrily over the top brutal cutscene
I highly recommend you picking up this game when you can

I'm a lifelong console player, and I've been using dual analog for probably around 14 years. I figured, hey, I'll go ahead and try this. If I don't like it, I'll just use it for KB+M only games and use my Xbone controller for others. So I turn on Fallout 4 and after playing with settings, find a config that really works. Honestly, about 7 hours into using the Steam Controller, and I'm already better with it than I was with the Xbone controller, which is almost exactly the layout I've been using for damn near a decade (360 controller, anyone?). Needless to say, it works, and it works well. Gyro aiming is also nice for fine tuning your shots, as it works remarkably well. One of the features I expected to be a gimmick is actually very useful. Very pleasantly surprising.
Hardware quality is solid. It's plastic, but it doesn't feel cheap. The only cheap plastic that's used is on the grips, and on the part that you aren't actually touching. It's definitely a quality plastic throughout the controller, and it feels nice in the hand. The upward arches of the grips may feel a little odd at first, but it's quite comfortable. The thumbstick is nice, the buttons work, though I would prefer it if they were clicky instead of squishy, the d-pad is... odd, and the right pad works great. The hyped-up haptic feedback is present, and as a skeptic, I have to say that it works really well. I can tell where my thumb is, what direction I'm moving, and how fast I'm moving. For some reason, the haptic feedback sounds like a geiger counter. Not sure why, but it's not actually distracting. There are 6 buttons on the back; two bumpers, two triggers, and two paddles. It all works very well. The only questionable part is the d-pad. Honestly, Valve should've just put in a physical pad, but I can understand if they were trying to give left-handed users the option to play southpaw like the weirdos they are.
TL;DR: Within 7 hours, I'm doing better at FPS games with this than I was with an Xbone controller, which is a layout I've been using religiously for 10 years, not even mentioning the various dual-analog layouts I used before the famous 360/Xbone layout. It's comfy, the trackpad works well, the haptic feedback is amazing, gyroscopic controls are surprisingly good, and plenty of buttons on the back. All buttons are also customizable, which is a huge advantage over other controllers. Literally the only questionable part about this controller is the d-pad. Unless they decided on a touch d-pad for the lefties, it was a poor design choice. That said, it works well enough. I can't imagine myself playing a platformer or a fighting game with it though.

This is my steam controller preview after two weeks of usage.
So far the Steam controller is a pretty powerful device, due to its flexibility its superior to an XB controller imo. however i must warn nothing can compare to mouse and keyboard. this is an alternative input method, its inferior to mouse but that doesnt mean it isnt functional. maybe you dont have a m+KB in your living room, or want to lay back in your PC chair and not huddle over a keyboard. this would be for you.
here's my pros and cons list.
Pros:
1) two function triggers - this allows you to place Zoom and shoot on the same button also i found adding normal and power attack to the same trigger in dark souls 2 frees up the right bumper for other actions.
2) the back grip buttons- It cant be stated enough, having the option to rebind two face buttons to the rear grips allows easier multitasking. like being able to reload, run and look at the same time.
3) two touchpads - when the right pad is set to either mouse or mouse joystick you are given superior aiming and look controls. i found that setting trackball on, sensitivity two steps above default and friction to low allows for full screen motion of the mouse pointer. The right pad while i admit it makes for a poor d-pad in fighting games can be used as a added mouse pad or as a great multi touch menu pad. also ive actually played through an entire game of super meat boy with it so its more than functional for platformers.
4) Steam controller binding UI: Having the ability to set multiple options for every game and for out of steam environment is truly powerful. i can set games that arent even in steam, have a preset for just using my PC and more. its very deep and you will be using it for weeks to master it.
5) Battery life: 2 AA batteries. two+ weeks of play when playing every day and ive still yet to need to change them.
Cons:
1) Face buttons: They are small and at times feel too close to the right pad, however with practice you can get used to them. or just rebind two to the back grip buttons and maybe even the outer rig of the left touchpad.
2) no rumble: This might not be an issue for you but for me when i play a racer it kind of sucks to not have rumble at all. haptics dont function same as rumble so it takes me out of the experience a bit.
i will update this as time goes on.

Overall a very good game.
The graphics may not be the best, but the gameplay is incredibly tense and fun. I was so sick of games like Battlefield where someone can take multiple sniper rounds to the chest and keep running like nothing happened. This game has a lot more realism, which I like, without it being overly frustrating or boring.
The devs are also pretty dedicated to authenticity, which is awesome. Unlike Battlefield, you don't have soldiers running around with an aresenal of the deadliest guns from all over the world. Weapon use is historically accurate and both class-specific, and faction-specifiic, with classes only available in realistic ratios (so you don't end up with a team that's 90% snipers). There are currently four factions (with more on the way) and you are given a different cosmetic customization slot for each faction, which is nice (so you can make your US Army character look different from your US Marine character, for instance). The asymetrical style of gameplay feels well-balanced and enjoyable.
The maps in the game are quite nice for the most part, though there definitely aren't as many as one would hope. Fortunately the devs are continuously updating the game, and more maps will be coming soon.
If you are interested in the Vietnam era and want a more hardcore/realistic multiplayer experience than something like Battlefield or CoD, then this is the game for you.

The game:
in short term. you buy investments and upgrades, then resets the world, then buys more investments and upgrades and then repeats. its an infinite circle of buying but has a rewarding sense of gameplay and a feeling of progression.
Adventure capitalist is a clicker game that you have in the background that you look into occasionally. in the beginning you will be needed to be a bit more active but as the game progresses the amount of time spent upgrading and buying is decreased. there is currently 3 planets to explore and an event sometimes. the earth is the starting planet until you get "x" amount of money then you will be able to buy the moon and after mars. every planet has a unique way on what to upgrade and changes as you progress on each planet. towards the late game you will probably face somewhat of an wall. the reasoning behind this is the developers has made the game a bit to much "pay to win". at the end game the amount of waiting time until progression is a very long haul.
- Currency: There is four kind of currency. the 2 main is the general money and angels. you will be rewarded with money each time an investment gives you money and you will be rewarded with angels when you reset the world. the 2 other currencys is mega bucks and gold. Mega bucks are rewarded when you reach a high enough amount that you can exchange "x" money for 1 mega buck. each mega buck increases in price when bought so you will be needed to get more and more moeny to get more mega bucks. mega bucks are used to upgrade individual investments and when an entire planet are invested with mega bucks the planet will get a permanent 10x boost.
- Events comes and goes but the main thing about events is that they reward mega bucks and gold to upgrade your planets. the only way to gain gold is through unlocks which is gained when buying a certain amount of buildings and reaching a "milestone". events offers new "milestones" that gives gold and megabucks.
- Tactics are very basic you look into what costs the least and what gives the most outcome. there is 2 ways to upgrade your income except paying which is called unlocks and upgrades. unlocks is when you get a certain amount of buildings which then gives you a boost to that building. upgrades is when you buy upgrades for your building that boosts their income.
all in all a great game but please fix the pay to win at the end.

After using it more I have updated my review.  I am almost ready to recommend it, but there are a few cripling flaws.  Look for the " * " symbol for where my changes are:
I played a handul of games with this, from shooters to fighting games*.  This is what I've found to increase my enjoyment:
1. I swear I never do this, but I'm using this controller less like an XBOX layout and more like the Wii U Pro one with X & Y and A & B switched.  This due to the simple ergonomics of having the right trackpad above the buttons instead of below them.  It's a shame that Valve decided to stick with convention instead of good HCI, but I understand their potential reasoning.  With that said, I would love to have the option to have tham automaticly swapped in the default Big Picture Mode so I won't have to rebind in every... single... game.
2.  Progressive heptic feedback is too weak*.  With a stick, I can physiclly feel how far I bend it.  With the trackpads, I need something similar.  Progressive heptic feedback would be the best solution and would make the trackpads feel less fiddly and more usable.
*3. The left trackpad simply sucks.  It has NO heptic feedback and is used for little more than an oversized D-Pad.  The most useful I've used it for is with fighting games with quick quarter, half, and full circle turns, which is great despite being unable to use charge characters effectively.  But other than that, it isn't replacing the left thumbstick like I wish it would.
*4. Not too big of a problem, but it feels like I'm relearning how to use a contoller.  While this isn't an absulute negative, it sets a skill floor.
With that said, this has potential to be my favorite controller of all time.  I pre-ordered for a reason and that reason is because I have faith in this company.  So to end on a positive note, here are what I found to be their good ideas:
1. The ergonomics of the controller itself.  It naturally opens my hands up to use the trackpads and most of the buttons feel good to press.  I personally love the triggers and bumpers.  I especially love the flappers in the back.  Unfortunitely, I have small hands and this controller is for normal people with normal proportions.  I know this is more my problem than yours, but it's been holding me back.  The analogue stick and buttons in particular have been a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥to use with my baby hands, but the trackpads lie perfectly, which is what matters.
2. Holy customizability!  I love it SO much, especially with the user made bindings!  Now, I would love to have a series of default setups I can make in Big Picture Mode as meanioned above, especially with shooters, that can then be tweaked based on individual game so that I don't have to rebind in every... single... game.
3.  The sound it makes when it turns on.  Makes my heart melt every time.
4. The battery thingy.  I love it.  Don't change a thing ;)
I hope that you actually read this and got something out of it so I'll update this review when I get a few more hours in.  Love ya guys.  Keep it up!

Paradox's take on the 4x genre meshes well with their previous games based on grand strategy, and offers a series of interesting choices on space-empire development and expansion.  The free updates and paid DLC to this point (Nov. 2017) have provided cool toys to mess about with, and given the company's development policy we can expect this title to receive continued support for some time yet.
I am most often frustrated with the war mechanics.  It is a pain in the butt to rebuild lost ships one hull at a time (some sort of navy template option to automate production and get some more convenient use out of non-core starbases would be most welcome).  Additionally, fleet battles beyond a certain size turn into a giant furball of confusion where I have some difficulty telling just what happened.  Or, maybe I'm just garbage.  One of those.
That said, I've apparently sunk a lot of time into playing around with Stellaris going by the Steam clock, and it is fundamentally a game that encourages trying different play-styles across multiple iterations.  The aesthetic's nice, the music's good, and the U.I. is intuitive (even if it'd benefit from some automation options, e.g. upgrading buildings).
Is good space game.  I like it.

When I first played this game, I played either as a xenophobic empire or a hivemind that devours the entire galaxy or a robot exterminator, wanting to wipe out all the biological life. All I wanted to do is rule the galaxy with an iron fist and make every other empire fall under my command or be exterminated.
It was foolproof! My empire was set up to be centralized towards the aspect of war and I built up my fleets to the point where my economy could barely sustain it and yet...
I failed every time.
My empires would sucummb to being bomb, purged, vassalized, tributalized(?), intergrated into another empire and so on and so forth.
I sat in my chair, in defeat and despair wondering where I had gone wrong. Was it how I fought my wars? Was it how I set up my economy? Did I not research enough? Did I not have enough planets?
I tried again and again, changing tactics, changing how my empires were run, the traits my species had but still failed.
In defeat, I chose one the most boring and possibly the worst (or so I thought) vanilla empires in the game: The United Nations of Earth. I thought that I couldn't possibly rule the entire galaxy with it's traits! Xenophile?? Egalitarian?? Wasteful?? There weren't what my grand plans couldn't possibly include, it's too inefficient!
The empire had a shaky start: I spawned on the very end of the galaxy's arm and restricted 1/3 of it from any other empires to prevent them from colonizing any planets within but this took a heavy toll on my economy, I could barely build my fleet without waiting for another two months or so and I had only colonized 7 small planets whilst there was already the damned xenophobic empire bordering me, superior to me in terms of fleet power and REALLY didn't like me. I thought I was finished, I was SURE I was finished.
It was then I got into a defense pact with a significantly stronger empire then me. They liked me (xenophile probably helped there). They had a stronger fleet power, stronger economy, way more planets and yet they protected me.
Under their protection, I uplifted a pre-sapient alien on an artic world in order to colonize the planets in the galaxy arm and eventually had enough unity to create a federation with the nice stronger empire. I was definitely safe now and the other empire also invited another stronger empire into the federation!
Feeling confident, I declared war on the xenophobic empire and although there was a slow and disastourous start to the war, their fleets came in and decimated the xenophobic empire and made them pay tribute to me.
Having had the acension perk of 200+ more fleet capacity and a stronger empire paying tribute to me, my economy quickly grew strong and I jumped from a measly 5000 fleet power to 22000 in just a year and became evenly matched with the other empires within the federation. (With two fallen empires giving me their battleships!)
Skipping ahead, I now have the tributary empire become my vassal (which I'm planning to intergrate into my empire), three different empires paying tribute to me, the other empires in my federation becoming increasingly weaker and my grand master plan starting to take shape...
When playing this, I learnt a valuable lesson
It's more fun to become ruler with friends and backstabbing them in the future.

The Binding of Isaac is weird. On the surface it looks like a simple old fashioned arcade game with some satanic, grimey elements, as you dive deeper however you discover one of the most impressive games in terms of design that I have ever played.
If you can grab the base game + Expansion it's 100% worth your time, It's a rouge like, dungeon crawler that keeps you addicted with its array of crazy, weird and disgusting items, enemies and rooms. It boasts an impressive selection of enemies and hundreds of obtainable items that change Isaacs stats and his physical appearance for the player to see.

The addiction stems from the difficulty, which for 99% of people, is very hard. As you beat the game which only takes around 30-40 minutes to complete, you unlock further levels to get to with new enemies, new rooms and more story. You find yourself just wanting to have 1 more run, which later on turns into 10 as you should've been asleep 5 hours ago but instead you're still trudging through the dark, creepy basments of your home.
Seriously, get this game.

Here's my thoughts on Steam's new controller, based on playing a few different games. I'll change things in the review as I play more with the controller. I received mine after about 10 days.
The Steam controller is pretty light, but the batteries give it a nice weight. The grips fit into your hands well and its comfortable to reach the buttons. Unlike the wireless Xbox 360 controller's awkward battery pack, the Steam controller stores the batteries in the grips where they are out of the way. There is plenty of space on the back of the controller between your hands, so your fingers aren't touching.
Every button, pad, and joystick on the controller are configurable through Steam. You can create, save, and share your favorite configurations for others to use and modify. You can bind either gamepad buttons or keyboard and mouse buttons to the Steam controller.
Just an average joystick really. It's got a different texture around the edge of the top of it so you can feel where your thumb is pretty easily. Haven't had any problems with my thumb slipping off. The stick can be clicked to perform more functions.
The right track pad is usually used to control the camera, while the left commonly is used as a dpad. Of course you can bind these to function differently. If you're comfortable using the track pad on a laptop, you should be comfortable with these. The pads can be clicked to perform more functions.
The pads aren't that good at shooter games from what I've seen, but they're still pretty fun. It may just be a problem with my bindings and settings. They seem to do perfectly fine in platformers without any changes however.
The haptic feedback is basically just tiny vibrations within the controller. You can enable and disable the haptics on different actions. The haptics feel fine, but I wouldn't buy the controller for them alone.
Honestly these are amazing, and I don't see any reason for future controllers to lack these buttons. One of my favorite parts of the controller.
They feel a bit out of position, but with both the pads being able to click and the two buttons on the back, it doesn't really matter.
Triggers have two stages, a soft pull and a full pull. You'll feel a satisfying click when doing a full pull. Both types of pulls can be bound to perform different functions and the sensitivity of the soft pull can be changed. A good example of a possible use for this in a fps game would be to aim down the sights of a gun with a soft pull and fire with a full pull.
The bumpers are large compared to the Xbox 360 and PS2 controllers', but other than that nothing really stands out about them.
I didn't even know the Steam controller came with this feature until I stumbled upon it in the middle of a game. You can rotate the Steam Controller to perform functions. I would imagine this could be used to control a steering wheel in a racing game, but I've only been able to test it out in Portal 2 as an alternate way of aiming the camera. I don't really have any opinion on it at this time.
Overall, the Steam controller is pretty cool. I'm not sure track pads are going to be the future of controllers, but its still pretty interesting. Everything else about the controller is great and I would recommend trying it out.

The second chapter from The Journey Down is a rather coherent and well designed title that brings Bwana, Kito and Lina ahead in the search for the Underland.
Visually, the game might not be first class triple A title worthy, but it does still offer very likeable sights, and above all, it improves over the first chapter of the series. The overall amount of scenes and puzzles do not increase, and the game remains very linear, but all of this contributes to a laid back and relaxed atmosphere that is emphatized by the soundtrack used, which - once again - is one step above the one used in the first chapter (and truth to be said, that one was good already!).
The characters are very well thought of, and despite being maybe a bit too close to the classic "good" or "bad" guys, they're very, very, precisely designed in every aspect, from their appeareance, to their voice acting, to the dialogues (the way they behave). More importantly, the 3 characters which appeared in the first chapter retain the same voice actor, and they benefit so much of it! Bwana still feels so funky, and you can't help but feel for him :) , same as for Kito, his friend. Other than Lina, all of the other characters are new but the voice over is very well executed with quite some personality (i've seen several triple A titles using far lower quality voice over job than the one you'll have the chance to listen in this game).
Gameplay wise, it's still more or less the same from the previous chapter except for more depth: you happen to came across a tool not working or someone needing some object(s), and you'll have to end up finding or crafting it. It's very basic, it might require a bit more thinking at times, but not that much either. Everything is well laid out, well within your sight. and even the inventory doesn't ever get too full of items you don't need.
Now, a big, important role is played by the music: i happened, more than once, to literally stop playing only to listen to the beatiful, relaxing, chilling music this game offers! It really is one of the few titles i can think of which has such a fitting and well done soundtrack which is contributing so much to the atmosphere. Well done!
What else? The game only lasts a few hours, but i dare to say it lasts the right amount of time. Every aspect is well thought of, you might happen to need to backtrack sometimes but it won't be a issue, time-wise (Port Artue is a very small town, it seems).

I'm not gonna focus too much on the aspects of the PC port. This is mostly gameplay.
Dead Rising 3 is a little different than it's predecessors. The game leaves behind the old territory of a zombie infested mall and instead traps you in a town much like the Case Zero DLC from Dead Rising 2. While the game is still sticks with the free-roam aspect, it seems a little more grounded to a linear design story wise. Sure, you can run around and complete optional objects, scavenge for supplies, blueprints, and stuff of that sorts, The main story can only be progressed once you reach the checkpoint you need to go to. This is a welcomned change of pace because you never feel like you're forced to wait around or do optional stuff just to progress until the next chapter unlocks.
You play as a mechanic named Nick. And while he may be the biggest wuss ever its a breath of fresh air to see a protagonist that isn't your stereotypical edgy and cool Mr. McBadass. You can sympathize with him a little easier because he's much more relatable. Although the game's mechanics don't really run parallel to Nick's personality. It's weird seeing him be so worried, scared, and anxious in cutscenes but in game you can headbutt zombies while wearing a dragon helmet and makeshift umbrella wings on your back.
So what aspects of Dead Rising have returned for this game? While the game has left behind the somewhat cartoonish feel of the first two games and instead focuses on being more grounded to reality, it still retains the colorful psycho characters and an array of hilarious weaponry. The combos for your melee are still there and are as awesome as ever. You can still invest PP points into your attributes skill trees to unlock new skills for melee, ranged weapons, running, smarts, etc. But there's a few new ones such as vehicle blueprints and skills as well.
Since Nick is good with his hands, you can now craft weapons on the fly instead of needing to go to a table. Along with this Nick can also craft two vehicles together to create mobile death machines. The graphics are also pretty good too, but I don't think what need in order to achieve those visuals justifies the extent of the system requirements.
And now the PC Port. This is a PASSABLE PC port. It's good, but it's not great either. The game runs fine, and while the game is capped to 30 frames, you can easily uncap it (create an user.ini file in DR3 directory and add this in: gmpcr_unlock_frame_rate = True). On lower end machines, this may cause the physics to bug out a little bit. I run on older tech just barely surpassing the minimum requirements and the only issue I've encountered was crashing a van into the highway medium caused its physics to lose its mind. However, despite not even coming anywhere close to the Recommended settings, I can still play this game maxed out with FXAA at above 30+ FPS. However once I played for about an hour the game started to chug and momentarily freeze. I can run it at medium with no issue though. And, surprisngly, the in-game rendered cinematics run worse than the actual game itself. You can see my specs below to compare how your rig would fair up.
Intel Core i7-920 @2.66 GHz (Quad Core)
Nvidia GTX 580
6GB RAM
The controls are a little... eh. Mouse 1 is your primary attack with Mouse 2 being the secondary attack or aiming mode. Q also acts as your heavy attack button, although I can't determine if Q and Mouse 2 are the same for melee. Navigating the menus is a bit of a pain because you need to use the bracket keys (yes, [ ] <- THESE) in order to navigate the menu. And for looking through the sub-menus within the menus you need to use the less than/greater than keys (<> THESE). What the ♥♥♥♥, Capcom? Thankfully you can just use your mouse to nevigate the menus. Mouse controls feel pretty good, but also kind of feel sluggish too. There's a good variety of in-game options to tweak the game for performance, so you're good on that.
Overall, while Dead Rising 3 takes a semi-different approach to the series, it still feels very much like a Dead Rising game and is a much welcomned change of pace from the prior two installments. It is personally my favorite of the trilogy. Do consider picking this one up.

In Out There Somewhere, you are Yuri, who has gone out to kill Grigori, when your ship crashes on a mysterious, and mildly hostile planet. You soon learn that Grigori is on the planet as well, on your search for the one thing that can get your ship running again: the Light Orb. It is a very good plot, and it controls really well. I found it easier to play with controller, rather than with the keyboard. The achivements in the game aren't that difficult to get, and the game doesn't really take that long to beat. There are two types of guns that you weild: the teleportation gun and the guass gun. The teleportation gun is pretty self-explanitory, and the guass gun can be used for killing enemies and breaking "unstable" blocks. Also, this game has an amazing soundtrack. It's one of ny favourites in a long time, but Skyrim, Mario, and Zelda's soundtracks are still better.
Overall, this game was a LOT better than I first imagined. The game is also child-friendly, so people of all ages can play. I highly recommend this game to everybody. You won't be disapointed.

If you enjoyed any of the Red Orchestra games, then you will surely love this game!
This game is great, both aestheticly and mechanically. If you want a game to live out all of your Vietnam War fantasies, then look no further! This may be a multiplayer only game, but for the price it is far worth it. The classes are nicely balanced for realism, and the maps are decently sized. I could easily put more hours into this game if I wasn't busy with my VR headset. The only thing that is missing is the cover system integreated into Red Orchestra 2. Without that feature this game does feel like any other FPS of today. Now that does not necessiarly equate to a bad thing. This game does an amazing job in making up for that. As I said the classes for each team are balanced out, so the Americans usually have the superior firepower, and the VietCong have the upperhand at booby-trapping and sabotaging the enemy advancement. This not only makes this less of a run and gun game like COD, but more of a strategical military simulator like Arma. One bullet wound is deadly in this game, and the developers have done a nice job in implementing a system in which you slowly blackout from a gunshot wound (unless you heal). If you live long enough to see advancement on the enemy position, you may find yourself fighting in the ranks of Lt. Dan, Bubba, and Forrest Gump. Literally everyone that plays this game likes to holler over the microphone saying their favorite Vietnam movie quotes. To me it never gets old when you hop in a server, and half of your team is Forrest Gump and Lt.Dan impersonators. Oh one last thing! As I said, the game looks very good, and the maps are no exception! The attention to detail is spot on! I really enjoy the Tet Offensive map. The last Vietnam game I have played that was almost as good as this was Conflict Vietnam. If you are considering getting a modern multiplayer FPS in the likness of the Vietnam Conflict, then look no further! This game is well worth its sale price, and was even worth the full asking price! I am sure with the community this game brings in, you are sure to have plenty of fun for a while to come!

Not exactly your definition of a puzzle game.
Me, and a couple of my peers got this game 90% off. I ended up paying something like $.50 for it or whatever, and for that price, it is somewhat worth it. So, what's the game like? Well... simple. Way too simple. The game really just consists of you, the player, running around collecting these "data fragments" and getting to the end goal. Maybe you jump up a lift, or activate a switch, but overall the package feels in complete. There are some "puzzle" elements in the game though. For one, you have a strange color changing ability (how original). You press a button, and you change from red to blue, or vice versa. Neat ain't it? Well again, this is mostly used to cross walls or bridges, it mostly is half-asses stuff that you're gonna forget. Also there are these colour cubes. Red and blue also, you chuck em across the map and they activate things... how fun and original. So how do you progress? Well as said before you collect these data fragments, which are placed around the map creatively... not really. In the easier levels you can find them right in front of you, and instead of solving puzzles to get to them, it's pretty much a scavenger hunt. Luckily they're almost always poorly hidden and easy to get to. There is a healthy amount of levels but you'll probably get through them in less than 2 hours. Co-op levels are very dumb, as they don't really give you an incentive to actually work together, and also it's local only, so in reality you can just complete everything yourself and just pick up the other controller and finish it. There is also a mode where you literally just chuck cubes in your opponents goal for 30 seconds or so, also local only.
How about some positives? Well there is some at least. The game is very easy to run. Your grand-mums computer could probably run it well. The music is quite nice, and that's it. WOW.

I love the Steam Controller! It takes alittle getting used to at first, especially if your very familiar with xbox controllers or playstation controllers. But i learned to love it in about a day. The endless options to customize the controls are great too. I thought it was alittle much at first, but i can see this level of customization being a huge advantage in game.
The only thing i could think of that would make this controller better out of the box would be rechargeable batteries and using the wireless  dongle/usb extender as a charging dock. It would also be nice to have a microphone built into the controller or some kinda set up where you can plug a headset into it. Something that would be cool to see in future versions would be the touch pads having some sort of display where it would show what keys you have assigned to the buttons, that would also change when you hit the modifier key(s).
I would also like to see some improvements with the mapping software to really improve this thing. When you are assigning keys and actions to the track pads and joysticks it would be nice if it showed you the radius of the deadzones in menu, as well as show you real time feedback of what position the stick/trackpad is registering so you can more easily set deadzones without having to switch back and forth between in game and big picture mode. I would also like to be able to use the controller keyboard feature on my desktop with out having to be in big picture mode.
I really just want to say that Valve/Steam knocked this one out of the ball park and hope they will take some of my or the communities suggestions to heart and really make this thing as great as it can be.

Pros: trackpad feature is pretty cool. Although I should note its not that much different from a trackpad on a laptop. FPS is very hard with a trackpad. The 2 extra buttons on the back are a nice touch. When using SteamOS or steam in big picture mode, sending messages to friends using the 2 trackpads is fantastic. I have never seen a better way to do controller typing. That is some true innovation right there. (CON this doesn't exist as an overlay in games).
Cons: The face of the controller is concave. The end piece of the controller hand holds hits the heel of your hand, I feel that if these didn't stick up so far the controller would be much easier and faster to maneuver around. ABXY location is different than every other controller on the market. If they would have swapped the right trackpad with the ABXY buttons I feel like it would be more instantly accesible for everyone versus "having to get used to it." The ABXY buttons feel small and too recessed.
Overall I would recommend to my friends to just get an xbox 360 controller for pc. It's cheaper, fits better in your hands, and you won't have to relearn an unfamiliar ABXY location. 2 extra buttons and a track pad aren't doing it for me. Honestly, if the trackpad and ABXY buttons were switched this would be a rave review, I can't seem to train my thumb to go to a different location than it has been going for the past 20 years. Please, reinvent the wheel, just make sure it drives the same.

I have read pretty much every notable review of the Steam Controller on the internet. Most of them seem to miss the point or don't understand everything the controller is capable of. Some say you can't play shooters with it, but I imagine most of those reviewers aren't aware that you can map two input types to a single PC input (i.e. trackpad to high-sensitivy mouse, gyro to low sensitivity mouse) or that you can map a single input type to two different PC inputs via mode switching (i.e. control the sensitivity of the trackpad mouse input dynamically by pressing down on the pad or using one of the paddles to switch modes). It's not as fast or precise as M+KB, and if you buy this thing to emulate joysticks with the trackpads you got it for the wrong reasons. But if, every now and then (or exclusively), you'd prefer relaxing on your couch rather than sitting hunched over a desk to play your PC games, and if you recognize that wireless M+KB with a clunky lapdesk doesn't quite offer a comfortable and relaxing couch-bound experience, the Steam Controller does the job admirably, and I imagine I'll just become more and more proficient with it with practice. If nothing else, I'd recommend it just to support the effort to innovate and create something new (and solve a problem, which I believe it does). The general mantra seems to be "if it aint broke don't fix it", but I think it's easy to think something isn't broken when you've become used to it over a period of ten or fifteen years. Steam Controller is a winner.

The steam controller is certainly unique, it's design is like nothing before, it's layout is suprisingly comfortable, and it's almost unlimited functions to personalise certainly make you feel like you're in control. It has a button, in every place, for every need that you'd what. It's compatable with so many games, and always makes using a computer, feel like fun again.
However....
The steam controller is brilliant in every way, but it just doesn't work... Yes, it works with every game, yes, it can be changed to however you like, but it will never be like mouse and keyboard... And the only way i can express an example of it is this: XBOX games, are designed for the controller, the steam controller is the other way round, the controller was designed for the games. And unfortunately, doing it this way round, just doesn't work. Yes, it is possible to play the games, but you can forget any chance of being accurate on FPS games, any accuracy required games will never ever be as good as mouse and keyboard. Even simulation games aren't the best purley because the controller just can't take the capacity of controls.
My controller now sits on a table, awaiting to be played, and believe me, I want to, I really really want to use it, but inside, I know, that it will never be that 'thing', to make playing games more enjoyable. Whenever i do try it, it is always a failure compared to my normal mouse and keyboard gameplay.
It is really unfortunate, because the controller is fantastic, but it's extremely hard to explain how it just doesn't work compared to mouse and keyboard. By all means, buy it, try it, you might love it. But certainly if you play similar games to what I do, mouse and keyboard can never be beaten. Steam are onto something big, something amazing, but unfortunately, this just isn't it. And I await the day when 'it' comes...

I would only recommend this to casual players, who never understood that in order to play human you had to outsmart the dinosaurs. Because now all they have to do is outrun them.
Some broken mechanics:
Med packs
Mines
kiteing (the ability to run circles around practically anything)
No human melee (Meaning no trapper knife kill. Oh, but don't worry. They're REALLY overpowered now. See further.)
The ability to remove the sniper's hat (making her WAY too camoflaged. This game has microtransactions, BTW)
Now, you'd think I was complaining because I got killed repeatedly as dino. While it did happen, I also played as human, surviving situations I normally would not be able to in the previous installment. Heres some dumb examples:
1. As Trapper, I was surrounded, but then I laid mines at my feet. Everything died.
2. As Scientist, I laid a med kit at my feet. Could not die vs. one dino so long as I stayed on top of it.
3. As anything, I could keep running circles around a T-rex or a Spino and not die for awhile. Sometimes I'd even be able to solo-kill it. (And while I haven't played as a T-rex or Spino, the fact they go down so quickly and are completely feared by ABSOLUTELY NO ONE BUT THE BIGGEST MORONS ON THE PLANET WHO DON'T KNOW HOW TO KITE OR SHOOT, makes me think playing one is a very bad idea. I may see a Rex get one kill. That's it.)
I short, I believe this game is a product of incessent complaining by casual players. The devs change one thing, then they got to change another to make it 'balanced'. It might be 'balanced' in terms of casual environment (everybody gets kills), but not in a competitive one. Whatever the case, the tense 'horror' part of the game is completely gone.
Does this game deserve to exist? Yes and no. Primal Carnage: Extinction is where the whinners can play, leaving the more serious players who want a better experience rather than just kills to play Primal Carnage in peace and stop having the dinos fed by dimwits. Also, there are some maps that aren't availible in Primal carnage someone might want to try (Beware invisible walls).
However, I also say no because people might play this 'sequel' and, after not really being engaged, figure that the previous installment could only be worse, and miss out on a truly competitive game. To give a proper comparison of Primal Carnage to Primal Carnage: Extinction, I compare it to the difference between Star Wars Battlefront (original) to Star Wars Battlefront 2. One game requires more strategy, and the other favors run-and-gun.
Update: Devs are willing to listen to criticism, and seem willing to rebalance the entire game for better reception.
Update 10/18/2017: Devs are unable to determine what is good criticism, and what is bad. Every time they get an influx of players, they listen to the bottom of the barrel. The bottom of the barrel gets what they want, and then they leave.

The second chapter from The Journey Down is a rather coherent and well designed title that brings Bwana, Kito and Lina ahead in the search for the Underland.
Visually, the game might not be first class triple A title worthy, but it does still offer very likeable sights, and above all, it improves over the first chapter of the series. The overall amount of scenes and puzzles do not increase, and the game remains very linear, but all of this contributes to a laid back and relaxed atmosphere that is emphatized by the soundtrack used, which - once again - is one step above the one used in the first chapter (and truth to be said, that one was good already!).
The characters are very well thought of, and despite being maybe a bit too close to the classic "good" or "bad" guys, they're very, very, precisely designed in every aspect, from their appeareance, to their voice acting, to the dialogues (the way they behave). More importantly, the 3 characters which appeared in the first chapter retain the same voice actor, and they benefit so much of it! Bwana still feels so funky, and you can't help but feel for him :) , same as for Kito, his friend. Other than Lina, all of the other characters are new but the voice over is very well executed with quite some personality (i've seen several triple A titles using far lower quality voice over job than the one you'll have the chance to listen in this game).
Gameplay wise, it's still more or less the same from the previous chapter except for more depth: you happen to came across a tool not working or someone needing some object(s), and you'll have to end up finding or crafting it. It's very basic, it might require a bit more thinking at times, but not that much either. Everything is well laid out, well within your sight. and even the inventory doesn't ever get too full of items you don't need.
Now, a big, important role is played by the music: i happened, more than once, to literally stop playing only to listen to the beatiful, relaxing, chilling music this game offers! It really is one of the few titles i can think of which has such a fitting and well done soundtrack which is contributing so much to the atmosphere. Well done!
What else? The game only lasts a few hours, but i dare to say it lasts the right amount of time. Every aspect is well thought of, you might happen to need to backtrack sometimes but it won't be a issue, time-wise (Port Artue is a very small town, it seems).
I don't usually complete a review with a vote, but if i had to i would rate this 8,7 out of 10 at the very least.

Amongst the sea of gushingly positive reviews for this game, I feel the need to point out a rather glaring flaw in gameplay. The Binding of Isaac is completely randomly generated, and while this means the game has a ton of replay value, it also leads to several occasions where the difficulty of gameplay reaches unprecedented heights. I have played several games in which I was unable to find a single key, rendering me incapable of accessing any kind of upgrades or items. I have played several games as Cain in which I made it through the first 4 stages without recieving a single health increase, only to inevitably perish at the 5th because it is actually impossible to survive any further than that with only two hearts. Worse than either of those offenses, however, is the fact that several 'upgrades' in this game are hardly upgrades at all, and arguably put a hamper on the overall experience. Several items alter your rate of fire in such a way that makes the game intrinsically more difficult. Other items lack synergy with each other to the point that collecting both is an actual detriment to one's ability to complete the game.
Now I have owned this game for 5 years, and admittedly, I love it and would recommend it to all my friends. However, this game is far from perfect (as many of the reviews on Steam would have you believe). I promise you, after having beat the game once or twice and unlocking most of the characters, you will notice more often than not that you are dying due to the game actually trolling you, either by giving you items that cancel each other out, items that are just plain unusable, or not giving you any items at all. My advice to anyone who plays this game is look up every item/upgrade that you collect and learn what they do, because there are several you will want to avoid at all cost.
That being said, this is a wonderful game with infinite replay value that I would recommend to everyone.

Combine that with a complete lack of such a warning on the main store page, and I'm just not inclined to give them the benefit of the doubt here.
Nevertheless, it is better than nothing.  Buy it when it's 90% off.

I purchased this controller for the sole purpose of handling steam games that still required a keyboard/mouse.  Maybe because they were old, remasters like baldurs gate, or games like divinity original sin (before the new version of course).  Games that aren't too precision heavy but still need a mouse.
This controller is perfect for that.
Well I decided to load up some shooters too just to see and it works well enough.  To put it bluntly its a track pad.  So playing a shooter on a track pad is the same as using one on a laptop.  You have the same basic controls there.
Overall, this controller wont replace a keyboard/mouse for hardcore KB/M games like SC2 or competitive counter strike like was originally implied.  But the controller is GREAT for games that require a keyboard mouse and casual shooters like bioshock.
As of now this controller has replaced my xbox 360 so i simply dont have to swap between the two.  The steam controller works well enough on shooters that theres no need to switch to a joystick.  However if you are looking to play serious DOTA, starcraft 2, CS, etc.  You are still going to need a mouse.  But I don't think thats really a surprise to anyone.

This game, Saints Row 2, is in a series of games (Saints Row) that are known to be very spontaneous and 'funny'. This game stands out in that series because it is not one of those spontaneous games, but it can be quite funny. This game is for the most part serious, has some really good character customisation, and has some really enjoyable gameplay.
Most of the time this game is serious, but that doesn't mean that the game is any less funny. The game is extremely funny, just in a different way. Having a game that doesn't constantly try and be funny makes the funny things that happen even more funny. And because it isn't always trying to be funny you will most likely spend more time playing it, because you will have other things that capture your attention with it, other than the funny things that eventually become old and boring. The game has a few stories you can follow, and each one has serious parts and funny parts in it, making for a good plot.
The character customisation is very good, and by that you may think I mean it has a few good hairstyles or something, but it's a bit different from that, even though they DO have heaps of hairstyles. Saints Row 2 has the feature of your character being able to have breasts when he looks like a guy, or no breats when she looks like a woman. It's very gender diverse in that. Not only that making the game more comfortable for anyone to play, but also having the option to choose voices, despite what your body may look like, you can choose a 'female voice' for a male looking character, etc. The game also doesn't gender you at all, gender netural pronouns are used in the game (they, them, their's), names aren't used, only your title. As well in the character customisation it allows you to have a certain walk, a certain insult and a certain greeting, even the facial expression that you will constantly have on your face. You can choose your skin colour, age, hair colour, eye colour, etc. The character creation is so good, that you can have breasts and still have a manly shape, or you can have a female shape and have no breasts.
Aside from all the breasts and hair, this game has really good gameplay outside of the creation screen. There are heaps of missions to play, heaps of clothes to get for your character, a big map, great radio music, a lot of 'activites' (sort of mini game things, it's hard to explain) to do, and they are quite enjoyable. There is hours of gameplay in this game, and there is a lot of freedom in this game to do whatever you want to do. If you want to go around killing people and getting into cars with skantily klad women, you can. But if instead you want to do activites and drive around listening to the radio, you can. A lot of these types of games should involve a lot of freedom, and often do, the freedom to shape your gaming experience.
I may seem like I am painting this game as perfect, it is by no means perfect, as every game has it's flaws. This game has horrible multiplayer, by that I mean if you don't like LAN you're going to have a difficult time playing multiplayer. But if you do like LAN, congrats, you can play the multiplayer, which is a very good feature if you can play it. This game also has a couple of glitches and bugs. One mainly is a cutscene going black, and making it harder to progress. This can be solved by skipping the cutsecne, but the problem with that is that you're skipping the cutscene.
If you played the other Saints Row games and you liked them, you might not like this one as much, as it's not as 'random' as the others, but you might also like it, as it is a part of the Saints Row series, and includes characters from the series and such. Outside of the Siants Row series, it is a pretty good game.

New Review(beginning 2017 Review): I waited quiet a long time to come back to this game to see if the Dev's would make some new improvements to the game.

there are still some minor tweaks i can see so far that need adressing. some debuffs to the commando class launcher, buffs to the spino and arco mouth box, dino eating issue for tyrants needs to be looked at, as you have to stand right on top of the carcass and look down to heal, gathering ammo and healing needs to be revised a little as i notice it doesn';t always show up until i look right at it as a human class.
other than that the game is starting to look pretty complete. i'd not be surprised if it would be offically released this year.
Original Review(Negative/initial year release Review):
I get that this game is still in early access, and that it still has a lot of kinks to work out, but each time I come back to see the changes, I'm honestly not seeing much improvement, or for that matter, improvement that makes this FEEL like a Primal Carnage game.
Even though I meet the spec requirements with flying colors, you really can't play this game without the over use of bloom effects that pretty much makes this game as violently bright as Halo 3 was. But at least Halo 3 was on a console that could easily tolerate the load, where as my poor system can't seem to keep up with it, and trying to play this on lower quality just sucks the life out of the game even more.
I get that they are trying to be more realistic with this game, than they were in the first in terms of movements, okay, cool. But you can't expect positive reception with what you are doing when there is a pace to the game people already liked from the very first game. To me things were more intense in the original, and rightfully balanced in that people were slow, and dinos tended to be quick and hard to escape than they are in EX.
Everything at first In EX was overly fast, and everything was completely wrong with the Dino AND Human class, and now that i have come back recently, dear god do the dinos feel soooo obnoxiously slow, and how i HATE with a burning passion how quickly any of the dinos stamina runs out. Rexes and Spinos seem like they have more fat on their body then they do muscle with how fast their stamina depletes, and don't even get me started on the Carno's, how clunky and slow they move unless they are charging, which, mind you can't last you to save your life because it runs out faster than the tyrants, that makes no sense. It's honestly been made easier to play a human than a Dino with all the negatives swirling about on the Dino side of things.
Not to mention all the lag. the game lags so horribly from all the plant life, and bloom effects it has to load that, I can't pounce as a Raptor when the ping increases with each player, can't nab anything as a Tyrant, cant fly as a Petra, and, well frankly I don't bother with the carno anymore because I just find no joy in it what so ever as I did in the first game.
So thank god this game was only a few bucks for me, because of having owned the original before this game opened for Early access, because it really isn't fun, and feels nothing like the original at all. just a pretty upgrade with crappy gaming mechanics and functions. I likely wont come back to play this game for a long, long while, and if i do come back, we will see if i can reverse judgment.

Well, this is gonna be a long one.
Primal Carnage Extinction was originally going places, looked like it could have been a pretty fun game. Now I can't say the same. Here's my review.
Gameplay and Bugs-
PCE in its current state allows you to pick from a set of playable characters in two separate factions and is essentially Team Fortress meets Jurassic Park. There are several game-modes currently in the game, including team-deathmatch and get-to-the-chopper(similar to capture the flag)
These are fairly fun games, if you can find anyone to play them. The combat system was a good idea that was not well executed. Currently there are lots of bugs and several exploits that allow people to dominate and destroy without ever being killed or even taking damage. Humans typically get mowed down by dinosaurs in every round and hit boxes can be a problem, with damage most of the time not even registering with a direct headshot.
These bugs do occasionally get fixed, but it tends to take months for another patch to be released and then maybe that bug will be one of the few that gets fixed. Still, even with bugs and issues gameplay can be pretty fun.
Maps-
There's several maps in the game now, and they all look pretty good and even add to the lore of the game. The graphics look pretty great even with settings turned down.
Developers and Community-
I don't usually base a game's review off of the game's community, but I can't give a good review of the game with it's current community's state.
The developers do work hard with what they have, but I believe their biggest mistake and the down-turning point for this game was when the developers decided to add skins and character customization to the game.
This very quickly became all the community was interested in, and over time the gameplay servers were replaced by free-roam no-kill servers filled with roleplayers squealing about new skins in the workshop. Team-deathmatch is nearly unseen now, because any TDM server that does come up is almost instantly filled with more people who'll only sit around and try to make real gameplay impossible for those who try to play it.
The game could have been good and if the community wasn't the way it was, I would definitely recommend this game to anyone who likes a fast-paced fps multiplayer. But there's no point in saying good things about a good game if the community doesn't let you play the game as it was intended to be played.
I do not recommend this game to anyone looking for any particular playstyle, unless perhaps you enjoy roleplaying and bartering with other people for game textures.
If I had to give this game a number rating, it would be 7/10. But with this current state, I wouldn't rate it at all.

Ok, another year has come and gone. Last year I wrote a review of WWE:2K17 and it was my first year buying a WWE game from the 2K franchise. I was pretty happy with it. If you havent read it somewhere I gave it a 7/10, which is pretty modest in my opinion. This year 2k18 was hyped up beyond belief and I am afraid I cannot give as kind of a review to this game that I so desperately wanted. So I am going to go through a fairly lengthy review and give my Pros and Cons and what I thought about my experience after having over 50+ hours in this game. So sit back and enjoy if you are feeling down to read a bit. And before I continue, thank you for reading this review and I hope it helps you make the decision on whether you will wait for it to go on sale, whether not to get it at all or whether to take the risk. Here goes.
I will go ahead and start with some positive things about this game.
Pros:
Roster Size: The roster size this year is awesome. It totally surpasses 2k17 in roster size. 2K17 had 134 wrestlers on the disk that went up to 177 with all DLC and alternate versions (explained in the next sentence). 2K18 comes in with 174 wrestlers on the disk and it goes up to a record breaking 203 chracters with DLC and that includes alternate versions of the same character (Like there are 3 versions of John Cena which each count as its own unique character). This is astounding, truly. But we will get to the bad part of this later.
Graphics: The graphics of this game are incredible. Due to a new engine, WWE 2K18 is able to do what none had thought possible. The Wrestlers actually look like their real life counterparts. Go on youtube and watch the WWE 2k17 vs 2K18 Randy orton entrance. The difference is astounding. However, 2K thought the could ride off of the graphics and use its stunning new feature to bypass its flaws, however they did not.
Carry and Drag System: The Carry and Drag system is unique non the less. But I found it somewhat difficult to use on the PC, though it may be easier on the console versions to use. Though when you finally get someone into the carry system, it does allow for some awesome combo moves. Like dropping someones head onto the top rope and then going up top for a elbow drop! Or laying a ladder from the barricade to the ring, placing your opponent up on the ladder and then going up top for a elbow drop! Either way, elbow drop! This new feature is also added to distract from the real issues behind the scenes which we will get to now.
Cons:
DLC: Ok, probably one of the most controversial topics when the game was only a few weeks from release. The DLC. Many people such as I watched twitter all day when they had their "DLC CHARACTER DROP DAY", in which they released a new DLC character each hour until all DLC character's names were releaased to the public. I was in class at college that day and sat on my phone the whole time reading people's thoughts on who they would add. Now 2K17 gave us 20 new characters to play in DLC. I and many others waited all day to find out that 2k18 only had a whopping 10 new DLC characters. 10..... 10.....
People were NOT happy. People were going to pay the same price of last years DLC but with half of the DLC. So if you havent bought the game yet, consider whether you are willing to pay the same price for half content, I did for the sake of the game and for making a review. Also might I add that at the time in which I am making this review not all of the DLC has been released yet, such as the Hardy Boys, the Rock and Roll Express and Beth Phoenix. However I have had fun with some of the NXT characters that are released such as Elias who I gave the IC title too in my Universe Mode. Either way it was a big slap to the community that 2K thought they could brush over with the pretty graphics and bigger roster. Dont be fooled.
Universe Mode: Not much to say here but felt like I needed to touch on it. It is essentially the same as 2k17, there is nothing really added here except for the "Power Rankings!" which really dont do much but add a small buff to wrestlers who complete a challenge.
"Backstage roaming on MyPlayer/MyPlayer": Oh boy, MyPlayer. Its ok dont get me wrong but "Free ROAM", not so much. Press the "W" key for about 30 seconds and you have seen the whole back area. Not really free roam. You can talk to a few people here and there but you still have really no control over your matches, championships are harder to get than 2K17 and the match cards make NO SENSE! I saw a match card the other night where Karl Anderson was fighting Brock Lesnar on a Monday night show. Now anyone who watches WWE knows 2 things, 1, Brock doesnt just show up to fight someone on a Monday Night show, if he shows up at all its for a promo which he doesnt even speak at, Paul heyman does that. And 2 Karl Anderson would NEVER want to fight nor would he fight Brock Lesnar. Then you have cards where Neville (Who isnt even with the company anymore) Is fighting Braun Strowman and Sheamus in a triple threat, though Neville was on 205 live. Its a messy system that makes these cards. I fought Mark Henry the other night, and he doesnt even wrestle anymore. Its just a bad bad mess.
No major Updates: Seth Rollins, the man on the cover, doesnt have his updated music.....
*Music Hits*
*Waits*
*Screams BURN IT DOWN!!!!!*
*No "burn it down" in the entrance*
Seth Rollins, The Usos, Big Cass, Baron Corbin, Chad Gable, Jason Jordan, and more dont even have updated entrance music. And speaking of Gable, I know that Shelton Benjamin came back half way through the year but you couldnt even add him as a DLC? I have to use a terribly designed Shelton from the download a CAW area to use with Gable and they dont have their theme music. Its bad, really bad. Baron Corbin's new entance music is some of the best entrance music ever and I have to wait another year to hear it.
"BE LIKE NO ONE": Here is the big whammy. This "Theme" for the game is false. Be like no one my butt. Almost everything clothingwise and moves wise is locked in MyPlayer Mode. You have to open chests and roll for those clothing items and moves. In 2K17 all clothing was unlocked already. Moves you had to pay your in game cash to buy new moves sets, which wasnt bad. But in this game you use your hard earned money to roll chests in hopes that you get the item you want and then here is the kicked..... YOU HAVE TO PAY FOR IT AGAIN! Thats right people, if you roll a chest and get a shirt, you have only just unlocked the shirt, but to truly unlock it you must pay for it again. Normall a chest roll is anywhere from 5000 to 15000 cash. And to unlock it it may cost a 25 cash to a couple of hundred cash. But you just wasted 5000 to 15000 cash rolling to unlock the item. Its a messed up system that makes you wait and use your "Luck" to "#BELIKENOONE". Again Dont be fooled.
In closing, this game had great potential. But failed worse than 2K17. Shiny graphics, THE NEW BIGGEST ROSTER, and that dumb prahse "BE LIKE NO ONE" was what they used to try to win people over, it worked. But if you havent bought the game yet, do your research before you make a final decision please. And read the review over a time or two. What I am telling you is no lie. If you buy the game or have bought it already you will find the same issues I am talking about here. I think at this point, the Devs listening to their playerbase and then adding updates on is the only thing that can save this game now. Just be weary before and when buying. If its not for you and you feel the same way, get a return on your money. In the end I have to give WWE 2K18 4/10. And thats being generous, I would not recommend it. Again thank you for reading. And if you have any questions feel free to ask or if you want to give your point of view on a particular comment of this review just go for it. Either way thank you and have a nice day.

Out There Somewhere is a 2D platformer game which would have fit right in back on the NES. While the graphics are probably a bit better than what would have been around back then in some places, on the whole this is a pixel graphics game whose gameplay harkens back to a much simpler time.
You play Yuri, a space cop in hot pursuit of Grigori, some sort of bad guy. You start out trying to shoot down his ship, fail, and then have to travel across the planet to confront him and collect a light orb to repower your ship and beat him down in the end-game.
The game is very simple. It claims to be inspired by Cave Story, Super Metroid, and Portal, but honestly it is its own thing, and not very much like any of those games. It is very linear, there isn’t much of a plot, and it is very centered around its central game mechanic – a teleportation gun.
When Yuri fires his gun, he gets teleported to wherever it hits, with whatever momentum he presently has being preserved. He cannot teleport if he is already right next to the surface he would be teleporting to.
He can also jump.
These two mechanics make up pretty much all of the gameplay in the game. You do eventually get a gun you can kill monsters and destroy certain blocks with partway through the game, which opens up a few more puzzles, but most of the game is centered around platforming with the teleportation gun – including one room towards the end of the game with no platforms in it at all, which the player scales by shooting shots across the room, landing, then jumping just as the shot hits the far wall.
The game cost 50 cents on sale, and is extremely short – this is the sort of thing you can beat in a single sit down. I was pretty heavily achievement and secret hunting and beat the game in 89 minutes my first time through. All that’s left at that point is trying to figure out how to acquire the last few secrets, many of which are pretty devious (such as requiring you to go through about a third of the game without saving once so you can die and respawn at the very start with the block-destroying gun, in order to acquire one of the secrets).
Was it worth 50 cents and an hour and a half of my time? I can’t say I wasn’t entertained by it, but it wasn’t high-quality entertainment – the game is decent enough as what it is, but it is not exactly aiming for the stars. If you like 2D platformers with simple, straightforward mechanics, this is probably a decent choice for you; if you like nice graphics, complex gameplay, a sophisticated story, or anything else like that, you’ll probably be disappointed by this game.

At first, the stem controller is a very foreign way to play. The controls are strange. However, the sleek and comfy design for the grip of the controller is amazing! I get a feeling of awesomeness when I hold the controller. So, how does this controller hold up in gameplay?
I have many different types of games (ranging from FPS to annoying, reflex-based games) and I have tested the controller on most of them.
Pros to the Steam Controller:
Excellent comfort design
Trackpads are extremely precise
Haptic feedback feels AWESOME
Button pressed are easy and hassle-free
Cons to the Steam Controller:
Bumpers feel a bit cheapy
The XYBA buttons are a *little* too small
The USB Wireless dongle does not snap into the controller
By far, for me anyway, the steam controller beats my xbox one controller for pc games. The only other neutral-con like statement is that, because of its precision, aiming wile zoomed in in certain games is a little too touchy....making fireing accurate shots difficult. This can be corrected via the gyoscope function.
This controller has excelled in the following games:
Portal 1,  2
Half Life 2, E1, E2, and Deathmatch
I am Bread
Long Dark
140
Mini Metro
The controller acted kind iffy in these games:
Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain
Alien Swarm
Overall, however, I would highly recommend the controller to my friends, family, and fellow Steam gamers.

Valve truly threw previous controller design conventions aside, successfully reimagined the possibilities of what controller design could be and boldly created something so revolutionary it prompts me to dare say, this may possibly have the potential to be the greatest input device ever created. Valve has truly redefined what we've previously come to expect from a controller and has set a new standard for peripherals in a whole.
With near daily updates, that add to its functionality which, will continually ensure its further evolution, the Steam Controller is the best investment money can buy for the PC gaming enthusiast who refuses to sacrifice their comfort, precision and customization abilities when in the market for a hand held input device.
(Please read below for the full review. Thank you for reading and have a nice day.)
Let's state the obvious first. The Steam Controller looks like it belongs in the seventh dimension. Bearing no resemblence to the designs of it's competitors, the Steam Controller simply looks out of this world.
With its sleek matte black finish and gloss trim, the Steam Controller is quite attractive and visually appealing. It's bizarre look will immediately draw your attention to its curious appearance. Curvatious and cool are the first things that come to mind when looking at this futuristic looking new device. The Steam Controller most definitely has personality to say the least.
The slick black touch pads, face buttons, triggers, bumpers and analog stick, all seamlessly blend into the Steam Controllers appearance adding to its appeal, with the final touch of an illuminated home button that serves its purpose, yet isn't intrusive.
Overall, visually the modernized Steam Controller design is a welcome change to what's become an almost standardized and boring peripheral within the industry.
Nearly symbiotic, the Steam Controller is by far the most ergonomic controller available on the market today. Incredibly natural feeling upon first grasp, the Steam Controllers design shines in many areas, yet its ergonomics might possibly be the strongest aspect to its design overall.
Its curvatious design feels incredibly appealing when in hand and this well thought out aspect of the Steam Controllers design will ensure that long play sessions feel just as comfortable in the tenth hour as it did in the first.
Simply put, Valve nailed the ergonomics to such a degree, that it makes competitors offerings obsolete within this category and that's an understatement to say the least.
The Steam Controllers key configuration customization is so incredibly broad it's literally improssible for me to even scratch the surface of the available options to the end user in a review.
With the easily understandable key configuration customization software available via Big Picture, you'll have access to nearly any combination of input devices at your fingertips. From trackball and mouse, to mouse-like joystick mode and directional pad, those examples are literally a mere fraction of what you'll have available as options.
Configuring the Steam Controller to perfection, isn't an easy feat by any stretch of the imagination, but when you finally adjust it to pin point accuracy, you'll be amazed at the results.
The Steam Controller is a remarkable achievement in bold controller design and ingenious engineering. With near endless customization abilities, the Steam Controller will only grow to be more flexable with each firmware and software update, while competitors controllers will remain limited by their lackluster designs and limited creative vision.
The Steam Contoller will far exceed your expectations as well as investment, pending you're willing to invest the time to learn to use this new input device to it's fullest potential. Simply put, what you put into it, is what you'll recieve and it's worth every ounce of effort and thensome if you value your gaming experience regardless of genre.
Valve has seamlessly created a new input device that makes you think about gaming and the way you go about it in a different way. If you consider yourself a serious gamer, then you owe it to yourself to experience this incredibly rewarding device.

It's, as the store description says, inspired by portal and it's futuristic FPS setting, where the mechanic consists of "polarities" (red and blue) that make you interact with different objects in the level, while finding 3 collectibles per level.
The thing that ruins it is, first off, the length.
I feel that considering how short this game is (i finished the singleplayer campaign 100% in a bit more than an hour) i feel that 10 dollars is not worth the price at all. I'd say that a price tag around $5 would make it better.
Second off is the fact that it doesn't make much use of it's main mechanic.
As the name implies, the main mechanic is the previously mentioned polarity. However, the game mainly consists of throwing and moving cubes around, with little to no polarity use, wich is dissapointing (I should also mention that polarity only affects 2 objects, lazers and hard light walls).
Overall, i think that with a bit of more working around the main polarity mechanic, and making the levels longer and more complex would make this worth the price, but as it is now i don't reccomend getting this normally (On sale, however, it might be a good way to spend an hour or so)
