Great game if you want something similar to Civilization and Sins of a Solar Empire mashed together.  Unfortunately Paradox didn't take much of the intrigue from their games like Crusader Kings, while their are individual characters there is no real interaction between them.  Paradox is consistently updating the games content (and fortunately they keep all the major patches available if you prefer a specific version of the game).
You can expect continued development from Paradox, but a lot of content will be DLC if Crusader Kings II is any indication, so expect to pay a hefty sum if you want more flavor.  The Workshop is a mixed bag of goodies, but a lot of content will require various DLC to use, which may become prohibitive in the future.
Now for a minor rant:
While Stellaris is good as it is now, it has a lot of potential to be much better.  Right now Paradox is trying to work out some of the imbalances in the gameplay.  I personally prefer if they focused on diversifying the gameplay, the aspect I enjoy the most in Stellaris is the exploration of the unknown while attempting to bring my interstellar empire a prosperous future.  While Stellaris has some strategy elements, I hope they don't sacrifice the diversity (and its inherent inbalances) in order to make the gameplay more "safe". I hope they overhaul the diplomacy at some point, but I wouldn't expect too much if your a Crusader Kings fan.

I like Stellaris, I do, but there's simply one MAJOR flaw that will potentially ruin your experience with this game: LATE GAME LAG.
What is this, you ask? Simple, once the game advances into it's medium to late state it slows down to an almost unbearable pace. Stellaris, like Hearts of Iron, has a handful of speed settings. You got your pause, your slow, normal, fast and fastest. Well, once you cross that sweet spot when empires start getting big, the fastest you'll go is NORMAL.
Now, I don't mind spending a lot time with my game, that's kind of the point, isn't it? But I don't want to spend all my sunday afternoon waiting for twenty or thirty in-game years to pass! It REALLY ruins the experience when you feel like you are spending your time waiting for the game!
If this where to be fixed, the game is very serviceable. It's no Hearts of Iron, mind you, if you were looking for any of the strategic depth of HOI I'm afraid you'll go wanting. In Stellaris, everything boils down to who has the biggest blob. You put all your fleet into one place and duke it out with your enemy, then it turns into a game of cat and mouse where whoever won chases the remnants of the loser until they are totally crushed. Makes for really dissapointing wars, with almost always a single flashpoint that decides the entire war (at least for AI, the player may recover if he's got enough resources and production capabilities, but AI is almost always doomed after loosing it's fleet).
So, do I recommend Stellaris? Honestly... no. I can't. At the time of this review I've spent (as previously stated) all my sunday afternoon with a game until I just had to surrender to the lag, and this is not the first time this has passed. You grow your empire, get powerful, ready yourself for war after hundreds of years of managing your planets and resources and then you are just condemned to watching everything in slow motion. Sure, you might get some excitement if you manage to meet the enemy in battle (AI will run away from you if your fleet is stronger), but after that's done it's back to the slogh, waiting to get enough warscore (usually by conquering planets, which isn't anywhere near as fun as it sounds, trust me) so the AI surrenders... And god forbid your enemy was large, otherwise you'll be hard pressed to conquer him. Most likely you'll just be able to take a few planets and be forced to wait out the cooldown before you can attack again and finish the job (or repeat the cycle over and over until you can).
So no, don't buy Stellaris. Expensive DLC and poor game performance/mechanics make this item not worth your time. Even on sale, the lowered price won't make the game run better and you'll face the same sad truth I just did... realizing you spent what little free time left you have in a game that cuts you out just when things get interesting.
Unplug the phone, hide the clocks, and draw the blinds.  Playing this game you'll easily forget it's Saturday.  Wait... it's Tuesday now???

This was a really enjoyable game. I especially loved the part that I am the leader of a gang and my character is a badass that doesn't hesitate to kill and not a wimp when I'm not controlling him. I originally wanted to buy this cause the main theme was purple, it was at a cheap price and was bundled with the sequels and it was an open world gang world setting like GTA. As I played it, it had its wacky moments which made me have a good time playing it while it had its serious moments too.
To be honest I thought it would look bad but honestly its not so bad, I maxed out the graphics settings and it turned out okay although a lot of the models are still blocky.
The character Models aren't the best looking but I quite liked the character I made plus the voice I chose for him, it was a happy accident where the voice and the face had a weird harmony and created a character that I really liked and was funny at a lot of times.
There is a weather system in this game but its only sunny and rainy, it was more of a nuisance rather than a sight to behold.
During the cutscenes, some of the items like phone, cash and other things that the characters would hold would just fly in the air and there was a time were my character and the enemy was teleporting inside the car which was a bit of a nuisance but it didn't ruin the game experience.
The gameplay was really fun, I like how I can take over territories or hoods as the game calls them and taking out enemy gang members. There are different activities scattered around the map if you are bored with the main missions or just need to gain more respect for missions.
The only thing I didn't like was the fact that my healing items needed to be toggled via q+directional keys and the worse part is that the directional keys left and right are binded to taunt and compliment which made emergencies hard when the I miss the q button and just press the directional keys... **UPDATED**
Initially (as you'll read below), the game ran horrendously for me. It was on my old PC which had similar specs to Xbox One but the game ran infinitely worse on PC. Besides the shaky release when the game would crash at launch, it had terrible performance. This game was perhaps the catalyst for me moving to console this generation. I decided I could no longer put up with the lack of guarantee for playability and so I bought an Xbox One (and PS4) and bought the game on that, and despite its 720p resolution, it had a much more consistent frame-rate and was highly enjoyable.
I have since built a new PC with much better hardware and I was curious to see how it would run. I put all settings on their highest, so it's completely maxed out at 1440p/144hz (with just motion blur turned off because I can't stand motion blur). Aaaand... the game runs seamlessly at a consistent 70+fps. At worst it goes to the 60's (which is still more than double the Xbox One's framerate at quadruple the resolution and of course max LOD, max post processing effects, etc) . If I were determined enough I could alter the settings in Nvidia Control Panel and maybe I could juice some extra frames out of it but honestly, I'm more than happy as it is. I already loved this game, and I'm not about to go into why I think its good. There are plenty of other gamers here who have given more in depth reviews. I just wanted to correct my previous statements and say that with this hardware, the game is highly recommended! Just remember to unlock the 30fps lock. In the directory, the same folder with the .exe file, just create a user.ini file, open with notepad and paste in 'gmpcr_unlock_frame_rate=True' (no quotes). Done :D
For reference my current specs are EVGA 1070 FTW, i7 6700k, 16GB RAM @ 3200Mhz.

Out There Somewhere is a puzzle game akin to Swapper, VVVVV, Portal, and any number of other games where there is a gimmick to move your playable character through puzzle environments.   Here you play as a tiny spaceman as he shoots rounds from his gun that instantly teleport him when the round hits a surface.  There are many different elements that flesh out gameplay like timed blocks, metal grates, beams that stop the round, beams that bend the round, beams that reflect the round, etc.   Your objective is nothing more than to reach the other side of the room so that you can journey on and collect space components to repair your spaceship.
The graphics are pretty simple but are charming in their own right.  It's just some dark alien tileset and the enemies as well as the player are also a tile. Coming from how the game is played you don't need any more.
The music is the only downside as nothing is catchy and may get on your nerves quick if you don't like 40 second BGMs from budget gameboy titles repeating over and over.
All and all you can do no wrong getting this for under or near 1 USD.  Check this out, it's great fun and pretty addicting.

I can't say enough positive things about this game. It's even better than Chapter One, which, while solid, felt almost like a demo or introduction to the game world, without revealing too much of its history and lore. This chapter gets into the real meat of the story. As in the first chapter, the art design, music, characters, and puzzles are all excellent. The main character, Bwana, is hilarious, yet doesn't follow the long tradition of point-and-click (and parser-based) adventure games going back to goofballs like Roger Wilco and Larry Laffer of being an inept loser. Instead, he's more of a happy-go-lucky guy who seems to be enjoying himself no matter what he's doing.
One of the really cool things about this game is that your character, in the course of solving puzzles to progress the game, actually does a lot of good and helps quite a few people improve their lots. It makes the game even more satisfying. I did get slightly stuck here and there on puzzles, but never to the point where I needed to look online for hints. Everything was quite intuitive, and I almost always felt inspired with an idea for how to solve problems. There are lots of clever ideas in the puzzles, and a few relatively straightforward but well designed logic puzzles as well. And you do get a ton of backstory and exposition about what the heck is going on. The game ends on a big cliffhanger, and I absolutely cannot wait for the next chapter. At the rate they're going, it should be amazing.
TL;DR if you've ever enjoyed pont-and-clicks, buy this game. You won't regret it.

Disclaimer, my recommendation is solely based on the foundations of the game and not based on the issues of the port, that I shall leave it to you to research and decide if it is a deal breaker or not. Even with a GTX 1070, I still get slight stutters here and there but it is not so bad, perhaps it may even be because of my hard drive as well. I shall not recommend to buy on consoles either simply because I do not own the game on them so it is up to you to do the research on that front if you choose to do so.
NieR:Automata, in its own right, is an excellent game, story and gameplay wise. Every single character is solidly written, or voiced (I recommend to turn on subtitles with Japanese audio) and are very interesting in general. Graphically though not technically impressive, still really good to look at, when there is no texture disparity (certain textures look god-awful eg one half of a road looks fine and the other looks like garbage, even the Resorep texture mod does not cover some of these textures, unfortunately).
The story is expressed in a way I did not see in video games before (I have never played any of Yoko Taro games until this), to experience the full story, one must go through THREE playthroughs on the same save. The first and second playthrough follow the same story line with the second playthrough as a different protagonist and adding bits of story to the first whilst the third is the continuation of that storyline, thus my point of needing three playthroughs (warm up your emotions beforehand :-) ). Even then, there are 26 endings, though only the first five are the main ones (excluding endings A and B since those are your first two playthroughs, ending E is the canon one, I believe. Thank god for that), the others are mostly minor ones if you failed to do something or choose to not follow objectives. UNFORTUNATELY, you are unable to roam the open world after finishing the story, but, you can still finish the side quests you missed by using Chapter Select. Take note, uniqueness of the story is up to the individual, for me, what makes the story interesting is not only how it plays out, but also what plays it out. Still, this game's story is right up there for me as one of the most memorable!
Combat is really fluid, no hiccups whatsoever and the animations for a perfectly timed dodge is so satisfying, though the second playthrough can get very tedious or outright annoying depending on how you view the hacking mechanic as that is more efficient in taking out enemies than simply slashing away (you will be playing as 9S who can only carry a single weapon). Enemies are well varied, ranging from small stubbies to the big bosses. Weapons are nicely varied as well, with most possessing the same stats but different characteristics so you will not need to use a new weapon that you bought for its stronger stats but you can switch out here and there if you are bored of using one or another. There are also well placed sections of the game playing as an arcade shooter but I shall leave that to you to decide if you would like it or not.

I have only started playing, but already I feel I need to provide a review. Why? Because the PC version does not deserve the bad reputation it has been receiving. It seems most of the issues at launch have been adressed, and using the excellent FAR mod allows you to tweak things in addition.
The keyboard + mouse controls are not the best I've ever seen, but being a lefty I have made far, far worse work in the past. Once you find a control scheme that works, it's perfectly playable, and the quality of the title reflects in the fact that at least in-game the key changes are being shown! That is not the case with all games, and a bonus for me!
As far as the game itself is concerned, and I say this as someone not that much into Anime, it's one of the most fun games I have played in a long time. I had to start over two times already, because you cannot save your game until you beat the first boss, but I didn't mind. You learn, you get better, and it's so much fun. I was apprehensive about the various play styles the game employs, 3D, 2.5D, platformer, top-down, even some form of 'Space Invaders', but, this is so well executed, and just in the right amount, or in a fitting scenario, that it is not confusing or out of place, but rather exciting and refreshing.
I haven't bought a game at full price for a long time either, but if one game is worth the price tag, than this is it. I'm running this on a Core2Quad and a GTX 670, and I have no frame drops, or any performance issues at all at 1080p. I'm using the FAR MOD with the bloom settings turned down to 'Medium', although 'High' might work, too. I don't really care, the game looks beautiful either way.
So, not being a super Anime fan, and not that much of a hack'n'slash fan either, I'm thoroughly enjoying Nier: Automata. The art direction, game play, fight sequences, blending of various play styles; the mix works so well to a point, that if you had asked me before playing it, I'd have not thought it possible.
If you're undecided, but even remotely feel like this could be something you enjoy, don't hesitate and wait as long as I did. Get it now.

This game allows for great emergent narratives. It doesn't impose any kind of lore and all aliens and empires are either created by the player or randomized. It offers a lot of customization options for both the look and playstyle of your empire. It's more of a sandbox for roleplaying than a real game. There's very little challenge, and the game can continue after one of the victory goals has been met.
I made one empire that has two races, one I roleplay as parasites with the "decadent" perk that makes them unhappy without slaves. I made another with two races that is an egalitarian haven where all are free citizens. My favorite that I made starts with robots and is roleplayed as an automated bureaucracy where a small group of programmers maintain the automated government.
A giant negative for this game is the lackluster combat system. The only viable strategy is to send your entire fleet after the enemy's entire fleet, and the one with the most DPS wins. There's no incentive to use better weapons or bigger ships, since the most basic starter ships are more cost effective for high DPS. Ground combat is also boring, since the more expensive ground units can also be spammed to death by the cheapest ones.
It's way too easy to have more minerals, food, and money than you could ever need. You'll quickly outpace all the AI and run out of things to build or buy. There's really no challenge to this game, so it's not a game as much as it is a sandbox.
I'm always finding new interesting things in each new galaxy I generate. Some of them are very subtle, like the pre-space civilization that ended up nuking itself to extinction when I wasn't paying attention. Hunting giant space monsters with my fleet is fun. Some planets may have a secret subterranean civilization that reveals itself in the form of a new race on that planet. Other planets have kaiju that will either join your army as a ground unit or rebel against you.
The exploration pairs really well with the roleplaying aspects. I had a playthrough where I discovered kaiju that joined my army. I researched "powered exoskeletons" and "xeno mounts" along with my kaiju soldiers, so it was fun to imagine a giant monster wearing power armor and riding a giant alien mount. In another playthrough, a slave race from an authoritarian empire spread as war refugees across the galaxy and became leaders of 3 different empires at a time.
Definitely get this if you want a sandbox for roleplaying, exploring, and emergent narratives. If you like games like Dwarf Fortress, you may like this. I wouldn't call this a game though, since there's no real goal or challenge. The combat and economy needs a lot of work before I could recommend this as a real game. It's still worth getting for what it is; just know what you're paying for!

Want the best controller money can buy? Your search ends here with the Steam Controller.
First, I'm not going to say the design is perfect. But, it fits my hands well, and there isn't anything too uncomfortable about it. You could nitpick that it looks weird, or you can get one and experience a better controller for the price.
This thing comes with: Controller, batteries, wireless adapter, adapter stand (you can plug the adapter into the stand instead of directly into the pc) and a USB cable (for the stand or direct connection to your PC). This is much more than any of the Xbox controllers come with, and it's cheaper at $50!
Next, you can customize basically anything you want. The best thing here is to check out some videos of the menus, but once you actually play with it, you will understand just how powerful this controller is. The comparison to this is for example, the Xbox one elite controller, and that costs a staggering $150!
And did I mention it has a gyroscope? You can use the right thumbpad for quick camera movements and the gyro for accurate aiming in FPS's or use it for steering in driving games.
Do yourself a favor and pick this up. You may not see it yet, but valve has reinvented the controller.

Features: As the features say: Four separate word games - Battle monsters, unlock chests, defuse traps and cheat deathl.  Nice variety.  The "cheat death" is a last opportunity to unscramble a word and return to full health.
The RPG element is reflected in the deep combat system - Buffs, critical hits, armor, character attributes, disables, attack modifiers.  Also, as your character levels, s/he can increase in strength (health), agility (damage), wisdom (mana, which increases power sqares), and luck (which increases the gold won in battle).
You can purchase potions that restore health, increase positive attributes for you, and create problems for monsters.
You can purchase equipment, but it's not clear how that upgrades/replaces previous equipment.
Drawbacks?  The reviews will point out that it doesn't support full screen + it doesn't have standard achievements.  The former no longer bothers me.  The latter isn't actually true:   You have in-game goals of unlocking each of 100 monsters, leveling each of 16 heroes (which requires leveling each skill set), and obviously completing all the 6 game stages.
Anyway, two final notes, the game keeps an ungodly amount of stats, which makes it interesting.  The RPG element is enhanced as you decide which types of characters to team up with + which skills become your most dangerous.

After escaping gangsters in Chapter One, Bwana, Kito and Lina arrived at their destination of Port Artue. Still searching for the Underland, Bwana and Kito are arrested and thrown in jail while Lina is taken as hostage by the police. What will happen to our heroes?
I enjoyed that point-&-click adventure because of the atmosphere. There is clearly influenced by Afro-Caribbean (as the characters are inspired from African masks but the way they're talking and the music is more from the Caribbean). Bwana still retains his cool personnality while being perhaps in another world. And that, dear gamers, that what I ask also from an adventure game: characters with a grey personnality as they're reflecting what we are: imperfect. Bwana isn't stupid. Some of his remarks show someone aware of his surrounding, feeling down because of his father's disappearance. Kito, his "street" brother, is a genius when it comes to engineering, despite his cool attitude. Lyna, well-mannered, stays polite and provides information on what may happen in the background. She's never pressuring the boys, apart when they foiled her plan. Besides, the fact that the ambiance is also leading to a comedy game is also doing that.
Here, the graphics are more "modern" as Port Artue seems to be more a city. The ambiance is now more jazzy, which isn't bad in itself. It's changing from the first game.
Anyway, the whole game seemed to be set in a film noir though here, the police is clearly corrupt.
The game is longer than the first chapter, which is a good point, though you need imagination to find sometimes a solution. Besides, the ending is quite different: after the foggy sad town, you're on a tropical island with sun everywhere.
Anyway, I'm very impatient for Chapter Three and to discover what happened really, as some twists were present in this game (not about Lina, though, despite what Bwana may think).
Don't hesitate anyway: The Journey Down is really a good series.

The Journey Down: Chapter Two is a memorable point-and-click adventure worthy of being being compared with the Monkey Island series and Grim Fandango, which obviously served as its inspirations. Every fan of adventure games knows that their overall quality has gone down quite a bit in the recent years, and it is very hard for the modern iterations to live up to the standards set by the old guard. However, while I was playing this game, I felt as if I was transported back to the 1990s. The production quality is superb, the soundtrack kicks♥♥♥♥♥and the noir atmosphere is amazing and creates the atmosphere of a 1950s noir film.
Most of the puzzles are sensible and not that difficult, although some of them can be solved out of order (ahead of time), which makes you wonder "What am I supposed to do with this item?", until you find a use for it later. Only the last one gave me a real headache and made me resort to a walkthrough, but given the overall quality of the game, all is forgiven.
TLDR: if you liked Monkey Island and Grim Fandango, do yourself a favor and get this game.

As far as I'm concerned this is NO downside to this game. It's completely satisfying, as is.
* Still plays like an spiritual sequel to
but with Afro-Caribbean and Pan-African design sensibilites rather than indigenous Mexican aesthetics. Absolutely gorgeous level design and character modelling.
* The puzzles are slightly more challenging than in Chapter One, with a healthy mix of lateral thinking, minigames, and inventory management.
* Even better storytelling than Chapter One. If this started out with heavy Indiana Jones vibes, then Chapter Two brings it firmly into D!ck Tracy territory, with dirty cops, intimidating mobsters, corrupt powers-that-be, and a bleaker urban noir vibe.
* Builds on the setting established in Chapter One. Fascinating, in-depth world-building, from the mistfarer trade and piracy on the "high soup" to the looming threat of the influential San Armando Power Company.
* Quality soundtrack -- a lively mix of laid-back Caribbean island grooves and freewheeling jazz.
Needless to say, I wholeheartedly recommend this game.

The recent sale encouraged me to try this gamr out. As a game Nier:Automata is excellent; animations are smooth and the mechanics are fresh.
The problem is its optimisation. First of all the FPS is hard capped at 60 on even the best graphics cards. The resolution was derped for me, it seemed to be stuck at 720p and I had to download the community-made FAR patch to fix it. After that the only problem was the framerate. On my GTX 960 I was getting 45 fps on minimum settings, 30 on max settings. The low framerate made the game very disgusting to my eye and I got a headache after my test run. The game is not THAT special looking graphics-wise and while that is not a thing to complain about, it definitely lacks optimisation. I do not see a reason for the game to run so poorly. For this reason I ended up not keeping it.
So, IF you have a setup that can handle this game (GTX 1060 or RX 580 at the very minimum) you should definitely give it a try. It seemed really nice and I will definitely repurchase it if I at some point end up getting a new graphics card.

-EDITED AFTER OFFICIAL RELEASE-
Would give neutral review status, but said button does not exist.
I previously said this game was a slight improvement on Primal Carnage, but now I take that back completely. It's reverted to being just like it use to be on PC, only now it has slightly improved performance (Graphics-wise) and an inventory system.
Only 2 new modes are introducted in the game at present; dino deathmatch (dino vs dino, but it is very buggy) and FreeRoam (no timelimit, no killcount.) Both modes are enjoyable but aren't without their faults; Dino Deathmatch limits the player to using the raptor, ptera, diloph and carno classes since the rex bite and tail whip have little effect and can easily be brought down by a pack of raptors. FreeRoam's only drawback is how boring it can become if nobody is roleplaying or if there is no prey to hunt; a much needed addition to FreeRoam to maximise its potential is bots for prey. I STILL hope this will be added eventually.
The graphics are roughly the same as PC, but are far less taxing on a machine and allow for better performance (we FINALLY got support for 32bit! No more crashing maps because of a bitwar mess!).
Sound hasn't changed; the sub-classes minus the Spinosaurus all reuse their dominant class soundfiles, and on some occasions the sound comepletely vanishes from the game with no logical explination or reason, and a restart is the only solution. (They say it is fixed, but it isn't.)
Next on my list is the item drops; the skins, while a nice twist to drops, are mainly generic recolours of existing skins and some actually remove your camo and make you stick out like a sore thumb in maps. Not at all handy for a stealthy raptor or diloph...but the skins do look nice, they're just not that practical. The skin-system is also a monopoly, with players able to "farm" multiple crates and skins using a bot rather than playing themselves, and then selling the rarest skins for insane prices. Personally I would rather just buy the skin DLC like in previous PC, since I don't have the time or motive to farm for the ones I want, but I do see the appeal in keeping one skin set and ditching the ones you couldn't care less about.
So I don't hate the item-drop system, it's just the way the prices go insanely out of control, but then that's the players fault and not the developers.
Speaking of players...
The biggest issue with this game is it's community; the roleplaying section of the group is great! The people are friendly, the games are fun, but sadly this game is actually a FPS/PvP game and does NOT have what is nessecary for an MMORPG like many people want (a dinosaur and human MMO would be great!)
So while I do like going on FreeRoam servers for the occasional RP, I also like to go into the basics this game was originally supposed to have; sadly many of these servers are empty or are full of item farmers, children who clearly migrated from TF2 for the loot, or bots that have wound up on the wrong server to farm for items.
There are also still many issues still not fixed in this game that have been repeatedly addressed by the community.
Old score: 7/10 (It was fun and buggy) My final overall score: 5/10. (Meh.)
+Like the new modes and maps
+Finally can have games with unlimited dinosaurs or no humans at all!
+Still easy to play, but has a LOT of bugs (so it can be frustrating at times)
+Skin drops are a good addition but are a bit out of control
-Key prices are a silly price; £1.99 per skin or object from a crate, when you can buy a skinpack for the same price?
-new sounds should be on the sub-classes instead of reusing their primary classes (STILL an issue!)
-some skins are unpractical and the drop system is still messed up even after patching
-sound and some animations randomly break
-unusual lag in areas containing rain make those maps unplayable
-chatbox vanishes too quickly and does not maintain previous chat if a game suddenly ends and a new one begins.
-Item farmers in Get To the Chopper and Team Deathmatch can ruin those games (we call them "Empty players" or just "Empties").
-Not enough reliable servers; many are laggy, the balance of FreeRoam, Team Deathmatch (Dino Deathmatch included) and Get To The Chopper are ridiculous and some servers will randomly crash and remain down all day.
-Unresolved, reported, bugs and issues have caused many players to abandon the game and thus reduce the amount of players. Don't expect a server besides Item Farming ones to be completely full.
So...should you buy this game? AT any price but 1 of your currecny (be it Euro, Dollar or Pound) I would say no; get it when it's dirt-cheap or when it's free to play. Full-price is simply not worth it considering it is like PC only with item-drops and a few (and I say it again; FEW) new features.

I wish there was a neutral option for rating this game, but I'll make do with a yes because at the very least it's better than the first. The levels look and feel nicer; old ones have been touched up and honestly the environments are absolutely picturesque compared to the first game.
From what little I've played so far the balance seems a lot better between the two teams. I've played and am relatively alright at both dino and human, so no bias here. Admittedly haven’t played every dino, so I can’t cover them all… but I’ll mention what I have in a moment.
As human I love the new weapon system and the fact you can throw down ammo and health for your teammates. While playing every dinosaur is an adequate threat within reason. I like that ‘tyrants’ only kick you around now instead of instantly killing you by walking on you. I’d much prefer they were taken out of the game entirely but I know that if the devs did that their fans would have a shitfit so I’ll just keep the opinion to myself. They have the terrible ability to ‘vacuum’ people into their mouths, too, which is annoying. But overall they’re a bit easier to take on so that’s good.
As both dino and human I have a teeny issue with carnosaur. It no longer feels like a stealth class which needs to get the drop on people in order to achieve kills, which was what I enjoyed about it in the first game. Not sure completely what it is… but I’m not the only one who doesn’t feel quite right about it. It seems a lot harder to dodge even when you see it coming right at you. And a lot less fun to play.
Raptor is perfect. Once you get the hang of steering with a mouse it’s a dream to play, and with the slower speed I actually have a chance of shooting it as a human. So long as my opponent hasn’t done what I previously mentioned, anyway.
Haven’t played enough of the spitter classes to know much about them, but the one that shoots acid seems a little too slow for how big and conspicuous it is.
The drop system disappointed me with the fact it only drops crates… but hey what can ya do. Maybe they’ll actually make it useful later on.
Overall it’s much funner than the first game to me and its nice not having someone hacking and ruining the fun for everyone every other time I decide to play. Gameplay seems more balanced, though it’s certainly not perfect. Not sure if it ever will be with the nature of the game, but it’s still better than the first.

The first thting I noted was the inside of the packaging presenting some form of temperment. It seemed as if the controller was handled by someone else, smudged and covered in hairs. Some parts of the packaging were also torn open, as if the package was a used product. I am not complaining though, as it surely could have been worst.
But, my review will still remain positive for my positive outlook on this intriguing controller.
Comparing it to any other controller on the market would be an injustice, due to it's ergonomic approach, and wonderfully original design. This causes it to stand out in the market, making it immediately appealing, like Nintendo's Power Glove.
But, unlike the Power Glove, this controller works surprisingly well at what it aims for. The build quality is sturdy, the stick  is great, the buttons are great, but those aren't the reason one read this review.
The touchpads are the main focus of this controller. and I always found myself in childlike delight messing with them playing in the original Half-Life game. The right touch pad functions similarly to a track ball that you would find in an arcade, creating a feel of roll when swiped with one's thumb. The utility is impressive, as playing Half-Life created no problems on hard difficulty, and using the controller even got me past hard moments in the game.
The touch pad on the left confuses me the most about the controller. It looks as if it wants to be a directional pad, but functions exactly like the right touch pad. Even if you assigned it as a d-pad, as i did in BattleBlock Theater, it's too big and insensitive to use. It has to be pressed down upon to create the same utility. If custimization is in order in the future, the touchpad should be downsized, and removed of it's clickable state. This would give it the feel of the Sonic the Hedgehog mobile ports and their incredibly refined touch screen controls. That, is my one major caveat of this controller though, as I prefer the directional pad over a stick in a sidescrolling platformer any day.
The last thing to touch on is the usage. This controller is very different, but that's not to say you should not attempt to adapt to it. A controller with this much potential should not be ignored by any PC gamer. Small tweaks to this controller are generally going to happen on launch. The xbox controller ent through that process, and I trust that Valve will find the modifications it needs to make.
I recommend this controller overall, and probably prefer it over my Xbox controller.

Valve created the steam controller with the aim of having a controller that would work just as well for PC games as it would for console ports. I was very interested in the way they designed the controller to adapt to whatever game is being played, be it a MOBA, and FPS, or an RPG.
Overall, however, I was unimpressed with the product. This isn't to say it's a terrible device, but I don't believe it holds up against the competition quite yet. Perhaps the only feature of the controller that particularly stood out to me as good was the paddles on the inside of the handles, which provide an easy alternative control in cases where managing all the buttons may be difficult. Past that is when the praise trails into disappointment.
The two trackpads that would serve as the d-pad and right stick of a normal controller are certainly interesting for their multiple uses, but ultimately fail when they need to be used for those standard uses. The lack of a bump for the four directions of the d-pad makes it very hard to be precise with. The trackpad on the right utterly fails to work as a right stick at any sensitivity I've tried it at. Even when I've used it to control the mouse cursor, I was baffled to find that the cursor decelerates instead of stopping when you lift off the pad (I've heard this can be changed, and perhaps this would make it better as a right stick as well).
Although I've heard some complaints about the buttons, I'm rather neutral to them. They are rather small but I've found that isn't a huge issue. The left stick functions properly, nothing special about that. The controller as a whole feels okay to hold, except maybe when you have fingers on both the R/L buttons and triggers. Connecting physically via the usb cable included can sometimes require you to unplug and plug it in again when the controller seems to drop its connection.
Overall I feel like the controller has a lot of potential, and as others have expressed, this feels like a demo of something much greater to come. I would advise people for now to spend their money on a modern controller or an adapter for one that they already have. Whether you do so or not, I would refrain on buying a steam controller until steam revises the hardware, or until controller profiles mend the issues with the controller.

While you can play as other characters, you start out as Isaac: A young boy whose mother hears or thinks she hears the voice of God telling her to kill her child to prove her devotion. Isaac flees into the basement-dungeon, where he has to fight against hordes of mutant-spawn and cut through blockades of feces, armed only with his (projectile, somehow damaging) horrified tears. At least at first. Later, he can acquire other weapons – for instance, his urine. In case the previous information didn’t make this abundantly clear: If you’re easily offended or grossed out, this is not the game for you.
The game has a certain graphical charm. Just like
, the art walks a line between fluid animation and crude child-like drawings, and the result is very easy on the eyes. You’ll notice the fluidity of animation more than anything else, though the actual environments are still well-done. Be prepared to spend time learning how to strike a balance between picking off enemies and avoiding them. If you run out of health, that’s it – it’s game over for you. This means you start right back at the beginning of the game without any option to start at a later level.
does offer considerable replay value. There are achievements to unlock, secrets to find, new characters to acquire, dozens of enemies to vanquish, and even multiple endings to see.
If you can roll with the macabre toilet humor and if religion jokes don’t put you off, AND if you enjoy games with non-optional permadeath, randomized content, tons of secrets and considerable replay value… it’s hard to go wrong with
.
- Huge amount of items to find
- Bosses are unique and challenging
- Tons of unlockables increase replay value
- Randomized dungeons
- Items lack any description after discovery
- Luck based difficulty
- No save feature

A really good point-and-click game. The story is interesting, the artwork is amazing, with a unique African ("Afro-noir," according to the devs) vibe, and the music is absolutely beautiful. It's part two of three, with three upcoming probably next year. This one picks up right after the cliffhanger ending of the first part and ends with another one, but the story in between does a good job of filling in more backstory and plot without hitting you over the head with a ton of exposition and setting up a couple of twists that lead to the next part.
The only real con I noticed were consistently inaccurate or misspelled captions. I expect at least one typo for any text-heavy game, but there are more in this one than I've seen in a number of amateur games. Some of the voice recordings are of a noticeably lower quality than the rest, but I only noticed that a few times.
Overall, very much worth playing if you like this style of adventure game, even with the episodic nature of it.
In this particular case, I would be absolutely okay with paying full price for the soundtrack as a separate purchase, because it is that good. Also, their original composer passed away last year and apparently there's an album of his music up for purchase., from which all the proceeds go to charity. I think it was a nice touch that they featured that as a very muted 'hey, if you like his music, you can get this, too' ad at the end of the behind-the-scenes extra that's unlocked once you finish the game.

WWE2k18 does a good job of hammering out some wrestling mechanics that are solid.  However, it needs some help in other areas for sure.
The major issues with the game are the MyCareer and to a lesser extent Universe mode.  MyCareer is terrible this year.  First, there is no way to import or export MyPlayer created wrestlers.  MyCareer requires a created wrestler, so you can't play it as a default WWE star at all.  Second, if you make a wrestler in free play you cannot import that wrestler for use, and must make a new MyPlayer CAS.  Third, if you make a wrestler in MyPlayer it only works in MyCareer, it cannot be exported to Universe mode or Free Play.  This is obnoxious.  Sadly creating your wrestler in MyPlayer is entirely subject to loot box RNG as the overwhelming majority of moves, costume pieces, etc are locked behind the loot box system.  Lastly there is way too much pointless walking around in the backstage area of MyCareer and a ton of deadspace that doesn't meaningfully improve on your game play experience.  For example, you must walk to and from a security guard to get into/out of your car every night that you perform.  This is just a frustrating waste of player time.  It might be different if you could get into confrontations and brawls in the backstage, but its mostly just a bunch of random wwe stars milling about aimlessly, and annoying WWE employees who stalk the main hallways getting in your way. The interactions you can have are pretty lame, just little custscenes with overlay text, really boring and pointless. It had me wishing for the single locker-room screen to manage this stuff from, just getting phone calls and texts to advance storylines like I recall from a previous WWE game. MyCareer mode can be considered a total failure in this year's version of the game.
In Universe mode there needs to be a way to focus it more on your wrestler, created or stock.  As it is, there is way too much show management and not enough focus on in ring action.  Most of it concerning wrestlers and rivalries that just waste the player's time with a bunch of fiddly micromanagement that will never be of importance to what their wrestler is doing.
Free Play is the only mode I found to be consistently fun to play, especially with the addition of match creation. Match creation is awesome, I would just ask for even more customization options here otherwise well done 2K here.  Maybe look into adding back create a finisher and we'll be in good shape.  Also I must give credit to 2K for making moves feel much more impactful this year.
In all modes, there are still far to many load screens, splash screens, etc. All breaking up gameplay flow and taking away from time actually in the ring playing the game.
The promo system is also just bad.  I messed with it for awhile, and its just not fun or entertaining.  Just being text overlays, which often don't match up with what you thought you were trying to say just did nothing for me.  Also the wrestler's gestures during promos seemed bizarre, I mean Brock Lesnar dancing around during a promo (Hell Brock even having a promo that isn't cut by Paul Heyman!) was silly. This whole mechanic needs to be scrapped and redesigned.
There are some issues with mechanics and animations, bugs etc.  In general it feels like the ring needs to be bigger.  Irish whip rebound grapples are a bit tough to consistently pull off because there is so little space in the ring.  Throwing opponents off hell in a cells, entrance ramps, tops of big rigs has a stilted delay to it that messes up the flow.  Hell in a cell in general is a bit of a mess.  The cage is too close to the announcer tables, and throwing guys off the top isn't as smooth as it could be. Doing moves through the center of the cell panels is basically non-existent.  I do like the return of total control type moves, but I missed not having a chokeslam position.  Perhaps in the future, offer a selection of total control move positions that a player can select in move-set creation? That said, it would also be nice if moves other than these could throw opponents off things and over ropes in a more organic fashion as well.
Bugs, the game has a ton, some highly debilitating, that prevent the game from even launching for some people, many that have required restarting a match because of severe animation glitches or wrestlers becoming stuck in the walls or outright falling through out of the play area.  These significantly hurt the game overall, because they are more serious than anything else, when they mean a customer cannot even play the game they've bought.
Online, I own this on PC, so I don't know how it is on consoles, but wait times for matches are so long I have never mustered the patience to really play online, so I can't  speak further on it.
Sadly, as much as I love WWE video games, this year's offering, with the unforgiveably bad MyCareer mode design and loot box shenanigans, I cannot recommend this as I wish I could.  There is fun to be had if you aren't affected too badly by bugs, bothered by the same things I am, or are fine playing in only one maybe two of the available modes, otherwise its a disappointment over previous games despite any improvements made to the mechanics.  Sadly even those get marred because for anything 2K made better, some other choices were made that made the game worse imo.  So its a net backstep overall.
I am a diehard wrestling fan, so I am able to find a way to make it fun despite all the missteps, but I cannot recommend this in general to folks.  2K is close, as a fan of these games, I can see the potential for a very good game just out of reach, but out of reach it remains and I can only hope 2K improves for WWE2K19, because it isn't there yet.

How about the game itself? Well, it is extremely hard for me to find a game that can entertain me, and this game is one of those that don't entertain me for long periods of time, but thats not why I'm even downvoting it. I'm downvoting it because of the loot system, for the most part. Look at the server list, and you'll see a barren wasteland of empty TDM and GTTC servers except for remote and sparsely populated ones, and then absolutely BOOMING loot servers that are 100% full.
Devs, you know you have a problem when your players care about the loot and not the gameplay. It also doesnt help when it seems half-broken aswell, getting the same sandstorm ptera SIX times in a row and getting no alphas. Not even  one rare after about 20 crates, has happened to someone, who then had to resort to buying them off the steam market in order to get anything half-way decent. Also, Im one of those people who don't have a job quite yet, and the fact that the only way to open crates is to BUY keys. I have to ask my previously mentioned friend for money whenever I get a crate, hanging on to that glimmer of hope that maybe, just maybe, I'll get a good skin. In case you're wondering, I only got one skin, atleast  until my friend had to trade a bunch of extras she had to me, then I got one, maybe 2 others that I already got from her. ♥♥♥♥♥♥ ones of course. I have seen very few if any new players that didn't have the original one, and to be frank, the gameplay is a bit lackluster.
The graphics are pretty good, but honestly who cares about that?  I don't think they should drop the loot system, just... change it in some way that I'm not entirely sure about. Maybe tweak the drop rates and make it so you don't have to buy keys, but instead drop them like crates? That would help with the younger people who dont have any money. Anyways, I just want you to know that I myself had the original game, and got it after hearing about it through youtube, and I just fell in love with the idea. There were times I really enjoyed it, too. But this game just isn't the same. I want the game to succeed, but its not going to at this rate.
Sorry for the rant, this is my first review, but I just felt strongly about this. I loved the original, but the loot system and what seems like almost corporate greed and just the gameplay itself just doesnt do it for me. I wouldn't recommend the game in its current state, especially when all the players care only about getting loot. I hope the devs realize what's happening and take steps in the right direction, get the sequel on its feet, but until then, Browse with caution.

For a while, I played the vanilla non-stop regardless of the obvious poor quality of the port, the game's THAT good. But after some time, even I couldn't hande the millions of porting problems the game has. It ran at a cinematic (*scoff) 20 fps and had the most unintuitive and obstructing menu controls I have ever seen, not to mention the embarrasingly wonky keyboard driving and the annoying "respect meter". As my problem with the "respect meter" is subjective while other are technical, let me focus on that first.
Basically, the game requires you to fill up a "respect bar" by doing illegal-type things and side-missions in order to do a main mission. Now, I understand  that this is to add some pace and player choice into the game, (because now I have to choose which gang's main mission I want to prioritize, etc,) but I much rather prefer doing whatever missions I want whenever I want and not being forced to do certain side missions I dislike in order to get to the main missions.
It's like force feeding someone chips before a five star meal. I like chips, but I would much rather eat them when I want to rather than being forced, thank you very much.
Thankfully, as you've probably guessed by the recommendation of the review, I found a solution to most if not all m issues. Enter the "Gentlemen of the Row" mod. After this mod the game runs at a more acceptable 45-55 fps  and adds optional controller prompts to replace keyboard prompts. And most importantly, the optional infinite respect mod solves my annoyances with the respect bs.
Been in love with the game all over agian ever since.

It's definitely a wierd looking controller, but after hearing some good things about, I decided to try it out.
*Note: Only tried it for several hours with Fallout 4 after using a standard Xbox controller originally.
TL;DR
Great controller for the keyboard/mouse crowd wanting to relax while playing.  Controller users might want to wait on a redesign unless you want to learn how to use a controller all over again.
I really liked the customization options for the controller, and the addition of the left and right grips allows for more keyboard shortcuts to be used on a controller that would be difficult to do on a standard Xbox controller.  The trackpads, even the "D-Pad" one are very on point.  I never felt like it didn't respond the way I wanted it to.  The ergonomic design was surprisingly comfortable, and I never felt my hands feeling like they needed to reposition even after a couple hours of play.  Having the community be allowed to share their personal touch on configurations is awesome, and made it easy for me to find one that I liked while still tweaking it midgame if I needed to.  This controller is definitely something that could really change gaming, if it weren't for a few things that I would prefer they change up a bit.
First and foremost, if you already are used to using a standard controller on your PC, know that you will find quite a learning curve trying to control your game.  Even after a couple of hours, I still sometimes hesitated to do something, either because I forgot what I had actually assigned for a particular button, or because I find the main X, A, Y, B buttons are just too low and too close to the center of the controller.  Many times I've tried to press A to activate something, only to find nothing happening because I was pressing Y the whole time.  The right touch pad is good, but I felt it was too sensitive, and a little high up, which meant I would be moving my thumb to hit a button only to slightly touch the bottom of the touch pad and have my character suddenly be looking down.  I had reassigned all the buttons to match their corresponding keyboard keys, so that Fallout would think I was playing with a keyboard and mouse.  That's where the grips defintely saved me as using a keyboard and mouse has the game assigning sometimes only one particular action to one key, unlike a normal controller which changes their usage depending on what's happening in game.  The reason I changed it to be a keyboard/mouse config was that I really liked the idea of having a mouse pointer to select things in the world, or make hacking or using V.A.T.S. easier to choose what I wanted to aim at.  For the most part it worked great, but the mouse cursor sensitivity seemed to change depending on whether I was in first person mode or looking at my Pip-Boy or other menu type screen.  Probably the biggest thing I feel should be changed though is the left stick.  It's radius seems to be much smaller than those used on standard controllers, and though I don't mind it's placement (I also use a PS4), due to this small turning radius, it is actually difficult to just make it recognize down.  It would more often do down/right, making menus a real pain to use.
I still think this is a good controller and has a lot of potential, but I feel I would recommend it more for the PC gamer that really doesn't use standard controllers too much, since those that do will have a much steeper learning curve.  I actually compare it to Year One Destiny, you can see the awesome potential it has, but there are a bunch of little things that add up to make you frustrated that they were so close to making it completely awesome.

At very first I must say I enjoyed the game a lot.. for a while. I don't like anime at all but I was very bored and I decided to try a game outside of my comfort zone. The graphics is ok, music is bit of repetetive and story was ok. Although the missing voice acting makes this product feel like low budjet game.
The game is extremely grindy. You can get levels quite fast at the beginning by doing quests but after level 45 things will change. The main quest ends about level 55 and after that you have to grind your level through dailies and dungeons. And that's really painful indeed.  Actually the one thing I liked was that you can run some of the dungeons on solo mode. So you actually had something to do while you waited your guildies to gather their group for 5 men dungeon run. I liked also the skill system and especially the thing that you can spend the attribute points like you really want. However there isn't too much options for effective character builds and that's the reason it feels very simple.
Crafting is also typical Korean style click&pray function. You farm the materials, find/buy the blueprint and click the "craft" -button. I was quite surprised when I saw the dumbed down crafting system because even the fishing is one kind of mini game. There aren't any kind of level or skill system for crafting or fishing. Fishing "skill" is based on your fishing gear and crafting level is equal with your adventure level. Nothing special... or actually there is. The crafting is huge money sink because the challenge is replaced with carfting costs.
Well, that was the game play in nut shell. Now I'm going to tell some things that I didn't like at all. The backpack size is very limited at the beginning. This encourages player to buy some more backpacks with APs. The AP is a game currency that you can only get with real money. Sure you can buy those backpacks with loyalty points later but you really have to play a lot to get enough points for 20 slots backpacks. Some people are sellng those through the AH but because of gold farmers the prices are very high.
Aaaannd.. those gold farmers. Seriously! That's the biggest issue in game at the moment. There is hundreds.. or even thousands of bots those are questing, doing dailies and killing stuff. For example I was in Navea (capital city) and counted over 120 bots running in same loop in 30 minutes. Can you imagine? The similar looking red haired gunners had a long endless train from quest givers to another. It was insane! I played GW2 since the beta and I thought there was very large number of bots. But no.. the amount of bots is nothing to compare the number of bots in AK. There is more bots in game than actually real players and Arial Games just can't get rid of them. People are buying gold and gold farmers are making more bots. There is already some lag issues because of botting and reporting doesn't help at all. That's is the reason I quit this game and I just can't recommended this game to anyone. Oh, except if you need a good platform for bot or two. This game is definitely suitable for that.

The second part of this Rastafari-themed adventure game miniseries is somewhat shorter than the first one, but makes up for it with a more engaging story, interesting locations, and complex puzzles.
The Journey Down: Chapter Two took almost two years to reach the players, but it was worth it. The overall tone got a significant revamp, giving it an actual feel of adventure and thrills instead of being a puzzle game with a funny cast.
Even though the characters still act the same way (which is a good point, since they made the first chapter so memorable), the plot is a lot thicker around them. You have to explore a new city where everything seems to be crooked and corrupted, and where the mystery of Kanandodo and his discovery run deeper than ever, making the story progress in territories you may have not even suspected…
…when said story actually progresses. Because the game’s difficulty has increased, despite being made for tablet players. There is less crazy adventure game logic involved, but you have to backtrack often, and a lot. And the last puzzle… even point ‘n’ click veterans may hit a brick wall there.
Still, the game is quite short, shorter than the first chapter, with around 2-5 hours of play time. But the content is so strong that this drawback is barely recognisable.

what is Nier Automata? a masterpiece of a game, probably one of the best examples that video games could be considered art
but lets start off with some cons instead of some pros
=CONS=
-game is in desperate need of a patch as the game has some stability issues when in full screen mode, however you could play it in windowed without any too severe hiccups (i got a gtx 970)
-framerate can have sudden dips sometimes
-cutscenes play at 30fps? (go get FAR, it'll make the cutscenes play at 60fps)
-theres one scene (no spoilers) at the very very end of the game which has a severe framerate drop, it was running at like 20 or 15 fps during that segment
-the entirety will leave you wanting more even after 50ish hours that the entire story will take you (including most of the side quests and alternate endings)
now for the praise the game deserves
=PROS=
-combat in nier is mixed, its hack and slash meets bullet hell but it feels very fluid and responsive, a thrill to cutdown enemies
-world is beautiful however will feel small when compared to most other open world games
-the music is also a masterpiece, beautiful music and is made dynamically, as its layered, there are instrumental only and vocal only versions of the songs which allows the music to play in a interesting matter while progressing a area, there is also 8bit chiptune versions of all the music for the hacking segment
-story line may seem strange on the surface or at first, but is a really great story, the multiple items (truely is only 5 real story endings and the other 21 endings are joke endings)
-character customization, and i don't mean appearance as that area is very shallow, however i mean the skill chips (special traits) that you can add to your character, like exp boost, drop rate boost, more percentage of personal melee/ranged damage
-likeable characters that you'll get a personal attachment to

First, I'll say I already completed the game on a different account with 45 hours in it. I’m currently playing through it again on this account.
Aside from its common technical issues, this is truly a great game. I didn’t think much of the game going into it, but by the time I was done, I was blown away just how good it was. For those that are unfamiliar with NieR Automata, you need to play through the game 3 times in order to experience the full game. The 3rd play through unlocks the 2nd half of the story. So, don’t stop when you finish it the first time.
As already complained by others, the only thing that drags this game down on PC are the known technical issues. On my first completion, I played with ReShade and crashed maybe 10-12 times out of the entire 45 hours. Playing through it again on this account, I’m using Reshade + FAR mod and I have noticed a significant reduction in crashes with the FAR mod. So, the FAR mod does appear to help and I recommend installing it before you start playing.
Overall, I did not find the crashes to be game breaking, just mildly annoying. If you make a habit of quick saving every time you fast travel, the crashes will only really have a minor impact when they occur. I do hope that they patch these known crash issues at some point though so more can enjoy the game to its full extent.
Despite the technical issues, I still recommend this game as it is one of those rare gems that everyone should play at some point. This game is easily my game of the year and I don’t hand that title down easily.
My overall score is a 9/10
If there were no crashing problems, I would rate the game a 10/10.

The social and political angles of the game are really what recommend it. The innovative use of values, government type, ethics, and traditions to build a unique culture and ethos for your empire is really unique and breath of fresh air compared to titles that have toyed with the idea in the past. It's especially satisfying that your citizens will form political issue parties based on their own random values, and reward the player for pandering to them. Another intriguing aspect is the various forms of FTL travel that add comfortable yet flavorful hint of unpredictability to the strategic nature of the game. Lastly the end game crisis mode effectivly adds an end game boss challenge which will test the mettle of all but the strongest players in the game, and providing a climactic ending to what would otherwise be an anticiapted outcome.
This game is really fun,and with a vast amount of dev support and workshop mods that make the game interesting.

As I awaited the arrival of my Controller on Nov. 10th, I watched a lot of reviews from people who got theirs in October. I feel like many of them gave unfair assessments of the controller based on a few key notes they made.
1. One thing I heard frequently was "Just get an Xbox One controller for $10 more, it's better." DO NOT LISTEN TO THIS. These reviewers are completely missing the point of the Steam Controller. It isn't mean to completely replace traditional gamepads; only to bridge the gap between KB+M and gamepads. It has completely customizable inputs, gyro/accelerometer, and the trackpads can emulate joystick OR mouse input. Through Steam you can even download configurations on a game-by-game basis that were made by the devs or the community, make personalized tweaks to it, and remap anything on the fly by accessing the Steam Overlay.
2. The concave design appeared to be a turn-off for a lot of the reviewers. After a couple hours of use I found it quite comfortable; it places emphasis on the trackpads. If anything, I had to get used to the face buttons being so far out of the way.
3. Several of the reviewers unboxed the controller, plugged in the wireless receiver, and hopped right into Counter Strike and said the controller sucks. While I scarcely recommend it for twitch-style shooters, the biggest offense here is not properly configuring your controller. There is definitely a learning curve here, and taking the time to set the controller up will simultaneously familiarize you with the layout. For instance, when I play a shooter, I use the right trackpad as a high-sensitivity mouse, then use the gyro as a low sensitivity joystick. After some practice I was able to jerk toward my target with the trackpad, then twist the controller in my hand to line up the shot.
Games I've played with the controller personally, followed by a ranking on how well it worked:
Grand Theft Auto V - not bad at all, using a community-made scheme. Combines the being able to control a vehicle with analog, with the superior shooting precision of a mouse.
Diablo III - this one took some creativity, but worked out really well. I set the D-pad to skills 1-4, and the Grip buttons underneath the controller to Left Click and Right Click. Left trigger for Force Stand-Still. Remaining buttons are for menus, map, potion, etc. Probably won't be pushing GR70 but you can sit back and farm Torment difficulties in comfort.
Call of Duty: Black Ops III - The dreaded shooter. I'm already not particularly great at the game, so mouse/kb is definitely preferred. This is where I set up the gyro, etc. Stil nothing on a good ol' mouse. In Campaign, Zombies, or bot matches it works with practice.
The Witcher III: Wild Hunt - Set the controller to basically be a normal gamepad. Works great, very comforable. Additional inputs on bottom of controller are used for keyboard stuff.
World of Warcraft - Similar boat as Diablo. If you get creative with key modifiers then you can map all the abilities you need. I wouldn't raid or PvP with it, but for solo leveling or farming it works just fine.
Dark Souls II: Scholar of the First Sin - probably the hardest for me to get used to, as it's the game I've played the most with my Xbox One controller. I set the controller trackpad to emulate mouse input for camera movement rather than joystick, and set the Right Grip button to B so I can sprint while keeping my thumb on the camera control. I think the hardest thing for me was how the shoulder bumpers angle downward almost, and the shoulder buttons are the most important in Dark Souls. The controller works leagues better than a keyboard and mouse for Dark Souls, but if you have a more traditional gamepad, may be better to stick with it for this one.
The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim - The biggest pain here was Bethesda locking the game to either gamepad, or keyboard and mouse, whereas the Steam Controller can openly emulate both at the same time. If a gamepad is detected in Skyrim (Also in Fallout 4) it renders your KB+M useless until it's unplugged. It would have been so easy to choose the default mapping 'Gamepad + mouse input on trackpad," but instead required customizing all the inputs for keyboard. That said, it works okay once you get used to it. Since the movement will be emulating WASD, and not a joystick, it kind of loses the only advantage that a controller has with Skyrim. That being said, it still works, and is a solid way to play that's wireless without getting Microsoft's expensive proprietary receiver.
Rocket League - Seemed like an obvious choice, since the controller comes packaged with it. It was a great use of the dual-stage triggers; squeezing the trigger accelerates, fully pulling it uses your Boost. I set the Grips underneath to jump and powerslide so I never have to take my thumb off the trackpad. Works really well.
Well that's all I've tried for now. I might do something similar for my YouTube channel with footage of me using it. Thanks for reading :)

SINGLE PLAYER EXPERIENCE:
ok this is a review after almost 2 years of owning  multiable steam controllers. I would say if you are wanting a replacement for your Xbox controller or your PS controller you've deffinitly came to the wrong place. The steam controller was made for PC games that COULD not work with a native controller at all. I have used this controller for Naruto storm 4, tekken, rocket league, terraria,and many many other games that already have native controller support; Let me tell you, your better off using a standered PS or Xbox controller. Now when it comes to TF2, portal, portal 2, Vindictus, and yes even CS:GO where you have to have percision aim, IT WORKS. I would say it works about half as well as a mouse, and when your sitting on the couch playing a game thats about as much as you can ask for, and thats with first person shooters. When it comes to some more slow paced games the steam controller can be a complete replacement for your mouse and keyboard, when playing a game like sims or weather your just waching a movie from your steam library this is the controller for you.
2+ GAMES EXPERIENCE
ok if your wanting this controller for playing games with your buddys or family on the cough like i do, these controllers are completly hit and miss. Again this review is after a year of me using these controllers so let me. on most games that ive used these controllers with 2 seperate controllers will show up and one controller, Again this comes down to the game you are playing, risk of rain, gungoun, and Binding of issac all have this problem. I've looked things up for this, checked my drivers, and even tried different cumputers completly; its the mixture of specific  games and the steam controllers. Other games it works great with, Rocket league, tekken, Dirt 3, and geometry wars 3 all have worked well with the steam controllers.
Random issues ive encountered
Sometimes the controllers will disconnect for NO REASON as in none at all. It is VERY rare but it does happen in even some of the worst moments. Over all these controllers have a HUGE range but sometimes they'll just randomly disconnect.
The vibration of course is not the best, or at least as good as i would like it but what can you really expect when its mostly just haptic feedback.
Pros
really long batterie life, the batteries that came with my controller are still in it (on my second one) after about 6 months of decent use. over all with extensive use 2 AA's will last you about a month take or give.
Completly remapable buttens, Every butten except for the Steam home butten can be remapped incluing the gyro scope sensors, making every game you play your own experience.
Ofcourse the mousepads on the face of the controller, no need to even explain those.
Cons
The mouse pads, you all seen this coming, the mouse pads should have had some kind of way to take them out and swap them with joy sticks and a D pad, just saying. could have had it a bit more modular.
the glossy parts on the controller get scrached pretty easily.
This controller is NOT bluetooth. PERIOD.
could have came with an audio jack in the bottom, just saying.
And all the other cons and problems listed above.
Over all, I would say the controller was very worth it for me, besides the random disconnecting and some issues with multiplayer games this controller does everything that it advertises. I would say to try one and maybe in the long run get 2 for some multiplayer fun. Happy gaming and praise lord Gaben.

This is an in progress evaluation....
TL/DR:
I highly recommend the steam controller. It's damn near perfect.  Hopefully Valve adds a directinput mode to push the SC to perfection.
Long story:
Tried in in Tomb Raider 2013, amazing. Takes some config though if you want to use the gyro aim because it requires you first to turn down mouse sensitivity. Then I didn't like the press and hold the right pad to activate gyro so I changed it to be when I fully pull back the right trigger, meaning I am trying to shoot at something.
Tried it in Race07 with Gyro as steering, amazing! Almost as good as a real wheel. Only small complaint is there is very little travel on the triggers making them tricky to use as gas and brakes, but works when you get used to it.
Tried it in EuroTruck sim 2. Gave me trouble but will try again.
I have an odd glitch where often it starts pressing down on the stick unless I bring up the steam interface and close it again. Not sure why. (Edit, They fixed this glitch a few days later) But when it is working, it's perfect. The gyro works great for steering. The touch pad makes a great mouse input.
Really the only issue I have seen is you can't tell it to fake being a steering wheel. Its either a mouse or a gamepad. But so far the gamepad move setting on gyro seems to work for everything I've tried so far.
Tried it in a few mouse only games. Another funny glitch is it doesn't always detect when your playing a game and doesn't switch off the desktop profile. But I've only seen this so far in worms pinball and epic battle fantasy. So not a big deal. In monster truck madness 2 it sticks to desktop mode in the menus until you start a race. The race is the first instance of directX and the overlay activating. Then suddenly the profile takes over. The profile stays on randomly after the race ends. So it seems the overlay, or something with directX is required before it detects and changes profiles. Any game that doesn't use directX (And maybe openGL, untested) doesn't seem to get detected as running by the controller. And it won't change profiles.
I tried it in a few games that require the right stick as a stick with mixed results. You have to move your thumb more to get a response out of the right pad. And it feels really alien not having resistance trying to centre the stick. I am undecided if it's actually bad. Just alien.
I haven't gotten used to Gyro aiming yet, still working on that. Just using the touchpad made me far more accurate, almost accurate enough to turn off aim assist. But I am doing terrible at using the gyro to close the gap enough to turn off aim assist entirely. Might just be a matter of practice.
I set up a Skyrim config and published it. However it refuses to show up as published. I dunno why. My Race07 and epic battle fantasy publishes show up just fine. Even have 5 users on my race07 profile.
Far as I have seen, only my Skyrim config uses both Gyro and analog input attached to WASD keys and mouse controls.
I figured maybe it just doesn't show me my own, but all my others showed up, just not Skyrim.
One thing though about Skyrim is, I think, as said above, the profile detection has something to do with directX.
I set Skyrim with the profile, and then added the save game manager, which is actually a shortcut with parameters to mod organizer, as my game launch shortcut in BPM. And when it launches it keeps desktop mode until I click play in the save game manager and Skyrim loads. Once Skyrim loads, it changes on its own to my Skyrim profile. Not sure how it knows I am playing Skyrim since it shows me as playing the launcher, not the game. But the profile figured it out.
This thing has a crazy number of options. And actually the only thing I have seen missing is directinput mode. It desperately needs directinput so you can customize more strongly. A few games I have tried would benefit from 5 analog inputs instead of the 4 xinput provides. And it would be easier to configure some mouse + controller games like Skyrim which are only happy to use both controller and mouse if the controller is directinput.
A Very different kind of PC controller.

A definite improvement over Chapter 1, which was just solid. Chapter 2 elevates Journey Down to the higher quality adventure games that have been keep coming out in recent years. This time around the game is up to its neck in noir and the atmosphere is really good. The writing doesn't rival the greats but the cast is likable and it has a fun story. The puzzles are logical though some are a tad bit trial and errory but they're overall good. I never had to consult a guide which is a plus for me. Hopefully Chapter 3 really ends on a high note because the game's been improving.

A great adventure all around The graphics are gorgeous (if a little janky in places, but come on , it is a small studio) and the story really takes off in this part. The characters are really nicely written, even smaller roles are very nicely realized and relatable.
The puzzles are somewhat on the easy side, but for once that did not bother me. Just nice smooth sailing throughout, without actually feeling under-challenged. It helps that the results of solving a puzzle are often quite funny.
The voicework is also very good, with a lot of charming accents, that do not feel stereotypical in their rasta vibe because of the obvious love for it.
But what really stands out to me is the awesome soundtrack. The Jazz tunes by Simon d'Souza are really something special and complement the scenes perfectly.
When I saw that he had died while the game was in development (it is mentioned in the credits and behind the scenes material) I was very saddened.
If you like adventure games, I wholeheartedly recommend this.
