I had previously reviewed this game as positive, but that was when it was a casual and engaging incremental idle game. While it still has that aspect for the main part of the game (Earth, Moon, Mars) the company Hyper Hippo has pulled some sleazy tactics with their new events.
On a regular basis they host 3-day events to give new content since they're too lazy to do a new planet. They've also boasted about this new Rankings board for the events. These 3-day events are actually really boring, barely idle, and require far more attention than they should to complete it before the timer runs out. That's not terribly important. The pathetic part is they try to trick you into thinking it will be fun and engaging by adding a leaderboard. The catch? The leaderboard is topped entirely by shill bots and fake accounts that don't actually exist. You have a 0% chance of getting top 1000 without boosts, 0% chance of top 100 without spending obscene amounts of money, and 0% of winning an event, ever. No matter how much money you spend if you decided to do so. That's kinda f*cked up.
Their bot shills pull numbers that are literally impossible to attain in the time frame the event gives you,. even if you buy thousands of dollars worth of boosts. That's disgusting. This somehow manages to be worse than the bots in Zynga mobile games, because at least in crappy mobile games you can still technically win. Tricking people into buying boosts, and then having those boosts be completely worthless? Holy crap Hyper Hippo.
They reward you with ~4500 gold for finishing Earth, which is the notoriously grindy planet that used to be almost impossible to finish. I spent nearly half of that gold on one event just to see how far it would get me up the leaderboard. 4500 gold is worth almost $400 on their store. There's nothing else it's useful for, so you might as well waste it on crappy experiments like this.
2500 gold got me nowhere, not even within a mile of the top 100. I did constant resetting and got boosts that effectively added months of angel accumulation to my game and it didn't even put a dent in my position on the rankings.
Now, I don't really give a crap about rankings in this game, but I just wanted to see if there was any legitimacy to their leaderboard.  Finding out it's all a steaming pile of bullsh!t is disheartening because I used to enjoy this game and thought they were a good company.
Tricking dumb saps out of their money to generate revenue is an objectively trashy practice that has no business existing in any industry.♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Y.O.U. Hyper Hippo.

The description tries to lure you in by mentioning Portal, but don't be fooled.  It's a puzzle platformer with a tech theme (though something tells me it's just an excuse to be minimalist in their design - the story consists of a few lines of dialogue slapped on the beginning and end of the game), and you place boxes on pads to advance.  The similarities end there.
The puzzles mostly consist of finding where to place a block to activate a bridge or jump pad.  Once you look around and locate it, it's usually just a matter or pointing and clicking to throw.  It will go in a perfectly straight line as far as it needs to and when it gets there it will be sucked in by the switch.  Not a puzzle, just basic observation skills. Some of the pads require you to bounce it off a wall, and those have very clearly marked targets.  Just "throw here to advance."
The other aspect of the game is toggling between red and blue, which changes which bridges you can use and which you'll fall through.  At the beginning these are pretty easy except that the default keybindings aren't great (and only remappable before launching the game) and coordinating it is rough.  I'm willing to accept that this is a deficiency on my part, and the controls may be more intuitive with a controller. Near the end, this aspect was getting challenging enough to be worthwhile on its own, but just as it got interesting, game over.
On one level, I spent 15 minutes trying to solve what appeared to be an interesting puzzle just to find that the solution was just to push a big button.
I beat it 100% (excluding co-op) in 2 hours, and it was mildly entertaining.  But I also got it on sale for 50 cents.  It's definitely not worth $10.99.

If you have good sources, this software is nothing short of incredible. It takes surround input and gives you realistic headphone stereo.
This isn't like the other headphone-surround tools I have used (Razer, etc), which produce an overly clinical sound. SSC uses room virtualization to make the sound echo from one speaker around the room, which takes the realism to a much higher level.
I have primarily tested this with Rainbow Six Siege and Mad Max. In R6 this has allowed me to quite accurately kill people through walls based on sound positioning. That is how good this really is.
SSC does have some technical issues for me, namely the sound 'popping.' This gets less significant over time, but it sounds really bad when testing immediatly after launching the program. In the five minutes it takes to actually get ingame the pops generally recede to an ignorable level.

TL;DR: Superb sound spacialization through your headphones.  Full home theatre experience, even when your household is asleep.  Responsive devs.  Very inexpensive.  I love it - huge recommend!
Update 13/Apr/16:  Now that I've racked up 160+ hours of usage (which will continue to climb for the foreseeable future), I want to add a quick addendum to my full review below to state straightaway that I've found Spatial Sound Card (SSC) to be nothing short of transformative to my audio experience on PC, and I now use it every day in my short list of "essential" software, with games, films, and music.  Once properly set up and paired with quality headphones, and while being fed with good quality audio (not all audio sources are made equal!), the three-dimensional soundstage created by SSC is phenomenal (even with stereo sources, it sounds like you are in a balanced studio with freestanding stereo speakers rather than enclosed in your headphones).  Frankly, I was too cautious in my optimism in my initial review, which was only based on ~10 hours of use.  In addition, the development team has proven to be responsive, communicative, and willing to incorporate user feedback into their updates.  My main criticism, lack of proper documentation, should be resolved any day now according to the devs.  At this price, it's an absolute no-brainer - pick it up and try it out.  The best surround video game audio I've experienced so far with SSC is Mad Max in 5.1 surround mode, with the SSC "Shanghai" studio preset and the LFE (low frequency effects) turned down a bit to eliminate distortion (depends on your headphones)... the roaring V8 car battles and getting caught in a raging sandstorm make me reminisce of the first time I ever experienced a cranked up 5.1 Dolby loudspeaker system many years ago.  The fact that I can experience this late at night with my wife sleeping undisturbed mere feet away makes me very happy indeed. :)
---------------------
Original Review:
Warning: Your Mileage May Vary.  My results, though, were impressive!
I  can see why, at this point, there are a number of negative reviews.  It's not at all apparent how to set it up properly, I can't find any documentation whatsoever, the various presets give no description as to what they actually do, there are no test sounds built into the program to identify how your settings affect the output and, finally, I imagine the end result may highly depend on your headphones.  I really hope the devs correct these aspects, because many users will understandably become lost and go for a refund.  But then they'd miss out on what this software can do, and that'd be a shame, because this is a unique little gem.
So I opened with the negatives, but what about the positives, which I feel won out?  Well, I've persisted with this software past the point of no refunds, and I've finally gotten it setup properly (I think), and the net result is that *the soundscape being played through my headphones sounds much more 3-dimensional than it did without this software*.  In fact, my headphones sound more "surround" than they've ever done (in 16 years!), apart from when listening to binaural recordings.  In the end, it actually does what it says on the tin, provided you can get it working.
First, my hardware setup is almost custom-tailored for good results with this program.  My headphones are a very loved set of Sennheiser HD600s paired with a small Headroom headphone amplifier plugged directly into the "Line Out" (not headphone jack!) of my (meh) Realtek onboard soundcard (Windows 7 64 OS).  Straight away, I experienced the "garbled sound" effect that many have complained of.  On my system, as with most I assume, I had to manually select my audio output device and make sure it was in WASAPI mode.  If you don't know your WASAPI from your ASIO, then maybe you didn't take audio engineering courses in university like I did... and that's why some documentation would be useful!  Anyhow... this fixed my garbled sound issue.  Next, I chose a preset... I have no idea what the difference between the different "city" themes are yet, but I've settled on "Dubai" for the present, chose the EQ preset for Sennheiser HD600s (very handy if you have a pair of the headphones with built-in eq presets), and then lowered the LFE (low frequency effects) knob by a fair bit (numeric values would be more useful than a knob) because the default LFE was creating audio distortion in my headphone amp.
I've tried two games with excellent surround sound to properly test everything: Portal 2 and Alien: Isolation.  And the litmus test was that I could walk into an area with a clear directional sound source, close my eyes, and tell more-or-less exactly where it was at as I walked around in-game.  It was much better than the built-in positional audio from the standard "headphones" audio settings of the games.  And in the end, that's what counts.
Also, I spent ~£5 for this software on sale, so I think it's important to maintain a little perspective.  I'm definitely going to get my fiver's worth out of it.  Heck, I'd pay that just to experiment with this software and encourage developers in trying to make cool audio tech.  This wasn't a snap to setup and use, and I doubt it'd be all that great with poor headphones, so you'll have to weigh your own circumstances up when considering the purchase: do you have good headphones, and are you willing to tweak and experiment to dial in your settings?  If so, I reckon this gives pretty impressive results.

Breaking Bones by Duplicator Studio is a simple Smash-em till the counter stops action game. There is no prize in guessing that this can get tedious very quickly, Those who where bright (or stupid) enough to buy the original ‘Beach Head’ will attest that hoards of enemy rushing at you all day every day does not make it a (fun) game (Some how they manage a second game for the series before the inept realised their folly).
The short sweet intro story is this. Portals have opened around your medieval world and hoards of skeletons are pouring out, devastating the land. Your King summons you, the only knight (baffoon) who is brave (stupid) enough to save the kingdom (cesspit).
You are so brave the first zone you come to, you throw your sword and shield into a lake at the far end of the map and cower in a hut, waiting for the hoard to pop out of lovely blue orbs.
At hand is an Iron sword, a bag of arrows (no Bow) and a key to a cage outside that has a husky/wolf inside. Once you grab key and sword, you let Bozo the dog out and he will help defend you (dogs just love bones you know).
Game play is passable but not the best, as the skeletons approach you start to swing away but there is no area damage done with any of the weapons (you are swinging a big axe and hammer at times), in fact you must keep your cross-hairs on the enemy or it is not counted as a hit, making this harder than what it needs to be. You do get three health elixirs in the first zone but they do very little in bumping back your health. Their is no inventory so don’t grab the bottles right away because you are actually sculling them, not storing them. There is also a catapult to use but this is a one chance wonder, because after your first shot (if it hits anything) it takes too long to load again before you are forced to fight one-on-one. Plus the catapult can not be moved (turned left or right) so you can only shot enemy who are right in front of where it is sitting.
In between waves of enemy you can try and retrieve your sword and shield but in the end I gave up on it because the sword was worse than the iron sword you start with (weapons dropped are better) and the shield was only slightly better than blocking with a weapon. In the end the game feels locked in hard setting, where a medium setting would be nice (or at least a few more health elixirs).
Game graphics is ok but feels dated. Movement is crisp but walking through a door requires you to jump through instead. Killing enemy also leaves lots of bones cluttering up everywhere which starts to drop frame rates plus blocks hits to enemy.
There is no music except at the intro screen and it is just a looping track. Option menu is a pop-up before the game starts and is mostly limited to Graphic Card settings and Key bindings (no such option menu in-game).

When I saw this Nier:Automata my first thought was "Oh great another hack and slash game with no depth, gimmicky combat abilities, an art style straight out of a JMMORPG, and weeb pandering trash." I have never been proven so wrong in my entire gaming career.
It's hard to describe the feeling of finishing NieR:Automata, at first it was that emotion of finishing an epic book saga. Awe at an amazing story coming to an end, a feeling of completion, and a tender heart for wanting to go back into the world that has had its story told. Then all I could think about was trying to share this piece of art with my friends and family, and that is what this game is
.
I don't think I have seen such an insane amount of detail and obvious design cohesion in any game in the last 10 years, the attention to minutia is on a level that I know the designers didn't need to put in, but they did anyway. The visuals are stunning with areas that are fairly compact, that allow for an interesting mix of familiarity with a sense of newness whenever the games story throws a wrench into what you think of an area to look like. That place you have been to 10 times and is starting to get too familiar? Well throw a giant robot in it, light it on fire, or blow up a chunk of it. It's an interesting mechanic that fixes the atrociousness of some open world games that feel emotionally empty, but allows for you to still remember ever single area in the game for every time you pick it up. Every area is memorable and has solidified itself in my mind, very few other games have I ever been able to draw the world map (through several changes too!) without having to replay it.
The visuals are so flashy, bright, vibrant, and also on tone. I love that the game gives you a bright (but muted) world and contrasts it with the character designs and animations which almost exclusively use a white, black, and beige color pallet that explodes with every single attack combo and skill. Somehow the developers made it so that the darker aspects where the parts that showed through the most, I wanted to watch every single combo hit land and every dodge animation.
Of course the visuals and the level design are held together by the music score. There wasn't a single track I thought didn't fit an area, felt out of place, or that I wanted to skip. The game does this very cool thing where it has 3 versions of the song that trigger when you reach certain places inside of a location or sequence that correspond to the level of action, pacing, or tone of the scenes. The music fits each area incredibly well with a score that yells "I'm the NieR:Automata music and now every time you hear anything in this genre you will think of this game". I think whomever scored this deserves a damn medal.
The combat is incredibly smooth and each weapon combination, pod skill, chip slot skill augmentation, etc. feels so unique to how you want to play the game. Whether that means never even pushing the melee buttons or diving headlong into a field of enemies with a big♥♥♥♥♥anime sword, it's up to you.
Speaking of up to you... Ever wanted to remove pieces of the UI to allow for more skills? Well, now you can. You can legitimately remove your minimap to gain slots for your skills. They even store your "OS" on the skill chip, that if you remove it, it instantly kills you and gives one of the games 26 endings. There is an option to self-destruct that can save you from a massive boss fight, but is triggered in the settings menu. The dialogue changes depending on certain options. The game keeps track of players bodies that you can use for temporary power ups or companions, so if you are in a tough fight you can enlist the help of the other failures. When I said there was attention to detail, I truly mean it, I kept constantly finding new things in the settings that would make a UI designer cream themselves.
I mentioned that the game gave me the same feeling I get when I read a book, true. But, I didn't think that a book was finished and "pretty good" at the 15-hour mark, but then get a surprise trilogy that is 3 times as long. Seriously after you think you beat this game once, you haven't. You have just started chapter 2. And the game doesn't hold your hand on this, I know many people who played this and just stopped after the first win... huge mistake. The 2nd run through is a perspective shift and is a little tedious, but the 3rd is incredible and yet again another thematic barrage and story. The story is cohesive, deep, philosophical, brutal, and heart wrenching all at the same time. I have nothing more to say for fear of spoiling a single aspect of how the story is laid out.
In fear of sounding like I'm sucking this games♥♥♥♥♥♥a bit much, it does have issues. For the love of christ if you are playing on the PC get a controller just to deal with the bullet hell and hacking sequences, because if you don't you will be met with one of the absolute worst controls on the PC. They decided to only let you shift my 15 degree angles that are seriously unpredictable. If this is a port artifact that person needs slapped for almost interfering with the rest of this piece of art. There are also some video rendering issues that make it seem like the cut scenes are almost lower quality and frame rate than the rest of the game. Very little is explained to you (for better or worse). Some arduous boss fights and combat in certain spots. If you take your time in single player games like me you might quickly realize that the first sequence that you spend 30 minutes on DOESN'T HAVE ANY SAVE POINTS. Servo, just Servo. And a hundred more little nit-picky things.
And that is what they are, little tiny problems. In the end this game made a lasting impression on me not for its problems, visuals, or game play, but because it wholly succeeds in telling its story in the way that the developers meant it to be. The insane and crazy design decisions feed directly into a choice that the developers made, and it paid off. The game feels whole. This is not a flat piece of cardboard that is♥♥♥♥♥♥out of AAA game cycle. This isn't another recycled trope filled shooter. It is not really anything but NieR:Automata, and it really is that. If I were to pick a game in the recent history to point out as an example of video games being art, it would be this game.
10/10 (minus whatever small fraction the god-damn controller PC port controls)

I know a lot of PC users have  been using the FAR mod (which literally stands for Fix Automata Resolution) for this, but I can't also help but feel like the added complexity of that particular mod is causing a lot of trouble for them.
Right now the DLC is priced at $13.99 - while it doesn't add anything critical or necessary to the game, it does offer some fun and rewarding late-game content, customization options (outfits and hair colors), and is worth it if you like the game. With being an former QA Tester of the original Primal Carnage, this is just atrocious. The recode was intended on being the exact same original game, but all polished and with all of the silly additions from Primal Carnage 1.3 gone. Review overhauled completely to make up for the big changes to the game in the last two patches! Enjoy~
~~~ In-depth
~~~
Primal Carnage: Extinction is the long awaited "update" promised to players of the original Primal Carnage after the abysmal 1.3 update broke the balance of the game almost entirely. The lack of transparency around Extinction - original named the "Primal Carnage 2.0 recode" - is something that should be made a note of before you do consider making a purchase of this game.
The game itself was released riddled with bugs, several of which that made the game unplayable for many, a chore to run for any length of time, impossible to host a server on and brought many disappointments in terms of skins for many players who found their DLC hadn't carried over. However, the developers have been working extremely hard to bring out content patches to fix stability and server issues (with two patches since early access release, already!) and have also greatly improved on the issue of transparency with the opening of a trello board. They've also been very active in responding to the community and issues posted (you can actually see two dev posts on this review in the comments) and have clearly dedicated a lot of time to a community that was, at launch, feeling neglected and perhaps a little bit betrayed.
Originally, when I first wrote this review, I didn't recommend the game. When patch #1 was released, this recommendation did not change, though I did praise the team on doing a very good job with their swift response and the obvious fixes.
As of patch #2, I feel like I can recommend this game as an early access title immediately
to get the discounted price. For those interested in the game, I would also recommend
so that you can perhaps experience and compare yourself. I would hesitate to yet recommend this title at
for now, but with the progress of each patch update and the continued communication from developers, I also wouldn't tell people to avoid the game if they had an interest.
- the graphics have been improved from the first game, with map overhauls, animation improvements and a better optimisation by comparison.
- new animations specifically give a more fluid and natural feel, though some might also call it "floaty" and this is definitely something that your personal preference will effect. Overall, I feel that they're much nicer and they give a much more natural movement to the dinosaurs, in particular.
- many mechanics have been changed for the betterment of the game. Although it still needs to be balanced, I will not hesitate to say that the
of these changes (not all) are an improvement over the way they used to be. With some tweaking, they will be excellent.
- the UI has been greatly improved upon, making it more user friendly and visually appealing. No complaints here, it's a small change that makes a big difference to aesthetics.
- an economy system for skins, new weapons and cosmetics is, to be honest, a much better way of dealing with additional content than paid DLC is. Although again, this will be something you need to decide for yourself, I can say that I personally like it, and look forward to playing games to try and get the drops I really want. I think this is a very positive change to encourage playtime for the collectors and encourage trade between the community.
- as far as the developer team goes, they seem to be making every effort to communicate properly, make sure there is greater transparency for the community, and patching the major issues fast. While this doesn't necessarily effect gameplay
it is definitely something to make note of, and a very positive change that is very welcome to see after the earlier silence.
- the dedicated server hosting tool has been improved, several bugs have been fixed on this end and the utility of the tool is much better. A welcome improvement I'm very happy to see, though I still need to do testing to see if server passwords are broken.
- the tyrant classes were far too powerful in PC 1.3, but as of PC:E patch #2, they still feel a little underpowered for their intended purpose. This is also in part due to a continuing hitbox error I seem to be noticing, though hit detection has improved somewhat. Generally, I would like to see the tyrants a little bit more tanky
the humans have their damage reviewed. It's still very buggy and tyrants still die far too easily. That said, however, practise does make perfect, so if you are struggling on your tyrant to deal with a 1v2 and perhaps even a 1v3, I'd recommend practise first before lodging a complaint. It is still very possible, you just need to play much smarter than of 1.3. And that's not necessarily a bad thing.
- the speed of classes seems all over the place. Some of the changes were necessary. Balance is, however, still needed. That every human seems to be a world record holding sprinter is a concern and something I feel needs to be looked at.
- the game will still CTD now and then on leaving a server. I don't think this is specific to my machine, but it's not a major problem either. Just something to be aware of.
- hitboxes still seem terribly out of whack and balance is definitely required here. This will hopefully improve as the stability increases further (as it has for the last two patches) and balance can be looked at properly.
- some people are still struggling with their DLC skins, which is understandably disheartening for them and is something to be aware of if you own PC 1.3 DLC.
- although the optimisation has improved vastly from the original game, moving away from the comparison, some maps on PC:E could do with optimisation passes. Patch #2 has seen the first optimisation pass of a map, which is promising and a step in the right direction, but be aware that is only one map of several.
- collision detection, while being worked on and improved, is still in need of a lot of checking in many places. It's still very possible for tyrants to reach places they shouldn't be able to in a number of maps or to almost "glitch" their way up gaps if they hit it at the right angle and a certain speed.
- mobility for classes, not just speed, seems a little off. Tyrants turn slowly when they walk, as expected, but can turn on a dime when sprinting, despite the increase in momentum suggesting they would need to turn slower. Some review is needed here. Similarly, class attack speeds need to be reconsidered.
Overall, the game still needs a massive balance check, and for picky players it might be worth avoiding the game until patch #3/4 when the dev team have had a chance to review such things. The fixes to stability are fantastic and I hope that game stability continues to improve and that the community and developers both continue to monitor it. And, again, I think it's really important to praise the developers for their continued communication with the community, which is going a very long way and ultimately making all the difference in the world.

Bought this game on a 50% discount and started playing it.
My first impression was oh boy this is horrible, have to get a refund for this pile of trash asap.
Next day i thought, ok i still have 1.5 hrs of playtime before i can claim my refund, so lets at least get out of the start/tutorial level....well....this dam game became one of my fave games in my collection despite its many issues.
The game is not polished, it is rough around the edges, was released too soon out of publisher desperation (they filed for bankruptcy btw), the players bashed it, the critics bashed it, it has everything going against it and yet...it is a fantastic and unique game that i couldnt stop playing even after i finished it.
When you think of pirates...Errol Flynn and Johny Depp come to mind, and a host of other equally unserious pirate depictions.
Well, this game manages to depict the ugliness of a pirate's life in all it's "splendour".
This game's story is so realistic that it becomes it's main problem.
I find it interesting how no pirate movie or game has dared to go so far into realism like this game, and reality is ugly in pirate world, very ugly, as it actually should be.
The main character of this game, the pirate captain Christopher Raven, will make you want to vomit over some of his decisions....and nope you cant be a nice guy pirate in this game, sorries.
I assume some more story choices were intended but given the lack of funds and the public hate, that never came to be.
You can bash this game on many reasons, many of them valid, but you cant take away how unique and original this game is, and how it is a masterpiece in its own right, unfinished and unpolished as it is.
The combat may seem extremely rough around the edges at first, but it gets better as you progress.
At first i hated how enemies always surround you and constantly hit you from the back, but then i thought to myself: hey how would a real life combat against a group of pirates go? Will they politely and gentlemanly take turns in fighting you, or simply kick and stab you in the back?
The combat is rough but it makes sense, when fighting a group of pirates you cant just stand there and display your awesome fighting skills, you have to run and hit and run again, which makes perfect sense.
This game got a lot of hate from the typical internet justicars thirsting for a lynching party.
Because of some hystrionics, they decided the developers were dishonest (without any real proof) and thus proceeded to "punish" them properly.
Its a shame that i cant recommend this game at full price, because it has several issues, but if you have an open mind and you ever see it on a discount, do yourself a favor and give it a chance. Its a wonderful and unique game.

Definetely one of the better AAA space strategy games out there, I would dare say it's possibly even the best one out.
Frequently updated, cared for, with content coming at a satisfying pace, even if you own the base game you will feel the changes, and you will be glad they came.
Gameplay wise, its much better to play online, with friends or just Multiplayer games, as AI in almost any AAA strategy games tends to fall behind on many aspects.Regardless, here they can be still be challenging, but the true "fun" comes from human to human interactions.
The game has a learning curve, but it is fairly easy to get in to, still requires a bit of patience, trial and error, but boy is it worth it.The feeling of satisfaction as you watch yourself improve, make better decisions, and eventually exploit the weak for your own goals and causes.
It will most likely take you a couple hours to understand the basics, I would personally recommend playing one race/ethos which depends on population happines, and then possibly transition in to some more 'complex' species.Early game now has slight RNG, but never game-breaking, mostly comes down to decision making and being efficient, something new players need to practice a lot. My personal recommendation would be to just start new games, and to not play until the late game, until you have a concept of how and what happens around the first 30ish-60ish years of game start.After than you will already understand when other 'transitions' of the game come naturally. You will much better assess later situations and threats, and will know when to do what.Learning the early game is the key to making it to 'late' game.
Best of luck to all of you that try it, and be patient with the game, it will reward you with many hours of fun and joy.
Best of all, this game is as moddable as any game out there.Highly recommend you check out the workshop to your hearts desire and mod what ever you like.It's easy to tweak things on your own even.

Besides some initial hiccups with performance, after tinkering around with the graphic settings I didn't experience any issues with the pc port(performance still is pretty lackluster).
Standouts:
Really cool unarmed combat with a variety of styles. Unusual for a sandbox game of its type.
Good:
Great overall sandbox game in the vein of San Andreas. Character customization, gun, vehicle variety and combat all around solid. Driving is alright, just feel like nitro could have been handled better, every time you use it kind of plays this dizzying visual effect that disorientates. Cool cinematics and servicable story with servicable characters. Most of the time it's silly and over the top but theres some darker moments. Tons of zanny mini games to keep you occupied even after finishing all of the missions.
Bad:
Loses steam halfway through. In the beginning you'll get like 5-10% throwaway filler missions, but that percentage will keep increasing towards the end of the main game. Same thing happens with the story where a lot of the final confrontations feel unsatisfying. Boss battles are pretty weak as well. The only standout is the samurai boss battle early on, even the developers knew that so they rehashed that exact battle setup with another boss.
Deal-beakers:
The forces of physics will be the hardest enemy you face in the game. The character might fall a few feet and die if he falls on the wrong step. Don't know if it's just the pc port or not but watch out where you jump and land.
Conclusion:
Get it if you're a fan of the silly natue of the grand theft auto series, especially the earlier titles.

A (really) short "puzzle" platformer where the level difficulties range from easy to easier. The colors are dull, and the music just as so. While the mechanic of changing your polarity could have been used to create very challenging puzzles, it was under-utilized throughout the entirety of the singleplayer.
For a basic game such as this, sure whatever it's on sale for 54 cents I'll try it. The main reason I wanted to write this review was to inform those interested in buying this game is that your jump only works roughly 30% of the time.
Your jump. One of the most important actions for a puzzle platformer. Works 30% of the time.
So what could have been a quick 20-30 minute playthrough took double the time, simply because my jump inputs failed almost always and I would have needed to redo most of a level.
How you could charge $10.99 for simple gameplay and broken inputs? We'll probably never know.

NOTE: At the time of this review I have a very nice PC and this game crashes on me between 10 and 40 minutes of gameplay. The checkpoint system is well done and I never lost much progress. With that being said, the following review is of my overall opinion of the game not including the crashes.
I have played through the first episode... and to be honest, the game has tons of potential.
I enjoy the art style... it's simplistic yet intricate at the same time.
The gameplay is the traditional Telltale style, but I am finding a bit more action in this one. You will have to move around and find objects... failing to find an object could cause you some problems later in the game. You have to kill zombies, dodge tentacles of death, save potential group members, etc...
Many decisions will lead to the same result in Episode 1. I’ve seen this in other Telltale games, these decisions will affect future episodes.
I applaud Telltale for including Minecraft specific items, crafting recipes, and mechanics into Story Mode. There was just enough “throwback” to Minecraft to make the game feel more than just the MC Voxel art style.
The forums on Steam for the game are already toxic with people who don’t have the game, who don’t like Minecraft, as well as some who cannot read the main store page. This is an episodic game, at the time of this review only Episode 1 is available… once you reach the end you must wait for Episode 2 to be released before continuing. Reading is important, please understand what you are paying for before buying it.
My primary criticism for Story Mode is that at no time dose the game explain which keys you will need to use and/or what the symbols on the screen mean. For example, an arrow pointing to the right is requiring you to press the “D” key (on a QWERTY keyboard)… yes, this game uses WASD as well as the mouse. You also will be using “Q” for rapid QTE actions (mashing Q as fast as possible to stop a spider from sucking your eyeball out) and “E” for various actions like Jumping or kicking an enemy off you when you are pinned down.
Overall, if you don’t have any pre-conceptions of what the game is, and what the game should be / mean to you… I feel it is a great start to a game with a ton of potential.

Let's have some fun and calculate just how many cards you'll be needing as both a veteran player and a brand new player to max out everything currently as it stands in the PTS.
First let's get the requirements for each rarity of card & lvl out there.
Common : Lvl 1-2 : +6, Lvl 2-3 : +9, Lvl 3-4 : +12, Lvl 4-5 : 15. Total for one common card : 42. Rare : Lvl 1-2 : +4, Lvl 2-3 : +6, Lvl 3-4 : +8, Lvl 4-5 : +10. Total for one rare card : 28. Epic : Lvl 1-2 : +2, Lvl 2-3 : +3, Lvl 3-4 : +4, Lvl 4-5 : +5. Total for one epic card : 14. Legendary : Lvl 1-2 : +1, Lvl 2-3 : +2, Lvl 3-4 : +3, Lvl 4-5 : +4. Total for one legendary card : 10
Now let's count how many of each rarity of card one single champ has :
Common : 8, Rare : 4, Epic : 4, Legendary : 4. Total of 20 individual cards.
Times that by the amount of champions : 20 x 34 = 680 unique cards.
Out of 680 cards, 272 is Common, 136 is Rare, Epic & Legendary
Now to multiply those numbers with these numbers.
To max all current cards as a new player (Cards currently owned by current players will be lvl 3, reducing grind significantly) :
Common : 272 x 42 = 11424 cards. Rare : 136 x 28 = 3808 cards. Epic : 136 x 14 = 1904 cards. Legendary : 136 x 10 = 1360 cards.
Total of cards needed to max all cards for all champs as a brand new player : 18496.

This game easily makes Call of Duty players cry.
Perhaps one of the best realistic FPS's of all time, RS2 combines realism with tactics, and the outcome is nearly perfect. The only thing that isn't the best are the graphics (pretty good, but could be better) but who needs graphics when you have amazing gameplay. Being able to cooperate and get along with others on your team is needed. The community is very serious, although kind to new players.
-=These controls aren't for the average Call of Duty player
-=you need to know how to deal with distance, as your bullets will fall over large distances (snipers must judge the distance to be accurate).
-=Helo pilots need to know the physics of the game, and the difference between fighting helicopters (the Loach and Cobra) and transportation pilots (Huey)
Rushing into an objective most likely will lead to a fast death.
You will die for basically no reason (snipers, traps, grenades, people sitting in the foliage, people sitting on a ledge above you, etc.)
Use your grenades, your HE grenades can easily kill you or others, whether at full health or not. Smoke grenades are best used to hide where you are moving. Signal grenades (binoculars too i suppose) are used to mark areas for the commander, so they can call in artillery, napalm, or a spooky gunship (just don't target anywhere close to you, you'll die.)
It is usually good to start out as just a rifleman, and work your way up through the different roles. An okay one to start as are machinegunners, pointmen, or scouts. they usually either look for enemy positions (scout), be the first one to be on the objective, and make sure there are no enemies and take any out if found (pointman), or to be defensive and hold areas down (machinegunner)
Just whatever you do, don't become the commander, that is a super important role only for very experienced players (150+ hours in-game?)
Being a rifleman is mainly my choice, because it is all around a good role to be. I have played a few other roles, but riflemen are going to by the main choice when you start out.

Have you ever played a game that left you speechless? A game that makes you hit pause and just stare at the screen for minutes and all you can say is "wtf just happened"?
NieR:Automata is that kind of game.
At first I was thrown off by the anime style of this game. I must admit when i first bought it off a steam sale I had it in my library for months before I actually played it. But when I started I was sucked in hard.
Where NieR:Automata shines brightest is in its story, music and atmosphere. The combat is exhilirating as well. The open world in itself is nothing particular and unfortunately reminds me of JRPG's with bland and boring open world. The boss fights are what I would consider "epic".
I wholeheartily recommends this game and it also made me buy Tales of Berseria on a sale, hoping it could satisfy my need for more fantastic story and wtf moments.
PS: To experience the full story of NieR:Automata you have to complete the game three times. Don't be alarmed, the 2nd and 3rd playthroughs are much shorter than the first one and when you finish the game on the 3rd playthrough, you can jump to chapter select to complete the achievements/quests/endings you didn't during your main playthroughs!

I just completed almost 18 straight hours of career mode, and I have to say, at least in regards to the career mode, they've come a long way. The story feels more genuine. Dialogue is still a bit dry, and there are no voice overs, but still. The feeling of the story, and your ability to interact with the story is much better. having all the discussions come in a physical form instead of just text and pictures helps bring it home. The customization is pretty epic too. Much better than 2k17. I haven't had any glitches other than the occasional background glitch backstage during a conversation. Sure there are things I'd change, but overall, this is the best delivery I've seen in a long time, and we got it day 1!
The only issue I have had thus far is the counter detection is all over the place. Sometimes you have 2 seconds to react, while others, it doesn't matter how fast or slow you react, it won't detect it, or will detect it before you press or well after. I'm sure that'll be fixed in a patch at some point though.
What I love is that the game itself looks much more polished. It's not earth shattering, like going from the half-life engine to Unreal4 or anything, but for those people that have spent a long time in this franchise, the upgrade is a very welcome addition. (If you have good hardware I suppose) I'd like to see more graphic customization options, and the ability to create and import your own titantron movies and logos, without the need for the server uploads. Having both options would be nice, but I've always thought being able to add your own content is an important part of creating a persona. The in game movie maker has always been subpar. I've seen some people knock it out of the park, but I have always had a tough time wth it because I'm used to my software for video editing, and getting my head out of that is hard.
As for everything else,
The girls still look crazy. Not AS crazy as in the other titles by a long shot, but now instead of them looking like silly putty with lego teeth, they look like characatures of themselves, sometimes with lego teeth. It's still a vast improvement, and I will not complain about it, because let's face it.. From 2k16 to now, there had been very little imrovement in that department, but now that the female divisions are picking up steam, it was about time they gave them more glory in the games. Keep up the good work!
Anyway, if you're a wrestling fan, it's worth picking up. I certainly don't regret it. Plus, the more sales they do on the PC platform, the more likely we are to be included in the future day 1 releases! (Even if they aren't released and unlocked at the time we wanted them to be ;)    MIDNIGHT EST PEOPLE LMBO!! )

I had it just for a day now, yet I'm more than happy for my purchase.
Just like many others, I wanted to try some FPS and for now I can say that it will be hard. Portal 2 and CS:GO were the choice of my testing games. I used the gyro to assist my aiming and my results are a bit mixed. It will take time to get the aiming accuracy I've developed with KB+M combo. There are tons of options, which doesn't make things easy. For FPS the most hard part for me personally is to fire with the trigger without moving the controller while aiming with the gyro. Practice will help but it will take a lot of time.
The other games that I've tried made me realize just how good the controller actually is. With simple games as Race the Sun/ Superhexagon/ VVVVVV there isn't much to fiddle with the controlls. Using the right pad for movement can appear over-sensitive and again- practice makes perfect.
Torchligh/ Torchlight2/ Legend of Korra- now we are talking! The first two have no native gamepad support and the KB+M mode is more than enough. With a few keybindings and switches, I can use almost all of the spells and I have no problem navigating, aiming, moving on the map. All that from the couch!
And why I think Legend of Korra plays better with this controller than my 360? For two reasons- finally a good camera controll (mouse joystick mode) and no more thumbstick press to lock on enemies! Those two alone made the game that much more enoyable. And I'm certain many other games like DMC, AC series will feel much better with it. I've always found the camera controlls on 3rd person games to be constrictive without a mouse and most of time I've ended up dying because I simply can't view freely. That alone is a game changer for me.
Anything I would like to improve on the controller?
- Tapping is not an option on multiple modes. It would be great to have it and helps a lot. Most of the times I'm seeing just double tap.
- Enable the keyboard outside of Steam- Windows/Linux/OSX desktop. Really, thus far this is the best keyboard for a controller. It would be great to use it outside of BPM as I already use the controller as a remote anyways :) I know the Steam Runntime has to running in the background.
Something I forgot to mention?
- It works in GRUB! For the people who don't know what this is- a bootloader. Most Linux distros use it and it is great for a machine with multiple OSes. I'm surprised that the Steam Controller worked as a charm there as I've had trouble not once or twice with my keyboard in the said GRUB :)

The build quality is mostly to blame. Cheap feeling, thin plastics. Horrible clicky touchpads that make me wince every time they depress. The haptic feedback would be great if you didn't have to shout over it (honestly, it is like an angry geiger counter!).
The buttons are awkwardly placed, especially with the large grips impeding your access to them. The grip buttons (paddles?) are very sensitive and actuate at the slightest touch, leading to some early foul ups in particuarly intense gameplay. Great I'm sure for twitch shooters or RTS games, but in those scenarios I couldn't imagine using anything less than a keyboard and mouse.
I like the custom configurations and community bindings. I like the fact the touchpads can be used for the desktop and universally across applications. But the touchpad is no replacement for a second analog stick and the build quality has much to be desired.
I can’t recommend this controller, it’s mediocre. Stick with an Xbox 360/One, PS4, Wii U Pro or Logitech gamepad.

The original PC was a great game. I rarely write reviews for games but this one in particular I believe requires some warning for those looking to buy it. This years game is a glitchy mess. I am disappointed that this was released in this state. I'll break it down to some pros and cons for those who just want a quick read.
Pros:
- The game looks much better then last year. The new lighting makes such a massive improvement.
- The amount of control of your matches now finally feel comparable to the wwe games of the last generation.
Cons:
- This game is a glitch-fest. I've never seen anything like it. So let me describe to you what my first wwe universe experience was like this year.
I had Jinder Mahal and Seth Rollins set to be in a feud. The start of the feud was supposed to be during a match between Jinder and Kalisto. I thought Seth would come out and interrupt the match; causing the feud. Instead both Jinder and Kalisto come out and, as the match was set to start the camera cuts back into the ring to show that Jinder has disappeared and been replaced with Seth. So now it's Seth Rollins vs Kalisto and then Jinder theme hits and is once again walking down the ramp but this time to watch the match.
So now I guess I'm supposed to interrupt the match between Seth and Kalisto? So they're having their match and a cut scene shows Seth getting thrown out of the ring. I use this opportunity to cause a DQ however, nothing happens. Kalisto comes out and grabs Seth and throws him back into the ring. The referee is still counting however because, for some reason, I am now apart of the match. I walk back into the ring and I am able to be apart of the match but Seth ignores me and focuses only on Kalisto regardless of how often I attack him.
It's just a mess. I quit on the spot. What's the point of setting up a feud if the game glitches several times to the start of the feud?
- The career mode is also a mess. It feels like a walking and loading simulator. I'm running this game on my SSD but the amount of load times in between every single event is draining. You can move around back stage before and after every match/promo but the speed in which the character moves is painful. I couldn't take it. Just to continue to the next week requires a minute of walking every, single, time.
The time it takes to earn VC is painful also. Every single thing you want cost VC in this mode and you do not earn anywhere near enough to boost your character. It makes the mode a massive drag. I put 4 hours into this mode alone and I only went up 3 points overall. It's just not fun at all.
- This game crashes often. Not much to add here I've crashed at least 10 separate times and it's really annoying.
- The AI is dumb as bricks. They don't know how to move in the ring. I've seen them get stuck trying to climb the ropes in random loops way to often. Or they just walk around in circles for no reason trying to find some kind of optimal path.
I want to like this game but this is beyond unreasonable for 60 dollars. Value your money and spend it on a product that actually has some self-respect.

A good attempt at making a unique hardware option but unfortunately its just not that useful.
Pros:
It is functioninal for more casual games that don't require speed, such as turn-based strategy games for instance. It also works well for games that only require one analog stick, so you don't have to fiddle with the track pads. The extra two buttons under the hand grips where your middle fingers through your pinkies wrest is a nice feature. It's two extra buttons that most controllers don't have and they're conveniently located. It is highly customizable and you can bind any key to any button and adjust how the track pads work (although they will never work well).
Cons:
Not as useful as a mouse and keyboard OR a controller. It's kind of the worst of both worlds. Aiming with the track pad is terribly frustrating, much more so than with a controller. The track pads seem to be low dpi and inaccurate. A standard Xbox One controller would probably be preferable in any game that requires speed and precision. I can't imagine many games where it would be more useful than a controller. Definitely not even close to a mouse and keyboard.The construction also feels cheap compared to an Xbox One or PS4 controller. It might be useful for surfing the web from your couch but as of now I found the Big Picture browser to be buggy and difficult to use.
Overall I would recommend just purchasing an Xbox One controller for gaming with SteamLink but the web surfing functionality might not be there with an Xbox One controller (I haven't tried it). There might be apps that can help to work around this issue.

I was excited for the Steam controller (pre-ordered day 1, got it in first wave in mid-October), got it, played around with it, had a really hard time getting the hang of it, and wasn't sure it was going to work for me. However, I found it to be really comfortable and had gotten used to being able to reconfigure any input as any button, and realized I could no longer live without dual-stage triggers and left/right grip buttons. I continued to practice.  I continued to tune the settings.  Now, other controllers feel simple, and uncomfortable, and are frustrating to use, and all I want is my Steam controller.  It just takes time, patience, and practice, as with anything new.

If you like using a controller but are sometimes frustrated with games that do not support it, this is for you. I'm not going to lie I have never been coordinated enough to use a mouse and keyboard and I'm not saying that it is a better choice, but compared to just a regular Xbox or PS4 controller the steam controller takes the cake. It has helped put life into otherwise frustrating games for me, like I said I'm not that coordinated, lol. I have used it from everything like The Secret World, Borderlands, Fallout 4, Company of Heroes... etc. The high-precision gamepad mode will change how you view controller accuracy once you get the settings just right. So I guess that is the con so far that I have found but not much of one, since you can have custom settings for each game each tailored to how much sensitivity etc you need for that game. With a few minutes of toying with the settings you will be golden. I have even used it to function my desktop most of the time now, once you get use to the sensitivity it is just that easy and I hardly use my touchpad on my laptop anymore. My friend tried it and was sold within five min not even playing in a game yet, so I guess that sorta speaks for itself.

TL;DR: This controller IS NOT plug and play. just about the only drawback to it. The custizations you can do with this thing is insane and the controller just conforms to your hand.
This controller is amazing it's everything I've been waiting for for years without really knowing it. I've never been big on using controller for PC games before simply because the joysticks feel like it limits my control. While the trackpads are great for emulating a mouse they aren't 100% perfect it's more like 90% perfect. I don't actually like touchpads on a labtop, but you know what the haptic feedback on these things make it feel so comfortable more like your flicking a mouse ball rather than a trackpad. The joystick simulation for the trackpads could use some work though because it takes a lot of movement to actually register as anything. It's a real shame I don't really want to use the joystick, but I find my thunb just resting on it and using it without thinking. The XYAB buttons are little bit of an odd possition, but you get used to their locations relatively easily. I find myself sliding my fingers over them to recognize which one is which. The soft pull on the dual stage triggers is a little shorter than I was expecting and the LB and RB are a little bit higher than I would like but their size make up for it. Both grip buttons are extremely comfortable to use and great for mode shifting the trackpads or anything else. The joystick can be configed to be 4 buttons although I would like to see a menu for the joystick as well. Last but not least the gyro on this thing is insane I have it on the second to lowest setting for finetuning shots just so it's not so speradic. The gyro is deffinetly something that you have to get used to using it's like a personal aim assist. You can also set different things to the gyro but I haven't yet played around with those options. Don't really see what the other settings would be used for.

TL;DR Nier:Automata has the potential to be one of the greatest games ever made. However, there are some design decisions and technical issues that make it not reach this potential. It is still definitely worth buying on sale, probably even for the full price.
The combat in this game is very fast paced and enjoyable. You will definitely not get tired of it as the game constantly keeps changing the playstyle that you are allowed to use. The story is simply amazing. Graphics and sound were also great.
And now, I'm gonna talk about the game's faults but before I do that, I'd like to stress out that this game is a masterpiece for the story alone, so it is definitely worth playing, even despite its faults and some technical issues.
The difficulty tuning in this game is not great. It is not terrible, but definitely not great. There is an extremely hard difficulty where you are killed by any hit, and then there are "normal" and "hard" difficulties which are just too easy because you are allowed to buy basically unlimited number of healing items which you can then constantly spam and never die. Also, there are "plug-in chips" which gives you passive buffs and if you get good combination of plug-in chips, together with the healing items, you are basically invincible.
On the other hand, there are parts of the game, when you loose access to vendors for some time and if you didn't buy enough healing items, you might run out of them! The game is extremely hard then and I was forced to play on easy for one boss fight because of that.
I think that this issue with difficulty tuning could be solved by limiting the number of healing items that you are allowed to use per battle, just like it is done in Dark Souls series. I'd like to point out though, that just the fact that I compare the combat in Nier:Automata to combat in Dark Souls is a huge compliment.
Then there are the technical issues. Oh boy, the PC ports... These technical issues are the main reason why this game doesn't have great reviews on Steam and that is quite unfortunate because these reviews do not review the game itself but only its technical aspects.
There is a weird bug with fullscreen mode, when the game doesn't really go fullscreen but leaves these black stripes on the edges. I solved this issue by using Window Borderless Gaming program and apparently there is even a mod that can solve it but just the fact, that you are forced to do such a thing, is not good, not good at all. Also, anti-aliasing is extremely demanding for some reason, so it is recommended to either turn it off or set it to lower.
I managed to get 60 FPS on my 60 Hz monitor with Window Borderless Gaming program and low anti-aliasing. If you experience any other technical issues, there is a great section in DIscussions, where you can find help.
That being said, I'd like to encourage people not to get intimated by the technical issues and give this game a chance, because it definitely is worth it.

I really want to like this game. The multiple gameplay styles are fun and engaging, the music and voice work is crisp and lovely to listen to, and the art style, whilst it may be too "fan-servicey" for some is really unique and imaginative.
I have also heard many good things about the story in NieR: Automata, unfortunately, I would not be able to comment due to the issues that Square Enix have yet to address, those issues being the numerous glitches and lack of support plaguing the PC port. This game suffers from poor optimization, driver support issues and resolution faults, and whilst some of these issues may be addressed with third-party mods it is still no excuse for Square Enix to simply try to brush this poor excuse for a PC port under the rug.
Along with another recent Square Enix published game, Deus Ex: Mankind Divided, I think it is fair to say that Square Enix simply does not care for their PC market. If any of these issues were to be addressed I would be more than happy to take a second look at NieR, however, in its current state I cannot recommend it to anyone.

Self described as the game you play between games, this game is already a red flag.
There is a reason it is FtP.
The time between games as every console dev has warned people on the package of their games is that 15 minute breaks once an hour is recommended, yes I'm aware barely any gamer listens to that, however someone giving counter intuative advice to sit there in the downtime to play another game doesn't bode well.
Now initially the game takes off as owning a lemon store, and you gradually build up to several lemon stores, then a delivery run, then upgrades and manages to increase profit and run stuff, eventually you have access to do this on a moon and another planet, however all the player is really looking at is a flat screen of numbers.
Queue taking advantage of gambling psychological studies.
As the bars full of time limit indicating the rate the player "earns money" (strong words for those who actually know what venture capitalism is), the bar is actually flashing, something our brains are wired to love like crack.
So what's the aim here?
It's simple enough, you have planet currency, let's say "earth dollars", and you have "mega tickets", and you have gold, that's three false currencies.
To get more earth dollars the game has to progress until enough money is earned to acrue "angel investors", which upon restarting and losing all that long awaited money actually stick around and add a "times 2" to profits, the % varies depending on amount of angels.
Another way to get more money is to buy ever price hiked "mega tickets" with your earth dollars, this may take a couple weeks for the first one alone, and it takes ten of them to buy a permanent upgrade for just one of your franchises.
This time limited can be overcome like any pay to play game, either with monumental patience, or micro transactions.
Microtransactions buy gold, gold is in turn used to skip several days forward for funds to have accumulated, or to buy mega tickets, or other such unnecesary features.
Another trick is that gold purchased is sold in uneven amounts, "whatever shall I do with my uneven amount of gold?", "I know! Buy more gold to even it out until I can spend all of it without waste."
The technique is not new, it is designed to take advantage of people who do not have patience, whilst providing flashy lights, the idea of reward, progression, and achievement, the joke is I'm fairly certain this game actually doesn't have an ending.
"The game you play in between games."
You do this because it's addictive, and it's free because a microtransaction money trap that is addictive.
Then there's the trap this reviewer fell into last night, after months of refusing to make a purchase.
The accidental click buy.
When in offline mode a person may tap "purchase mega ticket", it has the option to do this with earth money, or gold.
If there is not enough of either, it will tell you so.
If a player happens to unfortunately be online, with Steam having trapped their credit card details (yet another accidental click months ago), tapping "pay with gold" becomes a near seamless transaction that requires no Steam confirmation of billing address and so on.
How does a person accidentally tap such features?
We'll put that down to sheer lack of full attention whist showing people the game.
Not only are accidental transactions perfectly seemless, I've still yet to find an option to "contact us" and discuss refunds, and Steam has their own direct "contact us" buried under so many layers it's practically a phone redirection machine.
In conclusion, anything masquerading as a game when it is a cash milking machine, irrisponsible and greedy enough to take advantage of the simplest micro transaction without safeguards, is deeply concerning, and not recommended.

*Copied my description from RPGwatch and slightly edited it *
The most important thing:
This game is not Assassin Creed game nor is Ubisoft behind it. RC is pirate themed RPG with integrated shipfights.
If you wanted to buy parkour with shipfights AC4 clone, look elsewhere.
Raven's Cry plays totally like Sea Dogs and it's sequels and spinoffs:
Sea Dogs (2000)
Pirates of the Caribbean (2003)
Age of Pirates: Caribbean Tales (2006)
Age of Pirates 2: City of Abandoned Ships (2009)
And it seems totally inspired by those as they share:
- superb music
- clunky groundcombat with horrible opponents AI ;)
- totally fun ship fights
Differences?
Unlike Sea Dogs and the rest, you can't "improve" skills of your ship officers in Raven's Cry - skills they have by default never change. This is not a bad decision IMO as keeps you away from grinding since RC sidekicks don't really have BlackIsleish background story to share. At least not in this game, maybe in eventiual sequel...
Also you can't make a fleet and lead it in Raven's Cry (apart from friendlies that temporarily join your side during some quests). Another good choice as in Sea Dogs you could build an OP fleet and pwn everything.
If you're not sure what to think, you can test your taste with DRMfree Sea Dogs available on GOG.
To this day I don't know why critics panned it so hard. I've seen many games in my life and some definetly deserved 1/10, but this one totally didn't. And critics were showering the game with that score calling out whatever unforgivable issues seems only them had - not only nonexisting bugs (as I collected reports and posted a buglist in original game) but also issues related to the game story (slavery for example) like all of them expected kill_noone and remain politically correct Superman game and not an evil pirate in the era where political correctness was a fairy tale.
One thing I can say for sure.
Unlike (usually) overhyped visual candy I've played this year, mainly AC:Unity and FarCry4 where I uninstalled without ever finishing those because of utter boredom, I've finished original Raven's Cry twice without getting bored anywhere and now am on it for the third time in this Enhanced Edition, and again not bored to death like with grindy and repetitive modern mainstream games.
Enhanced Edition aka Vendetta corrected voiceover issue, added containers to make exploration more fruitful (although new added animals are over the top on half of islands), added hats as a new statbooster, introduced a crapload of new sidequests with some brilliant solutions to lack of humor in the original game (the bordello goat for example).
While earning $ perhaps became too easy after you obtain the second (better than schooner) ship, it doesn't steal anything from the game as now you can enjoy shipfhighs without thinking if you'll have enough of cash for later ship repairs.

I gave this game a proper ride of 54 hours (finished the game), unfortunately lady luck did not spread her legs for me (but her legs started to spread on Ch.4):
You cannot capture a ship you just boarded. This greatly affected my experience of the game and my recommendation. For a pirate ship game I expected to capture ships or at the very least, take over a ship I boarded. This game makes you go to different islands to find a person that is willing to sell you a different ship class, and this is the only way to change you ship. The schooner ship I got by killing a captain in the beginning does not count to my personal achievements because that was not a "Purchase." Even the old game Seadogs let you get a few first officers to capture boarded ships, command a fleet, and you could also switch ships after boarding. I can say that this game is good if you ignore glitches/errors in quests and lighting/camera/frame rate issues.
Things I like about this game:
+ The Cursing
+ The Sexy Women
+ Ship Battles
+ The right amount of weapons and upgrades
+ Dice Game & Raven pet (great ways to make money)
Things I hated about this game:
- Can't Capture Ships nor switch ships after boarding, and no Fleet
- When boarding you do not fight on deck of the ship with your sword and guns like in most good pirate games
- The steam interface seems to lock up the game for me.
- Tutorial windows pop up and go away really quickly (they should pause time and let you read it)
- Animals are a pain in the you know what and I find myself standing on them all the time.
- You cannot just sail and look around your ship without being in a fight.
- No spyglass
Things need to be improved:
/ Sword fighting can be better, maybe make block last longer (you get better at sword fighting with practice)
/ The world traveling map where you need to press Y to pause time and select a nearby ship to attack or city to visit should be a little slower. Maybe adding the word "New!" near the just opened island or area for a quest to make it easier.
/ They should have more mini games like poker and throwing knifes like in Quest for Glory 5 and make sure to have NPC voices in the background does not loop the same talk over and over again.
/ There should be fast travel in the city.
/ Having only one area that takes you back on the ship from an island is not good for some quests. Adding multiple areas around the island where you could go back on the ship quickly would make the game quicker and more fun.
/ When a bartender shows you a officer to hire it would be great to see your current officer side by side to compare.
/The quest logs should have a city name of where the quest needs to be done (on each quest).
/ I do not like to see old quest characters that are highlighted on my map they should be removed after the quest is completed and the items like old maps in the inventory should also be automatically removed when a quest is finished.
This game is better than the Org. Raven's Cry (but changing the game a little and making it like a new game was a wrong thing to do, just don't rush a game out next time) but still needs a lot of work to make it great. The game has errors like one time I could not go to any island (it would crash my game every time I tired) and had to restart an old saved game to fix the issue. Another error I had was when I docked in the city and my ship was sunk by the time I got back to it. Save on 6 or more different slots to be safe in this game.
This game gets a 7/10 but if they fix the bugs and change a few things above, it will be an easy 10.

Vendetta - Curse of Raven's Cry nails the pirate-adventure/action genre, as I hoped it would when Raven's Cry was first announced back in 2014.
I pre-ordered the deluxe edition of Raven's Cry over a year ago, having enjoyed Two Worlds II from the same developer and publisher. Reading about how buggy the game was on initial release, I decided to hold off on playing it pending the release of additional patches/bug-fixes promised by the developer. As it turns out, the developer made good on their word and released this updated version of the game, with a slightly different title.
I'm glad that the developers followed through with finishing the game and I'm also glad I waited to play this updated version, as it has turned out to be very enjoyable.
The updated Raven's Cry (this game) ended up coming out around the same time as Fallout 4, and costing about the same price. In my opinion, Raven's Cry is much more deserving of the 60-dollar price than Fallout 4. Whereas I found Fallout 4 to be unengaging and a regurgitation of its predecessors, I find Raven's Cry fun to play, with entertaining character conversations (actually, a lot of the writing is really intelligent and some - though not all - of the voice acting is really good) and a fun mix of naval combat and over-the-shoulder third-person gameplay.
This game, as I hoped it to be, is like a mix of Two Worlds II land-based action-RPG with Sid Meier's Pirates!-style navigation and ship-to-ship combat. It's fun.

Unfortunately Steam doesn't have a 'mixed opinion' option, but that best suits my thoughts on the game.

This is a run-and-gun clickfest augmented by an indirect fire cycle of artillery, napalm delivered via airstrikes, C47 gunships, and helicopter strikes, either simultaneous or one following the other, then rinse and repeat. I am an RO, RO2/RS vet. I love both of those games, and still play Darkest Hour and RO2 to this day. I missed a year on deployment of both of these games, and jumped right back in after the fact and am back in deep. So this isn't some sort of biased review to the level of difficulty or style of play the RO/RS series Tripwire has become known for.
I preordered RS2: Vietnam, like many other RO2 vets. I was extremely excited. After having played the game for some time, and put it down, and picked it back up, I have to say that between the atmosphere of the game, and the level design, something is off. I don't want to say that something is the Vietnam era theme, because it's actually a good change of pace, and differentiates the series a bit.
Some of the dynamics and playstles from RO2 remain; you spawn on your Squad lead, who also has the ability to mark artillery targets for the Team Lead, and so on. These remain tried and true. However I have noticed a lot of the playerbase from RS2, isn't verbal or it's 'every man for himself', a play style that usually doesn't lead to positive results in a game specifically built around 'every man has a job' sort of idea. I think Tripwire may have fallen a bit astray with this title as far as what made RO2 so popular (I would bring up RO1, but RO2 was a huge departure in style of play). The hard and fast aspect, is still consistent that Red Orchestra 2 started (RO1 was very, very slow going), but the aesthetic approach is a huge jump off and the style of gameplay is perhaps even faster than RO2 while losing a bit of the authenticity that made Red Orchestra 1/2 appealing, for a bit more action.  I'm personally having an extremely difficult time getting into RO2, and while I definetly will not say it isn't worth the money, nor would I say it's a 'bad' game, the game does need refinement. I would say if you're a Red Orchestra vet, then cautiously pick this one up, but don't expect to get the same experience from the game.  I will personally not be recommending this game, but only because I am given one of two options whereas I sit on the fence.

A solid controller with lots of unique possibilities and a great feel.
I've seen a lot of reviews from big media groups saying that the controller feels "cheap" but I disagree. It has a nice heft, and a whole lot of polish, even in the packaging and the subtly branded USB dongle.
You can tell a tremendous amount of thought and care went into making this controller, and it stands out in a few ways, primarily the customizability and the easy of typing (once you get used to it), which resembles two thumb typing on an older phone with a full keyboard.
The dissapointing thing is that there seem to be occasional glithces of the software. Sometimes when alt tabbing from Big Picture mode, the entire Steam app crashes, leaving the controller a useless mess in whatever game you're playing, and the chat (at least for me) seems to have a weird one message delay. Other than these software issues, which I'm sure will get patched later on (after all, the controller just came into full release), the controller is great, and it seems like a lot of the issues that people have with it are either from not using it enough or from patchable software bugs.
And although the Steam overlay is required for the controller to work, the Steam Controller simply seems like the best way to bring pc games away from a mouse and keyboard, and onto your couch, even for stuff that doesn't support a controller at all.

I HIGHLY reccomend this Controller, not only will this improve your preformance in FPS games but you can get immense levels of precision that you just can't get with the traditional analog stick setup(XBONE/PS4).
Yes it takes a little while to learn, yes the buttons are lower then typical controllers, however the gaines are absolutely amazing, the only people who will complain about using this controller are the kids who are born into the (CoD) generation, they don't want any variation, they want all FPS games to be the same and all controllers to be the same.
This controller simply put is fantastic, i found myself watching netflix from bed with my Fiance and using this as a remote to keep playing new episodes without leaving the bed.

Originally I bought this game as the protagonist looks like my Skyrim character wielding a Dark Souls weapon. Turned out that the game goes better than I expected: the main characters are quite likable, there are a certain degree of sandboxing, the flight mode session is awesome, some of the bosses are quite cinematic, and some of the themed areas/bosses are really nice. Actually it's the Oprea Singer boss fight on Youtube that made me decide to buy the game.
The OST itself is worth the money. I won't say it's peerless, but it's better than 90% of the game I played.
The story is a double-edge sword for me. On one hand the director is indeed good for inciting emotion, I was emotionally upset at the beginning at the third playthrough and had to take a break. On the other hand there are a bunch of plotholes in the setting, which is most likely the result of the director trying too hard to call down a dues ex machina to push the tragic theme. The side quests also include really emotional contents and a lot of "overly human robot" trope, which feel a bit overplayed. Also some of the reference to previous games (Nier Gerstalt) is too obscure, so you'd better look at Youtube channels for lore questions.

Oh, one other complain: the last boss, Square Enix, is so overpowered.
