UPDATE:
After completing my first playthrough I wanted to write a more thorough review of this game. It was something I had my eye on for a year, watched countless hours of streaming, and debated back and forth about whether or not to give it a chance. It looked good. Also weird. Also buggy and possibly frustrating. But there was something about it that left a strong impression, so recently I took the pludge and I'm so glad I did!
Nier: Automata can be best described as an open world bullet hell action RPG. The game changes genres pretty frequently, shifting seamlessly from an Ikrauga style SHUMP to a twin-stick shooter, to a 2D Gunstar Heroes type side scroller, to a Bayonetta style action game all within the first hour! The meat and potatoes of the experience is an exploration-driven action RPG set in a vast but desolate environment that combines elements of games like Dark Souls and Shadow of the Colossus. Remarkably the game never feels disjointed or gimmicky and nothing everh overstays its welcome.
The map seems intimidatingly huge at first but becomes surprisingly manageable over time, offering lots of rewards for thorough exploration. Walk in any direction long enough and you'll find something  - items, mobs, NPCs, new areas. If you can jump on a thing, fall off a thing, or fit through a gap you're going to stumble on a hidden area, and all of them are worth finding. Side missions will force you to traverse every nook and cranny, so eventually you'll know the world like the back of your hand.
Remarkably, side missions never get stale. While you're never given anything outside standard video game fair, you're never repeating the same exact quest type twice. It makes each mission feel more important than your usual RPG side quests, and makes them and the characters who give them to you surprisingly memorable.
The difficulty is rather interesting. It's incredibly scalable and should be able to please a wide variety of gamers. At it's hardest Nier: Automata is brutal - truly the embodiment of the best of bullet hell games. On normal the learning curve has a bit of a kick, but proves fairly straightforward once you get your barrings. It's on Hard where I had the most fun - the kind of hard that a Soulsborne game offers, where mistakes are quickly punished but skill is greatly rewarded. Dying becomes less and less frequent as you increase in level and playing ability, but remains a threat enough to keep you on your toes. By the end of my first playthrough I felt pretty invincible and the difficult journey to get there made it all the more rewarding.
On the technical side of things yes the game has a lot of issues in terms of the PC port, but honestly I've played games that gave me bigger headaches for lesser experiences. Installing the latest video card drivers and using the player made patch eliminated any issues, and I managed to beat the first playthrough without crashing. Once it is running fine the game looks good and runs smooth. The art style and world design takes some getting use to - areas are bleak, sparse, often monochromatic and borderline repetitive, but the world is large enough, varied enough, and memorable enough that it feels more like an artistic choice than anything else, and one that makes sense.
I'm definitely going to do all the playthroughs, find all the weapons, and do all the side missions before I'm done with this game. I hope enough people give it a shot that we see a sequel some day.

Self described as the game you play between games, this game is already a red flag.
There is a reason it is FtP.
The time between games as every console dev has warned people on the package of their games is that 15 minute breaks once an hour is recommended, yes I'm aware barely any gamer listens to that, however someone giving counter intuative advice to sit there in the downtime to play another game doesn't bode well.
Now initially the game takes off as owning a lemon store, and you gradually build up to several lemon stores, then a delivery run, then upgrades and manages to increase profit and run stuff, eventually you have access to do this on a moon and another planet, however all the player is really looking at is a flat screen of numbers.
Queue taking advantage of gambling psychological studies.
As the bars full of time limit indicating the rate the player "earns money" (strong words for those who actually know what venture capitalism is), the bar is actually flashing, something our brains are wired to love like crack.
So what's the aim here?
It's simple enough, you have planet currency, let's say "earth dollars", and you have "mega tickets", and you have gold, that's three false currencies.
To get more earth dollars the game has to progress until enough money is earned to acrue "angel investors", which upon restarting and losing all that long awaited money actually stick around and add a "times 2" to profits, the % varies depending on amount of angels.
Another way to get more money is to buy ever price hiked "mega tickets" with your earth dollars, this may take a couple weeks for the first one alone, and it takes ten of them to buy a permanent upgrade for just one of your franchises.
This time limited can be overcome like any pay to play game, either with monumental patience, or micro transactions.
Microtransactions buy gold, gold is in turn used to skip several days forward for funds to have accumulated, or to buy mega tickets, or other such unnecesary features.
Another trick is that gold purchased is sold in uneven amounts, "whatever shall I do with my uneven amount of gold?", "I know! Buy more gold to even it out until I can spend all of it without waste."
The technique is not new, it is designed to take advantage of people who do not have patience, whilst providing flashy lights, the idea of reward, progression, and achievement, the joke is I'm fairly certain this game actually doesn't have an ending.
"The game you play in between games."
You do this because it's addictive, and it's free because a microtransaction money trap that is addictive.
Then there's the trap this reviewer fell into last night, after months of refusing to make a purchase.
The accidental click buy.
When in offline mode a person may tap "purchase mega ticket", it has the option to do this with earth money, or gold.
If there is not enough of either, it will tell you so.
If a player happens to unfortunately be online, with Steam having trapped their credit card details (yet another accidental click months ago), tapping "pay with gold" becomes a near seamless transaction that requires no Steam confirmation of billing address and so on.
How does a person accidentally tap such features?
We'll put that down to sheer lack of full attention whist showing people the game.
Not only are accidental transactions perfectly seemless, I've still yet to find an option to "contact us" and discuss refunds, and Steam has their own direct "contact us" buried under so many layers it's practically a phone redirection machine.
In conclusion, anything masquerading as a game when it is a cash milking machine, irrisponsible and greedy enough to take advantage of the simplest micro transaction without safeguards, is deeply concerning, and not recommended.

TL;DR
Nothing like the original. Terrible controls. Somewhat buggy gameplay. Boring and ill-fitting graphics design. Most of the sounds are annoying. Thin, reverby music.
Yes yes, I've played the game for less than 10 minutes, but seriously, that was enough.
The way the karts control is horrible. Hitting the brake in a corner, accelerates you in the opposite direction of what you're turning. And no, it's not just that the camera moves to the side when drifting (which is annoying btw). I tested it several times. I can steer sharply to the RIGHT, while driving straight, by simply pressing LEFT and brake, and vice versa. I can hardly get through a hairpin and not hit the walls, unless I brake hard (without turning), and take the corner with 10 km/h. The original game is all about timing your handbrake turns, for just about every 90+ degree turn, and your shots (making no sense) following your turning, so they're always straight ahead of you (makes for great trick-shots). In this version, none of the weapons really feel awesome to use.
Then there's the movement and obstacles. The AI's seem to lag through the air when jumping, and for some reason it's like you're sped up to 5x speed when jumping, which makes it feel like you come to a grinding halt when you land, so the jumps don't even feel awesome to do. More like a weird feeling, than anything else. And you can get stuck between a tree and the wall, without touching either, when there is clearly a lot of room for you to pass between them. Also, the sound for when the karts smash together, is not good. Sounds like two cardboard boxes being smashed together, with some added distortion.
I'm not too fond of the graphics, either. In the old game, a fireball looked like a fireball. Here, they're just soft-white spheres with small spikes. And nothing quite fits together. Neon-green boost-patches and jumps? Large green question marks? It all just feels half-done.
Also, the music is pitchy and reverby, and doesn't really "fit", which reverby and pitchy music seldom does.
Which "Wacky Wheels" did you guys play? All the things that were unique and special about the original, are gone. This is just another cartoon kart racer, with the most terrible controls I've ever seen in a kart game, in my 27 years as a gamer.
I really wanted to like this game. I LOVE the original. Bought it when I was 12 with my own savings, and loved it to bits. I had seen the videos and screenshots, and knew I wasn't getting the exact same thing, but the only thing this has in common with the original, is the description on the tin: "Animals racing karts, shooting hedgehogs at each other. Also there are bombs, fireballs and spilled oil."

The core of my recommendation
is the very detailed and challenging naval combat combined with RPG elements set in beautiful landscapes.
Developers have truly put much effort into the game which can be seen during the play through.
Already the first 18 hours of my overall playtime I have spent with exploration, sailing and trading.
The Environment
The ambience sounds in my opinion are overwhelming for example you wander into the wilderness and  can hear all sorts of wildlife inhabiting the jungles and shorelines, never let your guard down as one wild cat or a crocodile might be hiding close waiting for the right moment to take your life.
The cities crowded of people such as beggars asking for a coin, musicians singing and playing different kinds of instruments, and many more.
The game does not only feature different times of day but also nicely done weather effects harmonizing with the great background music.
The textures are detailed, different gloom, shadow effects and reflections appeal.
It depends on if you are capable of playing this game at maximum settings but personally I have to say that this game even looks great on lower settings.
Naval combat:
It is a very advanced combat system, dynamic and strategic at the same time and that is why I explain my experience in more detail:
You start with a small schooner but later you can obtain different ship types.
Before you start your journey it is vital to keep a close eye on your ships stats.
The weight your ship can carry varies between type and the amount of crewmembers and cannon balls.
You have to make sure you do not overstock on ammo because you need space left for trading goods
You should not sink your enemies as the loot will be gone and you rather lose than make money.

Different types of shots are inflicting different damages such as destroying sails and masts, killing enemy crew members or destroying the ships broadside.
The damage done is visually impressive as you can see broken masts, fire on deck or holes. Furthermore the damage decreases movement or turning speed and if crewmembers die, the reloading time for cannons takes longer.
The boarding is very strategic and looks a bit turn based. You have the option to either continue using cannons damaging the vessel further or let your crew use their swords. After boarding is complete you have to decide which goods you take on board, if you have no space you can drop things you are currently not in need for.
Depending on what faction you attacked you just made some good friends while got on someone else´s shitlist
There are different types of crewmembers. The officers you can chose from have advantages and disadvantages.
Your first officer Donovan for example may proof not to be too efficient in boarding but is a great sailor as his men are able to improve your ships speed. You can hire your base crew in every harbor but of course they need to be paid and fed. If the morale is high the crew will make your life easier.
The changes you do to your ship by either upgrading it or equipping it with figureheads, sails and other things are not only changing it visually but also change the stats of it. You have to decide if you rather spend the time and invest a lot of money in your current vessel or obtain the next ship as soon as possible..
I love the AI in this game as the enemy acts intelligent
Man to man combat:
While I got used to naval combat fast, it takes me a lot of practice to master Chris's swordsmanship (opposed to gunnery).
It would have been nice if there had been a bigger tutorial mode.
At the beginning which had let you practice a bit more with the different types of weapons you can use and how to target the enemies.
However the quicksave function becomes very handy in here since you can save almost everywhere.
You also can heal yourself by using potions.
You have to be careful where to draw your sword or where you send your raven to steal as nearby people will attack you.
Getting surrounded leads you into serious trouble and results in a fast but painful death which makes it again very strategic as you have to pay close attention where and whom you fight.
Remember that sometimes it is wise to redraw for a moment rather than cut your way through because Chris is not a one man army.
I also have to mention that the AI here is again intelligent and will in fact be able to either protect himself and might give you a little support. The enemy currently needs to learn how to circle obstacles.
I enjoyed the idea a lot to include a raven into the battle system as it is a really cool ally for a pirate and his skills become very useful.
If you have a gamepad controls might be a bit easier compared to the keyboard.
Story
I will not say much about the story since I do not want to spoiler anything and it might depend on taste.
The story is not linear and it has several endings and a different progression is possible which adds plenty of replay value.
I enjoyed the character design and the voice cast.
Final words
There are a few bugs in game which I will write on a list and sent to the team but I am sure that the developers are going to fix them. Everyone can see that the staff is present if one visits the forum.
In my opinion the quest log needs some fine tuning as I sometimes have trouble to find out if a quest is in fact done or if there is still something left to do. The interface could be a bit prettier too.
Vendetta delivers a lot of fun and interaction no matter if you play story quests, side quests or join mini games such as dice games etc.
I already have 35 hours on my playtime but certainly I will make it 200 in the near future. I would also recommend this to every of my friends who is into the pirate theme and naval combat.

I would like to recommend that you read both the negative and positive reviews and make up your own mind before dismissing the game. I was initially in the negative, but have recently changed my mind after a few more hours offline (I have probably played closer to 5 hours)
You may ask what changed my mind, well after updating my AMD drivers and replacing a power cable for my HDD I haven't experienced  the same jerkiness and slowness that I was having before even when everything is set to low.
It's amazing, even though everything else was working fine, something as simple as a power cable and a driver update can make a lot of difference.
Update : I had to roll back to 15.11 drivers as the Crimson drivers were causing micro shuttering due to a downclock issue with the driver. The issue has been acknowledged by AMD so wait for a fix
However I must warn any potential purchaser and start with
Negatives :
The game still has some performance issues, but I have found these only occur in the following situations, with the following results and don't impact too negatively on the overall experience.
1. When there are a number of NPCs and you are in a town, bar etc, the frame rate can vary between a buttery smooth 60 and drop to as low as 30 in the first town. In the second town it drops to around 25.
These drops occur in all towns but are usually outside of combat situations, and are noticable but don't impact the game too much.
2. Ship battles drop below 60 to about 48FPS.
*Regardless of rig or graphical settings these issues have been occurring for people. While some people don't think this is an issue, I'm in the camp where I would much prefer 60 but because the game is no longer jerky and laggy that I can get past these.
3. A few bugs
I had an issue when my saves were taking a while to load, and then it crashed. After reloading it worked fine and fixed my issue I had with the save (I couldn't walk out of the bar, was hovering in mid air and textures were taking a while to load.
The rollback to 15.11 fixed the textures issue, and after the crash, the save fixed itself.
If you can get past the negatives then your in for an awesome game.
Pros :
Supports 21:9 native - as an owner of an ultrawide it is awesome to be able to play a game without having to do some modifications. The HUD and the game scales correctly to the screen without any issues. In game cutscenes are 21:9 native, the FMVs are 16/9 with black bars.
The map is 16:9 with black bars, and the inventory screen is also 16/9 with black bars.
The combat system with ships is fairly simple, but fun. There are 3 different types of cannon balls depending on the damage you want to do and ship battles feel fun and fluid.
The swordplay is awesome, but does take a bit of getting used to. If your expecting to press attack and just win, well your in for a bad time. You have your basic attack with mouse 1 and block with mouse 2, dodge with space, power attack with E and a special finishing move you can unleash.
The combat actually requires skill and timing and this can be brutal but I believe fair. Once you work out how to play the game, it is a lot more fun then say the witcher 2 sword combat which is mash the attack button to win.
Mixed :
While I like the dialogue as it is cheesy and campy, this may not be to everyone's taste.
There are a few times where sentences tend to roll into one another, or the dialogue inflection isn't quite on point for the dialogue being spoken. There's also a couple of times where I have clicked next to advance the dialogue, but only the next line of text comes up and you have to wait for the dialogue to finish.
It reminds me in a way of the Witcher 1 dialogue in that it kinda feels like that it was written for another language and would sound better that way.
On a side note I tried German Audio and English Text - Awesome but the subs don't stay on screen long enough during a cutscene or a scene that automatically advances the spoken dialogue but it is in no way a dealbreaker.
There are also a few minor bugs but the dev team is working on them. Read the forums for more info.
To sum up :
I haven't got far enough with the rest of the game to rate the missions and the rest of the game so I will update as I go through.
I hope the devs don't take this the wrong way but with a bit more optimization, a bit more polish and a patch or two to fix bugs and QOL (Quality of Life) issues I would have no problem recommending it without any warnings.
As it is I am having fun, the game cops a lot of flak (some warranted, some not so) so I would suggest give it a shot, and if you don't like it refund it. You have nothing to lose.

First, I bought Raven`s Cry before and got a free copy of Vendetta - Curse of Raven`s Cry. I write this review in english, but thats not my native language and I losed a lot since I cant practise it much, but I hope you can understand what I mean.
This game doesn`t use DRM, you get an CD Key and you can register it to get 2 special weapons but its not a must do like it was with Two Worlds 1+2, an internet connection is not 	required, you can play it offline, you only need one to register your game if you like.
What changed?
Well, honestly I cant see much changes as said, but there are a few, for example graphic looks better a bit, but few cities are still too dark, when you travel to islands like Port Royale or Black Rocks, it looks realy beautiful, much better then on Raven`s Cry. Pups have now more tables and drunken peoples, they are not emty. But a few pups still look like they forgot to place a table in the middle or forgot the lightning because one was realy dark, also there where not addet more Party Games, so you will only finde mini games to make money on 2 or 3 pups, all other didnt had one, what is sad because I realy enjoy making my money in that way then buying food, canabis, alcohol or tee and travel to the countries to sell that for a bit more money then I payed, what makes realy less provite since traveling cost also money and food for your crew. I play this game in german, so I cant tell you if the english voice acting is better then it was on Raven`s Cry but I can tell you, that in german it doesnt match always with voice and mouth movements.
Fighting System:
New? I´m not sure if its realy new, for me it was better on Raven`s Cry if I remember it well, but I dont realy like it on Vendetta.  Its frustrating when you fight agains 3 or 4 enemies, you have always to escape or run a bit away to see all enemies, the fighting camera is♥♥♥♥♥♥ you can only block 1 enemie at a fight, the camera choose his enemie, you can switch it but its anoying when you fight, also there are often bugs when you try to hit or when you fight standing in water, there is no way to jump backward so he always jumps up. its rare to fight only with 1 enemie they are always to 3 or 4 or more what makes it realy hard and you start to save after every fight. Slow motion finishing is a new thing in this game but I never had one so maybe its only for high skilled pirates, witch make this "new thing" useless,
Ship:
Cant see much improvement, Ship is still slow, controlls are okay after you found it out, how it works, you have now free sailing in the game, fights are mixed, sometimes 1 ship sometimes you have to fight agains 3 or 4 ships. There are different levels and Ships, you can upgrade all parts like on Raven`s Cry,
Gameplay, Quests and more:
The good one is, you can Save your game whenever you like, also the game uses autosave witch can be disabled on settings. You have now more Quests and Characters, what makes the playtime bigger then it was in Raven`s Cry. Details are better now on the Characters too, Enemies drops not always items when they died, also sometimes you get double items, so you have more too sell. There are new Animals who attack you, only the crabs and birds are friendly, so be carefull if you see a monkey or a wild boar. The Map is the same as on Raven`s Cry and the missions I did for now where the same, only reward changed and its a bit harder now to level up. Your Inventory can pick up as many Items as you like, at least it was never full for me and I had a lot of items, weapons and herbs in it. Also you can always run, no matter how full your inventory is.
Rating, recommendation and short info:
If you liked Raven`s Cry and bought it, then you normaly already owen this Game, if you didn`t played it, give it a try. This Game makes realy fun and its better then Raven`s Cry because they fixed a lot of Bugs and Glitches, also graphic lookes a bit better and you have a lot of hours to finish this game if you do all quests and side quests. For peoples who never played Raven`s Cry but loved games like Risen and Two Worlds give it a try. Since you can now refunde on Steam if you didn`t played more then 2 hours, and the game is worth for you the price, then buy it, you have nothing too lose if you don`t like it after trying it a bit. (refunde it and get your money back).

Its up to you what you like to do, for myselfe, I enjoy this game and I have a lot of fun with it. I got this for free since I already had Skyrim + all expansions.
I'd say this is worth buying if:
1. You've never played Skyrim before and you don't know what you're doing.
2. You'd like to play a prettier version of Skyrim without mods.
I personally have spent quite a lot of time on this game already but always fell back to spending more time modding it than actually playing the game. Mods are lots of fun and fix so many issues this game have, there are tons I love and would recommended... But if you're like me and you would like
your games, it might be a better idea to play the game vanilla to avoid going insane.
This edition is great for that. You have all those little graphical enhancements built-in and (mostly) glitch free, don't expect anything new content-wise though.
If you already own the base version and didn't get this for free, don't buy it. You can get more or less the same result with mods, spending an extra $50+ on a small visual rework is not worth it.
As for the actual game, I'm sure most people know of Skyrim by now so I'll try to avoid the more obvious things:
Skyrim is very popular for a reason, it's a great RPG. It's a great game and the amount of content is insane, definitely a game  a lot of people can sink a lot of hours into. Great as it is however, it's also full of flaws. Filled. A foundation of mistakes. Oblivion and Skyrim (I haven't played Morrowind very much so I can't really comment on it) are what I've considered my favorite video games for a long time and as much as I would like to say they are perfect, there are so many things about them that frustrate me and make the game not as enjoyable as it could have been.
The main issue with Skyrim is that it fails to innovate. It wasn't as much of an issue in 2011 but seeing the game getting re-re-re-re-released and seeing what Fallout 4 ended up being makes me extremely worried for the future of the series. I think the biggest problem is that the game is founded on old mentalities, old video game design. It's as if most of the game is the way it is because "that's how video games are" than because it makes sense.
There are countless mechanics that are tracked but cannot be seen, the interface and stats are extremely lackluster. I can understand the argument for "Immersion" but in a game that boasts an incredible amount of content, not being able to track my progress drives me nuts. Most of the interface doesn't work well with KBM and was clearly designed with consoles in mind. Not being able to sort through your inventory, through storage etc. There is so much about this game that almost forces you to be disorganised and inneficient.
Engine-wise, while there is a significant leap in visuals, the Special Edition JUST now fixed the dreaded and ancient alt-tab issue. The game doesn't run particurlarly well, never properly supported borderless windowed, never supported refresh rates above 60 FPS without messing up physics. Every interior is instanced. Even if they're fast you constantly have loading screens.
Your first couple of hours will be filled with wonder and a thirst for exploration you can never quench. You will however realize that there isn't much more to discover than in a randomly generated game after that, unless you are very dense. Most of the loot is randomly generated, enemies respawn, so many locations re-use the same asset to the point where they look nearly identical (when they kept boasting about the fact that each dungeon had been hand-crafted... they just failed to mention that hand-crafted means a couple rooms manually paired together in different orders). Unique assets are so rare that you feel like you've discovered something amazing when you see one, even if it's insignificant.
Back on efficiency; This game wants you to be inneficient so bad. You can pick up everything. Most people that never played a game like this will
to pick up a bunch of stuff because they assume it come in handy, to resell it or whatever. The truth is, there is no point. Most of the stuff in this game is useless. In fact, even the things that
be useful is useless. I've only made one character on Skyrim SE and it was my sixth in total. It's the first character I've decided to play efficiently and complete everything with.
There is a very important concept where items will have more or less value depending on their weight. It's very simple but most people won't think about it. All you have to do is divide the value in gold by the weight to get the septims:weight ratio and you'll soon realize that a 30 weight mace that's worth 300 gold is actually garbage compared to something that's 1 weight and over 10 gold. Because of that, gems and potions are always worth picking up and will have insane ratios whereas most equipment is useless. I know it's stupid but the moment you start planing what you pick up with that in mind, you can basically just run through everything and ignore most of the loot yet become rich.
Some quests are fun and interesting. The rest you wonder why they're there at all. Why would you spend so much time completing a tedious quest that hardly has more to it than something out of an MMO when the reward is the amount of gold you would get selling some random trinket you'll find just about anywhere. Dialogues are neither interesting or engaging, they'll often drag on for too long and your "choices" are only really there to give you a voice because they usually change very little to how things unfold. This honestly ruins so many of the actually interesting, fun or original quests in the game. There is so much content that could have been cut without affecting the quality. The guild questlines and daedric quests are some of the only memorable ones.
Speaking of which, the game suffers so much from letting you do whatever you want and go wherever you please. For two reasons:
1. Most of the game has to scale in difficulty based on your progression in the game, which results in weird things like overpowered wolves (not as much of an issue in Skyrim than it was in Oblivion).
2. You are constantly being sent all around the world without ever feeling like you're "done" with anything.
Freedom is something a lot of people like in a game. However, I believe that if you need to rely on scaling difficulty, you haven't designed the game well. I wish some areas were more dangerous than others. I wish I couldn't go places because the enemies are too tough. I wish I'd face an enemy that makes me go "WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥" and only come back once I feel I've become strong enough. Those take away from the experience so much for me. Being allowed to do whatever you want is one thing, being
to is another.
One last thing: The combat is not interesting, no matter how you see it. That's what you spend the most time doing and it's just not fun. You end up cheesing it all the time because the tools you're giving just don't really work that well. Progression sounds exciting but in practice it's boring (spells are a good example). By the time you're that strong, the game won't be challenging anyway and if it is, it won't feel like a challenge, it'll feel like a chore.
One game that fixes nearly all these issues for me is The Witcher 3. I found it better in nearly every aspects and it makes me sad because I love the elder scrolls. Seeing Fallout 4 shows me that Bethesda is not willing to re-think how they make games and what makes them fun. I expect TES VI to be the same I've seen with their games since 2006. I still expect loading when I go inside houses. I still expect face close ups when I talk to people. I still expect a clunky first-person combat system.
Nevertheless and surprisingly enough, I still recommend this game. Play it! It's fun for the most part.

The only thing this is worse at than anyother controller ive seen is there is no physical D-Pad just a smooth emulated D-Pad. I rarely use the D pad so thats no big deal for me.
Games I have tested this on as of the review below
Rocket League:
I originally bought this controller because my Logitech wasnt able to handle the quick presses and twitching needed for 1v1 Rocket League and broke. This controller plays Rocket League just as good as I played it with my Logitech i am currently Silver III on most ranked modes, close to Gold I on 1v1. This controller has improved my Rocket League by allowing me to bind Jump and Boost to one key for faster Aerials.
Mount & Blade Napoleanic Wars:
I was able to create a confiiguration for this game real easy. I used Gyroscope for aiming and have all the hotkeys i need in various spots for comfort. I need to do a bit more tweeking of sensitivity and put on a damper for when i squeeze the trigger but the game played great with the controller. It is easier to play this with Mouse and Keyboard from a aiming aspect obviously but as a not so competitive shooter the Steam Controller works fine and will only get better for this.
Torchlight 2:
This is the game I spent the most time on. Setting this up was easy and made playing the game more fun because I dont have to hunch over the keyboard and reach for hotkeys. It takes a little getting used to as far as using the touch pad for moving but once that learning curve is done it becomes second nature.
Starbound:
This one is a little difficult to setup for mouse movement because of the type of game it is, but im sure ill figure something out and it will be a lot better experience when I do. Hotkeys are very important on this game and I hate reaching for them.
Edit: Also forgot to mention, typing on this controller is surprisingly fun to learn and easier than expected. Its harder to get to the friend chat area than it is to type the messege from big picture mode.

Keeping in mind that this is practically a first gen buy of hardware, I found the controller to be over all enjoyable. I doubt in the future they will bundle Rocket League and Portal 2 (Like what I have, so I may affect the review.). With just the controller itself it fit pretty well in my man hands that span from middle finger to bottom of palm (19 cm). There is a nice little bit of weight for the bottom handles and thumbs naturally in the center of the track pads. The analog stick a nice and responsive and the buttons have nice press to them. They don't click but they have some force to them. The plug and play nature makes it nice and easy to set up. Also there is a wireless option taking double a batteries to power but works just as well plugged in from a male USB/Micro USB wire provided. Wireless adapter included as well.  I know many complain about the layout of the controller but as someone who use to play console PS 1,2, and 3 then stopped for a couple of years for PC mouse and keyboard the controller is a nice welcome.
General Computer Use
It is a little convenient when you endlessly browse the web. I would recommend for those who like to poke around reedit or tubmlr and do not need to type. There is a bit of a slide but it’s easy to get used to. The clicks are set default to the triggers with the respective right/left click. There is not steam controller software, which I know of, that can allow you to edit it for general use. Maybe in big picture mode but I could not easily find it.
Game Play
I found that playing takes a bit time to set up. Obviously this will not replace you mouse and key board for games like Dota but I doubt that was the intended use. This works much better with FPS games and a few turn based strategy. I have not yet tested in on driving games. At the time of the Review, I tried out Fallout 4. The controls are a little weird and for some reason the paddles are not registered as separate button. Instead labeled as A. I wish the paddle was separate button commands not just ones remapped one the controller. This may change after the review is posted. I tend to play my games on the more sensitive side and found that I had to manually increase the sensitivity in game. I wish there was way to get it across the board. For at the very least all valve games.
Overall
For the first steam controller I like it very much. The construction feels nice in the hands and each component is finely crafted. If you really want one and have the spare cash to spend I would recommend to try it out. Otherwise I would wait for the next controller to see if they can improve on some of the sensors and output. I wish there was some software I can boot up to edit controls either across the board or for general use. At the very least re-calibrating would be nice for those how like the extra sensitivity or to dull it down a bit,
Pros
-Feels nice in the Hand
-Weight is Distributed Comfortably
-Well Constructed
- Easy To Set Up (Just Plug and Play)
- Decent controller substitute for PC user
Con
-No Easy To Find Edit Software
-Color (Black Is Nice But I like other colors.)
-Some games to not pick up the paddles.
-First Gen Hardware (Take that as you will)
-No Add-Ons (Cases, skins, Overlays, etc.)
-Replacement Parts. (If the paddle break or get lost looks like it’s time to get a new controller.)

When I recieved mine yesterday, I was just expecting a normal run of the mill controller that I would just plug into my pc and use. Boy was I wrong. When I held it in my hands for the first time, the controller fused itself to my skin and molded right in. Unlike how other countrollers may need some time to get comfortable with, I got used to the Steam Controller right away. I've seen many people saying how "Oh, it's just another controller to use". Well you're sorta right, but it looks and feels comepletely different from a normal console gamepad. The touch-sensitive trackpad makes it feel like you're using a mouse. The buttons, analog stick, trackpads, and right and left triggers are all in the right positions, proving for easy manuvering and non-painful stretching. If you are looking for a controller to use for fighting games, racing games, etc, this controller is a must buy. One thing I do recommend though if you buy it. The material they used on the controller is pretty shiny and will "smear pretty easily", so wash your hands before you use it so you dont't get gross fingerprints on it. But other than that, I'm pretty satisfied with the $50 I spent.

Conclusion...
Solid controller. Surely fills the gap between games that don't offer controller support and ones that do. Love how you can easily switch profiles on the fly! That is one of the coolest features. The controller feels really good and the touch pads surprisingly feel natural. All in all, I give it a solid 8. Only knock are asthetics with glossy plastic and feel in hand. Solid purchase otherwise though!
Concerning the actual feel in the hand...
It doesn't feel as "high quality" as an xbox controller does, but it certainly doesn't feel cheap. I'm not a fan of the non-textured plastic face. The flippers on the back are great!
Concerning the funtionality and usability...
Pretty awesome how the controller doubles as a mouse when not in steam on the Windows side. I've not tried in Linux yet, but I'm sure it's probably the same. The touch pads are pretty awesome. I can really see how this pad once fully accustomed to it will kick♥♥♥♥♥ I hoped into some Unreal 3 and did surprisingly well. Again, it just feels natural. I have pretty large hands and I feel like I have to stretch for the XYAB buttons. Not sure that it is a stretch, so much as I just struggle to hit them due to my sausage fingers...mileage may vary here.

This thing is a god send. I've always loved playing with controllers but I love computers so much more than consoles. Now that I have this thing, I can play any game in my library with a controller. THIS DOES NOT REVIEW MYPLAYER MODE AND INSTEAD TOUCHES MOSTLY ON UNIVERSE MODE PLUS A FEW OTHER NOTABLES:
Universe mode is extremely disappointing and overhype. What people are mistaking for being hugely open to creativity is just an extremely shallow game mode. The promos are absolutely awful and don't at all follow a superstars real life personality. They book w/e trash matches over and over. Rivalries feel basically weightless other than they fight each other constantly. There's really no weight anywhere other than what you pretend. And I get that works for some people, but holy♥♥♥♥♥♥is it lazy development. Instead of putting in work to make interesting things happen in the game, you play pretend way too much and really it's extremely difficult to get into when there are no real in game consequences or legitimate goals other than a few basic things like win vs certain people or titles. I was hyped to play and people were giving legitimate reasons to get excited, but overall it's just way overblown. The game is far more shallow (outside of the creation suite) than I'd hoped.
Also the matches, even with adjusted sliders, are pretty meh. You can finish or get finished in any match pretty much instantly. There's no real back and forth because a few minutes or 5 minutes or so into a match and one special and it's over. Even with slower momentum and high stamina etc it's really easy to obtain and it becomes impossible to lose (or win depending on your side) in those situations. It doesn't feel like an authentic match.
Elimination chamber, for example, is hilariously stupid with computers specifically. The players all come in extremely quick. You get eliminated really fast. And it's just over. Nothing feels epic whatsoever. Idk what the hell people got so hyped over for this game. It really blows my mind.
In the really old games, like No Mercy on N64 for example, matches could really last extremely long and be prone to real back and forths. Even when I last played Here Comes the Pain and SVR 06 it could sometimes happen even in it's extremely dated and flawed gameplay. And the GM mode at least had real goals. Like Universe mode obviously has a good chunk more of options, but it's over a decade newer. You can imagine just as much in SVR 06 and on top of that have real goals the game implements, but in Universe nearly everything has to be up in your head. It's unreal how much of a lack of depth there is in this♥♥♥♥♥♥ I didn't have my bar extremely high, but was hoping for a straight improvement over the last set of games I played. There are definitely some, but the amount of shortcomings is inexcusable and I simply can't believe how many people are utterly impressed with what they offer when it's so lackluster, especially compared to extremely old versions of the game that aren't even that far behind in so many aspects and in other parts of the game legitimately have more options. How pathetic is that? I mean you can 2v2v2 TLC match in SVR 06 for example, but in this game you can 8man tag or battle royale etc, but can't do that 2v2v2 with 3 or 4 teams lol. In this rant I'm missing details and could definitely hammer it in more, but I feel like I touched it up enough to get my point across.
If you're playing with 3-4 or more friends online or in personal prefarably, then ya go for it. It can be a good amount of fun and you can do whatever you want as you go along. But Universe mode is not what it's hyped up to be, it's extremely empty and bland. Matches are not authentic whatsoever. The game just lacks general polish. My not so high bar of expectations was not close to met after recently playing SVR 06 and other older WWE/WWF games. It's astonishing how many things can be done so wrong.

The game is a great improvment from last year and they have finally added features that where removed back in WWE2k14 like custom match rules and the ability to start the match with finishers, I really like the addition of the carry mode and the new animations look really good. However trying to run this game in 4k has some problems. i am running a i7 7700k running at 5.2 Ghz and a GTX 1080Ti running at +150Mhz overclock, which will run shadow of war at max setting with the high rez and 4k packs installed (for e.g) at a solid 60FPS in 4K yet WWE2k18 is having a lot of problems keeping a solid frame rate. I could switch it down to 1080p but it just looks janky. so I would recommend this game if you are a fan of WWE and you play in a lower resolution than 4K but if you like to play in a higher resolution (like I do) I cant recommend this game.

I've logged 80 hours to decide this, but unfortunately I have to err on the side of negative because I'm not prepared to put any more effort in.  And I really wanted to like it.
However never has it better been said that "your mileage may vary".  You may not worry about re-ordering every commander (of which you may have many) every turn even to move to another province, so to move across a large map with a slow moving army is going to take a lot of user input before they ever get to do anything.  By the 4th version of the system I would hope there would be more tools to avoid this micromanagement.  You get that with other games, not here.  So ultimately you have to decide whether the undoubted rewards are worth the huge effort required.

The reason I got this game was because the cards from it sold for more than the game itself cost when it was on sale... I expected absolute garbage from the game, yet found myself pleasantly surprised. There's actually a pretty good little game in here, worthy of attention even if it's not on sale oddly enough.
The basic concept is you start out in a rather limited 2D space shooter. You get shot down, fall to the planet, and then have to collect parts to repair your ship and escape. The writing's mediocre at best, and the plot's hardly anything to write home about, but the gameplay really does shine surprisingly well.
You have three buttons, other than left/right. These are jump, fire a gun when you find it eventually, and fire a teleporter gun. This sounds simple. It's not. They actually put pretty good effort into coming up with some creative puzzles that take a bit of thought to overcome with these few tools.
Momentum's carried over, so if you fire a teleport shot, and it has enough time to travel, you can jump upward as it hits and keep going up from where you portal to. This is put to surprisingly good use with some really rather clever yet deceptively simple looking puzzles.
Toss in a bit of exploration and some hidden goodies, advanced stuff and bonuses scattered around, and it's actually not a bad game at all.
Yeah, the story sucks. Yeah, the dialgue is awful. Yeah, it's only about an hour long from start to finish. But you know what? It's CHEAP. And to be blunt, the gameplay itself is good enough to ignore all that and just sit down to a fun little puzzle game that vaguely has some ever so slight similarities to metroid.
I can actually recommend this game at full price. It's actually worth it. Just don't expect it to have good writing is all. =P

I like the overall concept of this game and I normally enjoy the style of gameplay, but I can't recommend this title because the game feels very sloppy in the way it detects collisions. The obstacles' hitboxes are often much bigger than their appearance suggests, and they're not even consistent between levels. That results in very frustrating gameplay where you fail a run seemingly out of nowhere, thinking you had a good flow going.
The keyboard and gamepad control the game very differently, and different levels are much easier with one or the other, which feels like a design oversight.
Also, the UI is a bit shoddily designed for keyboard and gamepad, mainly when trying to restart a run. It should be a simple press of a button, but instead it's a list menu which is prone to interference by the movements you were doing in your recently failed run. Very often you'll select "exit to menu" instead of "retry".
Overall, the otherwise potentially very fun game is crippled by very simple design mistakes that are a bit too obvious in a game of such a limited scope. I think the designer was quite lazy.

I have been wanting a steam controller since they first announced it. I was well aware that it is the first of it's kind and could have easily been a flop but I was optimisistic about the controller and decided to gamble 50 bucks on it and pre-order it. I'm very glad that I did. I was very surprised to find out how well it works with first person games (including FPS games) and rocket league. It actually ended up exceeding my expectations. Works great for mouse games too. I use it to play hearthstone sometimes. It does require time to learn how to use and time to find profiles for games that work best for you but once I had it set and and spent the time to get comfortable with it I actually prefer it over my 360 controller for ALL games.

So, I've only had this controller for a day now and probably played about 4-5 hours worth of games, so this might be limited.
The controller is of decent build quality, and while the positions of buttons and the grip are not something I am used to from prior controllers it does not seem bad - in fact, it seems quite ergonomic overall. It just will take getting used to.
It allows me to play games fairly well from comfort. I've primarily used it to play Far Cry 3 so far, and with proper input bindings it works very well.
Though this is where the trouble comes in: the software for configuring the steam controller is incredibly mediocre, and the documentation is highly limited to say the least.
One example of a missing feature: the ability to bind a button or pad or whatever to cycle through controller modes, or toggle different modes on and off. Instead, you have to hold down a single button down whenever you want the "mode switching" to work, rebinding other keys temporarily. Unfortunately, this is unwieldy in many situations, and you can't use the actual buttons on the front of the pad for this (limiting you to the triggers, bumpers, grip buttons, and for some reason the haptic pad buttons as well).
If you know what you are getting into - that the controller software is currently unimpressive (and big picture mode is incredibly unwieldy and buggy, yet required to customize the profiles for whatever reason) - then you might enjoy using it. It fits its intended purpose - the track pads especially. You need to configure them properly for whatever game you play, and I highly recommend binding another key to mode switching for sensitivity changes, but in any case it works.
Recommended, but make sure you know what you're getting into.

Simple Review:
I gave one to my 8 year old daughter, who up till now did all her PC gaming with an XBOX 360 controller. Her initial response was, "It's kind of big".
We spent a day playing through all her favorite games (Castle Crashers, Dungeon Siege 3, Grow Home, Goat Simulator, and Risk of Rain) and no matter what kind of game it was she was able to play effortlessly with the Steam Controller. She even managed the 3D games better than what the dual analog sticks allowed her before.
At the end of it all she now prefers the Steam Controllers. I like them a lot, but I was worried they'd be too big of a jump (with the touchpads) for her but she needed no instruction and picked them up intuitively.
+1 to smart design that even an elementary school child can grasp and understand.

I'm sure this is because I'm not used to it & I don't have it fully configured yet. But the layout & how this controller handles (at the moment) are terrible.
I come from a long background of using a Playstation style controller. To me inverting the right stick/touchpad with the button layout was a bad move. It makes every use feel clumsy & all my gaming sloppy. My mind & hand are trained to go where the buttons are supposed to be resulting in me hitting the wrong buttons or the touchpad.
As for the touchpads, the sensitivity is way off. To move the camera I have to swipe multiple times to get to where I want the camera to be. I'm sure this is just because I have to adjust the sensitivity.
So far everything feels sloppy & poorly laid out. When you can't do the things you know you can do & your skill level tanks because of a controller layout, gaming almost feels demoralizing.
I'll revisit this review, but 1st impressions (to me at least) are not good.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
UPDATE:
It's been a long time since my 1st impression & I have to admit I barely picked this thing up at all because of that. It's too tempting to pick up the DS3, I'm almost guaranteed a good gaming experience with THAT controller.
However, over the past few weeks, I've been forcing myself to use the Steam Controller(Mainly because my DS3 is breaking down & needs to be repaired/replaced). Anyway I've been getting some usage out of this & it feels like time for this update. My 2nd impression is still not entirely positive, but better.
After some time my thumbs have started to hone in on the button locations. I still stumble & occasionally have to look at the damn controller to get my bearings, but I'm managing.
The touchpads still feel gimmicky, out of place & larger then they need to be. Yes the sensitivity can be changed(this addresses what I said earlier), but it still feels off & imprecise. Not sure how people play FPS games with this abomination.
The controller itself is very hefty. There's a lot of weight & bulk here. The fact that it is in your hands, is always in your mind. A good controller, is one that you forget you are holding & functions as an extension of yourself. This is not, 'that'. Also because of it's size, It never feels like it's sitting correctly in my hands. The buttons in the back & the bumpers/triggers always feel like I have to reach for them. I have average sized male hands, not sure who this was designed for.
The ability to configure buttons/settings through Steam is a great idea & works well, but I was able to do that ages ago & a lot easier with XPadder.
Overall I say this thing is somewhat functional, but an uncomfortable 2nd choice when it comes to what controller I will use when gaming.
Side Note: While playing Saints Row 2. I ran into parts of the game, that are made completely unplayable because of the terrible touchpad. Namely the "Ho-ing" missions where you have to push & hold a direction on the touchpad. A stick that you can hold, will stay in that position. This abonmination moves that direction & immediately recenters. Also ANY targeting is a terrible chore. This thing is a pile.

This controller provides something that no other controller on the market offers. It takes some getting used to of course, but that could be said about any new input device. It took years to learn to type properly, and when I got my first laptop it took some time to get used to using a trackpad instead of a mouse.
This controller provides trackpads that operate like trackballs. Steam provides a plethora of configuration options to tailor the controller exactly how you need it for each game. The downside here is that there is a lot of options, so you may spend some time tweaking each game before the controller is perfectly comfortable.
The controller itself feels good in the hands. The buttons are a bit too "clicky" for my liking, and I find I have to reach a bit for the top triggers, which is something I don't have to do with a PS controller. Something else available are the underside "paddle" buttons. I find these very useful for first person shooters, for jump, run, or crouch depending on the game. I do accidentally push these buttons sometimes when things get intense though.
Overall I think this product is a great success, providing something unique and advantageous over most any other game controller out there. Excellent product!

Tentacult is a perfect example of a great concept executed badly.
At first it's quite fun, even cathartic, watching people scream and run away as you attempt to
befriend them, but the numerous problems that build up as you play and make Tentacult seem more like an early access game than a final version. The two worst offenders making this game feel unfinished are grouping/path-finding and the level design.
Grouping/path-finding - everyone seems to be having trouble with this. You can get your little buddies to clump together by pressing space, or on an Xbox controller by double tapping (for some reason?) the A button. Pressing these buttons will only help if your newly converted friends are within a certain limited radius, but if they have gotten themselves wedged somewhere, prepare for some tedious maneuvering or leave them behind.
Level design - it's really unpolished and includes a lot of unclear obstacles. There are invisible walls that block you, and visible walls that you can walk through. Numerous times I have experienced clipping through the ground, and sometimes (what I assume people are mistaking for the ability to jump) being ejected into the air due to obstacles or sometimes for no apparent reason. I could be wrong about that; maybe there is a jump button, but nothing on my keyboard or Xbox controller seemed to do it and since the in game controls only list WASD for movement and nothing else (not even space for clumping), I'm assuming the "jumping" is caused by flaws in the level design.
Some of the later levels can be frustrating so the urge to give up may be great. I struggled through to the end and was rewarded with
Despite it's problems I do like Tentacult; it just has too many issues for me to be able to recommend it to anyone else.

I so wanted to give this game a positive review or would of settled for a neutral option but the bugs are a game breaker for me. The game starts off so well & is indeed both fun & funny but the difficulty ramps up very quickly & the bugs start to bite harder as you progess.
My first problem was the game would not return to the start if you selected the option screen, in fact it locked up completely meaning task manager required to get out, it does not do this every time therefore I did manage to actually play.
Then any changes you make in options have to be reset every time you fire the game up, it does not remember your settings.
The worst bug however is the sticking/jamming, not a problem at the lower levels as there are plenty of people to convert but as the difficulty rises the population dwindles quite dramatically & the number of snipers/grenadiers rises meaning you cannot afford to lose any of your little dudes by them getting hung up the map & becoming sniper bait.
There is mention in a couple of the other reviews that you can jump but having pressed every key I still can't get them to do it, perhaps its a perk reserved for controllers only.
Having spent over an hour trying to get past level 6 I finally give up. I know it can be done as I've seen it on You Tube but then the guy who did it gave up trying to complete level 7 before skipping it, I stopped watching at this time so perhaps he went back to it, I lost interest as he couldn't do 7 then there seemed no point in perservering with 6 only to get stuck on the next as well.
Pros: It cost less than a £/$
Lots of fun with plenty of humour at the lower levels
Cons: The jamming / sticking problem is a real gamebreaker as far as I'm concerned
The background music is awful after a short time, the music on the menu screen is far better imo, although music is a personal taste so you may like it.
Settings / controls are vague, I turn the music off at the start but as I progress the level rises again & has to be reset again & at the start of every game.
Just because a game is cheap it does not mean that is an excuse to produce/release a buggy game
One more observation, at time of writing, I checked the other reviews before writing this to see whether I was the only person having problems, I have more time in game & more in game achievements than any of the other reviewers, for so many positive reviews I wonder why so many of them have already stopped playing it.
I don't believe people should be allowed to write a review whether positive or negative on any game when they have only played for a few minutes, it can be very misleading at times.
If the devs were to refine the sticking or introduce more people into the maps people would have a better chance of progressing in what is in fact a potentially good fun game. 4.9/10

Three achievements away from completion at the time of writing, and in excess of 440 hours... not including time spent playing on either of my cell-phones.
I can give pros and cons, but this game doesn't really follow a standard model so I will approach the review a little differently. Do I recommend it? Yes. Not because it's super in depth or complicated or even value packed as far as things to do. But, because - in its extreme simplicity - it is arguably one of the best designed games I've come across in a *very* long time.
If you're the kind of person that watches the progress bar during a scan or a massive install - even if you know it'd take hours - then you'll get hooked fast. I keep logging on and expecting something to change (other than events). I hope for quests. A town to enter. Skills. Adventures. Yet, none of that exists. It's all about watching progress bars, lots of them, and reaching goals.
Ultimately, it is the sheer simplicity of this game that is brilliant. It takes a little bit of thought. It takes some strategy to get the best results. It takes a great deal of patience. So, if you want a time killer that you keep coming back to, then do play this game. Seriously, it's worth it because it's so cleanly made.
As an aside ~ on every single instance I've had to deal with customer relations ~ the staff are friendly and helpful. I imagine this is in part because I am polite and clear in my requests for help and I'm not a jerk about it, but also because they at Hyper Hippo are a great team. I've had 100% of my issues resolved in reasonable time, and with generous professionalism. That speaks volumes about the development team and the kind of company it is. In short, it's a company worth supporting.

QUICK NOTE: At the time I'm writing this, the game is on sale at $0.54 (95% off). At that price, I could recommend the game, sure. Unless you absolutely cannot get enough first person puzzle/platforming, I wouldn't get it otherwise, especially not at $10.99.
---
You play as a hacker that is being paid (presumably) a large amount of money to hack into a level and steal data through some physical manifestation of your target's... network? Mainframe? God knows. The point is you have to go through 12 levels (followed by another 10 bonus levels), collecting 3 Data Fragments per level.
The main gimmick of the game is that you can switch your "Polarity" at will - between red and blue. While a certain color, you will collide with objects of the opposite color (such as lasers, which will kill you), but pass through objects of the same color. There are also cubes (pretty much tiny Companion Cubes) which behave in a similar fashion. The cubes will power things when plugged into a slot, very similar to how Companion Cubes could hold buttons down to keep platforms suspended, etc. in Portal. Add a couple generic objects, such as launch pads and moving platforms, and you pretty much have the entire game.
The game unabashedly takes a lot of inspiration from Portal: levels feel like sterile, self-contained test chambers, the only difference is that everything's dark grey instead of white, and you don't have a charming robot voice monologuing you or telling a story while you progress; the large and open, but still linear level design; and a general futuristic theme (though it's admittedly silly to mash both Portal and Polarity into such a vast genre and expect it to mean anything).
You don't need to collect the 3 Data Fragments to technically "beat" the level - rather, you can simply progress through the level and find the exit. This is where most of the difficulty comes from. However, Data Fragments are required to unlock the next levels. They are usually poorly hidden, if not put directly in plain sight, and by simply walking around the room you can easily tell how to get to the fragments. The worst the game will do is put them behind a small puzzle, or out of your immediate field of view when you enter a room. To put it into perspective, the only levels I needed to play more than once were the first and second levels, where I missed one fragment each, because it was placed slightly out of sight or in a corner that I had carelessly overlooked.
It doesn't feel good to collect data fragments because the level design is not challenging at all. The main "puzzle" in each level often requires next to no thinking. I beat all 22 single-player levels in about 50 minutes, and was fairly bored the entire way through. Sadly, this is why I can't say I recommend this title.
It's not that the art style is uninspired and simple - that doesn't necessarily make a game bad.
It's not that the music, and the general sound design for that matter, has a generic, forgettable 80s futuristic feel, which I'd normally think was quite humorous or charming - lots of devs these days just use stock royalty-free music and nobody seems to mind that too much. At least this has custom music (I think).
It's not that it's trying to copy Portal - I don't see a huge amount wrong with following the footsteps of a very successful puzzle game and trying to recreate that formula!
It's not even that the first person animations, head bobbing, and movement glitches make it painfully obvious this is a 3D Unity game. Or that my Logitech F310 - a fairly good controller when it comes to compatibility - would only work during the main menu and the two "cutscenes" that exist in singleplayer.
The problem is the frankly depressing lack of content, and, more importantly, the content that
there is unchallenging, unengaging, and simply not fun. As a developer, I'd be disappointed if I spent a significant amount of time and effort building a game and only could be bothered to make a few mediocre-at-best levels that don't even show the potential of what few mechanics that DO exist. As a consumer, I'm very confused with how this game has so many positive reviews - must just be me being out of touch with the puzzle game community. Don't expect level design that lives up to Portal, or any other good puzzle game I can think of, really.
TL;DR - Game's really dry on content, and what content
manage to find its way in is insultingly easy and boring. I'd say it's worth neither your time nor your money. Get on a crazy 95% off sale, if at all.

Please note: This is a review for the first episode in a series. For more reviews of other games, head over to website;
Telltales cookie-cutter games have reached fans from all different IPs; The Walking Dead, Back To The Future, Game of Thrones – and now, Minecraft. It is easy for a Minecraft fan to look at this game and think they will enjoy it due to the name that has been slapped on it, but I do not think this is the case. Minecraft Story Mode will appeal more to fans of Telltale games than it will to Minecraft fans. I am not a major Minecraft fan, but luckily Telltale have made Minecraft Story Mode so that you do not need to be one to understand what is going on.
As soon as you begin the game, you get a choice if you would like to be male or female. Both options will give your character a different voice actor, be it Patton Oswalt or Catherine Taber. The story introduces the character that we will be playing as, Jesse – a ‘happy go lucky’ character with some friends that you can tell really mean the world to him. Oh, and don’t forget Jesse’s pet pig, Reuben.  Jesse and friends are about to partake in in a building competition at Endercon, but some unlikely and fullscale events occur that make our protagonist band together with friends and some unlikely people to try and save the Minecraft world.
Anyone familiar with the usual Telltale game mechanic will understand what this game will entail before they even start it up. From checking the Steam forums and user reviews, I can see that there are quite a few people that are not familiar with Telltales games. They were literally expecting a single player story for Minecraft, but that is not what Minecraft Story Mode – A Telltale Game Series is. For those not familiar with Telltales games, this is a heavily narrative driven game where you make conversational choices that will have an effect on the story. At certain parts in the story you are free to walk around and solve a few puzzles. I did find that the puzzles were scarce and extremely easy to complete, and the areas where you can walk around were very small with invisible walls keeping you in the cage like area.
Quick Time Events are a big part of Telltale’s mechanics. At certain parts of the game you will need to spam a certain key on your keyboard/controller. For example, you will need to spam Q to try and get released from the grasp of a large monster, or tap left to try and dodge an enemy’s attacks. In this new game, QTE’s are less important than they have ever been. In other Telltale games, if you miss a QTE, then something bad would have happened and you would have needed to restart the scene- In Minecraft Story mode, if you miss a QTE, you do not need to reload a save. Instead, you continue the story with a slightly different thing happening (although I have not noticed any differences except for a small cut scene change i.e. getting hit by an enemy and falling down when I was meant to dodge it, I just got back up and carried on running).  This change has meant that you really do have less gameplay than a normal Telltale game, if you class QTE’s as gameplay. However, this does mean you can sit back and relax to the story without getting annoyed if you miss a random QTE.
I found that  Minecraft Story Mode – A Telltale Game Series Episode One had as very interesting introduction, and as someone who doesn’t really play Minecraft (except for the Alpha, I played that A LOT) I didn’t find myself confused or needing to understand anything – You do not need past Minecraft knowledge for this. There are some times where you have to use a crafting table to craft an item using Minecraft recipes, but they are so obvious and you even have a ingame recipe book to help you if you managed to get stuck.
Minecraft is heavily known for being a building game, but in Telltales adaptation building is very scarce. There are only a couple of times where you build things, and those are just Quick Time Events that you really have no control over, the only control you get is a conversational choice where you get to choose what to build from a couple of options. I would have loved for a more ‘Minecraft’ feel to the game, such as in a time where you have to build you can go and collect a few materials and build a structure that you want to build.
The voice acting on this game is where the best points will come from – it’s brilliant. All voice actors have done a really good job to give me an authentic Minecraft Story experience. With a game so heavily on the dialog, subpar voice acting would be the death of this game, luckily, that isn’t the case. With some big names such as Patton Oswalt, Billy West and Paul Reubens, it would be a struggle to find someone on this game that you do not recognise. Each voice actor, combined with the story, gives some great personality to the in game characters. to the point where even on the first episode, there are characters who I already feel sorry for, and others who I dislike.
Since this is a Minecraft game, everything is made from blocks to resemble the world that makes Minecraft so popular. Minecraft has the charm that gives you free reign to do what you want, build what you want, explore where you want – Telltales version has lost all this, the only charm you will see will come from the characters and story. I really feel like Telltale could have dropped Minecraft entirely, made a new IP and still kept the same story (changing a few aspects as to not infringe con copyright) But I can see that they are clearly hoping the Minecraft name will make it sell, and it definitely will, although I do feel that many people will dislike the game because they are expecting it to be more like Minecraft. I have also noticed some errors with the blocky characters, often when you are up close to the characters face and they are talking, you will see some bugs where two textures are fighting over the same screenspace, causing massive texture flickering (I saw this the most with Ivor’s beard).
The music in the game is exactly what you would expect. The original Minecraft soundtrack has been used, but it seems like there has been lots of new musical scores introduced (I don’t recognise them from the original game, but it has been a long time since I played it) All songs used really fit in with the vibe that the game is trying to portray. Whenever something fast and exciting happens, the music will be fast paced and exciting – and vice versa when something sad is happening.
As with typical Telltale fashion, at the end of the game you will see every choice that you made and it will compare it to the average choice on what everyone else made. I love that Telltale shows us these statistics, and it really is fascinating to see how mean other people can be to the in game characters! These choices in the game really give Telltales games some great replayability, just to see how different the game will be if you play differently from the last time – If it would even change majorly at all!
I would highly recommend this game to any Telltale fans. Although it is not currently as good as their other games such as The Walking Dead, I have high hopes that with the upcoming episodes it will turn out to be an amazing story. If you are not a Telltale fan, or have never played any of the games before, I would recommend doing a bit of research on this before you purchase it – It is not a Minecraft in the typical fashion, so do not expect it to be. I very much enjoyed playing the first episode, but I could have easily played a game that had a similar story without it being a Minecraft themed game – So far, I really see no reason for this to be Minecraft themed, except to try and make a very large sum of money off an already massive IP.

Honestly, I used to love this game. i was a newbie and was introduced to the so called 'overwatch rip-off'. Thanks to a youtuber i no longer watch. But around OB59 this game just became un-playable for serious fps players like myself. Here's a list of things i would consider before plunging any time or money into this game.
Pros:
1: Free To Play. This game doesn't have amazing graphics like overwatch, but then again over is 60 bucks and paladins is free. for a free to play and keeping constantly updated, this game looks and plays decently.
2: 25+ Champions. while Overwatch and many FPS games have very limited amounts of characters with limited mechanics, Hi-rez is pumping out characters and new mechanics quite quickly. there's a new patch every month or so, and in it includes limited bug fixes and enjoyable characters.
3: The community isn't super toxic. The community in this game is actually quite kind. I've made many long time friends thanks to this game.
Cons: Unfortunatly, there are many more cons than pros. This game NEEDS to be fixed, but for now, the cons are endless.
1: BUGS. this game has way too many bugs, even for a free to play game with limited resources, the bugs are simply too much. There have been bugs popping up in streams, as well as league games.
2: The amount of patches. For new players, the amount of stuff that's popping up is hopeless. the characters Hi-rez pumps out are just getting more expensive, and to even try them all i had to get the founder's pack, which was 20 bucks.
which in my book, is not worth it.
3: Paladins is a cash-grab. Paladins used to be a fun game where everyone was kind and loved the game, but they keep pumping out characters, and skins that you need real money to achieve. more and more, paladins is just becoming a useless cash-grab project for Hi-Rez, i wouldn't be suprised if when this came out, it cost money to buy.
4: The Aimbots/Wallhacks/Etc. The amount of hackers who play this game are massive. Hi-Rez needs to listen to incoming player reports, as well as get a new Anti-cheat. Paladins' Anti-cheat is useless now that this game is gaining traction. if people can't aim, they need to leave the game.
5: False advertising. This one is simple, Paladins is advertised as an FPS, but recently Hi-Rez added a feature that lets you go from First Person to Third Person in the click of a button. It used to be fully fps, then 3rd person in spawn, but now you can play the whole game third-person. This, and many more mechanics are useless.
6: The Ranked Games are completely unbalanced. If you lose, your rank goes down. if you win, your rank goes up. It's a stupid feature, and with all the Ranked games i've played, im still only Gold 4. Hi-Rez needs to change it to personal status. When you do well in a match, your rank goes up, if you do poorly it goes down. This is a change that is NEEDED. and hi-rez does not care. Its all luck of the draw wether you get a newbie/toxic team or not.
7: Continuing to Balance Things. Hi-Rez is making this game extremely balanced. This game is also advertised as a 'strategic team-based game', but Hi-Rez continues to Balance characters and make changes to game mechanics to where it is not needed. The Characters are not supposed to be completely balanced, and thanks to this, Hi-Rez has removed 80% of it's characters from Ranked gameplay, because they are COMPLETELY useless in certain situations, against other super balanced characters. Hi-Rez needs to stop buffing and nerfing characters where they are dependant.
I Could continue, but this review would be a book series. Hi-Rez needs to take in what the community is saying, but until then i DO NOT recommend sinking money or much time into this broken game. Play it if you want, but do not buy anything until Hi-Rez decides what Paladins is supposed to be.
