Pretty similar to last year's, it has the biggest roster I've ever seen in a WWE game, decent tweaks and features on MyCareer and graphics are much better than last year.
Game performs very well, there's a lot more 30fps action this year though, which kinda sucks, but none of the actual gameplay itself is 30fps. Not dropped under 60fps even once during gameplay, despite everyone complaining about performance. I have an i7 7700k at 4.8ghz, 16GB RAM and an Aorus GTX 1080Ti with a 3440x1440 ultrawide, no issues at all...
Framerate seems locked to 60, kind of annoying on a 100hz monitor.
As for the people complaining about the issues, it could be driver related or your PCs could just not be good enough, seeing people saying they're getting 20-40fps, which is pretty bizarre. Optimisation can vary but I've had legitimately zero issues with optimisation myself.
If you liked last year's, you'll like this year's game. It just does everything very well, although if you don't actively follow wrestling, you might not need the upgrade. But do be aware that 2K17 originally came out over a year ago and it was out of date even then. This game already has a few out of date things, but you'll find your favourite superstars and shows.
I'm pretty surprised the game doesn't have Seth's "Burn it Down" theme considering he's the cover star, it also doesn't have Emma's new theme and a few others.
Overall, I'd recommend it if you are an active wrestling fan, I don't see why not, it takes WWE 2K17, brings in graphical and gameplay improvements with an updated roster.

Oh wow, I never reviewed this game? Is it good? Well, do you want to make elaborate fantasy creatures and figures with highly detailed back stories to rule over fictional nations with origins in mythologies from all over the world and ultimately guide them on a path to supreme godhood over a randomly generated fantasy world full of unique cultures and other mythological figures vying for power?
Alternatively, do you want to make your avatar a "Freak Lord," name him "Rick James," and use him to continuously sacrifice virgins to create armies of freaks in the pursuit of the ultimate super freaks that will help lead Rick James to godhood (all literal things you can do, though not actually the most competetive strategy)?

Dominions 4 is a one of a kind Turn Based Strategy game. It requires users to get past a UI and graphics interface that can be counter-intuitive to modern gaming standards, but once you do players will find a rare gem of a game that has more variety, thematics, and the capacity to create stories than any other 4X on the market.
The game is fun as a single player experience, which is honestly where most of my time in game has come from, but it really shines if you can find others to play with. That said, the game is more interested in incorporating the great variety of factions, spells, equipment, and units that make each play through unique than it is on strict balancing, so it is worth noting that you want to be sure to find the right folks that fit your play style. From my experience, the community is usually a fairly positive one and I have generally had good experiences.
The price point throws a lot of folks off, which I respect, but I still say this is one that is worth the full price of admission. I would love to see some of the unique mechanics here, especially how battle resolution and preparation is handled, be incorporated in more games in the turn based strategy genre.

Steam needs to add a "neutral" review option already. I really WANT to reccommend the hell out of this game, but the PC port is so bad that it becomes really difficult to do so. So I'll just pick "yes" solely because the actual game itself is really awesome, but you're gonna have to potentially do a lot of manual installation of community-made packages that contain optional mods and numerous bugfixes if you want the best experience.
Not gonna spoil anything plot-wise, but this isn't some "GTA clone" as the drones have been parroting for years. The game is a wonderful combination of bats**t wackiness and grounded realism. Everything the game has to offer is wonderful so I won't get into it much, but instead I'll focus on the negatives of the PC port.
*This port wasn't done by Volition (the original devs), but CD Projekt (not CD Projekt Red) who really flubbed the port job.
*Has really terrible audio quality overall, it sounds like 64kbps mp3 quality, not even joking. This goes for every sound in the game. There was a community fix for this which fixes the radio stations at least, but everything else is still jacked up.
*Has odd CPU timing issues where on some machines the game will run multi-times faster than the normal 1x speed it should be running at, leading to disorientation and annoyance.
*Prone to random framedrops and fluctuations regardless of how good your rig is
*All multiplayer relied on Gamespy's servers to function -- now that Gamespy went under, the only way to enjoy multiplayer or co-op is via a VPN tunneling client of your choice, but even then it's not guaranteed to work. I tried and failed with a friend across two different VPN programs and we had zero success. Some people have this issue, there is no universal fix.
*Can randomly crash sometimes, of course.
Now the community patch, called "Gentlemen of the Row" indeed fixes many of these issues among many other game logic bugs and whatnot, as well as coming with a huge number of optional gameplay mods and content mods that add a large swath of new vehicles, clothing, animations, customization options, and more. Definitely get that if you want to play this. The CPU timing bug requires another fix which you can find via some rudimentary googling.
Hope this primer helped someone.

Now you might be wondering why I was about to
this game, obviously the main cause being one of the worst ports that I have ever experienced on PC, it is absolutely terrible to the point you can’t even fullscreen the game in 1080p, but (this is a complete game changer… literally) I wouldn’t run the game without a mod, this mod is called FAR and it's just a requirement. FAR fixes the most important problems that make
have really bad performance and also some stupid problems like the full screen. Anyway moving on from the port lets get to the
.
.
The FAR mod fixes most of the performance issues but the game still very rarely struggles to run on a smooth 60 FPS on
for me and I know other people struggle to achieve that constant 60 FPS as well. There is 2 reasons for that, firstly the game ain’t greatly optimized but for what it is it ain’t that bad, secondly… this game sometimes makes you question who on earth would of thought to put so much action into a single fight scene, like honestly I am extremely impressed that in most of the fights I actually keep the 60 FPS when there is literally a war zone going on in the game.
As
is a 2017 title you can’t say it stunning for its time, but you do have to keep in mind that this game was designed for the PlayStation 4 audience and not the PC (yeah I know it kinda sucks that you get nearly the same graphics as PS4). The game still looks great in my opinion, it definitely isn’t ugly and it really has its own personal beauty in its graphics.
Firstly I shall start with the Voice Acting, as you can obviously tell this is a Japanese game, and I actually can’t talk about the Japanese dubbing as I haven't actually played the game enough in Japanese to be able to judge it (also I can’t speak Japanese), the English dubbing though in my opinion is really good, the voices chosen for the characters really fit and the acting behind the dubbing is really professional and honestly enjoyable to listen as well as immersive.

Moving onto Music… Wow, just wow, I can say that the music is just outstanding in every aspect. Music in any game is a key feature, and it ain’t easy to give it character and an original feeling after so much has been already done in within the gaming industry, this game has hit a jackpot in its musical design, the way that the songs suit the situations, the way they transition and the way they just sound and feel while you are playing makes
soundtrack a true masterpiece on its own as it carries so much feeling and emotion with it, you can tell that these soundtracks were made not just for the purpose of the game but also to alone be significant enough to carry a story with them alone, the vocals to most being the strongest aspect.
This is probably gonna be the shortest part of this section as it will cover the Sound Effects. Vibrant, Contrasting and Lively is probably the best selection of words that I can use to describe the Sound Effects in
, they really stand out and to the experience as they are really crisp and well chosen.
One of the coolest customization mechanics in this game is definitely the chip system, at the beginning of the game you start off with like 32 “units of storage” in which you will already have your HUD and some other basic chips installed, you can remove and add different kinds of chips for different components of hud and different abilities as well as buffs and physical enhancements, the 32 units can be increased rather easily to its max capacity 128 pretty early on in the game.
There is a very large variety of weapons available in game and the good thing about them is that the majority of them are unique with their unique upgrades and perks but there could be some actual customization to them, you can only upgrade them and that's it. Another thing about the weapons is how you equip them, there a plenty of possibilities with equipping your weapons as it will actually create different attacks and combos which I found really cool and you will find out that some characters are better with different weapons equipped in different slots. Your Pod can be described as you personal canon and ultimate, it can shoot different kinds of things depending on its upgrades and also can perform a skill ability which is a bit like an rechargable ultimate, there over a dozen of those skills to find throughout the game and not all of them are actually offencive, some act as support and some get you around the battlefield faster, they are generally cool abilities that really can help in the chaos driven combat
has to offer.
There are cosmetic outfits in the game but they have no stat changing abilities, they are a cool touch and some are really fun to use… especially a certain one from the DLC ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°)
The Combat in this game is truly fantastic, anyone familiar with Bayonetta and even Devil May Cry will feel at home, it is really fast paced and relies heavily on dodging and dealing damage with all the things I listed above pretty much in a really smooth and stylish way, the animation overall in this game are fantastically animated and the movement of combat just seems to flow and it all looks nice and easy when you watch it but the moment you start to play you realise that this games combat, especially in boss fights is heavily reflex based and its absolute carnage. The

I think the best part of experiencing NieR:Automata for me is that I found another world I can just fall into. What I mean, is when I was younger I remember immediately after coming home from school, I'd turn on my Playstation and play games like Kingdom Hearts or Final Fantasy, day, after day, after day. It didn't matter that I had beaten the games a long time ago. It was just enough to plug myself into that universe. I loved having the option to grind to level 99, to hunt for materials to create the ultimate weapons, to unlock the hardest bosses. I welcomed the excuse, the opportunity, to return to that world. Sure, a lot of games did that, but they felt void, empty after the game was completed. Static. I had no urge to return. Not that that's bad in the slightest, but it's those games that linger in that way that really get to me.
Really the feeling of getting lost in these worlds is due to different factors, and the attachment I feel for N:A is far different than the attachment I feel towards the aforementioned game series. Let's see. Well, to get into some of those factors, why not start with the how the game actually plays?
The gameplay is a visual accomplishment in and of itself. And not only is it entrancing to watch 2B and company fight, but it feels satisfying. Combat can be as fast-paced or slow-paced, you can struggle or be OP, make it choppy, or make it a dance. Button mash, or create some nasty combos (granted, it would probably be hard to execute those in a lot of the combat situations). If one way doesn't fit your style, switch it up. The game does an out-of-the-ballpark, stellar job at leaving you in the dark in regards to figuring out how to do stuff, so experiment. Find out new stuff, new ways to do things. At least for me personally, experimenting's pretty fun.
Not only combat, but literally just moving around in-game is fun, I think. With the speeds that 2B and all can run at, it's a blast to just run around the map trying to keep up top speed while trying to land smooth jumps, leaping from building to building, branch to branch.
Personally, one of my favorite things to do in this game is to just grind away, going around fighting enemies in areas where some of my favorite music plays. It's super relaxing, and therapeutic in a way. Which leads me to:
The music in this game makes no effort to hide or blend in with a scene. It demands your attention. And it certainly deserves it. Although I had heard previously that the soundtrack was amazing, I wasn't expecting it to be as beautiful and mesmerizing as it was. There were quite a few moments where the atmosphere and the music collided so perfectly while I was playing that I had to stop and just take it all in and appreciate it. Other times I was engrossed in fighting, but even then, the coordination between the musical elements, the setting, the fighting effects, animations, it all just aligned so perfectly it's hard to ignore just how beautifully, and I don't mean just visually, everything was orchestrated.
And then there was the story, the oh so philosophical story. Truthfully, the story is actually one of the least-contributing factors as to why I love this game. Although I think it could have been executed better, I do love the story, and I definitely found myself to be thinking about it long after the (many) credits rolled. A flicker of a thought here and there. An itch. Finding myself having lain down in bed, staring up, thinking. It didn't leave my mind. And the game honestly does a good job at making you question things all throughout the playthrough.
Although this may not make a lot of sense now, it might later:
I've always found games to be an absolutely powerful art form, not something to be scoffed at. Sure, games can be light, brainless. Simple. But video games can and
have the ability to be hard-hitting and engrossing, meaningful and important. It can take the visual storytelling from movies, the written storytelling from books, the auditory storytelling from music, and, most of all, place you in control to experience it all first-hand. And I hope that, if you haven't already, you can experience NieR:Automata for yourself.

I ain't a butt-person; I'm overwhelmingly a boobs guy. But dayam, the "main" character 2B's voluptuous plump booty is mesmerizing. It's not even the typical jiggling you'd associate with a 3D model--her robot butts don't actually jiggle at all--but the way her cheeks, accentuated by her high-riding leotards, slide up and down sensuously as she move. Even though zooming out is more helpful, I always zoom camera up close in order to properly appreciate her enthralling runway catwalk (in high heels!) or awesome sanic dash. Heck, even climbing up or sliding down ladders with a low camera angle provide huge amount of PLOT.
And dem thighs, man. If you're into thighs, hers are T H I C C and glorious. Her high leggings squeezing out some plump synethic meat from her thighs... delicious. She's truly bringing Glory to Mankind.
Gameplay-wise, NieR: Automata is very forgiving if you want it to be. There's super EZ babby modo for kindergarteners and Chads (where you basically can't die unless you really go out of your way), but even in Normal mode, you can breeze through most fights by abusing Evade iFrame dodge spam and stacking in-game enhancements that become quite OP (shockwave, heal on hit, auto-regen, taunt + crits, counter, overclock bullet-time, etc). On Difficult and Very Difficult, you pretty much get one-shotted or two-shotted by even common enemies if you mess up your iFrame dodge, so as long as you don't abuse the OP in-game enhancements, that will be the challenging way to play for some of you Virgin masochists out there. The combat is fun, though the camera is something you'd have to wrestle with. There are also occasional parts where the game shifts into bullet-hell, side-scrolling, platforming, or puzzle modes; they are typically brief enough to feel refreshing instead of bothersome.
The visuals are superb. Beautiful post-apocalyptic environments. Aside from glorious robot butts and thighs, the combat animations and combo types for different weapon types are fluid and dazzling to watch. Enjoy dancing with Japanese steel folded 1000 times. Spears and knuckles are also entirely valid weapons to wield if swords and greatswords aren't your thing.
Other than the first protagonist 2B, there are two other playable characters in subsequent playthroughs (multiple playthroughs are required to unlock all routes/endings, but the game gradually unlocks QoL features that make subsequent playthroughs faster/easier). Remote-controlling enemies and "hacking" mini-games on the 2nd character provide a very different playstyle. While the 3rd character has a similar to playstyle to 2B, going full berserker glass-cannon mode is extremely fun.
The story is fine; jRPG philosophical stuff, so your mileage may vary. Many players will love it and write tl;dr essays analyzing the themes, but it's not 2deep4u to confuse casuals. What starts out as an "Us-vs-Them" war gradually shifts into an existential, self-finding quest and story about robot love. Throughout the first playthrough, the game drops both foreshadows and hints that lead up to the very nice TWEEST that show up in later playthroughs, though the backstory and explanation behind the twist (in the subsequent routes) didn't turn out to be entirely satisfactory for me. Still, the central characters and their relationships are a strong point of the game, and the additional playthroughs and extended routes peel back more layers to the story and enrich the world setting. Note that you do NOT need to play the first NieR, but you'll have greater appreciation for the connections and enjoy seeing returning characters.
I also enjoyed collecting all the joke endings. What happens when andoroids "unequip" their OS? What happens when androids eat fish? What happens when you initiate self-destruct in a space station?
AMAZING soundtrack. The first NieR Gestalt/Replicant's soundtrack was universally considered top-class, yet despite having such high expectations, I was blown away by NieR Automata's soundtrack and found it to be even better. Some of the gorgeous BGMs, upon triggering, compelled me stop playing for a while just to savor them. A few of the sentimental BGMs play only after completion of touching/heart-wrenching/bittersweet quests and will smack you right in the feels. The Japanese voice acting is spot-on; you can do English subtitle + Japanese voice to enjoy 2B's voice actress who voiced Misaka from Attack on Titans. Heck, even the English dub sounded pretty darn good if you aren't weeb.

My initial impressions are that the Steam Controller has some excellent potential, but a pretty steep learning curve, and still has a few bugs in it.
At this point, I'm absolutely loving the analog stick on it.
I've gotten spoiled by the ones on the Power A Mini controllers I use because the entire assembly is smaller than the ones on the official 360 controllers.
That give the stick a shorter physical throw, which improves the response I feel at my end.
This stick has that same smaller analog stick on it, but couples that with the ability to tailor the inner and outer dead zones, as well as setting the stick to perform an additional function, when it hits the end of travel.
The left track pad isn't nearly as good at controlling movement, which is why I think they were forced to add the analog stick.
The track pad does a good job as a clickable D-pad, or can be set up to do the D-pad functions on touch.
It can also be set as scroll wheels, for things like inventory management.
There is a "first touch equals center" function on it, so wherever your thumb lands on a given touch is "center" for that pad, until you let off it, and retouch it.
The ABXY buttons are a bit weird because they are so low on the controller, but the two-stage triggers, and finger buttons on the back can be mapped to those functions, so that's kind of a wash.
Using the two-stage triggers and back buttons allows you to use the right trackpad at the same time, which looks like it will finally give me control of the camera in Rocket League, but I'm still learning/tweaking that.
I did run into an issue using the dual-stage triggers on Rocket League, where setting the left one to do reverse on the analog portion, and handbrake on the full pull seems to send both signals when you hold full pull.
The car will start to handbrake, then keep handbraking while it backs up, causing a complete loss of control.
That could be operator error though, in the way I have it set up.
I played with several different modes on that function, but all of them exhibited this behavior.
The bumper buttons suck compared to my Power A, and Big Picture Mode doesn't seem to allow them to be forwarded to Teamspeak, where I usually use the right bumper to mute/unmute my microphone, so I can use voice activation when I want, but not leave it on all the time.
Like the trigger problem, that could just be me not setting it up properly yet.
I'll have to investigate that one further.
I haven't gotten the move functions to work properly for me yet.
I played with them a bit, right at the end of the night, but didn't make any real headway with them.
I'll leave that for later.
All-in-all, the things this controller can do are impressive.
I think it's definitely going to replace my Power A for most games.
I don't see it as a replacement for my mouse/keyboard because the precision just isn't there.
That could change over time, as I get more comfortable with configuring it.
I see it as a great addition to that though...once I figure it all out...and get used to it.
When you factor in modifier keys, the number of inputs available on the thing is astronomical for such a compact, handheld input device.

I don't really like leaving negative reviews for games or other products in general, especially not for those which work as intended. This review must therefore be an exception - I give this game a 3/5 for a first download and play, though replayability is zero, so from then I would give it a 0/5.
The (mostly) good:
The game runs well on my old (9 year) gaming laptop, and the music is fairly catchy if a little annoying. It's quick to download and get into the game, and easy to play.
The layout and menus are well put together and everything is smooth and seemless - the sort of game you could run on most modern devices with other things going on in the background (i.e. as the game description states - whilst a proper game downloads).
It's somewhat interesting in how it works and it's humerous - notably the game managers being references to popular culture, the use of outrageous amounts of money, and the free add ons.
The bad:
Nothing really happens - the game is just a counting program which you increase the levels of counting by clicking boxes. Though it's superficially more than that, I couldn't get past the pointlessness of what it is.
To summarise - I wanted to like it, but there just isn't enough to the game for me.
It looks to me like a mobile game, not really a game I would want to play on pc.

Paladins is a Overwatch genre game, so to say, which is a combination of Team Fortress 2, class-based FPS, and MOBAs ideas. Of course idea wasn't to clone that game, Hi-Rez studios wouldn't be able to develop game with assets so fast from the point of times when OW various gameplay or classes were revealed. I mean, some kinda-clones classes were already in 2015 closed beta before OW trailer reveals. But they surely took some ideas. anyway Androxus is totally Ripper ripoff, albeit a bit less edgy, and whole Top Play replays. But don't know, it's like with "Doom-clones". Everybody is welcome into genre as long as they try to be better or have unique features. Well, or DotA clones.
Think of Street Fighter 2. You don't discredit every other 1v1 fighting game for taking good ideas, now do you?
I am more wondering why it took so much time for TF2-killers to come out. It was lonely.
It came out in 2016 and was available on Steam. Calls itself Open Beta but the only excuse for that by this point would be how some heroes may get heavy reworks that would make mains sad.
Then again, they do say that they patched game out to be more similar. Closed Beta looks much more different, with huge maps and being able to ride horse anytime. I mean, I prefer more close and personal of TF2 style gameplay rather than battlefieldy sniping but the players of that version must have been feeling betrayed with such huge core design changes. Should have been a separate game.
I also like how this modern game runs much better on my laptop than Team Fortress 2 which is much older game. Shameful, Valve, shameful.
As for F2P, from gameplay standpoint you can use in-game recourses to unlock champions and "card", that change hero stats somewhat and such. Latter one isn't grindy to unlock and you already get starting full set of them. Like, they are very cheap with in-game recources. So it's all cool.
It does however use Easy-Anti-Cheat or something, hum.
As for what makes this one unique in the genre? Well, indeed, it's close to Overwatch. But it has Pip the Fennec Fox. Healer, has arcing bomb weapon, increased jumping ability, handsome. Case closed, Paladins win.
Hum, or was that "Fennek Fox" in English? It also has Fernando the knight with flamethrower that is too hot for anybody and shields, so it's cool.
Ah, yea, and other things. You got various heroes. Each has it's own primary attack and then 3 whatever-abilities. There is no mana concept or ammo, just cooldowns. And of course, Ultimate ability which takes time and effort to feed it up to 100%. There is good TF2 shooting fun, aiming is forgiving here, it's not Counter-Strike. Thankfully. 5v5, can't change hero once match starts. Don't know about competitive, but in casual you don't see what another team picked until it all gets locked down. Payload and single Control Point modes combinations. I think it could use more of TF2-style overtime in more modes. And yep, health regenerates when you don't take damage for a while, going away from action. Some peeps think it's casualization but I say it design that calls for champions who are able to catch up and finish people up before they escape.
Once the match starts it shows some more unique features, mostly taken from MOBAs. First, there is a card system. No worries, when I say "cards" I don't mean those awful capitalist system trading-or-not card games, it mostly means just stats changes or abilities changes. Such as healing when your sentry is destroyed a bit. There are 3 legendary cards, that change hero stats enough to differinate play styles somewhat, just pick one at the start of match. You can't change cards. Then you pick one of deck of normal cards that you customize from main menu. In normal deck you pick one of 5 cards and then you got 7 points to level em up, one card having up to 4 level. Sadly, it's not all that balanced yet. For example, Barik needs some cards that will help his sentries health otherwise it's pointless to play as him. Can't change normal cards during match either. It's mostly something you choose once you see composition of your team and enemy team.
Another thing that helps you to counter composition of teams now that you know what heroes are on each team is shop system. Yep, like in MOBAs you get credits during gameplay and even more if you do your class's job. Then you get to buy one item from 4 categories each having 4 items. Well, those are passive things. Unlike MOBAs however it's not "+2 agility, -1 whatever, intellegence", it's more clear "gain health on hit" or "bonus damage against shield" so it's not overcomplicated for no reason. Thus I highly recommend to turn off auto-purchase off, you can figure these out rather quickly.
Oh yea, and when you spawn you ride the horse so you can arrive to hot action faster.
Though the thing I don't like is finding out how they removed some skill-shots since 2016. Such as Fernando's fireball doing more damage the more enemies it passes through. Or Barik doing more damage with shotgun to enemies that turret is currently aiming at. Ah well, it's not done yet, will see where it will go. After all, I kinda liked game in current state, having just played now. This is what I dig.
Also, cool graphics. Music is fine, a bit too generic, not something I care at all. I wish music in modern games were much better.
But yea. It's totally cool. My new dig. But shall see where they will lead the game to.

I have no idea just how many hours over the years i've sunk into this game. (I bought it on Desura all those years ago, so my steam hours aren't at all accurate)
In short; this game is big. There are dozens of different races/factions - 'nations' - spilt accross 3 eras. There are hundreds of spells, units and items to learn.
The depth of this game is absolutely incredible, each individual soldier has a multitude of individual stats, each armour piece and weapon listed seperately. It matters in this game too, because if your soldier has a shield they're less likely to die to non-magic missiles for example. It goes further than that, what is that shield made of? If its metal there are spells which can cause it to rust and thus be useless.
Each of the nations is based off real-world mythology, from Norse and Arthurian Legend to Japanese Goblins and Devas. There are Vampires and Giants, Elves and Beastmen, even the otherworldly horrors of the deep sea. Most of the nations play on land, but some sit in the water, and others move easily between the two.
I mentioned spells, well the game has a stupid number. I have no idea just how many. These are broken up between schools, and then each spell has alignments (fire, earth, death etc) which govern which of the various mages in the game can cast what (in laymans terms.)
This review of course does not do this depth justice. If you're at all interested in this game, go what a few lets plays on youtube. PERFORMANCE ISSUE UPDATE (LOW FPS)
Updating from my first review.  Ive now managed to solve my low fps problem which made the game unplayable.
For those specifically playing on latop devices, in the nvidia graphics control panel, click on manage 3d settings, then under prefered graphics processor, click on 'high performance nvidia processor'.  WWE 2K18 may not automatcaly run on your GPU, rather your CPU with the intergrated graphics chip, which will give you a very poor game performance.  Once you quit the  game, go back into the nvidia control panel and then reslect 'auto-select' so that the laptop will run back to normal.
This has solved my oringinal performance issues and the game now plays very well. All in all a  good game. Havent played a WWE game since WWE'14.  Fun and enjoybale.  Hope this helps anyone with similar  performance issues that i had.

Brilliant game. While the trailers may make it seem that Volition doesn't take story or character seriously, Saints Row 2 is just a great game overall. And, yeah, the story isn't the strong point, but this ain't no drama with loads of dialog. The protagonist doesn't have time for that. Instead, you'll mostly find yourself in gun fights, helicopter fights, boat fights, fist fights, etc, while also taking over the city and taking back your territory.
Set about five years after Saints Row 1, the protagonist wakes up from their coma and you get to re-imagine him/her due to their severe burns from the explosion at the end of the first game. I opted for a British male so from this point on, I'm referring to the protagonist as a he. When he wakes up, he realizes he's in jail and immediately remembers why. You break out with Carlos who joins your gang later as a Lt. The Boss (protagonist) realizes that he has to become the leader of the 3rd Street Saints and decides to free Johnny Gat during his trial because of all the killing he did the first game. The two of you recruit three Lts, Shaundi, Pierce, and Carlos, and from there, you start to take over Stillwater, one district/mission at a time.
What's truly remarkable about this sequel is the cinematic direction they chose with the cut scenes. The cut scenes are simply amazing and I even went ahead and watched some of them twice, just because they were that great. The writing is pretty good, and there are 80000 lines of dialog, over twice from the first game. The protagonist speaks in this one, giving him a more rounded personality versus being a drone. The overall story is nice, and they were aiming for hyper realism, as in over the top, bizarre action. There are activities on the side, usually street racing, causing chaos, trail blazing, insurance fraud, etc, which is definitely a lot more fun than bowling with your cousin.
On the tech side, the graphics are decent. The PC port isn't amazing, but it's functional and you're actually able to play it. Can't say the same about GTA IV. Saints Row 2, being a 2008 release from a lesser known company, is definitely not a  great looking game, but the overall city design and character design, and how much customization there is makes up for it. The devs definitely put a lot of thought in the overall feel of the game. I really enjoyed making money and buying cribs, building an empire, more or less.

The Ultimate Match edition of King of Fighters '98 is the best in home experience that you can have with this fighter outside of buying a Neo Geo. The roster is rather large and includes a good number of exclusive characters, so you'll have a lot of teams to experiment to your liking. While I feel that the series started strongly at '94, '98 is the first King of Fighters that I felt become the powerhouse that most players remember today, with a robust yet easy to pick up system and the presentation and art having a dramatic lift from previous iterations. It also adopted the Dream Match mainstay, expanding from SNK series like Fatal Fury and Art of Fighting, while deliving deeper into more obscure franchises like Psycho Soldier and Ikari Warriors. This version also has the updated Ultimate Match that has returning cast like Geese Howard while also giving the option of playing a Neo Geo rom of the original version of The King of Fighters '98 for the purists.
The only issue is a mainstay in most SNK ports, being that the netplay is bad. While the connections are up in the air, it's hard to even find a decent match online. Sadly, there is not a large community currently available, so unless you have a group of friends, it's best to go in expecting not to get much mileage out of the online play.
Nearly 2 decades later, The King of Fighters '98 still holds up as a very competant fighter and is enjoyable to go back to every now and then. While I recommend The King of Fighters XIII as the best overall representation and evolution of the series, '98 is still a very well made game and worth checking out to see the roots of SNK's most well known fighting franchise.

Who should buy this game?
You are a masochist regarding first person shooters.
You are a Red Orchestra 2 fan.
You are looking for a shooter that isn't as arcade as Call of Duty or Battlefield but is also not a military simulator like Arma or Squad.
You like the setting of the Vietnam War (Including lots and lots of Jungle).
You don't mind a game without single player content.
What you should expect?
1. You will die a lot and thats not only true for Rookies.
2. Asymetrical gameplay. For exampel: The US Squadleader is a moving spawning point on the map. If he dies you will be spawned further away from the frontline. The VC Squadleader can dig a tunnel that  serves as  a spawning point. (There are limitations to the tunnel digging that make it frustrating to find a suitable spot for a tunnel).
(Balancing asymetrical gameplay is very difficult and it will never be fair 100%)
3. Somewhat teamplay. In a best case szenario the commander coordinates the battle with his team and the majority does what he says. (it always gets better if people know each other)
4. A mostly friendly community.
5. NAPALM Strikes and really cool looking Artillery explosions XD.
6. Mostly solid shooter gameplay. (picking the right item from your kit is a bit clumbsy in the beginning.) You will get the hang of it. :)
I definetly recommend the game.

After playing Red Orchestra: 2, I was expecting another masterpiece that simulated the horrors and feeling of war. What I got instead was Rising Storm 2. Rising Storm 2 takes all of the aspects that made Red Orchestra 2 an amazing game, and numbs them down to the point that they don't matter. Nobody sticks with their squads, because the game seems to encourage (if not just allow) "running and gunning". This could easily be fixed through Realism mode, but for some reason, Realism mode didn't make it's way into RS2 either. There are also plenty of crippling bugs that make this game a pain to play, some of them being broken damage models (most noticeable on the SVD, wherein it doesn't do damage), and just buggy and half-complete gunplay.
This game was an obvious attempt to grab the Red Orchestra fans' money, as they capitalized on their previous success, only to deliver a very sub-par and dissappointing experience.
TL;DR: If you enjoyed Red Orchestra 2, You'll despise this game.

This fantastic game is a hallmark of tactical realism following RO2 and Arma. I can't say I've been there, but from impressions alone, the experience has been both horrifying and awe inspiring. With its minimalistic UI, one shot kills, wall penetration, bullet over penetration, screaming, burning, moaning, whimpering, face spiking (punji traps), and it's UNFORGIVING artillery, this IS one SOLID game. It's new, but the Tripwire Interactive gang knows how to support and carry this game on just like its predecessor Red Orchestra 2.
One more note: If you like to RUN & GUN, the artillery and riflemen with 100+m precision will mercilessly beat it out of you. It will NEVER forget to remind you that you're NOT the plot armor wearing protagonist. Napalm and White Phosphorous will burn you, Rockets and Artillery will tear you apart, and you will barely comprehend the brief flash in the distance before the bullet takes you down. Stick with your teammates, use your smoke, keep supressing fire, and you will be victorious.

One thing to note is that this is not like CoD or Battlefield, so be wary before buying it. Overall, a really fun game with interactive (hence tripwire interactive) and great devs, who give out free content updates (new factions, weapons, cosmetics, maps, etc) to a pretty great community. I recommend highly you at least try this out.

I got my controller yesterday, Nov. 10. Right on time. I've had it for less than 24 hours, and i'm already in love with it.
Some Pros:
1. Touchpads are really nice. The right one works like a trackball, while the left one works like a scroller, but can be used as a d-pad as well.
2. It feels amazing in your hands. I know, I know, it looks kinda funny and bulky. But it was designed with comfort in mind, and you'll be able to tell that right out of the box.
3. Super configurable. Steam's big picture mode allows you to create your own controller layouts, choose a preset layout, or download layouts for the game you're in straight from the steam community. And all of this can be done in just a few easy steps.
4) The back triggers are pretty nice, as well as the dual stage triggers on the top.
5. You can use this controller wired or wireless.
6. Works as a fully functioning mouse when you turn it on.
7. Is godlike for FPS games (and Portal omg) since the trackpad on the right can be configured for precise aiming.
Just a few cons:
1) it might take you a little bit of time to find the layout you want. It'll be worth it though.
2) the haptic feedback might take some getting used to.
Other things:
1. It does take 2 AA batteries. Not sure how the battery consumption will be, but i'll update on that after I spend some more time with it.
2. If you, like me, have put a ton of hours into Rocket League with Mouse/Keyboard, chances are, your experience with this controller in the game will be worse than expected. Had I waited for the controller, my experience would probably have been better for this game.
Overall, I absolutely love this thing, and I highly recommend buying it. It will change the way you play steam games forever. Thank you, Valve, for making such an amazing controller.

That pretty much sums up this game. I haven't yet tested the multiplayer (I'm still far too new to have a chance against more experienced players), but from playing several games against AI I can already tell that this is just the kind of game I have wanted to play for a very long time.
For those who know Heroes of Might and Magic this game looks familiar from the beginning, but turns out to be quite different in the long run. As in HoMaM armies need commanders to lead them around the map, and most spells are cast by commanders. Another similarity is that nations and units are based on various mythologies.
What differs is how strategic the games feel. Dominions is mainly played on the world map, which is grouped into provinces. The player has to manage owned provinces (prepare defense, use commanders to construct buildings, etc.) to keep a steady income of resources and gold, and to be prepared should an enemy try to attack. On the other hand one can often choose one of multiple provinces to attack an enemy, and one has to scout for those that are not well prepared. This makes the player feel a bit less "directly involved" than Heroes of Might and Magic does, but on the other side one feels more "in control". What further contributes to this is that one needs a lot of commanders, as some of them will be busy building or researching, without ever leading an army.
What also makes this game stand out is the incredible depth of simulation. A lot of things can happen in Dominions, and all of them have elaborate rules. I think it's enough to say that the manual has over 450 pages (mostly tables) to demonstrate how detailed this game is.
Anyhow, it's one of the best turn-based strategy games I've played up to now.

WWE 2K18 is the fifth installment of the WWE 2K series that began with WWE 2K14. It is also the first WWE 2K game that released its PC version at the same time with the console versions. Here's my experience so far.
GAMEPLAY: Apart from being able to carry opponents in 4 different styles, not much has improved since last year. Like most yearly sports games, WWE 2K18 ends up taking another baby step towards improving the gameplay. Glad they increased the max amount of allowed wrestlers from 6 to 8 in this year.
CREATION: This deserves its own column because it's a blast. You can create your superstar, your move set, your entrance, your victory pose, your arena, your championship and even your titantron video. It's really appreciated. Hopefully we'll see the return of Create-a-Finisher soon.
MYPLAYER: Some people would argue that this is basically grind mode and I cannot blame them. Everything is VC-locked or hidden behind loot crates. No microtransactions though, and you can rack up 1000 VC in around 4-5 matches. Along with sidequests, it should be easy to rack up VC. You can usually choose if you want to run-in, cut a promo or have a normal match, so that's good. Unfortunately the promo engine, while it's good, is not what you would expect from a next-gen game.
That was the review for now. I'll have a look at WWE Universe and then complete the review. For now though, maybe wait for sale.

Saw this game on the Humble Store for $0.99, so I decided to try it out. Do not buy this game at full price.
Pros:
+ The sound effects ( most notably the hit sounds ) are pretty nostalgic if you grew up with old martial arts action movies.
+ Decent roster size.
Cons:
- The hitboxes are extremely inaccurate. Sometimes I'll be hitting my opponent with an attack when they're clearly not in range of it.
- The controls feel very clunky. They're often unresponsive. It's really hard to execute a grab attack, which usually requires you to press two buttons at once. Most of the time it just doesn't work.
- The background noises are terrible. The volume of the ambient noise for some of the stages are somehow not adjustable, so no matter what your SFX and Music options are set to, you'll still be hearing the background noise. Not to mention that the tracks are looped badly. You can hear the abrupt cut of the tracks from the end to the beginning when the loop goes around.
- The AI isn't very good. There isn't any defensive options other than blocking, so it's really easy to lock down your opponent with spamming combos.
- The game is supposedly abandoned when there is clearly a lot things that could've been fixed or improved. The devs have went to work on a similar game called "Shaolin vs Wutang".
------------------------------
Overall, the game is just a mess. The controls are awkward, unresponsive, and clunky. The sound design for the most part is amateurish and lazy. It could've been a fun game, but unfortunately it just doesn't hold up. Please save your money and do NOT spend $10 on this game.

don't let my steam "hours played" metric deceive you: KOF 98 is a game I played for 2-3 hours a day, every day, for months after I first got my hands on it. It was a game with 56 playable characters -a ridiculous amount at the time, even more so today - and I made it my business to get to know them all. By the end I could play a team at random and have a decent chance at pulling out a victory against my friends.
KOF 98 Ultimate Match takes that core gem, that timeless classic, and throws in even more characters. So now there's no need to ask about your fav because your fav is RETROACTIVELY IN THE GAME (unless your fav is K9999, sorry)
I admit I'm smitten and old and my perspective is hardly universal: if you're new to KOF or fighting games in general, this is a lot to absorb. And the game's tutorials/challenges are terrible at explaining just what the hell is going on or what you need to learn. But if you can find your way into this game it can give you an infinite amount of replayability. And SNK packed this game with so many colorful personalities that I promise you that you'll fall in love with at least one character who may or may not be named Yamazaki.
This game deserves the "Game Within a Game" award for having the original KOF98 within it. And people tend to play the original over 98UM anyway.

This fantastic game is a hallmark of tactical realism following RO2 and Arma. I can't say I've been there, but from impressions alone, the experience has been both horrifying and awe inspiring. With its minimalistic UI, one shot kills, wall penetration, bullet over penetration, screaming, burning, moaning, whimpering, face spiking (punji traps), and it's UNFORGIVING artillery, this IS one SOLID game. It's new, but the Tripwire Interactive gang knows how to support and carry this game on just like its predecessor Red Orchestra 2.
One more note: If you like to RUN & GUN, the artillery and riflemen with 100+m precision will mercilessly beat it out of you. It will NEVER forget to remind you that you're NOT the plot armor wearing protagonist. Napalm and White Phosphorous will burn you, Rockets and Artillery will tear you apart, and you will barely comprehend the brief flash in the distance before the bullet takes you down. Stick with your teammates, use your smoke, keep supressing fire, and you will be victorious.

I loved the previous games, and this one is just as good, although a little more arcadey and fast paced. You'll still get your fair share of intense moments though, whether it be an F4 Phantom flying over with two canisters of napalm to burn out the VC, or watching your squadmate clutching his chest on the ground before staying still and not uttering another word after being shot in the chest.
One thing to note is that this is not like CoD or Battlefield, so be wary before buying it. Overall, a really fun game with interactive (hence tripwire interactive) and great devs, who give out free content updates (new factions, weapons, cosmetics, maps, etc) to a pretty great community. I recommend highly you at least try this out.

Now you might be wondering why I was about to
this game, obviously the main cause being one of the worst ports that I have ever experienced on PC, it is absolutely terrible to the point you can’t even fullscreen the game in 1080p, but (this is a complete game changer… literally) I wouldn’t run the game without a mod, this mod is called FAR and it's just a requirement. FAR fixes the most important problems that make
have really bad performance and also some stupid problems like the full screen. Anyway moving on from the port lets get to the
.
.
The FAR mod fixes most of the performance issues but the game still very rarely struggles to run on a smooth 60 FPS on
for me and I know other people struggle to achieve that constant 60 FPS as well. There is 2 reasons for that, firstly the game ain’t greatly optimized but for what it is it ain’t that bad, secondly… this game sometimes makes you question who on earth would of thought to put so much action into a single fight scene, like honestly I am extremely impressed that in most of the fights I actually keep the 60 FPS when there is literally a war zone going on in the game.
As
is a 2017 title you can’t say it stunning for its time, but you do have to keep in mind that this game was designed for the PlayStation 4 audience and not the PC (yeah I know it kinda sucks that you get nearly the same graphics as PS4). The game still looks great in my opinion, it definitely isn’t ugly and it really has its own personal beauty in its graphics.
Firstly I shall start with the Voice Acting, as you can obviously tell this is a Japanese game, and I actually can’t talk about the Japanese dubbing as I haven't actually played the game enough in Japanese to be able to judge it (also I can’t speak Japanese), the English dubbing though in my opinion is really good, the voices chosen for the characters really fit and the acting behind the dubbing is really professional and honestly enjoyable to listen as well as immersive.

Moving onto Music… Wow, just wow, I can say that the music is just outstanding in every aspect. Music in any game is a key feature, and it ain’t easy to give it character and an original feeling after so much has been already done in within the gaming industry, this game has hit a jackpot in its musical design, the way that the songs suit the situations, the way they transition and the way they just sound and feel while you are playing makes
soundtrack a true masterpiece on its own as it carries so much feeling and emotion with it, you can tell that these soundtracks were made not just for the purpose of the game but also to alone be significant enough to carry a story with them alone, the vocals to most being the strongest aspect.
This is probably gonna be the shortest part of this section as it will cover the Sound Effects. Vibrant, Contrasting and Lively is probably the best selection of words that I can use to describe the Sound Effects in
, they really stand out and to the experience as they are really crisp and well chosen.
One of the coolest customization mechanics in this game is definitely the chip system, at the beginning of the game you start off with like 32 “units of storage” in which you will already have your HUD and some other basic chips installed, you can remove and add different kinds of chips for different components of hud and different abilities as well as buffs and physical enhancements, the 32 units can be increased rather easily to its max capacity 128 pretty early on in the game.
There is a very large variety of weapons available in game and the good thing about them is that the majority of them are unique with their unique upgrades and perks but there could be some actual customization to them, you can only upgrade them and that's it. Another thing about the weapons is how you equip them, there a plenty of possibilities with equipping your weapons as it will actually create different attacks and combos which I found really cool and you will find out that some characters are better with different weapons equipped in different slots. Your Pod can be described as you personal canon and ultimate, it can shoot different kinds of things depending on its upgrades and also can perform a skill ability which is a bit like an rechargable ultimate, there over a dozen of those skills to find throughout the game and not all of them are actually offencive, some act as support and some get you around the battlefield faster, they are generally cool abilities that really can help in the chaos driven combat
has to offer.
There are cosmetic outfits in the game but they have no stat changing abilities, they are a cool touch and some are really fun to use… especially a certain one from the DLC ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°)
The Combat in this game is truly fantastic, anyone familiar with Bayonetta and even Devil May Cry will feel at home, it is really fast paced and relies heavily on dodging and dealing damage with all the things I listed above pretty much in a really smooth and stylish way, the animation overall in this game are fantastically animated and the movement of combat just seems to flow and it all looks nice and easy when you watch it but the moment you start to play you realise that this games combat, especially in boss fights is heavily reflex based and its absolute carnage. The
different characters that you get to play as in this game all have a very different combat style and you have to use their specialities to your advantage if you don't want to struggle on higher difficulties as the enemies, especially in the end game can really smack you in the face. The combat is entertaining and even after 85 hours I still find it fun and not at all boring, a perfectly executed combo with some great dodging will get you really far in this game and damn you will be doing it in style.
I really can’t say much in this section as I don’t want to ruin or spoil anything, listen and read everything because even weapons have background stories in this game not mentioning the amount of items and archives you will find throughout the game that will help you understand what is going on and what happened in the previous
game. The story written by Yoko Taro will honestly drive you through a roller coaster of emotion and surprises while at all times you will be questioning life, existence and what is actually real. This game managed to make me cry like 3 times, and I mean proper cry so I must say that if you like a jaw dropping and really gripping story then you will really enjoy this little gem. I guess I can tag along the astonishing attention to detail that this game got  just perfectly.
Can you not tell by the length of this review… It deserves GOTY in my opinion for so many reasons and this is probably the best money for content game that I ever bought.
is a 2017 masterpiece of a game that will be overlooked by many. I want to thank PlatinumGames, Square Enix and Yoko Taro for allowing me to have this experience and cry my eyes out.

I think the best part of experiencing NieR:Automata for me is that I found another world I can just fall into. What I mean, is when I was younger I remember immediately after coming home from school, I'd turn on my Playstation and play games like Kingdom Hearts or Final Fantasy, day, after day, after day. It didn't matter that I had beaten the games a long time ago. It was just enough to plug myself into that universe. I loved having the option to grind to level 99, to hunt for materials to create the ultimate weapons, to unlock the hardest bosses. I welcomed the excuse, the opportunity, to return to that world. Sure, a lot of games did that, but they felt void, empty after the game was completed. Static. I had no urge to return. Not that that's bad in the slightest, but it's those games that linger in that way that really get to me.
Really the feeling of getting lost in these worlds is due to different factors, and the attachment I feel for N:A is far different than the attachment I feel towards the aforementioned game series. Let's see. Well, to get into some of those factors, why not start with the how the game actually plays?
The gameplay is a visual accomplishment in and of itself. And not only is it entrancing to watch 2B and company fight, but it feels satisfying. Combat can be as fast-paced or slow-paced, you can struggle or be OP, make it choppy, or make it a dance. Button mash, or create some nasty combos (granted, it would probably be hard to execute those in a lot of the combat situations). If one way doesn't fit your style, switch it up. The game does an out-of-the-ballpark, stellar job at leaving you in the dark in regards to figuring out how to do stuff, so experiment. Find out new stuff, new ways to do things. At least for me personally, experimenting's pretty fun.
Not only combat, but literally just moving around in-game is fun, I think. With the speeds that 2B and all can run at, it's a blast to just run around the map trying to keep up top speed while trying to land smooth jumps, leaping from building to building, branch to branch.
Personally, one of my favorite things to do in this game is to just grind away, going around fighting enemies in areas where some of my favorite music plays. It's super relaxing, and therapeutic in a way. Which leads me to:
The music in this game makes no effort to hide or blend in with a scene. It demands your attention. And it certainly deserves it. Although I had heard previously that the soundtrack was amazing, I wasn't expecting it to be as beautiful and mesmerizing as it was. There were quite a few moments where the atmosphere and the music collided so perfectly while I was playing that I had to stop and just take it all in and appreciate it. Other times I was engrossed in fighting, but even then, the coordination between the musical elements, the setting, the fighting effects, animations, it all just aligned so perfectly it's hard to ignore just how beautifully, and I don't mean just visually, everything was orchestrated.
And then there was the story, the oh so philosophical story. Truthfully, the story is actually one of the least-contributing factors as to why I love this game. Although I think it could have been executed better, I do love the story, and I definitely found myself to be thinking about it long after the (many) credits rolled. A flicker of a thought here and there. An itch. Finding myself having lain down in bed, staring up, thinking. It didn't leave my mind. And the game honestly does a good job at making you question things all throughout the playthrough.
Although this may not make a lot of sense now, it might later:
I've always found games to be an absolutely powerful art form, not something to be scoffed at. Sure, games can be light, brainless. Simple. But video games can and
have the ability to be hard-hitting and engrossing, meaningful and important. It can take the visual storytelling from movies, the written storytelling from books, the auditory storytelling from music, and, most of all, place you in control to experience it all first-hand. And I hope that, if you haven't already, you can experience NieR:Automata for yourself.

I ain't a butt-person; I'm overwhelmingly a boobs guy. But dayam, the "main" character 2B's voluptuous plump booty is mesmerizing. It's not even the typical jiggling you'd associate with a 3D model--her robot butts don't actually jiggle at all--but the way her cheeks, accentuated by her high-riding leotards, slide up and down sensuously as she move. Even though zooming out is more helpful, I always zoom camera up close in order to properly appreciate her enthralling runway catwalk (in high heels!) or awesome sanic dash. Heck, even climbing up or sliding down ladders with a low camera angle provide huge amount of PLOT.
And dem thighs, man. If you're into thighs, hers are T H I C C and glorious. Her high leggings squeezing out some plump synethic meat from her thighs... delicious. She's truly bringing Glory to Mankind.
Gameplay-wise, NieR: Automata is very forgiving if you want it to be. There's super EZ babby modo for kindergarteners and Chads (where you basically can't die unless you really go out of your way), but even in Normal mode, you can breeze through most fights by abusing Evade iFrame dodge spam and stacking in-game enhancements that become quite OP (shockwave, heal on hit, auto-regen, taunt + crits, counter, overclock bullet-time, etc). On Difficult and Very Difficult, you pretty much get one-shotted or two-shotted by even common enemies if you mess up your iFrame dodge, so as long as you don't abuse the OP in-game enhancements, that will be the challenging way to play for some of you Virgin masochists out there. The combat is fun, though the camera is something you'd have to wrestle with. There are also occasional parts where the game shifts into bullet-hell, side-scrolling, platforming, or puzzle modes; they are typically brief enough to feel refreshing instead of bothersome.
The visuals are superb. Beautiful post-apocalyptic environments. Aside from glorious robot butts and thighs, the combat animations and combo types for different weapon types are fluid and dazzling to watch. Enjoy dancing with Japanese steel folded 1000 times. Spears and knuckles are also entirely valid weapons to wield if swords and greatswords aren't your thing.
Other than the first protagonist 2B, there are two other playable characters in subsequent playthroughs (multiple playthroughs are required to unlock all routes/endings, but the game gradually unlocks QoL features that make subsequent playthroughs faster/easier). Remote-controlling enemies and "hacking" mini-games on the 2nd character provide a very different playstyle. While the 3rd character has a similar to playstyle to 2B, going full berserker glass-cannon mode is extremely fun.
The story is fine; jRPG philosophical stuff, so your mileage may vary. Many players will love it and write tl;dr essays analyzing the themes, but it's not 2deep4u to confuse casuals. What starts out as an "Us-vs-Them" war gradually shifts into an existential, self-finding quest and story about robot love. Throughout the first playthrough, the game drops both foreshadows and hints that lead up to the very nice TWEEST that show up in later playthroughs, though the backstory and explanation behind the twist (in the subsequent routes) didn't turn out to be entirely satisfactory for me. Still, the central characters and their relationships are a strong point of the game, and the additional playthroughs and extended routes peel back more layers to the story and enrich the world setting. Note that you do NOT need to play the first NieR, but you'll have greater appreciation for the connections and enjoy seeing returning characters.
I also enjoyed collecting all the joke endings. What happens when andoroids "unequip" their OS? What happens when androids eat fish? What happens when you initiate self-destruct in a space station?
AMAZING soundtrack. The first NieR Gestalt/Replicant's soundtrack was universally considered top-class, yet despite having such high expectations, I was blown away by NieR Automata's soundtrack and found it to be even better. Some of the gorgeous BGMs, upon triggering, compelled me stop playing for a while just to savor them. A few of the sentimental BGMs play only after completion of touching/heart-wrenching/bittersweet quests and will smack you right in the feels. The Japanese voice acting is spot-on; you can do English subtitle + Japanese voice to enjoy 2B's voice actress who voiced Misaka from Attack on Titans. Heck, even the English dub sounded pretty darn good if you aren't weeb.
Controls are fine IF AND ONLY IF you use a controller. I love KB+M; if I could, I'd much rather play most console games with KB+M (as long as genre suitable). That said, don't even bother with KB+M in this PC port. Unless you use 3rd party methods to get around the problem, native KB+M is practically unplayable because of the way Evade is default hard-mapped. I strongly, strongly recommend using a controller.

This game is a true gem. But undeniable it is also a very niche game. I hope with this review i can help you in your decision if you should buy this game or not.
Lets start with the obvious stuff: the negative.
- the graphics are the worstest graphics i have ever seen in a game. Like in every game you get used to it, and im still happy that at least every differnet unit has their own little picture, from which you can set them apart, but besides this, the graphic is very unsatisfying.
-its very hard to get in. To play the tutorial (which is basicly a 1v1 game against a very weak AI) you have to print a 400 pages manual (or at least the tutorial part of it) so that you can follow the steps is it and have the chance to slowly understand what to do and how to play.
-The AI is not very smart and in the Single player game their is no diplomacy option which means that after the AI or you have declared war to each other, their will be war until the end.
So basicly what is the problem with the game is the very poor presentation and its very hard to get into it. Their will be no feelings of success in the first hours so i can totally understand if someone wants to give it a try, buyed it on steam and then refund it after two hours because in this short time he did not get any fun at all.
But if you can overlook the presentation here are the reasons, why in my opinion this game is such a wounderful one.
- The scale: This game offers 100 different nations, everyone with a unique backstory based on ancient tales i dont know how many hundret gods, hundret of spells 1000 of units...you name it. The scale of this game is immense and if you belong to the kind of persons who always wants to try new things out, then this game will make you happy.
-With the huge scale their also comes: tactics! While the balance of so many nations and spells+ unitcombinations may not be perfect for hard core players who wants to play the best way possibile, since their may be some nations that are just stronger if you play them right, then other nations, but for a more "casual" player the amound of possible tactics that you can develop and try to outplay the opponent are immense!
-the community: While this game is a very niche game, with only a few sells, the community is still very active, and it is way more likely to get help if you have a question in this game, then in even the most tripple A games. The community members are as far as i can say very friendly, and since they are so active you also shoudlnt get to many problems in creating or joining a Multiplayer Game.
- The Multiplayer: To be honest i have to admit, that while i like MP games, and i like strategie games...i never played a round based mulitplayer game besides Civ5 before. To long are the games, to stressfull the games, so i never enjoyed playing in Multiplayer. But in this game the multiplayer part is the true way-to-play of dominions 4...and gives me the best multiplayer experience i have ever seen in a game!
The biggest reason is: the free diplomacy. (together with the awesome community) Because while the most games have very "forced" diplomacy, which means if you make a non aggression pact you are just unable to invade the opponents lands until this contract is active, and if you give someone in a trade 500 gold for 10 magic swords you get instantly the 10 swords.
In dominions 4 the diplomacy has no strict limitations, and is very based on the trust you develop with the other players. Which means that you write real messages to them and ask them for stuff like a trade deal or a non aggression pact and they can write you one thing...and do something totally different.
So you can for example make a non aggression pact for 2 years, and all went well but then suddely, when your army is on the other side of the world, your "ally" betrays you since he have diplomacy against you which you dont know and invades your lands, you can give him 1000 gold for magic items that he dont send you and stuff like this.
So you have to figure out in the game itself how you should punish such untrustful diplomacy. Because you have to think: Can i really trust this player who have already broken a non aggression pact against his other neighbor? Do i support the other player who claimed that he was betrayed from his "ally"...or is this player just tries to trick you into a war?
From this open diplomacy so many intense "game-of-thrones" moments happens, and it really gives you the feeling of an emperor of your nation who has to find out his best way to get more power. Will you betray your weak ally to get his lands, knowing that this will hurt your reputation, and will make further diplomacy harder? Will you play honorable and dont attack a nation that has a non aggresion pact with you, while it is weakend from a war against a other nation? To risk that this nation will overcome your nation, if you give it enough time to regain its power?
This open diplomacy is of course a very risky option, since when you have the "wrong" players in your game that just dont communicate with you what so ever and start attacking you for no reason without any messages, this will really harm the fun that you get from this game, but thanks to the awesome community, most of the players i have seen so far are more then willing to "roleplay" the diplomacy which leads to the most interesting situations i have ever seen in any video game.
After a while you get really into your games, you truely begin to trust some, misstrust others, you feel great joy, if a plan works as intendet and will cry in frusttration if your masterplan gets crusht by the plans of the other players. This leads to the most immersive gaming experience i have ever seen so far in a round based strategie game.
If you love the idea of a diplomacy where like in the real world anythink can happen and a strategie game that is very hard to get into, but has so much to offer that even after thousend of hours you still have more to learn, then i really can recomment it to you.

This game is a stone-cold classic that I played a million times in arcades. It's definitely one of the best old school fighting games ever, and the Steam version plays great. There's a really huge cast of memorable fighters, so many special moves to learn, strategies to pick up, tricks to learn, and team combinations to try out. KOF 98 is a really great introduction to SNK's legendary library of fighting games, and it gives you a good sense of why their games are still cult classics: unique characters, stylish designs, awesome music, sophisticated fighting systems, and subtle gameplay details that are tough but rewarding to master. This Steam version of the game even includes extra characters like Kasumi and Eiji, rebalancing and gameplay tweaks, and some cool challenge modes. This is probably the best and most definitive edition of the game that's ever been released. It even includes the original game for you purists out there.
You have to remember, though, that this isn't exactly an HD remaster or something. The game plays great but it looks just like it did almost twenty years ago. It may take some getting used to if you've become accustomed to graphically sharp modern fighters like Blazblue or Guilty Gear. However, I think you'll be able to overlook the outdated visuals when you realize that the netcode is pretty dang good. If you're interested in playing online matches, you can buy this game with confidence. It's a bit of a hassle at first to host or join a game with your friends, but once you've got everything set, it's quite smooth and plays really well. There were a few lag bumps, but nothing major. This is the closest thing you're going to get to be a kid back in 1998, plopping quarters into the roller rink arcade and getting trashed by your friend who knows all of Terry Bogard's moves.
Must have edition for any fighting game fan

"The King of Fighters '98 - Dream Match Never Ends/The Slugfest" is one of those games that never get old (and get even better as they get older). Great roster of fighters, excellent art and almost-unmatched gameplay makes an unforgettable fighting experience! Its graphics and visual effects continue to be impressive even almost twenty years later, with beautifully-animated sprites and rich backgrounds, accompanied by superb voice acting and some of the loudest sound effects I've ever heard.
As this is a "dream match"-style game, released after the conclusion of the Orochi story arc, there isn't much to say story-wise; it features most of the characters which appeared from KOF '94 to '97, Rugal returning as the final boss (using his "Omega" form), and the "Ultimate Match" version has additional characters, such as the Boss Team and Eiji Kisaragi, among others. Ultimate Match also adds new backgrounds, along with a new fighting style, "Ultimate".
KOF'98 still keeps itself fresh, exciting and relevant after all those years. Its competitive potential is enough to keep players hooked for hours, fighting against each other, and the computer-controlled fighters can also pose a great challenge for those who prefer to spend their time playing by themselves. However, its matchmaking service is lacking (well, at least it does not seem to work as it should here; maybe it's a connection issue) and online battles are plagued with delay, rendering the game almost unplayable sometimes. I wish there were more players available for online matches, nonetheless.

This is a great f2p model.
Pros:
*Most paid features are purely cosmetic.
*Pretty nice graphics.
*Each class seems to play entirely different.
*Some quests are pretty creative.
*The community is nice.
*Bazillion amounts of in game achievements, for those of you who like that.
Cons:
*When you reach certain levels, you'll sometimes automatically be given a quest. This is alright, except for the fact that a huge screen will pop-up to explain the quest to you, even if you happen to still be in combat. This really isn't so bad, I'm just holding a grudge because it caused me to die once.
*There's a lotta dudes on here that roll a female. I'm well aware this happens on every mmo, but I'm not kidding when it's normal to see female characters outnumber male characters 4:1 at times on this game. I personally don't really care about this, but this is just a fair warning to any fellow bros out there who may get seduced by internet "women"
*Game just feels way too easy sometimes. At first it made me feel like I was a champ, but then I realized that I was getting to be a high level and the game is still giving me baby steps.
*My biggest gripe is the repetitiveness. The second area has a lot more shops than the first area, which is to be expected, and some of the new shops were pretty cool. The third area had the same exact shops, which I thought was fine. But then I get to the fourth area and realize that for the past 3 areas, aka 30 levels, the shops have been the same. Obviously the equipment was different, but it follows the same forumula (Area 2 sells Area 1 equipment and Area 2 equipment, Area 3 sells Area 2 equipment and Area 3 equipment, etc). At least up to level 40 there was not much variety in the equipment you get. I know at higher levels the loot is a bit different, but this was pretty annoying to me.
---
Overall, this game is f2p and has some expected faults. However, being p2w is not a fault, as this game doesn't go by that. Any free game that I can put roughly 24 hours of enjoyed playing time into is fine by me. There will be plenty more hours to come.
