It's not often I'll write a review for a video game. This is my second. I also plan on appending this at a later date once I have played through the game multiple times.
NieR: Automata follows on from the events of the Drakengard and the original NieR games. None of which I have ever played, or watched, or know anything about before this entry. But amazingly, Automata pulls you into to a story that becomes a small part of you. Now I've done a little research into the previous entries, I understand how some of the elements can tie in to previous games. However, at least in my eyes, the story can stand completely alone.
You play as 2B, a combat android deployed from 'The Bunker' which serves as a base for the military if you will. Earth has been attacked and taken over by aliens and is now inhabited by machines. Along with 9S, a scout android. You begin your journey from humble beginnings to help the humans go back home, after hundreds of years away. Additionally, after you've completed your first playthrough, you can experience new playthroughs with additional content, cutscenes, fights and more. I'm currently on my 2nd, and I hear the 3rd is massively different.
The gameplay is a lot like Bayonetta or Devil May Cry, easy to learn, harder to master, always fun. You can use different weapons, abilities and chipsets (perks that buff you, extra health, easier dodges, lifesteal, that kinda thing). It never gets old and even on normal, whilst not being a particuarly hard game at this level, still challenges you.
Sound, oh boy, the sound. The voice acting, for the most part, is supurb, there's a few minor charecters who could be a little more convincing, but hey, you can't expect perfection. The main cast is voiced flawlessly and whilst the game isn't very dialogue heavy, you grow attached to these characters very quickly. The music is in a league of its own, and whilst it's not the kind of music you would listen to independently, at least for me, it bonds with the visuals and settings perfectly.
Lastly, my final note is a negative. As I have to be fair. It's not an issue with the game itself, but the port. Now, it isn't bad, but its not good either. Personally, I found no issues fps wise. I did however, have an issue with 1080p gameplay, whilst the game itself appeared to be displaying correctly, my steam notifications and fps counter where rendering at 720p. I hear other users have bad fps dips, in which I haven't noticed any.
My advice, if you want the game, you probably already bought it. If you're unsure. Jump in, buy it in a sale or full priced even. I was incredibly surprised and I was half expecting to play it for 2 hours and then never touch it again. This game is a masterpiece in my eyes. I won't forget this game anytime soon. No way.

So my buddies and I have put some time into this game, and it is fantastic.
Many people will write reviews about how bad the gameplay and controls are, but really what they mean by bad is different. Many vets of the fighting genre will immediately say that this game is bad, because they can't immediately pick this up and dominate it.
This game is 100% about flow, and range management. This game punishes you severely for spamming, you have to be measured and calculated with your input. Every character has a different flow to them, and you will not be able to pull of any combos untill you get a feel for their flow. You have to commit fully to your attacks, and cannot cancel an attack animation to block. The moves work off of a LP RP/LK RK system, and all make sense in the context of advance/retreat/high/low(Think Soul Calibur, but 2D movement). The combos are free flow for the most part and build off of your basic attacks. For example (LK,RK,ForwardLK,BackRK), where ForwardLK would be the same attack by itself etc. Instead of games like *cough Tekken where it would look more like (forward, back, LK, up right, LK RP, down left, slap your controller, do a head stand, LK RK LP, UP, down, sacrifice a newborn) to do a combo that has nothing to do with what those inputs do by themselves.
So if you like fighting games where there is a ceiling for new players where they have to memorize convoluted, nonsensical combos to stay competitive. Where you can stomp on someone because of the time you've put into a game, regardless of their skill at mechanics. This isn't for you.
If you enjoy fighting games that are all about timing, range management, and flow. This is for you.

I picked this up for just over a pounds in the sales, and at that price it's hard to complain.
There's depressingly few straight forward one-on-one beat 'em ups on Steam and that was why I picked up Kings of Kung Fu. Unfortunately, this is no Tekken. The problem starts with the premise, because everyone is based on real stars of martial arts movies they occupy a narrow range of body sizes, and there are no very large or very small characters, and the set of moves is much more plausible than most games of this type. But that means they're also more narrowly similar than most games of this type and this makes the gameplay feel much more samey.
A better game might rise above this but Kings of Kung Fu occupies the cheaper end of the spectrum. Characters have relatively few special moves - which are relatively difficult to pull off - and these moves don't mix it up much when you do use them. Characters are typically very static during their moves and rarely advance making it hard to press attacks and this is probably what motivates the poor quality hit detection where moves often seem to hit without making contact. Much of the interest of movie martial arts sequences comes from sequences of blocking moves but there is little use of this in the game.
All-in-all, it was probably worth a pound but it's hard to recommend as a fighting game.

I love strategy games.  Europa Universalis, Victoria, Hearts of Iron, GalCiv, and Civilization, just to name a hand full.  This game looks outdated.  It took me a while to learn how to play, I even had to be patient enough to watch let's play videos, and I am glad that I did.  On the surface, this game appears overly complicated and difficult.  However, once you learn the secrets within, the game opens up a lot of possibilities, and your enemies fall beneath your feat, regardless of difficulty.  In this game, you pick a fantasy kingdom and make a pretender God.  You then expand your God's dominion and kill the other pretender Gods so you become the supreme God.  There isn't really an economy, just provinces are rated with certain industry and commerce values.  The more land you own, the more security and stability you provide, the more your dominion grows, the more you prosper, and the larger your armies.  The end goal is pretty much capture the ascension nodes, take as much territory as possible, and kill off any nation you can.  Simple, but effective.  If you can find friends to play with, the game is that much better.

Dear friends, I know that many would have you believe that the Pale Ones are extinct, save for the occasional emergence of an Earth Reader or the primitive Pale Ones that are sometimes encountered in remote regions. I am here to set the ancient records straight.
Long have I labored in service to the Ancients, dead and forgotten though they may be to most of the civilized world. Only after extensive research and tireless experimentation had I uncovered a ray of hope in the sea of Agarthan darkness.
Of course, it is without doubt that in these late ages, the truest and noblest of the Pale Ones magistocracy have fallen. Only nearly forgotten memories and decaying mummies remain. But I knew there must be a way towards something more, some way to rekindle this magnificent people.
At first, I placed my hopes in a Wish spell... but it came to naught. No matter how I phrased my wish, e.g. "resurrect the pale ones", "awaken the ancients". "rebirth of agartha", nothing worked. The arcane powers behind the spell continued to inform me... "I cannot give you that."
Finally, some of my most skilled and dedicated Ktonian Necromancers happened upon an archive in one of the lowest reaches of Deep Agartha... an ancient record that held an account of some of the greatest of the Pale Ones.
Ecstatic, I raced to cast the powerful Wish spell... only to have my hopes dashed when I received the dreaded "I cannot give you that." After arduous experimentation, my most talented Servants of the Oracles finally uncovered the answer... I would need to wish for them by title, rather than by their given names!
With renewed vigor, my mages and I prepared the ritual. After a great deal of gems disappeared into the nether, finally what I had worked towards stepped out of the blazing astral light! An Earth-Blooded oracle, in the flesh, alive and breathing in these Late Ages! It was Ogon, Founder and King of Agartha!... but it was not.... to my gravest disappointment, it became abundantly clear that he did not know his own name... nor did he recall his ancient knowledge... he was a blank slate... a newborn, almost.
I stowed the King away, letting him putter around and reacquaint himself with the world. In the meantime, I turned the entirety of my magocracy towards finding a way to help this Revered Ancient remember himself. After many months of diligent study, the secret was uncovered! Some obscure incantation known as the bestowing of a Divine Name, held the key to restoring our fallen king to his old self.
The spell was cast. Finally, at long last, the King and Founder, Ogon the Earth-Blooded, awoke to himself! And he despaired. His friends and family were dead, and his entire kingdom was a tomb populated by tiny, warm-blooded freaks that worshiped the rotting flesh of his people. I was devastated by his melancholy. All I had wished was to restore Agartha to its former glory, but this suicidally depressed Founding Father seemed anything but a good omen.
After many weeks of frustration, I resolved to continue on my course. Soon after, I had brought back Golog, the esteemed and long-lived Oracle of the Dead. I restored his mind in the same manner as I had Ogon's, and soon he was aware and amiable... well... I say amiable. More like cynical and curmudgeonish. However, according to historic records, this is not very different than how he was during the prime of his life.
I swiftly introduced King Ogon to Golog, confident his spirits would soar at the sight of his living brethren! Alas, I was badly mistaken. Golog was as much a dissenter in his younger years as he was later in life, and I found that he had spoken against the invasion of the surface world by Ogon and his son so many centuries ago. Golog displayed an obvious air of superiority and his demeanor fairly reeked of a sentiment of "I told you so". Ogon, naturally, found this completely repugnant, and shut himself away in a lower cavern just to be rid of his old, smug political rival.
Close to despair myself, I bade my mages search the archives again. They came up with another oracle, one who had been close to Ogon in life. And what was more, it was a female! Her name was "Moss Agate" and she was a member of the Closed Council that Ogon had founded. Quickly, we gathered our gems and ritual tomes and Wished her into existence and restored her old memories.
When we finally pried open the door Ogon had locked, Moss Agate lumbered through and Ogon's eye fairly popped out of his socket. He cried, he laughed, he seemed like he must have been in his younger days. If only it had lasted. Joy turned to nostalgia turned again to that deep bitterness that had gripped him since his memories had returned. It seemed contagious, for even Moss Agate seemed to take on his feelings soon after.
I realized what needed to be done. I gathered them, the three oracles I had resurrected, in the now neglected and decrepit Hall of the Ancients. I released them from my service, so that they might make their own way in the world, away from the painful memories of the past. As I watched them gaze around themselves regally, I saw for but a moment what they were seeing. The halls were richly adorned with orange and purple tapestries, embroidered with every conceivable gem from the deepest reaches of the earth. Many revered and vibrant oracle and lord lounged around these pristine marble tables. All was a bustle with activity.
Now, when I looked around, those halls were drab and barren. The shuffling of arthritic feet could be heard as Ktonian Necromancers and alchemists wandered the halls in search of odd tomes or ritual materials. Quiet whispers could almost be discerned, seemingly coming from the direction of the burial caverns, but no other voices filled the halls.
It was then that I bade my grand entourage farewell. I sent them on their way with two mummified Oracles, that they might keep them company on their journeys. While this diverse group may not have been the closest of companions, they were now all that was left of the glorious past of the Pale Ones. I believed they would stay together unto the end.
This oil painting is the last image I have of their departure:
Perhaps, even now, Moss Agate is with child, and the rebirth of the Pale Ones is already underway. Or perhaps they have decided to let their great race pass from the world.

'First View' review video of Steam Controller & Link above. As the video is fairly old now (due to testing it only weeks after it was released to pre-orderers), I'm going to write my 'final' verdict here after testing it a little more.
I really enjoy the Steam Controller, it's feature-filled and a fantastic little controller for gamers who just don't necessarily enjoy the console but still want to kick back and enjoy their fast-paced, action games on a little trackpad that isn't a laptop trackpad.

I recommend this to PC gamers for sure! But as other reviews state, it's very true this isn't for people who want to convert from consoles to PCs - this is, in my opinion, merely just for PC gamers who want to have their PC games in the format of a controller that's most suiting.

Gonna rewrite this to make this more of a review.
The steam controller is valves attempt at merging a console controller with a PC mouse pad, it works quite well, however is a tad difficult to adjust to for some people, this controller includes haptic feedbacks so your fingers have a physical notion of how you are moving things, 2 additonal bottom buttons that can be used for whatever you see fit, a gyro sensor for tilting(which is quite useful for some FPS games.) the buttons can be changed to whatever keyboard/mouse/gamepad button you which, as well as can be set for multiple keys for button for commands(such as ALT+TAB) it is wireless and runs on two double A batteries which have a insane run time, and they have added other features such as the touch menu and action sets via updates.
This controller can be used to technically play any steam game or non-steam game(in most cases) it runs through steam so it is required to work correctly it is still somewhat a work in progress since they keep adding additional features but they are added often enough and I thank valve for not just leaving it as is in release.
On a personal note, I mostly use my steam controller to wirelessly control my PC from my bed or the living room couch(via steam link) it is not as effective as a regular Mouse/Keyboard configuration but it does the job very well, of course it is also very good for games if configured in such a way that works for you.
Button configurations are made by community and game developers and can be freely edited by the user to whatever placement works for them, this gives you a chance to experiment a little if you do not like what is set by default.
Overall the steam controller is a fantastic product, even more so if you are a user with hundreds of games and want a controller to play them all.

There are some problems with the Steam controller. The buttons sit a hair too low, for example. Maybe 3 hairs, whatever. Otherwise, it's freaking awesome. There is a learning curve, and the customizability is daunting, but anyone who claims to be part of the PC Master Race should understand the power that comes with getting under the hood. In a nutshell: Dominions is hands-down my favorite RTS wargame to play.
Dominions 4 is another installment in the Dominions series of wargames. These are the most faithful representation of and expansion on tabletop wargaming that I've ever played.
Dominions 4  expands on what's possible and manages quite a bit of (stat tracking) tedium for you with the computer making for a much more enjoyable experience (for me) than a tabletop littered with miniatures. And game play that would be impossible to do with a manual set of mechanics is implemented flawlessly.

This is simply the best strategy game I've ever played. It's the kind of game you could write a novel about your experiences in your last game. What makes Dominions 4 special is the fact that every single game feels unique, for real. You can't just read a guide and use the same meta-strategy over and over for a specific nation, because each game and each turn requires tons of planning. The feeling of making the right choice in the right moment is awesome. And the opposite goes for a stupid mistake or bad planning. Consequences can be really chaotic, but not always unforgiving.
I've read several times that this game is hard to get into. I really don't agree with it. It's really easy to get the basic concepts and the real difficulty comes with the huge amount of content the game has to offer: nations, gods, spells, units, items, management, customization... And this is something you will learn with time.
Magic is really great. It goes from tiny fireballs to huge spells that can make the entire map goes into an eternal night or spread diseases worldwide. So magic is not just an alternative to normal weaponry or armors; magic can completely change the fate of the events.
I won't go deep into nations, becuse there are like 60? 70? But you'll find tons of them based on old civilizations and mythology: Roman empire (with undead version on a certain era), a mix between Spain and France heavily based on Inquisition, germanic barbarians, nordic giants, fire creatures, a chinese nation, a japanese one with demons from japanese folklore, nations with monkeys, spiders, fishes, shrimps, ♥♥♥♥ing crabs, squids, winged beigns, demons, trolls, dragons, eagles, dawgs, wolves, direwolves, hobbits... blablabla, tons of nations all of them with extremely different units and gameplay.
Graphics are for sure paleolithic-school, but somehow it makes a better experience for me, as it creates a nice true RPG experience, kind of reading a book.
And lets not forget the crazy situations that may happen during a game: an entire army out of place because your bard was flirting with their commander, a game you are about to win when your prophet is about to claim a throne but then he dies when it's about to reach it because of pestilence or a broken limb, a commander sent to some important mission suddenly finds a frog and adopts it as pet, a battle between Dracula vs Cthulhu because... why not.

Aura Kingdom is almost a caricature or a deconstruction of the whole concept of a Massive Online JRPG. The character designs immediately call to mind Magic Knight Rayearth; fashion is pretty and elaborate with lots of frills on display, hair is long and available in a variety of fanciful colors, and all swords are huge. Combat is pretty easy to learn, each weapon type has some kind of small gimmick that helps to keep squashing the various adorable monsters roaming the world from becoming stale quickly. A similarly easy to learn fishing mini-game is also worked in, with its own equipment and interface. Cosmetic gear is entirely seperated from statistic-granting combat gear, leading to the situation whereby your character can look like pretty much whatever you want without impacting the ability to fight effectively.
This is the kind of game where there's no dungeon finder, but 14 seperate dance emotes. Where new abilities are learned automatically on level up or are chosen for free, straight from the character info window, and are re-chosen with fairly minimal penalty the same way. It's a very soothing kind of game, great for mellow, casual players or people just getting acquainted with online games.
...In summary, if you spend most of your time foaming at the mouth and screaming into a headset mic about why your last raid wipe or lost ranked match was everyone else's fault, give this one a pass. Try chewing on some wood instead.

As an Anime fan, but not a big MMO fan, i was in search of japanese created games and i stumbled upon this.
I can't say much about this game yet becouse i am writing this review after 6 hours of gameplay.
Well, first things first. This game is trully an Anime like game. This is the biggest plus in this game so far. NPCs are quite unique, though i sometimes feel a repetitive scene when fighting some mobs (especially humans, like pirates), but still creature mobs are so unique and interesting that i feel a pleasure just roaming and watching them pass me by.
Bad thing is that quests are dull. Like, take that, bring that, kill that, collect that. It's pretty much repetitive. But its not a problem for a free game (most of the rpgs have same kind of quests anyway). There are many hidden quests, that start with the player checking some container or an item. And there are alot of bounties, side quests and stuff like that. It's all about numbers, not quality.
There are 9 classes to choose from. The character creation is so loyal to anime/manga fans that most probably most of you will enjoy. There are some elements that are quite new to me (becouse i dont play MMO often). Like, none of the skills have mana requirements, only cooldowns. And there is no typical Strenght, Endurance, Energy leveling. You get ATK Points and DEF points. In ATK section you level damage, critical hit chance or attack speed, and in DEF section you level armor rating or evasion.
You can have a pet here. Ranging from faries to ponies (Yes, MLP fans, this game is for you too!) That pet levels with you and it can get you presents every 10 minutes for some kind of energy points. To restore points, you need to talk with your pet. The dialogue is pretty solid, sometimes fun. So you need to take care not only about your character, but about your pet as well.
Overall, this game is still in open beta stage. There are some bugs, sometimes server lags and that kind of stuff. This game isn't the perfect game ever, some things really bug me (like, why doesnt character look depend on a costume but not the armor?). But still, i had a pleasure playing it. So check that out, for a free game and for a beta stage, it's awesome.

It's KoF 98 with a bunch of options and many settings & modes to find something your pace or play style.  Definitely a must for your library if you're into fighting games at all (and obviously a recommendation for KoF fans).

Back in 1998, this was the most anticipated title after the thrilling conclusion of the Orochi saga as seen in the King of Fighters 97. Although this title lacked any sort of story at all, it made up for it with the inclusion of all characters seen up to that point including those had been retired or killed during the story, as well as an overall improvement in gameplay speed & balance.
This particular version of this game is actually the third revision of the game, apparently based on the arcade version of "The King of Fighters 98: Ultimate Match" while adding some requested changes (such as the return of the assist attack, that for some unknown reason was taken out of the previous game!). Which explains the lack of extras such as reworked 3D stages & an arranged soundtrack that were featured in home versions such as the one released for the Playstation 2 at the time. But do not let the lack of those extras discourage you from playing this excellent title. Featuring perhaps the largest roster seen in the series thus far, you may rest assured that you are certain to find characters that suit your playing style.
All in all, this is a highly recommended title for KOF fans that may have missed the second revision of the game back at the arcades, as well as younger fighting game fans who have an interest in old-school fighting games.

The consensus is that this is the best game in the series; and I would not disagree with that statement.  If you have played any of the older KOF games(pre PS3/XBOX360), then this game will be familiar territory.  The game has a solid roster, good game play, and doesn't get too complex with it's bars/meters. Overall, it is a very solid fighting game.  As for this edition, there are several changes.  First, there are additional characters added since the original arcade version including several boss characters from past games.  Second, some of the characters received new or modified moves and (S)DMs.  Third, there is an inclusion of a 3rd mode that is included which is customizable from a combination of extra and advanced modes.  As for online, there isn't a lot of people playing the game so finding a match can be challenging.  However, overall, this is a solid game, and for any fan, it should be a must buy.
In summary, if you are a KOF fan, I absolutely recommend this game, but likely, you've already purchased it.  If you are a fighting game fan in general, or would like to get into the series, this is definitely a recommended title.

After putting hundreds and hundreds of hours into Overwatch I have to say that this game is a refreshing pace from Overwatch. There's a overall feel to character dynamics as you play, there are different builds and different ways to play every champion in the game. Not only that but there are ways to counter healers and tanks in the game.
What i mean by this is every game, depending on the mode, you start off with a certain amount of credits. These credits can be used to purchase reduced cool downs on abilities, increased healing taken from other sources such as healers, reduced splash damage from players, reduced direct damage, the ability to destroy tank shields very very quickly. It's a very fun change of pace and I highly recommend this to anyone. Give it at least 10-12 hours to get used to every character, learn different play styles, different builds. I was a little anxious about the controller after reading a few reviews that seemed to highlight the (in the opinion of the author/site) flaws of the device.  But after getting my hands on it and using it for a few hours, I'm confident in recommending this controller.  Of course it does take some getting used to, but so did keyboard and mouse when I switched from console gaming to PC years ago.
I found that this controller is great for games already designed for a controller, as it allows you to customize and expand your current configurations by allowing you to use a single button to create alternate functions for the track pads and buttons.
As for games not designed for a controller, this device is even better.  Point and click games have just become more relaxing, as the trackpads and triggers, as well as the customization ability, work seamlessly and allow you to game from the comfort of your couch.
Although this controller is great, I don't expect it to replace keyboard and mouse for FPSs though.  Aiming felt really precise, but the trackpad still doesn't provide the complete control of a mouse.  I also found myself constantly touching the trackpad by accident, which often made my aim and view sporadic.  The two-stage triggers are implemented great and provide great control and sensitivity, yet again, they take some getting used to, especially if you usually just mash the triggers.

I'm only rating this as a not recommended because Valves current software for the controller is laughably terrible. There are undefined strings everywhere in the configure options so you don't know what the ♥♥♥♥ you're changing unless their incredibly vague names somehow strike a chord with your brain. You can't use the joystick and left pad at the same time, ever, which is actually an impressive ♥♥♥♥ up on their end. The D-pad simulation is INCREDIBLY finnicky on what it thinks an input is, if you're a few degrees higher than absolutely horizontal then it'll think you want to ♥♥♥♥ing jump. Configuring the thing is incredibly time consuming, and getting configs from the comunity is very hit and miss currently, sometimes they just don't work at all and unset all the configs you've done.
The build quality is great and it feels amazing in my hands, but everything on the software side of this controller screams out that it was never, ever QA'd by anyone besides the developers. It still needs serious, serious work. The controller itself works amazingly well technically and has an insane amount of potential, but currently it still feels like you're beta testing Valve's next new thing, that they'll abandon entirely a year from now. Oh and Big Picture mode still needs a mountain of work, and you can't configure the controller at all unless you're in big picture mode,that's fun.

There are a lot of pros and cons, but I was using this controller at my desk instead of on my TV because I dont yet own the steam link but my opinion will change by the time I recieve that.
PROS:
-The ability to customize nearly everything. I really like the fact that even if the game doesnt have full controller support you are able to customize every single inch on that controller.
-The back "paddles" I really like this option so that I dont have to take my thumb of the pads every single time I need a button. I will use Rocket League for an example. I really like the fact that I can use Boost and Jump on the back instead of having my fingers on the buttons.
-The triggers were extremely comfortable for me and I have fairly small hands, unlike the Xbox controller these triggers are wide which I really like. It has a click to them when you use them as well and you can go to the setting and actually choose what you want the triggers to do after you click it hard enough.
-This one might sound strange but I really like the fact that the controller has a very nice gloss to matte ratio. For those of you who will be using this in your living room odds are you will eat while using the controller once and a while, so your hand will get greasy. The controller is not full gloss like the Wii U, it is both gloss and matte which has a really nice feel to it.
-Finally but one of the most important, input lag. I have been using an Xbox One controller for a majority of my games and I had been getting a very noticable amount of input lag. The steam controller has none from up to 7-8 feet which for those of you who will be playing in a living room is fine.
Now lets go to the Cons because there are a few.
CONS
-You HAVE to use big picture mode, and while most people wont mind often times I find it extremely frustrating to do simple tasks like browse the web because of how complicated it is to change tabs or type.
-This one is HUGE on the controller. Typing. I really dont like that the sensitivity is so low that you often times slip your thumb of the pad getting rid of the cursor. It has been extremely annoying but as I said, something to get used to.
-Batteries... I hate the fact that there is a micro USB slot on the controller but it uses batteries. Come on Valve. It makes me think they might go down the same route as Xbox and add rechargable batteries, and no one wants to spend more money maintenancing their controller after spending $60.
-Not very good on FPS'. I gave the controller a really good try on CS:GO, TF2, and Black Ops 2. I just couldnt do good. It might just be me but it was just uncomfortable on FPS' mainly because they are so fast pace.
Thats all for my opinions on the controller! If you are interested in buying a steam link I recommend you get this with it!

I really wanted this game to be good. It has a great cast of characters based on real martial artists such as Bruce Lee and Tony Jaa, each doing an alright job at replicating the fighting styles of those they're based off of. But this game just... isn't very fun. Early on, the game seemed to show promise even though it was rough around the edges, so I wanted to support it, but it just doesn't tap into the potential it has. I realized it needed a lot of work when I first played it, and stopped playing and gave it time because in that state, it was playable, but not too fun to play at all. Sadly, when I came back, I just couldn't find the interest in putting a lot more time in, because the game felt pretty much exactly the same as it did months and months prior. The sound design can be somewhat annoying, especially the sometimes incredibly obnoxious background noises on levels. There are moves that look like they hit, but don't, and moves that look like they didn't hit, but did. The story mode is so barebones, it's hardly worth playing more than once. Why not at least try to make it a big deal that these characters are coming across eachother (In Mortal Kombat X, even if two characters didn't exactly meet eachother, they would still have something to say to eachother at the beginning of the fight, to make it feel more personal, rather than just another fight). That IS one of the selling points of the game, I'd say. Plus, there really is a great cast of characters, great stages (such as the same place where Bruce Lee fought Chuck Norris in Return of the Dragon, cat and all, haha), and a soundtrack that kinda gives off that Wu-Tang vibe that could work with a game like this, but it just isn't enough. I'm a kung fu film fan, but I just don't find any interest in playing this game anymore than I already have.

Gameplay can feel clunky at first, but it also makes you think and reserve your actions for counters and mixups. It's not the deepest fighter, but definitely not brainless either. You can maintain spacing and punish whiffed attacks with awesome looking combos, and of course iconic signature kung fu movesets.
A few small gripes I had with the game were the easy jab combos. It's possible to land once and time the next jab to connect an 11-hit whopper easily. Damage scales, but still. Also, I think the achivements may be buggy. I played well over 100 games against my 8 year old niece (winning at least 120 accumulative not consecutive), but the achievement didn't unlock. It is in fact listed as 100 CONSECUTIVE won games, but who plays 100 games in one sitting?
Either way, as a huge martial arts film fan, this game is pretty fun and definitely worth checking out.

It's still Skyrim. If you're looking for a full remaster with hyperrealistic graphics this isn't it at all. Most of the improvements are on a technical level and the game is aging just as you'd expect it to (quite well, but aging none-the-less.)
The modding drama I did not find to be much of an issue, most of the quality of life mods were already ported and ready at release and I'm sure by this point they've ported most everything. Everything except the script extender but here is the thing:
Script Extender and people's messy scripts were the reason modded Skyrim ran so poorly in the first place. Make mods within the dev's intended scope that the game architecture was built around and surprise surprise you can get 100s of mods in and it runs smooth as silk. This probably true for old Skyrim too, but you may as well play this version since it is the more updated one.
You can get this version to look really nice and actually run at more than 5fps, actually PLAY the game with the cosmetic mods instead of just taking stills for your blog.
So to sum up:
-Youll be let down if youre expecting a roboust full modern rerelease/remake. This Skyrim and nothing more.
-If you're expecting absolutely nothing but literally Skyrim with a new title, you'll actually be impressed in spots.
-If you're still playing Skyrim (and frankly a lot of people are, gaming standards have been on sharp decline since it's release,) there is 0 reason not to get on board with the new one. This is Skyrim, there is no vanilla Skyrim anymore to even consider.
-If youre the type of person who plays Skyrim with no mods (lol,) this is probably the best place to get your feet wet since installing everything isn't such a pain anymore (no more billions of third party software to install and figure out.) Just watch out if you see anyone Beth or otherwise charging for mods, just dont ever pay for mods, not worth it.
Personally I think they are stretching it releasing this game hoping for Skyrim to remain the flagship that it is for years to come with the updated version. There is no new content (not even DLC) and no major changes to keep it going, interest will continue it's steady decline because if you've been playing Skyrim since release you've seen it all and this 'remaster' wont change that. But I understand the reason they did it, to get sales off the new gen consoles as well as give the active modders something to do, maybe give some of the fallen off modders a reason to load up the old CK again and port their old mods and after that who knows.
Anyway, that's my take on this one. Id hate to lie and say this was the best way to do something like this, it's definitely 100% business and trying to reestablish the Skyrim name among younger gamers of this generation. But at the same time, I struggle to find anything overly negative to say about SE, despite being past bored of playing Skyrim over the years myself. At the very least they didn't introduce a whole bunch of problems and changes that ruined the original or anything.

The Dominions series is clearly a labor of love. There are so many factions drawn from so many historical settings. Nordic history? sure. Native American history? sure. Roman, gothic, celtic, lovecraftian history? yes yes yes. Customizing your faction is interesting. The strategic is 'just one-more-turn' compelling. spell research is very deep. The game has a very indie feel to balance- ie not balanced. For whatever reason that doesn't bother me. The soundtrack is inspiring. The graphics are weak, but there is a vast number of units, each lovingly represented by a few blurry pixels. The battles are automated- which is good and bad. It'd be nice to choose each units actions, but most battles are hundreds of units, it would take forever. Strategically, the AI makes pretty good decisions. Even after playing a lot, it's not always clear why certain battles turn out the way they do. Once your empire gets large, it suffers from classic micromanagement issues. Even with its dated look and flaws, this game is a beautiful, wonderful experience to master.

The effect was that new players quickly became frustrated and left, which dried up the pool of houses that you could actually be reasonably assured to complete, meaning that the game had literally no point unless your intent was to just feed the players sitting in their palacial death-mansions. This was not helped by the absurd price of the game, and the devs bizzarely principled stand on only having one sale ever. They clearly value their game to a very high degree, but that pride seems to have ultimately hurt the game.
The game now has an average player count per day of around 0.5, and the peak players in the last 30 days was 2. This is a multiplayer only game that has half of a human being playing daily and never more than a couple at one time. It no longer functions as a game.

So if you came to this game because you loved Minecraft but have never heard of Telltales Games before or don't know what their games are like I HIGHLY suggest you do some research beforehand. This game is not the same as Minecraft. Telltale Games focus on dialogue and telling a story with player chocies and QTEs along the way. GAMEPLAY should not be expected to function just as Minecraft does. The game comes out in Episodes priced at $4.99 each. Currently on steam you can pay $24.99 and get the first chapter. If you're worried about paying for more chapters, worry not. If you paid $24.99 right now, you never have to pay for the later episodes as you've paid for all of them upfront.
This is Telltales doing what Telltale does. I can see the complaints about the story, but they're going for an 80's adventure movie feel here. If that's not what you like and don't think the plot/story is great because of that (too straight forward/predictable) then more power too you. It just isn't the story for you. I found the Minecraft world was handled quite well. Nothing feels like it was thrown in "because it's Minecraft," and the world just functions by it's own rules. I haven't noticed the game being self aware and making a bunch of Minecraft jokes or the character's doing things like questioning "how does putting these things on a table creat something?" or anything like that.
If you have played other Telltale games before, you know what to expect. This time though Telltales is doing more of Family-Friendly (or at the very least PG-13) story compared to previous games. It's light hearted but can also be serious when it needs to for tough choices. Did I enjoy say, the premise of the Wolf Among Us game more than this? Yes. I did. But that does not mean this is bad. They're two totally different tones.
In the end, if you're a Minecraft fan but don't know Telltales, or even if you played previous Telltale games, do your research before making the purchase to see if it's right for you. Heck, read a review or watch a let's player go through the first chapter and decide if the game works for you.

This is my first game in the Red Orchestra/Rising Storm franchise so my perspective is a bit of a newbie to this style of hardcore shooters. I will try to hit in a couple of points for people interested in this game.
1. This game is BRUTAL for new players of the genre. The time to kill is very quick. You will get 1 shotted very frequently and when you arent you will be bleeding and need to find a safe spot to hide to bandage up. You will need to unlearn some of the habits from other shooters and learn to love cover and the almighty smoke grenades (YES THEY ARE USEFUL HERE)
2. There is a lack of a tutorial mode, well kinda. They have tutorial videos that lets you that explains to you the basics and tho they aren't much I do recomend new players to see them because they explain game modes, classes, and some special functions to be effective. Besides the videos there is a weapons range that lets you test your guns to get a fell to them as well as a Helicopter map thats lets you practice flying in a safe enviroment without getting shot an fast respawns. Now this tutorials are adaquet I would like to see a boot camp style tutorial to guide a player through the game so when they join a real match, they aren't on a Cobra chin gun not knowing how to actually shoot the gun, (This has happend)
3. This is a team game. If your team isn't communicating and coordinating you will be whooped by the team that is. There is a power sturtuce in this game as Squadmates listen to the Squad Leader and the Squad Leader listens to the Team Leader because he is capable of calling in Air Support, Artillery Strikes, or Buffs to your respawn. You have to take the initiative and command or learn to grow.
4. The community is very fun. It's not toxic but expect memes. Lots of filthy frank memes. They don't do it because they are actually racist of something its more of a joke. A messed up joke but still a joke.  Some people will be putting on a personality, some will be acting, some want to be shocking for the sake of it. Try not to take it to seriously.
5  The ambience is great, the rock and roll in the screen and as the americans win. The rupturing explosions. The chatter of soldiers. The sheer panick of players and♥♥♥♥♥♥pops off. It gets crazy and it does become that PTSD Simulator people say about the series.
I can go on about how the helos are fun and customization is fitting, or how the developers will be supporting the game for time to come, but you can learn that as you play. What I want to say is that Rising Storm 2: Vietnam is fun, thrilling, and crazy, would recommend everyone to try it even thou it may not be a game for everyone.

You can't use a touchpad for the same functions as a control-stick. It just doesn't work. :(
The size/shape of your fingers can make touchpads cumbersome in any event, and the fine control needed for gaming makes them an inneffective choice for gameplay.
For most games, the right stick functions as the means of controlling the camera. The haptic touchpads have all the control of those annoying little mousepads they build into Laptops-- and they are just as frustrating to use.
The Left touchpad has some promise; it feels like a distinct improvement over the older four-way touchpads. It is far too large though.
The rest of the buttons are too small, the springs in them are too weak, and they are located too far from your thumbs.
Hiting the right button at the right time is far too cumbersome for a device that is meant to allow you to control something in a video game.
The extra buttons in the grip seem like an interesting addition, but they are located in the place where you grip the controller the hardest; it is far too easy to hit them by accident. This means you have to have an awkward and uncomfortable grip on the controller to use it. And forget playing any scary games-- you might break the side buttons.
The haptic feedback itself is incredibly innovative, but has far too steap of a learning curve. Analog controls may be less technologically advanced, but they allow for far greater adaptation to individual users (you can only push a control stick so far and so fast, which makes learning to use them easy. Haptics require far more calibration to the individual user than Valve realizes. Firmware updates can't change that).  Even the videos used to advertise the Steam controller show that it takes far more movement and elaborate contortions to use it for the same functions that are simple with either a stick or a mouse. The Wi gaming system also had incredible advances in technology, and it also rendered its controllers too cumbersome for gameplay.
The physical resistance of a control stick will ALWAYS be able to offer better feedback, control, and precision than any haptic advances. Mouses offer better fine controls than gamepad sticks because of the way they function and are used, not the inherent technology within them. And trying to bridge the two has thus far only made something mediocre by both standards.
I respect Valve, and I REALLY respect innovation and experimentation. But the problem with trying to re-invent the wheel is that the first few attempts you make, may end up producing something square.
I don't want Valve to abandon the controller, but I am sad to say that this product will require an almost complete redesign to be useable.
Sorry guys. Better luck next time.

I know that I dont have a lot of playtime logged, Mainly because I like playing fighting games with other people. But I feel I have to write this on a playthrough of the single player. Here goes.
This is definitely fan-service material, and the stars are easily recognizable enough to make the dream fights we all talked about when we were younger come to fruition.
OK, now for the gameplay.
TOTALLY COMPETENT. Its somwhere between Dead or alive and Karateka. Easy to play, thoughtful, but crazy♥♥♥♥♥spike in understanding the flow of fight between characters. Mainly because I'm a TEKKEN/Soul Calibur fighter, I can totally understand the allure of this fighting game style, but becuase the fighting styles are so vastly different, the hit boxes dont allow for a back and forth sway to the battles.
"what would you do to correct the game?"
I would not change much, but here is my list:
-Keep the blocking, but strikes and kicks could double as parries because meeting fist with fist would cancel the attacks, and counter the unbalances and disadvantages between the fighters. to keep it fair, add a parry meter that depletes as strikes connect, and blocking fills the meter.
-I appreciate the ability to create your own combos, but it just needs to be looser. because of the vast style differences, once the parry system is in place, the styles of the characters can flourish, as opposed to being stuck waiting for an opening. this would keep everyone using ALL of the characters, because bthe would be attacking, either in defense or offense. the parry meter would slow the fights down if the parries are used too much, causing the fighters to back down to relenish the bars.
- Street fighter 2 system in strikes. IE All Short atacks do the same damage, all Fierce attacks do the same damage. the net result would be faster characters would do primarily smaller damage, while stronger characters would do more.

LONG VERSION:
I would give this game a "Medium Recommendation" (between yes and no) if Steam allowed me.
The CONCEPT of this game (what it's trying to be) is better than its EXECUTION (what it actually is.)
The game has its flaws, most notably the borderline tank-controls and the occasionally soft animation. But ANYone who loves Kung Fu movies will understand this game is paying deep repsect and homage to the long lost days of low-budget Hollywood martial arts. And for that, all is forgiven. Hell, just having four generations of martial arts masters (Sho'Nuff AND Chuck Norris AND Donny Yen AND maybe somebody who kind of looks like Jet Li)  in the same game is cause for celebration by most contemporary Kung Fu fans.
There IS a way to create a game that honors the legacy of cheaply made kung-fu movies, but because of controls and murky animation, this game somewhat misses the mark... but it's VERY much on the right path to kung fu grindhouse greatness. I do hope the developer continues to update it, smooth out some of that animation and sharpen the fighting controls.  (I will happily edit this review after any significant update.)
RECAP:
-great game to play with your young kids, so that alone is reason to buy for me
-fans of kung fu may enjoy this (if they can forgive the controls)
-cannot recommend for casual gamers (yet)
VERY FUN TO PLAY

I was a big fan of old school martial arts movies... Bloodsport, Enter the Dragon, The Last Dragon for those that want to mix Kung Fu and break dancing.. which heck if you were alive during the 80's those were the two things which you loved...
This game much like the 80's  an acquired taste.. it has some great classic characters....  an amazing sound track and the old grainy look will leave you busting out your breakdancing gear unfortunately the game play seems stuck in 80's right along with all these classic characters.
The game isn't fluid at all, the trailers are downright misleading.  You'll never play the game as fluid and smooth as the trailers show.  The controls are stiff and slightly unresponsive..  The Hit detection seems to be at best flawed, sometimes you'll see your foot fly through someone face with no dmg... other times you'll hit thin air and see someone fly to the ground like a sack of bricks..  Also the AI is weak, you can win by using the same move or combo of moves over and over again..  Cheese factor is high in this one...
If you want a good compaison think of the Original Mortal Kombat, this game's combat and character stiffness seems nearly identical if not slightly worse..  although button responsiveness MK has a massive leg up.   I won't say the game can't improve, but seeing as the Development team removed the Early Access and the last update aside from adding cards to the game was done about 3 months ago I'm pretty sure it's a safe bet the game won't be improved any longer.
This just isn't a game I can recommend with a 9.99 price tag, if you can are a huge 80's kung fu flick type of guy.. it might be worth it just for some kicks and giggles, if you're a fighting game fan, you have far better choices for far cheaper prices..

I think I might be hooked again. This game is so much fun after you get past the slow beginning. It's the definition of open world/sandbox, rpg or just in general. With that said, I'm sure most folks know wtf Skyrim is by now, whether or not you've actually played it. Most folks will probably just wanna know the difference between Skyrim Special Edition (SE) and the OG.
SE, as shallow as it sounds, is pretty much a upgraded graphics port of the modern console version. It's a 64bit DX11 game while OG is 32bit DX9, meaning since it's 64bit the game is using all of your ram, while 32bit OG limits it to 4gb. SE being 64bit, should run much smoother on modern systems, especially if you're using a sh*t ton of mods. It's actually a lot deeper than that but thats pretty much the tldr version of it. SE also comes with all the DLC.
Another thing that needs to be mentioned is the topic of Creation Club (CC). CC is a way for the devs to try and capitalize on the modding community. It's basically a market place for you to purchase "mods" that have always been free in the past on the OG. There are a bunch of free mods on the CC as well but over all I say f*ck it, don't support this garbage. As with the above, thats the tldr. You can find more info on that topic elsewhere if your interested. Nexus is still the go to place for mods.
As of this writing mods for the OG on Nexus still greatly outnumber that of SE. Plus the OG has steam workshop. That doesn't mean you cant get SE to look damn good though. It's been over a year since release and the modding community has been hard at work, and it'll only get better. The script extender SKSE just hit alpha recently for SE, so it's only a matter of time before SE takes over the OG imo.
Overall I would say this is the definite game. F*cking CC aside, it's still the same old Skyrim, looks better than vanilla OG and should run better when heavily modded now and into the future.

A very enjoyable game to learn how to play. However there are times where as a player it can be frustrating trying to understand what certain things do. Indeed there are scenarios that crop up that confuse veterans of the game now and again.
A quick pros, mos and cons
Pros:
Massive customisation available in god creation stage
Strategies can be altered mid-game
Cute graphics for different units, and there are many of them
Nations feel very unique, they all have their own niches, and there are many of them.
Game devs still adapt the game even after all this time.
Randomisation in map creation leads to unique game scenarios
Mos: (neither a pro or a con but something I think a new player must know, must know = mo)
_Battles are scripted beforehand, you cannot interact with them while they are in progress. But you can watch the replay and learn from your mistakes or successes.
_God creation is important, if you pick a bad set of scales before the game properly starts you could find yourself in a difficult situation with no way to escape the situation. Don't be afraid to start a few test games to make sure exactly what plan you have in mind for the units you will be working with.
_Not all spells are equal. Especially when considering the variety of unit types. Some spells don't work underwater, some don't affect mindless, undead and some simply cannot be cast without communions or blood slaves.
Cons:
Graphics are super dated, although they're very cute for what they are.
Sound effects can be a little loud at times. Snakes and archers have the sound dialled up to 11.
Information overload is a big problem. Guides are a must. I would recommend watching a playthrough.
Information availability can be a problem too. Sometimes there are questions I have that simply bring up no search results.
The sheer variety of nations and spells and units can be a challenge to keep in mind.
Due to the massive variance in the nations and starting conditions game balance may not always be ideal.
Underwater combat can feel a bit limited in variety and some underwater nations do require a bit of game experience before attempting to play.
Random babble:
Things like figuring out encumberance (spell/melee encumberence is a big deal), what curses do and how important reinvigoration is can trip you up. For instance units with "cold blooded" fighting in cold climates suffer an encumberance penalty when fighting in cold terrain, to the point where in very cold climates these units are a liability.
Or if you click on the "Morale" in the unit card this brings up the unit upkeep, which is how much the unit costs per year. Kind of a big deal when figuring out why a unit costs a certain amount. This vital info is just tucked away under a little word.
Or that Undead seem great right? high morale (basically unbreakable), no upkeep and can go underwater...riiight up until you hit an enemy who uses priests, then all those undead summons get banished into nothing. One size does not fit all. (However with the right build you can totally make undead nations work. Watch out for multiplayer with them though, due to their dominion killing population other players generally want to kill them quick)
This is a game of layers. Once you figure out one layer a dozen more lie beneath. However once you figure out ideal paths for your god, scripts for unit combat, what gear you need and research goals the game is fairly straightforward. The rest comes down to good old fashioned strategy, (depending on if you play multiplayer or singleplayer this will differ significantly).
Due to how much you have to micomanage everything your strategy can change quite drastically and thanks to the  massive number of spells available you will be able to adapt how you play. The rest comes down to how much time you have to spare.
The game really shines in how you use your mages and thugs. Also not all Gods (or Pretender gods) are equal, some are designed to be combat monsters from turn 1, others are designed to support your nation from behind the curtain while other still lie imprisoned waiting for the time to come into the world. There are valid reasons to use each of them.
It's a God game of god games, you control everything and yet when the battles come all you can do is watch. It can be very rewarding watching all that time you spend preparing scripts for your units come together at just the right moment.
For all that it's not a difficult game, it really isn't. It's just a matter of having the time spare to learn what you need to know. If you have that time this game will take you on an adventure that novel writers and film makers could only dream of.

Not to sound like the proverbial hipster, but this game became garbage the moment it hit Steam.  Or maybe it was a few updates prior to that.
I've been a long-term Jason Rohrer fan and enjoyed Castle Doctrine up until a certain point.  Like a lot of games - comparably Rust - you need to devote a lot of time to CD, but also be aware that all that time can be robbed from you by a more experienced/wealthier player.
You build a house with the starting cash of $2000 using the various tools that are given to you all in the hopes of protecting your family (expendable) and your cash (expendable, but you really want to keep it safe).  It's almost like game design within a game.  You need to find a way to exploit any potential thief that enters your home on a meager budget, and then hope that when they die/give-up, you can upgrade your house with the items that they (hopefully) left behind.
I used to compare the building experience as "psychological" or "anticipatory".  While building your home, you needed to think like the robber and predict their every move.  With travel happening on a four-way plane, there's not many choices.  Will they open this door or the other?  Will they break through this wooden wall or the metal one beside it?  Anticipating the players' actions can be beneficial to your own progresss in CD.
The downfall of this game were the players on the wealthy spectrum.  They've built systems utilizing floor-pads that need to be pressed at the right time, in the right order or maybe not at all; and the wrong move means you die or the door (out of many doors) leading forward will be perma-locked.  There can be so much going on behind the walls of some of these houses that it's hard to just guess.  You can brute-force it, but the only people capable of that are the people you're robbing because they can afford to buy all the equipment necessary to break into ANY home.  Even your measly $2000 fortress.  THAT'S why this game is broken.

It's not often I'll write a review for a video game. This is my second. I also plan on appending this at a later date once I have played through the game multiple times.
NieR: Automata follows on from the events of the Drakengard and the original NieR games. None of which I have ever played, or watched, or know anything about before this entry. But amazingly, Automata pulls you into to a story that becomes a small part of you. Now I've done a little research into the previous entries, I understand how some of the elements can tie in to previous games. However, at least in my eyes, the story can stand completely alone.
You play as 2B, a combat android deployed from 'The Bunker' which serves as a base for the military if you will. Earth has been attacked and taken over by aliens and is now inhabited by machines. Along with 9S, a scout android. You begin your journey from humble beginnings to help the humans go back home, after hundreds of years away. Additionally, after you've completed your first playthrough, you can experience new playthroughs with additional content, cutscenes, fights and more. I'm currently on my 2nd, and I hear the 3rd is massively different.
The gameplay is a lot like Bayonetta or Devil May Cry, easy to learn, harder to master, always fun. You can use different weapons, abilities and chipsets (perks that buff you, extra health, easier dodges, lifesteal, that kinda thing). It never gets old and even on normal, whilst not being a particuarly hard game at this level, still challenges you.
Sound, oh boy, the sound. The voice acting, for the most part, is supurb, there's a few minor charecters who could be a little more convincing, but hey, you can't expect perfection. The main cast is voiced flawlessly and whilst the game isn't very dialogue heavy, you grow attached to these characters very quickly. The music is in a league of its own, and whilst it's not the kind of music you would listen to independently, at least for me, it bonds with the visuals and settings perfectly.
Lastly, my final note is a negative. As I have to be fair. It's not an issue with the game itself, but the port. Now, it isn't bad, but its not good either. Personally, I found no issues fps wise. I did however, have an issue with 1080p gameplay, whilst the game itself appeared to be displaying correctly, my steam notifications and fps counter where rendering at 720p. I hear other users have bad fps dips, in which I haven't noticed any.
My advice, if you want the game, you probably already bought it. If you're unsure. Jump in, buy it in a sale or full priced even. I was incredibly surprised and I was half expecting to play it for 2 hours and then never touch it again. This game is a masterpiece in my eyes. I won't forget this game anytime soon. No way.

First and foremost, you need to understand that Saints Row 2 is one of the most abominable ports ever to grace the PC platform. It's notoriously bad, kind of a poster boy for bad ports. If your computer isn't pretty good you're going to have trouble running it, and that generously assumes you're running Gentlemen of the Row (a pretty sweet mod that combines port fixing with some extra content drops.) Don't even think of running the game without modding it, and safe often because crashes can and will happen with regularity.
That aside, many people regard Saints Row 2 to be the best Saints Row game in the series. The engine may be rough around the engines compared to SR3 and SRIV, but it is absolutely brimming with content compared to its successors and Stilwater is a delight to explore compared to Steelport.  There's more to do, the missions aren't going to be slight modifications of activities like you would see in SR3, and the sheer amount of content to discover and explore is amazing.
For players more familiar with the SR2 experience I would also warn that the DLC is exclusive to the 360 version. You may prefer that if you have the title or really want every last drop of content.
Overall if your PC is good and you know what you're doing I would heartily endorse this game as the best in the series.

The Binding of Isaac is an arena style, action-adventure game where it follows the main protagonist, Isaac through the depths of his basement and unknown to escape his insane murderous mother after she receives a sacrifice demand from God. It has an interesting story that is based on events in the Christian religion. This being said, there are many other references such as item names and bosses (Scapular item and Satan boss). You start out with playing Isaac (other characters can be unlocked) battling through six floors until you finally meet and battle your own mother. Additional floors are unlocked with a DLC. The DLC is vital if you want to understand and truly enjoy this game. It unlocks an additional five rooms, all filled with new enemies, new items, and new forms of dark humor, and allows you to generate many more endings, featuring an epic battle against Satan and Isaac himself portraying as a disciple of God.

I remember playing this game long ago, at the time like all MMO's Aura was something fresh for me to jump into and offered a different experience other mmorpgs couldn't give off. Aura Kingdom is a game that's simple to learn and grasp, I was able to get into it and learn a lot of things in a manner of minutes! The variety of classes allows a unique gameplay style for everyone, and the secondary weapon you can get later on just makes things even more challenging and fun.
The biggest pros in my opinion are:
-Variety of classes (more to come!)
-Eidolon systems, you don't need to be a summoner class to get an epic companion to fight with you!
-Awesome flashy skills
-Epic dungeons to explore with friends and intense, challenging fights
-Unique story and background, everything has a story
-How well the game pulls you in, once you start, you really can't stop playing
In contrast however, the cons in my choice are:
-You'll find yourself repeating fetch and kill quests, the occasional special quest with something else to it
-Unable to skip boring cutscenes that last awhile
-How unfair dueling systems can get, a level 70 can challenge a level 30 to a fight, seriously?
-Servers can be unstable time to time
-Leveling, becomes ridiculous in higher levels, quests only bump you up like 2%
The thing fantastic about Aura, there's always something to do, regardless if gameplay becomes reptative. How you play Aura is up to you, but the biggest things you need to remember:
-This is an MMO, if you understand the basics, you'll know long hours and patience go a long way and are needed to enjoy this game
-People have the grinding style of leveling, but in Aura that method won't really work, espicially later on, just do your quests, it wont kill you
I personally enjoy Aura, if you love MMORPG's and want to find one to kill time, have an awesome adventure with friends, or just flat out looking for something new, this is the game for you. I promise its worth every minute of gameplay.

Being the first fighting game to get ported to Linux, I really wanted to enjoy Kings of Kung Fu. But sadly, there is just nothing to enjoy here. For a diehard fighting game fan who has emulated everything I could get my hands on, this even manages to stand out as one of the worst I've ever played.
Movesets are dull and uninspired, as the devs' insistence on realism means there are no projectiles, long range pokes, invincible reversals, mobility options, or anything you could think of that could make for interesting gameplay or matchups. You might as well just stick to your jabs up close and sweeps at range because there's not much else to do. And the input detection somehow manages to be worse than Street Fighter 1, there are a number of moves I simply cannot get to come out ever, and nothing I can do consistently.
During Early Access the developers promised online, only to silently cancel this feature later. So without it you'll be stuck fighting very dull AI that will either stand there and let you hit them or abuse perfect reflexes. You'll find yourself falling back on just sweeping as they wake up over and over, since they don't understand what to do about that. Again, it manages to be worse than even the earliest fighting games and learn nothing from decades of evolution in the genre.
Perhaps if you have a lot of nostalgia for the films that inspired these characters, you may get some amusement out of the fanservice. But if you came here looking for an actual good fighting game, look elsewhere.

looking for a great strategy game? tired of the boring mechanics of the "one more turn" games where you mostly just wait for the next thing to happen?  where most factions end up feeling the same in the end?
thats how i felt when i picked up dominions and found, to my delight, an endless playground of fantastic mytho-historical epic religious wars.  none of that "just one more turn" crap.  dominions doesn't suck you in by making addictive gameplay, it compels you to discover what can happen in the myriad worlds that are created when new games begin.
here's some examples:
Being able to recruit Elephant units, I decide I might as well rely on them to stomp through a bunch of independent provinces, letting my horde of archers fire safely from behind my Elephant squad that just tramples everything.  Until I brashly attack a swamp province where a few wights weilding Bane Blades confront my Elephants without fear, hacking into them and causing Decay status to quickly start killing my elephants... which saps their morale, which causes Elephant Squad to rout, trampling over my archers and making the whole army retreat in shame...
Playing as the Arthurian inspired nation of Man, my god the Tiwaz of War leads a huge army of archers shooting flame arrows, blessed swordsman, summoned creatures, and knights into the capitol of the bird nation Caelum.  I've already destroyed most of their standing army and expect to take their capitol easily.  Too bad I didn't count on their god being a fountain of blood that none of my units could seem to damage... the fountain rained lightning bolts and other magicks down upon my army and routed it, leaving me drained and confused about how to regroup.
I'm an underwater Arch Mage with godlike powers riding on a giant lobster.  I hear the distant call of the ancient ones from the nation Rlyeh, the madness that is Lovecraft and Cthulu.  My dominion spreads insanity and death wherever it goes, and hordes of insane cult members flock to join my army.  Tentacled Illithids and Star Spawn are the commanders of this rabble, using their mind power to dominate those with weak will.  Strange alien beasts appear through the star portal to serve, to bring about the dominion of the Dreamlands, madness for all...
I'm a fountain.  Not a fountain of blood, but an Oracle, the god of the fairy folk who were driven into hiding when men came to Ireland.  My army is small, but powerful, the Sidhe and Tuatha have the power of Glamour, and appear to be in many places at once.  With my powerful bless, a small group of Sidhe warriors can stand up to a whole army and turn it to rout.
Now imagine a game where all of this is true at the same time, ideally with humans driving these nations.  An epic Play by Email experience awaits!

KOF 98 was one of the greatest games in The King of Fighters franchise. And when KOF 98 Ultimate Match first came out in consoles, it has major improvements compared to the original, including ALL the characters from KOF 94 to KOF 97. Unfortunately, the Steam port is a crippled version of the console versions, especially regarding visuals and music. While in the PlayStation2 version you could choose between the classic 2D and re-vamped 3D stages, and between the original soundtrack from the NeoGeo arcades and the arranged soundtrack that played in the original console ports, the Steam version comes only with 2D stages, and the NeoGeo's OST. No options to choose 3D stages or arranged music at all. This was a disappointment to me. Overall, the game itself still retains most of the original's essence, but it lacks features the console versions had. It simply makes no sense, does it?

While I would recommend that people who are, like me, interested in fgighting games but not very good at them start with KoF XIII, KoF98 is certainly worth your time if you fancy something a bit more complex, featuring as it does 3 core systems and over 40 characters. I only occassionally play it compared to KoF XIII's solid mechanics and KoF 2002's insane roster of characters but KoF98 has a lot of little charms that are missing from the latter games. The stages are more characterful and change between bouts with all sorts of little details hidden away that they didn't seem to bother with in the later games. There's a lot more character interactions before the start of rounds which is an excellent way of fleshing out who these characters are and how they relate to one another without resorting to sometimes lengthly dialogue excahnages as you get in KoF XIII and Blazblue. It's probably the toughest of the KoF games on Steam and because of it's multiple systems, has a lot more depth to it but it also has some of the most overpowered characters as well (Orochi in particular).
The bottom line: If you're a casual fighting fan like me then KoF 98 offers a good roster of characters and some of the best visual design in the genre (which is why I like it) but KoF XIII is generally prettier and a lot easier to get into.

Polarity is a short, Portal-type game, but slightly changed. If the game is 95%+ off at the time of you reading this, it's worth the 30 cents or less. When the game is not on sale, it charges a whooping $11. I played for 2 hours, and beat most of the game. (with only a few bonus levels remaining) The game advertises a co-op mode with a few more levels. I managed to beat all of these alone. Only 1 or 2 of the co-op levels actually require 2 people. Even in these "2-people parts," you can still manage to do it alone with some timing. The game only has 37 levels, most of which are easy and take less than 5 minutes each. Most of my gameplay time was me getting stuck trying to figure out how to get an optional prism, which are like stars in other games. 3 per level. If I had just skipped past this, I would've completed the main "story" in about 20-30 minutes. I spent a good 40 minutes fumbling around in 1 level for 1 prism. The bonus levels shouldn't exist, and be implemented into the main "story," as they're the same as the regular levels, with no added challenge, like most games' bonus levels. The game also continuously adds new mechanics to the levels. At first, you might think this adds challenge. It does not. With each new mechanic, an older one is removed. By the end of the "story," you have about the same amount of mechanics as there were in say, level 4. I do not recommend this game, unless of course it is $0.30 or less, then, I believe, it is worth that amount.

Nier Automata is many steps up in terms of gameplay from the original Nier. Combat is fun, beautiful and works fluidly and is by far the saving grace of this game. As a standalone game, Nier Automata is relatively decent. However, when compared with its predecessor, from my perspective, the game falls flat in terms of memorability and lacks the beauty, charm and soul of the original.
The game's soundtrack is by no means bad, but it is in no way even remotely as grand as the original Nier. It is certainly many steps backwards.
Character development seems extraordinarily rushed and while 2B and 9S are "cool", you really couldn't care too much about them. 2B has known 9S only for a terribly short amount of time and yet, it's as if they've known eachother for years and have gone through hell with eachother time again about 5 minutes after they meet.  The entire cast of the game is easily forgotten, whereas in the original you WILL remember and mourn every character in your party, and the NPCs you come across.
The story certainly isn't in the least memorable. It's bland, predictable and certainly what you'd expect from the modern day hack & slash RPG. This is especially so if you compare it to the first game, which to this day sends shivers down my spine with how haunting it is. For new players, while there are a number of references to the original, you won't miss anything too important if you haven't played it. The story has multiple endings which require multiple playthroughs, which provides a "new perspective" on the game as the developers like to put it, which is also a welcome addition and does show some level of dedication in the development of Nier Automata.
In terms of bugs, there are few that I have encountered and absolutely none that have been gamebreaking. All issues related to the gameplay and sorted themselves out without my intervention.
If you're searching for a game that will stay with you forever, you absolutely MUST play the original NieR on PS3/XBOX360. If you're looking for a fun hack & slash to pass the time and you're not interested in a great story or don't have time to be immersed into a virtual world and become involved with the characters, then this game is certainly recommended. It is by no means a bad game, just not a great one when compared with the original.
