Excellent! Somewhat plasticky, but for the price it is really good and the hardware seems really well thought out. Configuration is a pain in many games if they do not support controllers directly, but they've done all they can to ease that process with developer recommended profiles, community shared profiles, templates etc. You can't really beat mouse and keyboard for a lot of things, such as FPS gaming or RTS, but this thing makes them playable on a controller, which is no small feat. I think the Steam controller is pretty much everything I hoped it to be, but I think I didn't have unrealistic expectations to begin with.

So! This is BRAND NEW controller technology, it's never been done before!! It's a controller that's meant to bridge the gap between traditional controllers and mouse and keyboard combos!
Taking that into mind, and understanding that this type of input device is the first of it's kind, you need to make your purchase knowing that NO ONE is a master at using this input (yet) and that it has a learning curve. No one, I repeat NO ONE will open the box, set it up on Steam, open a game and feel just like they're playing with their old controllers. You will NOT be a pro right out of the box.
Now that that disclaimer has been said, and you're thoroughly frightened, let me reassure you. You can adjust ANYTHING on this device. ANYTHING. Deadzones, sensitivity, haptic feedback levels, control types. Do you want the pad to simulate a mouse? A trackball mouse? A joystick? Do you want mouse acceleration? Do you want smoothing? So on and so on.
So at first, I came in with the impression that WOW, this is going to be exciting and work great! And so I thought, what better way to test and celebrate Valve's first foray into hardware than to fire up Half Life 2 and kill some Ant Lions?
Welp, it was difficult. I felt that it was too slow at times and when I wanted to make diagonal movements while aiming, it wanted to choose the absolute of either UP or DOWN. I did my best, I tried adjusting the configurations (which as of now can only be adjusted in BPM FML.) but just couldn't get it right.
Frustrated with my purchase, I decided to truly put the controllers feet to the fire by taking it into one of my favorite, frenetic, high energy, twitchy first person shooters, Robot Roller Derby Disco Dodgeball.
I went to make a configuration, and noticed that the developer himself had made a binding for the game (Erik you rock!) and so I chose that, and went into my game.
Huh... I was actually doing pretty well for once! So I kept playing round after round in arcade mode, and eventually beat one of the bosses. I was aiming well, and twitching around corners and landing hits like it was nothing! I finally felt vindicated in my purchase.
I realized, maybe Eriks configuration is my preferred style. So, I set up my Half Life 2 game to have the same config as RRDDD and voila... It was great. Well, not PERFECT yet, but I made more adjustments and was doing quite well.
In the end, this controller is about practice. If you purchase it, don't throw a fit because you're suddenly crappy in games you're normally great in. With adjustments (you WILL make adjustments, don't get this controller if you prefer a plug and play kind of experience) you'll get comfortable in no time.
Also, as of now, 10/17/2015, before the official release, there are some software bugs. For instance, if you set the left circle pad to be a left joystick while the right circle pad is the same, you'll have some ghost movements that are especially noticeable when navigating menus.
One more thing, firmware updates will be coming for this controller, and we've got an amazing PC modding community that is actively being encouraged to play with this thing, and it's so versatile, I can't wait to see what they come up with. I mean, right now, while I have Steam open, I'm able to use the controller as a mouse to left click, right click and use my computer from my bed! I'm browsing the web right now with it. (Not typing with it though, I can't bring up the keyboard interface outside of Steam... YET, wait for those mods!)
Okay finally, I recommend this controller. But only for those of you who like tweaking things, and want a comfortable way to play all your PC games from your bed/couch/bathroom.
UPDATE: 11/10/2015
Just to add, I LOVE using this controller outside of games to just use my computer casually. It's terrific for just replacing your mouse. Whenever they release the ability to use the steam on screen keyboard then I'll be set. Also, I haven't noticed any bugs with the firmware anymore. I use this controller every day, I LOVE IT NOW. Also, I've gotten to the point where I match my abilities with keyboard and mouse, with the steam controller. It has effectively replaced my keyboard and mouse in gaming. Excellent work Valve.
UPDATE: 7/5/2016
They DID add an update to use the keyboard outside of Steam. Double click the joystick and bam, there it is. Love it.

I adore it, I really do, because It is a big jump to a new way to play games. I don't think it's COMPLETE yet, but it is a major step forward, and the fact that it can get software updates to improve it is a major attribute. As EVERYONE says, it has a learning curve, but the learning curve is as big as you make it. If you want to master every possible way to use the controller then it is gonna be a while. If you pick a format and stick with it, it doesn't take too long. One of the major improvements over another game pad is it can be configured and told to work like something else, making it adaptive... but this makes it a lot more to learn then a simple controller.
The problems i have with it? A few things i thought there would would that there isn't. MOST of these missing things can be fixed via additions in the future. As of this writing, some things the controller should be able to do but can't is...
*Can't map a button to bring up the keyboard
*Can't make the gyro work as a 'shock' senser and only respond to quick movements.
*Can't select the analog mimicing trackpad mode on some games
As for general Pros
+It also for vast new options and customization and tweeking of the way you play.
+it is comfortable and my hands actually rest in the perfect place for it.
+Battery life is weirdly good.
+Haptic feedback is freaky cool
+The grip buttons is something every controller in history needs. Jump has a new home.
++ Many other small things that i get as i go along.
Cons
-Learning curve
-Adapting the controller to you takes time, and it is hard to tell if some tweek you're making is because of the learning curve or because this is an actual improvement.
-The Analog stick mode of the track pad... doesn't feel quite right, i've practiced it a bit and most of the time it is extremely hard to control. I can't tell yet if this is just another thing i need to adapt to or not but all the other trackpad modes don't act so weird.
-The customization menu needs some work. It feels a bit messy.
My suggestion for those considering buying it? Are you patient, interested in someting new, and okay with exiting your comfort zone? If yes, get one. If no, find someone with one and try it out for a bit, if it peaks your intrest still, THEN buy one. It is $50, not too much money to drop on something that could change how you game.

If you want my simplest opinion, "Is Stellaris worth it?", then stop right now, and go and by Stellaris + Utopia + Synthetic Dawn. If you want reasons:
In Stellaris you can create you're own species, determine it's govermenta; structure, it's stance to war, aliens, spirituality and  whether or not you can have slaves. You then pick a starting weapons type (From a choice of mediocre, terrible or kinetic) your starting FTL (Slow, Restricted by lanes, restricted by stations) and off you go to conquer the stars.
Or not. To give some context, the only other space 4x I've played is StarDrive 2. It uses a Civilisation style of production, aka, each planet produce production units per turn and that gradually build's something. In Stellaris, instead you gather minerals which are placed into an empire wide pool and then are used to buy buildings, ships and space stations which take time to construct. Notably, this gives a lot more of a starting choice. Do you rush an (extremely) early colony ship, or do you start exploiting all the resources you can access from orbit? The latter is cheaper and provides and earlier return, but that colony provides more benefits longer term.
So Stellaris is a lot more interesting in it's early game content. Rather than setting a planet's production queue and then leaving it, you have a bit more interaction in this process, which is increased by the fact that planets have tiles, which serve as both building slots and income. Building a mine on top of a rich resource deposit adds the output of the two together, meaning that you do have to take some input in how you build planets.
The mid game however is where things collapse awkwardly. The tiled planets pose an issue in the amount of micro require per planet, though that is offset by the fact you can hand them over to the AI and not have to touch them. Then, once you've amassed a large fleet, you "Doomstack" it, FTL it into enemy territory/fleet, have a big fight, then the winner spends the next 5 years invading enough planets to force the peace it wants. Then you wait 10 years of truce and bingo, round 2!
Except that you'll have snowballed even stronger in those 10 years.
Late game there's some items to shake up the balance of power, such as end game crisises and Awakened Fallen Empires, but a player on a roll can often crush these too easily.
However... where does Utopia and Synthetic Dawn come into this? Stellaris by itself is alright, but those two DLC give the game alot more variety. Utopia gives ascenscion paths, megastructures and biological hiveminds, while Synthetic Dawn gives the ability to start as machine hiveminds, including the Borg. The increase in variety helps stave off the feeling of "been there done that" that can take over in the mid-late game, and combined with Leviathans and Horizon Signal give's Stellaris a lot of replayability.

The game has been officially released so here are my thoughts about this title. First of all i wanna congratulate the small developing team for bringing such a game to life. Its really nice to know that there are so many passionate indie game developers that can offer so much for so little. Kings of Kung Fu is an original fighting game, based on old kung fu movies and the game itself couldnt be a more sheer tribute to those films. Now on to the game itself.
The good stuff:
1. Amazing nostalgia feelings for the old Kung fu movie era
2. One of the greatest soundtracks i have ever heard, homage to those old movies style
3. Full and interesting and everexpanding roster of characters based on real fighters (Bruce Lee and Chuck Norris!!!)
4. Great level design and amazing details to make you feel like you are a part of a kung fu movie.
5. Nice and easy gameplay, but hard to master.
The bad stuff:
1. Controls are not as responsive as they should be.
2. Combos are hard to master
3. Combat still has some bugs that need to be wiped out (you can win a whole round just by doing low right kick ^^)
4. Graphics are really nice and polished, but for this day and age not the top quality i would like.
5. No online multiplayer
To conclude, for me Kings of Kung fu is a really good game. It has some flaws, but considering the effort it has been made by a rather small team, i would say this is something most of us can pass through. For the most part its a really enjoyable game and you will have tons of fun playing either by yourself or with some of your m8s locally. At the moment there is no online multiplayer, so i know for a lot of you thats a turn off, but still it could happen in the future. If you like old Kung Fu movies and if you ever wanna see what it Feels like to be Bruce Lee facing Chuck Norris once more, buy this little gem ^^

A huge disappointment. The new characters are interesting, it's great to have Extra mode be useful for once, and the balance changes are welcome, but the good pretty much ends there. The netcode, even after multiple patches, is questionable at best --- playing the original '98 with proper rollback is still the way to go. The exclusion of 3D backgrounds and an arranged soundtrack is no tragedy, and the game is perfectly playable without them, but still rather bothersome. The real problem lies with the game itself --- the damage has been turned far, far down from the original '98. The amount of health that each character has is more akin to XIII than the older entries. This would be perfectly fine for a game like 2002, where long combos dominate high level play, but a huge part of '98's appeal is the lack of such combos: most of everything is under ten hits, just enough that learning combos will give most players an edge, but huge combos do not dominate competitive play and the game remains tactically well-rounded. Turning the damage down in such a game makes matches draw on for a bit too long, long enough to stagnate. As a result, Time Outs are far more common in this game than in the original '98, and strong tactics are far less threatening --- the game is less about being constantly on your toes and more about getting your opponent into a situation where you can hit them with your character's best tactics several times in a row in order to do as much damage as using that tactic once would do in the original '98.
Some older fighting games just don't really translate well into the modern scene --- see Super Street Fighter II Turbo HD Remix for a perfect example. It might seem like a good idea to tune down damage and nerf strong tactics for these games at face value, but this ultimately destroys much of what made these games popular to begin with. The reason why people still play Super Street Fighter II Turbo, Samurai Shodown II, Street Fighter Alpha 3, and indeed King of Fighters '98 is that they are very high risk/high reward at all levels of play. One mistake can doom a player for an entire match in these games. There's a sort of tension to these games that modern fighting games lack almost entirely (though they make up for it in other aspects). This revision fails to capture this almost entirely. It tailors the game to a modern audience --- one that has King of Fighters XIII anyway, and has demonstrated time and time again that it doesn't care about this game in the slightest, as this game failed in arcades and failed to make it into any major tournaments.
If you just want the new characters and don't mind gimped damage and weakened tactics with almost nothing to replace them, this game is decent. However, the original version of this game is the way to go if you value the things that made it fun. Most people should either play the original '98 on GGPO or Fightcade or something, wait for King of Fighters 2002 Ultimate Match, which translates far better into a modern setting, or just get King of Fighters XIII.

I had some reservations at first about whether the changes added to KOF '98 warranted its rerelease and sale price. After some time with it, it's become clear that this tweaked and expanded version truly is a worthy update to one of the best fighting games ever made. A handful of new characters expand the roster a bit, but the addition of a significant amount of alternate versions of both pre-existing and new characters really beef up your options for team creation nicely. The changes are rounded out by a slight rebalance, the addition of a new mode to Advanced and EX, and online matchmaking. Throwing in the original version as well was a nice touch. Most of the criticism leveled at this game seems to come from the fact that it's not the PS2 version. This is still one of the most rock-solid fighting games in existence, with or without a few cosmetic bells and whistles, the absence of which hardly justifies a negative review. It's colorful, balanced, charming, fun, and accessible. If you're new to KOF and cut your teeth on XIII, pick this one up and get a taste of fighting's golden age; There's a good chance you'll find this game superior to its later installments. If you're a Neo Geo veteran, you'll come to enjoy the changes even if you're a hardened purist.

Great game all around, however the PC port is simply horrendous. Get the Gentlemen of The Row mod, and be sure to turn Dynamic Lighting ingame to Simple, but also be sure to turn Ambient Occlusion to All. Dynamic Lighting at all kills FPS on any system, but leaving it at simple w/o Ambient Occlusion make the game look like complete♥♥♥♥♥♥ AO at all will not make the game unplayable, and will also improve the visuals significantly. Now, the game itself:
PROS:
-Great storyline (SRTT and SRIV have comparatively weak stories)
-Ridiculous amounts of fun (like Saints Row has always had)
-Stilwater > Steelport
-More character customization than SRTT (SRIV does contend, however)
-Beautifully constructed world (unfortunately marred by the otherwise horrendous PC port)
-Fun Co-Op that can still be enjoyed today thanks to mods.
CONS:
-Horrible Port (can be fixed but I still can't hit constant 60 FPS without making it look absolutely terrible)
-Won't appeal to people that prefer the newer games (this game still has a Grand Theft Auto feel to it, whereas SRTT and SRIV are completely unique)
-DAMN THE STUPID SPEEDUP BUG (ruined 25 percent of my story immersion). Fortunately it can be fixed.
-Audio quality for everything is abysmal compared to 360 and PS3. The radio stations can be fixed, but the SFX and Voices are stuck at Compressed Bit Syndrome (Mod fixes are in development)
CONCLUSION:
I got this game with the Ultimate Franchise Pack on Summer Sale for $11, so I cannot complain. However, for $10 standalone you will need to have lots of patience for me to recommend this.

How best to put my experience with the Steam Controller...?  If you were given a test, and the question was, "Game Controller?", this would be the wrong answer.  I have been using game controllers all my life (born and bred on the NES before PC).  While keyboard & mouse are great, I have always felt more comfortable with a game pad.
It really feels like the designers of the Steam Controler went out of their way to design a game pad that was the opposite of everything that came before it.  The stick and buttons are opposite where you would find them on every other controller that has come before it.
Nothing feels "right" with this pad.  The N64 controller felt more like the "correct answer" than the STeam Controller.  When I first laid it in my hand, it instantly felt wrong.  The buttons and pads felt out of reach, and oddly placed.  To go from an Xbox 360 controller to the Steam controller requires extra thinking because the buttons are not where one would expect.  The triggers sit back in the pad, rather than forward.  With the right pad being touch sensitive, it is difficult to get a proper grip to aim with the right pad and fire with the trigger at the same time.  After a short period of time, one's hands become a fumbling mess trying to perform all the functions required.  The lack of a "solid" feel is further embelished by the fact that the whole thing just feels cheap and flimsy.
This whole project needs to be scraped and follow a more standardized concept.  I have been looking to replace my game pad for a long time.  The Steam Controller is not the answer to my desire.

I've been using this for 2 weeks now, and I'm 100% sure I'll never play a game with K&M and Xbox controller again. This is hands down the best controller on the market. It achieves everything it set out to do, and greatly enhanced my gaming experience.
However, there's one catch.
It has a very steep learning curve. It's like learning a musical instrument, like a violin. Everyone has to go through the stage when your "music" sounds like slaughtering pig. And it could be very frustrating. I, like many people, felt very dissappinted during the first few hours, when I couldn't even finish the regular difficulty of a CoD campaign.
And just like learning to play a violin, once you pass the initial learning stage, it gets better and better, until you realize you are holding one of the most beatiful and versitile instrument ever created.
I whole-heartedly recommend this to anyone with the time and will to learn it.

I really like the game, I really do, but this game has a crazy amount of problems...
Because of this, you have to wait again for 1-10 minutes, and if this happens again, you need to wait again, and again, and again... Several times it happened that matchmaking failed 3-5 times in a row, because of that it took 30-40 minutes of waiting  before the match starts.
A terrible team balance, sometimes you can get in team 2 unranked persons, 1 gold, 1 platinum, when other team can get 2 masters, 1 diamond, and 3 platinum players. Same with the profile level, one team can get almost all players with a profile level of 50-60, when in the second team 80-170. Same with character levels... I can't call this a good balance, it's a terrible balance. Almost all the matches is an one-sided slaughter, either your team or the enemy team is completely crushed, battles on the equals is a very big rarity.
Bad balance of characters. The thing is that the game has a very large number of characters, much more than the Overwatch has for example. I understand that it's very difficult to balance them all properly, and especially the new characters which just appeared in the game, too often they always too overpowered, and that's all still fine, but the problem is in other things...
Too often they buff and nerf the wrong characters, or the wrong skills, or the wrong stats of the characters. No, they do not return the character to the state in which he was before, THEY CHANGE ALL THE CHARACTERS SO THAT THEY WILL FIT THE BALANCE OF THE CHANGED CHARACTER, and guess what, of course they fail in this, and the balance becomes a complete mess, they are trying to balance even more, and each time they make this worse and worse, worse and worse...
I also like the card system in this game, but the way they implemented it completely ruins the game... The one who has a good deck has a really big advantage against players who do not have it, and play with a standard deck. I tried myself to play with a standard and customized deck, and depending on the character it becomes easier to play in 2-8 times.
The problem is that you can not create your own deck for free, you need to grind, and grind very and very a lot to have a possibility to create a deck for all the characters, my counter now shows that I spent 366 hours in the game, and I'm not even close to creating decks for even half of the characters. Plus you can not buy cards for gold, you are buying them for another currency, and it grinds a lot more slower than gold! And all of that leads to the fact that you have to play only as a couple of your main characters, and it's sucks hard!
But all of that is not the worst thing in the game...
The most terrible thing in this game, is bugs fixing. Almost everything is broken in this game, animation, skills, ults, interface, and a lot of game mechanics. Sometimes animations break down, and you can not see your weapon, and your weapon attack animation (bullets, flames, lightning, etc.), or in the third-person mode (even when using skills that forces the third person mode, like a Fernando shield), the character can just move backwards, or something like that. Also, the animation of the enemy can break, and because of that it will be difficult to understand what is your enemy doing, because you do not see his animations, and whether he attacks, when he is protected, and etc, it's just 3d model without animation that slides on the floor. In one patch even the animation of death for one character was broken, it was the same thing that I described above, except for one exception... The enemy froze in a pose lying on the floor, so his body was sliding on the ground (but in fact he was alive), and because of that it was difficult to see him, plus to cause damage, you need to hit not where the enemy is, you need to hit in his character model, so it completely broke the character's hitbox. I mean, it's fine when character is standing, but not when he is lying on the floor. Skills and ults sometimes just do not work, especially ults, they may not work until you'll die. Today I had an endless double jump playing as Meave, well, kind of... I could jump in the air an infinite number of times, but instead of giving me a boost, they make me glide in the air. Plus the controls was very strange and buggy, I do not even know how to describe... I could describe bugs in this game for a long time, but there are too many of them!

Because the development team is focused on creating new skins, each patch has a tons of new skins, but this does not fix bugs, and with each new patch there is more and more bugs appears, with each new patch the game literally becomes less and less playable, and this is what I do not like the most about this game.
When I started playing, I really liked the game, but with every patch the game became more and more glitchy, until we began to have what we have now...
I can't recommend this game, if you have money and you want to play in something like this, to be honest, just buy Overwatch, it a lot more polished than this game.

I admit I went into this with a dismissive attitude, expecting to write a negative review. And sure, it is no masterpiece. But then I remembered I'm hardly the target audience here. I would say this game is aimed at 5-9 year olds and the more I think about it, the better suited for them it seems. The graphics, the jokes, the pacing, the minigames... all of it is properly tailored for that age group. It manages to convey just enough tidbits of historical info without risking boredom. And it strikes a surprisingly skillful balance between joking about the subject matter and being serious about it (leaning towards the former).
Again, it's not the most impressive piece of educational gaming ever; it's kinda barely average. Yet it's a net positive. Also it has a minigame where you stack bodies like you would blocks in Tetris. How could I downthumb that.

Hey kids, want to learn about the Plague?
This point and click adventure game intends to teach children about black plague while guiding the child protagonist on minor tasks with the ultimate goal of curing his ailing mother.
The game takes a challenging approach to this issue buy showing how finding the real answer to the plague first required eliminating the wrong ones.  Unfortunately this is weakened by being unclear at times what things should be learned as true or understood as past mistakes.
Gameplay is pretty standard point and click fetch quests with the occasional mini game to break up the flow.  These minigames felt unnecessary and at times, such as stacking corpses failed to put a fun face on the macabre.

"Playing History" are nice little educational point-and-click adventures. The Plague explains you reasons and causes and let you be a little detective to find a cure for your mother. The text is rich, the graphics are poor. And it has some little savegame bugs and no further achievement descriptions. But with a little combine they are doable in no time. Very weird is the dealing with dead bodies. There's even a body tetris minigame. LOL

The game is point-and-click based and comes up with some small riddles, puzzles and hidden combinmations. You can gather items and money to complete certain side quests and the main story.
The game is quite short but has a charm to it which kept me at it. Totally recommend this if you want to beat an hour.
Also perfect for kids.

Aside from being able to play KOF'98 within STEAM, against players from every corner of the world, this game is a disappointment.
Allow me to explain: SNK released this game two times: First in arcades, using Taito X2 hardware and some time after in Playstation 2.
The version currently in STEAM is a direct arcade conversion. The arcade version is the NEO-GEO version with all the characters and fancy menus.
The PS2 version of this game features a enhanced soundtrack, taken from arranged albums of the KOF series, 3D rendered backgrounds and several improvements over the arcade.
It's kinda sad that SNK pushed an inferior port to STEAM in order to make more money. You see, the Taito X2 hardware is essentialy PC hardware, so they have done a minimal effort to bring this to us. The PS2 version should take more money, so they went with the cheaper solution.
Do not buy it, unless you don't have access to a PS2 or you desperately crave online matchmaking.

To try and describe Saints Row 2 without mentioning the Grand Theft Auto series is nearly impossible, which is a shame. It is a shame because, for all intents and purposes, Saints Row 2 stands on its own two feet, and improves on many elements of the open world formula. While the game's graphics are less than perfect, and the controls can be a bit finnicky depending on one's system, the gameplay itself and the nearly endless facets of it are where this game shines. Where San Andreas had the player customizing CJ, Saints Row 2 has the player customizing everything from his or her character to the cars, weapons and safe houses that dot the game's map.
The game's biggest shortcoming is a lack of scope, and this is one of the few areas where the Grand Theft Auto series outshines all others. The game consists almost entirely of taking over territories and decimating enemy gangs through story-driven missions. While this is hardly a failure of Volition, it does pale in comparison to a game like GTA: San Andreas, in which story missions and territories played only a small part of a bigger picture.
In conclusion, despite being a lackluster PC port, Saints Row 2 is an incredibly enjoyable and insane ride, and certainly not one to be skipped. Its endless amount of customization endear it, and allow for countless hours of replayability.

If you're looking to downvote this because it's "Recommended", I'd ask you not to but this is the internet, anyone can voice their opinion. Thus, I'd like to kindly ask you don't silence mine and instead give me a rebuttal in the comments, I'd love to hear your side of the story :)
Coming from someone who was an initial investor of Minecraft's Alpha (stopped playing end of 2013 as university began right after school and other reasons), I really like what Telltale have achieved. Yes, it's not "sandbox", if you were expecting that from Minecraft:"Story Mode" then you are sorely mistaken. I'd imagine if this is a success for both Microsoft and Telltale that future stories could be told. It is not without its faults, but if you look past its issues you will find a potentially great story.
You play as Jesse, and you choose the gender. 3 skins for each gender, with varying skin tones and similar clothing. I think Telltale have done a nice thing there, because while it's still not "you", YOU yourself are controlling how Jesse interacts with their friends and environment.
The story in a nutshell is [four] heroes (dubbed The Order of the Stone) from decades ago fought the Ender Dragon (the final boss of Minecraft, you must take a portal to reach its dimension) and saved the world. Jump to recent times, Jesse and their friends (while they may not know it yet) are budding heroes with skills akin to the original four. Jesse and their friends meet with a new mob (something new, no spoilers from me!) that threatens their world. It's up to these brave young souls to find the remnants of the Order and save the world once again.
In essence it has all the Telltale aspecs to the game - Dialogue choices being good/neutral/a♥♥♥♥♥♥ dramatic cliffhangers, fighting scenes, quick time events - and it does these parts pretty well. I won't lie, the fighting scenes and quick time events are more lenient but that doesn't mean they aren't without context or feel "useless". As for the maturity, there is still swearing (hell, crap) and
. Voice acting is on point, I can't say much about it as it's my opinion but it has Lee-♥♥♥♥ing-Everett in it, and Pee Wee Herman!
So where does it fall short? The story is pretty predictive, I kind of see us becoming the next "heroes" (everyone has a trait akin to the original Stone members). The animations can be clunky at times, with character voices not synchronised. Lastly, the only other thing I can nitpick is there's not too much room for exploration. Most of the other games while also linear stories had areas you could explore (still to a point, but there was more to uncover, side stories, etc).
For what it's worth, hold off unless you're feeling like you want to invest. In my humble opinion, I have faith in Telltale to complete their content in a quality and timely manner so paying $30 Aussie dollars is justified.

Rising Storm 2: Vietnam is a first person shooter that is similar to the likes of Battlefield as the levels are larger than games like Day of Infamy and also include helicopters as pilotable air vehicles.  Nothing is locked from the start, you can pick any class if it is available.  No weapon unlocks just skin unlocks which make zero difference other than the kevlar for the US forces.  The basic one is a bit bright and easy to see.
The game is good but it also has its issues.  For instance, latency on US servers is rediculous.  I'm in Texas and I join servers relatively close to me and still get 60-120 ping.  This isn't an internet issue on my end as I have zero problems with everything else I play and my connection is fiber with low latency and high bandwidth.  Other issues that plague the game are getting stuck on things in levels and hit registering.  While I don't have nearly the amount of problems with hits registering in RS2 compared ot DoI, its still a small problem.  I don't notice it unless its obvious, like when I am point blank and dump a whole mag into someone and they turn around and kill me.
Outside of those issues, the game plays well and all the weapons feel balanced.  People will always moan and groan over things like flamethrowers but their range is so limited that if you got burnt up by it then its your own fault.  Adjusting the sights of your weapons and taking into account bullet trajectory is a big deal for longer range weapons and using the RPG and grenade launchers.  Getting hit in RS2 can mean death or wounded.  Sometimes you can bandage sometimes you are hosed.  In the end, I find most of my deaths are from stupidity of the moment although I don't die that often at all.
The first thing you are going to notice are those that run into battle and moan and groan that they died.  This is not a Call of Duty game and you will get rocked doing that.  Slow and steady, check your area move as a squad.  The commander is a pivotal role in the game, if for any reason there is none, assume command.  If you don't and no one else does you are losing out on artillery, napalm, respawns, recon, etc.  I would rather have a bad commander than no commander.  Squad leaders are responsible for marking targets, digging tunnels, and being a spawn point for your squad.  When playing RS2, play...your....role!
As far as the graphics go, they are mediocre.  It isn't a AAA game and was never trying to be.  I find the sounds to be fairly decent and the controls, for the most part, to function correctly.  I have had a few times where I watched my guy reload the weapon and I pull the trigger and "click".....fuhk....  It happens but doesn't happen often enough to matter.
I think one of the biggest detractors from the actual gameplay that aren't bugs are the lack of levels.  There are hardly and levels to play while more is being promised later this year.  While this doesn't matter that much to me, it does to others and causes a mediocre playerbase.  Around 1000-2000 players during peak time and a bit lower during non-peak.  This isn't to say I have never had a problem getting into a server but it can be irritating to get into a queue because only 8 or 9 servers are running and all full.  Getting into another server that is empty rarely results in it filling up.  Better marketing, less bugs, and more levels would breathe better life into this game.  I really enjoy playing it, it fills that hole in FPS gaming for me as I am a bit older these days and the slower nature of the game suits me.

In valves attempt to bring PC gaming into the living room like consoles and still keep the PC performance they launched 3 new pieces of hardware. The steam machine which is supposed to be a affordable PC, the steam Link which allows people to steam from there PC to their TV wirelessly and still retain 60 FPS, and what I will talk about today; The steam controller.
At first glance the steam controller looks very odd. Unlike any controller it’s concave instead of convex. Also there are two touchpads. The touchpad on the right can emulate an analog stick, touch pad, and a track ball. The one on the left can emulate the same thing as the right touch pad. Both touch pads can also work as D-Pads. There is only 1 analog stick and it’s on the lower left of the controller. This at first felt very weird but after time I felt I prefered the touchpad instead on a second analog stick in most cases. Another weird this is where the face buttons are. Unlike the 360 or dualshock controller the face buttons are below the touchpad and a little to the right like the wii u pro controller or gamepad. For me this felt more natural since I had time to adjust to the pro controller but I know most people don’t have a wii u so this  may take a while to get used to. Luckily on the back of the controller there and 6 buttons. There are 2 dual stage triggers on on both side with can be used as analog or digital, or both at the same time.The bottom two buttons can act as their own button or they can replace another button such as the A and B button. I personally have them replace the A and B button so rarely have to take my hands off the touch pads but it’s all personal preference. Overall the Steam Controller looks very cool and it’’s very comfortable to hold. It has a decent weight to it and feels pretty durable. OK now that I went over the controller I’m going to talk about how it performs ingame. To get ingame you just hit the team logo in the middle while logged into steam on your PC. You can also hit the controller in the upper right on the steam page when you're logged in. This will take you into BIg Picture Mode. Big picture mode has all the things you normally can do in steam but allows it to be easily navigable with a controller. Ill talk more about it later. Head to your library and select a game.You are able to select template if it already has contoller support or you can choose user made templates even if it doesn’t. You can also make you’re own and make it the perfect setup for any game  The first genre i’m going to go over is Platformers.
This controller is GREAT for platformers. It’s had instant responsiveness to my inputs and is very precise. I actually found myself using the back 2 button to replace the A and B buttons in games like Sonic Generations. This allowed me not to have to jump between buttons to perform multiple actions. This also worked fell for precision retro 2D platformers like AVGN adventures and Shovel Knight. Bit Trip runner also worked really well and I was able to not use the face buttons at all. The steam controller is one of the best controllers for Platform games and is MUCH better than using a keyboard.
As I launched CSGO I didn’t have a good feeling, controllers have always been 10 times worse than keyboard and mouse for FPS. Surprisingly it works really well but it depends on the template. It works better than any other controller. It’s nowhere near as good as a keyboard and mouse but when the touch pad's sensitivity is cranked up it’s actually quite enjoyable to use. Single Player games like Wolfenstein and Half Life 2 work the best because you don’t have to compete against people with a Keyboard and mouse, putting you at a huge disadvantage. The ability to sit back and play a FPS without using a 360 or dualshock controller which are horrible for FPS was really nice. In competitive games like Quake or Counter Strike you might as well have a blindfold over your eyes because you will have no chance while playing competitively.
Third Person Games and Sandbox games work really well. Games like Mad Max or fighting combat games like the Arkham series work really well and using the touchpad to rate the camera is also much better than a normal analog stick. MGSV worked better as well and it was easier to navigate the menus then a keyboard due to the fact that Konami didn’t program mouse functionality in the menus for some reason. GTA V worked well and was easier to drive. Surprisingly it wasn’t difficult to shoot either but I personally would use a controller. For 3rd person games I do think it’s better to use a keyboard and mouse but I didn’t feel that my in game performance was impacted too much by using the Steam controller. The touch pads excel in third person game as a camera and I think Just Cause 3 and Fallout 4 will work fine as well (unless you play fallout in first person like me) :P
Racing Games didn’t really change when comparing it to a 360 controller but it’s better than using a keyboard and mouse. I tested Rocket League, Track Mania, Sonic All Stars Racing Transformed, and Trial Evolution and they all worked well. For some reason though Project Cars just didn’t work and I had to use keyboard controls but I seem to be the only one, yay……. The steam controller is slightly better than a 360 controller but it’s not worth it if you’re buying it for racing games.
Sim Games shocked me more than any other genre of games when using the steam controller. I didn’t think it would work well but it’s far better than any other controller in history when it comes to emulating the Keyboard and mouse in Sim Games. I tried Cities Skylines first and it works really well, I’m not as fast when I’m using a controller but I was able to sit back and casually play games like Roller Coaster Tycoon, Euro Truck Sim 2, and Space Engineers. If you’re a big fan of simulation games then I highly recommend the Steam Controller. Train Simulator, Agriculture Simulator, and goat sim work well also if you play those games.The Thing with Fighting and RPG’s is that I don’t really play either of them. I only have 1 fighting game and I just picked up undertale so I don’t really feel that I can make my opinion of these two genres of games. If you're a fighting game fan then you most likely already have your fight pad or prefered controller already.
Moba’s like Dota 2 kinda fall into the FPS category when it comes to how the controller performs. These types of game typically are really competitive are require the use of a lot of keys and bindings so any controller is impractical. If you’re into Moba’s than just get a moba mouse and a gaming keyboard.
One of the last things to talk about is the Steam Big Picture Mode that works really well with the steam controller. Big Picture looks really nice and there rarely is any load time when you perform an action. only on occasion the store took a little longer to load or for some reason didn’t load at all. Most things can be accessed  by one button making navigating easy. Typing with the controller is a billion times better than using any other controller ever. Using the touch pads to type makes it much easier and allows you to type at the same speed you text. You can also instantly switch to your keyboard and mouse at anytime if you feel the need to do so.
Overall the steam controller is a great piece of tech and has a great price considering what it can do. I highly recommend it over a 360/dualshock control and it’s only $50. . You really can't go wrong with the controller. It works with uplay and other stores if it’s connected to steam. The Steam Controller is a great piece of tech that any PC gamer that needs a controller should get. I give it a 9.1 out of 10.
It looks okey, it feels great and is working awesome as a PC remote control. Love it!

DISCLAIMER: THIS REVIEW WAS WRITTEN ON THE 10TH OF NOVEMBER, 2015. ISSUES IN THIS REVIEW MAY BE FIXED IN LATER PATCHES/UPDATES!
This is a great piece of hardware if you want to make the jump from console to PC, just as it was intended to be.
Pros
-Simple to set up, only an idiot couldn't do it
-It's comfortable
-Light
-Can be wired OR wireless
-Fully customisable (minus the steam button which turns it on, off, and puts Steam in BGM), and allows to bind 17 buttons at MINIMUM, but 21 buttons on average. Because of the amount of customisability, it's hard to say how many buttons you can bind do it WITHOUT taking into consideration what the user will actually use
-Comes with batteries
-Nice box, keeps it secure and undamaged
-Doesn't require rebinding if the game already has pre-existing controller support, though even then it's still customisable
-Long battery life
-Secret and unadvertised gyroscope
-Adjustable haptic feedback
-(NEW FEATURE) Allows to rebind the controller for use on desktop
-Community bindings for if you're too lazy to rebind anything yourself
Cons
-Wire for it is too short
-Haptics are just vibrations (not that bad though)
-Can only bind keys in BPM (Big Picture Mode), including keybindings for desktop use
-Isn't 100% on point with a mouse, but not far either (this can be improved if you make use of the gyro as well)
Things to note
-If you've already gotten used to KB+M, this controller is NOT for you, and do not get it unless you're really interested. This controller is SPECIFICALLY aimed at getting console players who are used to playing with a controller into the PC gaming space. This controller is fantastic at doing its job, and can't recommend it enough.

TL;DR - Absolutely worth every penny. Hands down the most comfortable, and capable controller I've ever used (spanning back to Atari 2600 days). I've been using the prototype since December 2013 and I couldn't have hit the pre-order button for this one any faster without breaking something.
If you've pre-ordered one, or if you've just picked one up from a local store, welcome! If you're on the fence, please take all reviews with a grain of salt. There are far too many unboxing and first impressions that immediately dismiss the controller as useless, not worth buying... don't fall into that trap of hearing this one side of it and basing your decision on that. When you see the things people like
,
,
, and
are doing, it's hard to form any argument about what a Steam Controller can't do.
This is not something you should pick up for 30 minutes and make your final decision based on that. This controller has so much depth and customizeability that you really need to give yourself a day or two, possibly even a week or two to really dig in and see what it can do. You have 30 days to request a refund, and however many days you want to sell it to someone else looking for one. There's no rush. Take the time to get used to the controller, you won't regret it.
But oh man, when you do... when you don't give up after the initial awkwardness, when you re-learn the motor skills this controller needs that may not come second nature like they do with the Xbox and Playstation style controllers you've had 20+ years to build up the muscle memory on... oh man, when you do, you find it is an amazing controller, easily surpassing anything you can do with a Playstation or Xbox controller, and if you're willing to put in the effort to really get comfortable with it, it can absolutely rival keyboard and mouse.
Now, that said, there are still going to be games that come more naturally to you with keyboard and mouse, or even a standard controller. That doesn't mean they're unplayable with the Steam Controller, that doesn't even mean you can't play very well with the Steam Controller. It all comes down to your comfort level. If you've spent years honing your reflexes on a keyboard and mouse or controller, don't expect you'll be able to jump in with a Steam Controller and be right back up to the level you're at. But if you're willing to give it some time you will absolutely find yourself getting better and better, faster, and more comfortable, and you may very well equal your skill level with a keyboard. Who knows... you may even surpass it.

You're Marchione, a little boy living in Italy at the time of the plague epidemy. Your quest? To find a cure for your mother (who could be infected) and information about the disease, while avoiding to catch it.
The goal here is to learn about the medevial society but also the plague. Like in Slave Trade, you're travelling from screen to screen, speaking with people, looking at some objects, using the chrono goggles to find items that are out of time (and enabling minigames too). And then you have to make some choices: should I speak with someone infected, taking the risk to see my health decline? Should I cure my mother or Mrs Dona? Should I stay in the city (infected or sane) or go to the countryside (infected or sane)?
While I didn't expected the gameplay of Vikings - The Plague being the first game of the series -, I found the same problems as in Slave Trade: not enough minigames, discussion simulator, not enough documented (I suppose that you have educational material if you register on their website). You have Tempus, acting as your guide

I got Saints Row the Third from a THQ humble bundle sale and loved it! I've heard many times that Saints Row 2 is actually better than Saints Row the Third so when I saw the Saints Row complete pack available as part of the 2015 summer sale, I decided to pick up the whole pack. This was cheaper than getting Saints Row 2&4 separately despite already owning #3.
After about an hour of game play with periodic crashes and infrequent auto-saves, I found a much needed mod that fixes hundreds of bugs called "gentlemen of the row", which allowed me to play without crashing long enough to discover I do not like the game. The lack of GPS guidance on the minimap for player-set co-ordinates makes navigating the sea of streets which do not connect logically in a large world an absolute pain. Then if you actually want to play the story missions, you need enough "respect" (aka xp for doing random things, or missions, or activities) to start these story missions. Since ammo is scare and money is hard to come by at the beginning of the game, I decided to try out the race options. I tried 3 different varieties, the first is a normal race where you go through checkpoints competing against computer AI, the second a time trial through checkpoints where I was provided an awful car, and the third a time trial when provided a dirt bike. Racing against the computers was nightmarish because they could easily bump me far enough off the road that I miss the checkpoints and then I have to manuveur my cumbersome car back to the checkpoint and then try to catch up to the CPUs that steer flawlessly. The only way to catch up is to cut corners and drive on grass. I hit the smallest bump on the road, my car flipped upside down, and I could not exit until the car exploaded. The time trial with a car was okay, but the car provided was lame and the check points did not clearly indicate which route to take to the next checkpoint, which made the race tedious. Lastly I discovered that motorcycles in this game are impossible to stay on. I hit the smallest rock and went flying fifty feet from my vehicle, which resulted in me "abandoning" the vehicle and having to start over. I finally got far enough in the race where I had to jump a canyon and upon hiting the obvious jump ramp, the game thought I had crashed and I got sent flying across the canyon while my dirt bike stayed behind.
If you are willing to install mods to fix bugs, hunt around for mods that provide better GPS (if such a mod exists), improve motorcycle usage (if such a mod exists), allow you to bypass repect requirements (if such a mod exists), and many other mods that may be necessary, I could see this game being fun. Unfortunately it is a lot of work to make this game playable.
tl;dr: mods required to be playable, inferior to Saints Row the Third. Buy that game instead when it is on sale. If you already own that and want more Saints Row action, get the 4th game, or replay the 3rd, don't bother with this lame installment.

The story takes place after the first game.
Prologue: Your character wakes up in the Stilwater Prison Infirmary after the final mission of Saints Row. You meet a man named Carlos who tells you that you've been in an coma for almost five years and that the Saints have been taken out by the three new gangs of Stilwater. You then escape the prison via a boat you and Carlos have just stolen. After gunplay on the back of the boat, Carlos shows that Ultor (prevously a clothing company) has taken control as sort of a government to the city. During the second mission we see Jonny Gat, a former saint, about to be given the death penalty. Before that happens though your character frees Jonny and has to get the Saints back together. Insert Pierce, Shaundi, and Carlos. Three new members your character brings into the gang.
Gangs: Your character gives these three members different gangs to look after.
The Ronin: The Ronin are looked after by Pierce. The Ronin are a Jappenese gang controled by a young man named Shogo. His father, Akuji. later comes into the story after hearing his son is dissapointing him. The Ronin wear black and yellow colours and use samurai swords as melee weapons.
The Brotherhood: During the first mission your character and Carlos go to see the Brotherhoods leader, Maero, to make an agreement with both gangs and split Stilwater but, the Stilwater Police show up, abruptly ending the conversation. When back at the Brotherhood's base of opperations, the character and Maero have an arguement over how the deal goes when Maero tells that the Saints take 20% of Stilwater and the Brotherhood taking 80% of the rest.
The Sons Of Samedi: Samedi are a group of drug dealers with a famous product named Loa Dust. With a leader called The General, a bodyguard named Mr. Sunshine, and a deadbeat DJ named Veteran Child these guys dress in Jamacian styled clothing and uses Voo-Doo powers.
Epilogue: After the Gangs are taken out the Saints direct their attention to Ultor and try to take them out. This finale is something to look for as I can't give out any information of missions for possible spoilers.
In the end this game is hours of entertainment. I've been playing since 2012 and am still finding new stuff in it. If you still aren't sure, watch Nerdcubed's video on it. 10/10 In My Opinion

I really like the game, I really do, but this game has a crazy amount of problems...
Because of this, you have to wait again for 1-10 minutes, and if this happens again, you need to wait again, and again, and again... Several times it happened that matchmaking failed 3-5 times in a row, because of that it took 30-40 minutes of waiting  before the match starts.
A terrible team balance, sometimes you can get in team 2 unranked persons, 1 gold, 1 platinum, when other team can get 2 masters, 1 diamond, and 3 platinum players. Same with the profile level, one team can get almost all players with a profile level of 50-60, when in the second team 80-170. Same with character levels... I can't call this a good balance, it's a terrible balance. Almost all the matches is an one-sided slaughter, either your team or the enemy team is completely crushed, battles on the equals is a very big rarity.
Bad balance of characters. The thing is that the game has a very large number of characters, much more than the Overwatch has for example. I understand that it's very difficult to balance them all properly, and especially the new characters which just appeared in the game, too often they always too overpowered, and that's all still fine, but the problem is in other things...
Too often they buff and nerf the wrong characters, or the wrong skills, or the wrong stats of the characters. No, they do not return the character to the state in which he was before, THEY CHANGE ALL THE CHARACTERS SO THAT THEY WILL FIT THE BALANCE OF THE CHANGED CHARACTER, and guess what, of course they fail in this, and the balance becomes a complete mess, they are trying to balance even more, and each time they make this worse and worse, worse and worse...
I also like the card system in this game, but the way they implemented it completely ruins the game... The one who has a good deck has a really big advantage against players who do not have it, and play with a standard deck. I tried myself to play with a standard and customized deck, and depending on the character it becomes easier to play in 2-8 times.
The problem is that you can not create your own deck for free, you need to grind, and grind very and very a lot to have a possibility to create a deck for all the characters, my counter now shows that I spent 366 hours in the game, and I'm not even close to creating decks for even half of the characters. Plus you can not buy cards for gold, you are buying them for another currency, and it grinds a lot more slower than gold! And all of that leads to the fact that you have to play only as a couple of your main characters, and it's sucks hard!
But all of that is not the worst thing in the game...
The most terrible thing in this game, is bugs fixing. Almost everything is broken in this game, animation, skills, ults, interface, and a lot of game mechanics. Sometimes animations break down, and you can not see your weapon, and your weapon attack animation (bullets, flames, lightning, etc.), or in the third-person mode (even when using skills that forces the third person mode, like a Fernando shield), the character can just move backwards, or something like that. Also, the animation of the enemy can break, and because of that it will be difficult to understand what is your enemy doing, because you do not see his animations, and whether he attacks, when he is protected, and etc, it's just 3d model without animation that slides on the floor. In one patch even the animation of death for one character was broken, it was the same thing that I described above, except for one exception... Rising Storm 2 sadly fails to grasp the success of it's previous predecessor Red Orchestra 2, this is shown by fact that this game is beginning to have a dwindling player base that is expected to collapse in the years to come. As a Red Orchestra fan, I was dragged into the hype for RS2, sadly, this game is a massive let down to all those who enjoyed the previous Rising Storm.
Content in this game is lacking. Currently, there are only six maps to choose which suffer game breaking design issues such as the janky terrain that gets players stuck. On a more positive note, the maps look beautiful with colourful foliage, waterfalls and smoke effects however they lack the size of RO2 which allowed you to flank enemies strategically but instead we get limited maps that focus on the centre of the map. This phenomenon causes the lack of diversity in gameplay, which makes the six maps rather stale.
Weapon variety in the game is severely lacking. Players are often limited to the choice between the M4 and AK-47 due to the lack of balance for other weapons such as the shotguns and submachine guns; this is because the guns lack real use in in-game situations. Why use shotguns in open long range maps? Why use submachine guns if they lack the power to kill?
The game is plagued with very stereotypical cheesy voice acting. The Vietnamese voice actors are probably one of the worst voice actings I've heard in recent times; they especially get tiring when you hear the same voice line for like the 500th time.
However, the game still feels like a Red Orchestra game with the PTSD inducing explosions and intensity that we'll never be able to capture in other games. Newbies are expected to get destroyed with the unforgiving gameplay that Rising Storm 2 gives you. However this game wasn't enough to beat Red Orchestra in most aspects; personally, I would recommend buying Red Orchestra 2 as it provides far better gameplay than RS2 will ever achieve.
TL:DR not as good as RO2, buy RO2 instead

Definitely worth the money. I purchased this as one of the early early pre-orders and have been using it just about every day since I got it.
You should be warned though, It does have a learning curve to it, and it will feel awkward until you have put a few hours into it, but once you get the hang of it, it is hands down better than a 360 controller. Also in my opinion, first impressions aren't the best with this device, and I admit I almost hated it right out of the box.
The weight is distributed into the grips instead of in the middle due to the battery placement and without batteries it feels a lot lighter than it looks. The plastic housing also feels flimsy at first, and a lot of people giving their first impressions say that the controller feels cheap. I found the device to be very sturdy.
It also takes a bit of time to learn how to hold it, as you can't grip it like you would another pad without it being uncomfortable. Button placement is a bit off and also takes some getting used to since the buttons are under the right pad, which acts like the right stick, but again, give it time.
Once you are past the initial rocky bits, the customizability of the controller is where this thing really shines. The trackpads have a lot of different settings, every button is customizable and you can even program in macros and multiple key commands. As an example, I was able to program the grip buttons to perform the sideways slam in Mad Max. You can also use some buttons as modifiers for others, a common one I have heard about in shooters is to use one grip button to turn on the gyro to help with aiming.
The only real complaints I have are some issues with build quality, some buttons click very nicely, others are squishy and don't give much feedback when pressed, and the activation force on the track pads is a bit high for my taste, so clicking them is a chore. I also feel the tolerances on the battery compartments are too strict. I had one pair of rechargable batteries get stuck because they were a few millimeters too big, while another set fit perfectly.
Other than that, I have nothing but good things to say, the batery life is great so even if you don't go with rechargable ones like I did, you won't be going through them that quickly. The process of customizing the controller is easy, albeit time consuming. I even like Big Picture mode, though it could use a few more features compared to the regular desktop client.
So far It's working flawless - instalation was quick and it went with no problem - everything is working perfect!

UPDATE#1: after reading a lot of comments and reviews about the steam controller, I started to think that I may have judged the product too early. Maybe 20 hours are simply too few to get used to something like this. Still, what i wrote below, that I cannot change, becuase it is really what i felt and experienced during my 20 hours with the pad. ---
I'd like to start this review saying that I'm still happy to be one of the early buyer of the Steam Controller because I'm always keen to support new ideas, and I really hope someday there will be a (lot better) Steam Controller 2.0; but, right know, I really can not recommend this pad to anyone. There are better alternatives for everything you may play.
First, the d-pad is the worst i've ever tried. Too big, too imprecise, too generally uncomfortable. I was really hoping for a good d-pad to use with street fighter 5 and beat'em up in general, but I was overwhelmingly disappointed. Even the 360 d-pad delivers in camparison. The best you can do with this d-pad is navigating menus.
Second, the new trackpad that's now in place of the right stick is too inaccurate to be good with any game at all (I've tried it with several and it failed all my tests). It's hard to describe why it doesn't work, but it doesn't. Absolutely not recommened for competitive online games like fps or tps. I even tried it with games that have very little gameplay like telltale series and life is strange, but the inaccuracy of the trackpad made the experince so frustrating that it wasn't even fun playing.
Third, the a,b,x,y buttons are very badly placed. The whole steam pad was cleary designed with fps in mind, but as I stated before, due to the inaccuracy of the trackpad  I would not suggest playing fps or fast paced games in general with the steam pad unless you like to be overwhelmed by frustration.
Fourth, the batteries slots are too small and I have to struggle everytime i need to replace them. I use 2100 mAh rechargeable batteries and never had this problem with similar products. It may seem a little issue but trust me, it's really annoying.
I recevied the Steam Pad at the end of October and played with it for over 20 hours before selling it to a friend, simply because i couldn't find a single game in which it could give me the edge over other controllers.

MINOR SPOILERS FOLLOW
This game isn't long, but that doesn't matter, because it is a well-constructed game.  Initially, you begin with a side-scrolling space-shooter sequence that takes you through an army of rival space ships.  After the initial boss fight (which you are supposed to lose), you begin exploring a planet armed initially with only a portal gun.  You'll find an actual weapon later on to fight enemies with and to help with solving puzzles.
The game is basically an action-platformer in the vein of games like
with its exploration for various items, including extenders to your life meter and components which can power-up your repaired ship at the end of the game.  There aren't a whole lot of mechanics to the game, which is fitting for its short length.  This also makes the game easy to pick up and play.  There is a good challenge to the later sections, but there is nothing that truly feels overwhelming or unfair, which is a testament to the overall game design.  The price is fair as there is replayability to earn achievements.  For such a short title, there is a fairly large number to attain, and I can see people earning all of them with lots of practice.
I can find very little to criticize about this game.  You do have to be careful of scene switches because you can walk and/or jump into a hazard without fully realizing it, similar to
, though not nearly as unfair as in the latter title.  Also, in some of the vertical sections, I had to stop and search for my character, who was just about as far down the screen as possible, usually in a corner!  A brief, flashing arrow pointing to your character would help here, but this is not a big criticism.  It's possible to solve every room on the first try if you're observant and careful; I can even see a few people maybe having a deathless run on the first playthrough.
has just the right length for casual gamers while being robust enough for those looking for a challenge, especially those seeking to 100% the game through both winning and through completing the achievements.  I highly recommend this game.  It is both well-crafted and extremely well balanced.  Buy it!

I'M PLAYING POLARITY
I was on Steam and searched for crappy 10-Cents-Games. I found Polarity and bought it (with Soundtrack) for 24 Cents. I booted it up and saw a crappy interface. But as I started the game, I realized I found one of the best puzzle games I've ever played.
Did you ever wonder what a futuristic puzzle game without a plot would be? I tell you what I'd be. It'd be POLARITY. But no plot is necessary for this awesome game. To be honest, there is a plot, given on Level 0. But be careful, You might miss it if you blink.
I was very sceptical about the concept. It revolves around switching modes, so-called "Polarities". You have 2 Polarities availiable, RED and BLUE. And you can switch between them freely at any time. The first three Levels are Tutorial Levels introducing you to the concept of polarities and switching them. There are many new elements and mechanics I have never seen in any game before, like the Cubes. Like Polarities, there are two of them. Blue cubes activate blue switches and - you guessed it - red cubes activate red switches. It also introduces you to the concept of collecting Data Packs, which kind of work like Marios Star Coins.
The goal of the game is to get to every three Packs in each levels and finish the stage, of course. There are 14 Levels, 10 bonus levels and a challenging cooperative mode. The price of 10 Dollars is - sadly - too much for this game. I recommend it to anyone who can get it on Sale.
My final rating is a Tangram out of ten.
Like Tangram, It seems clunky and edgy, but if you get the hang of it, it is a pleasant and fun experience. The Co-Op-Mode serves as a big challenge for anyone, who likes to puzzle with a friend.
There are small minor graphical glitches, but that may be because of the fact I play it on Maximum Quality.
TL;DR: Good puzzler. Red and blue. Switches and cubes. Good game.

The story takes place after the first game.
Prologue: Your character wakes up in the Stilwater Prison Infirmary after the final mission of Saints Row. You meet a man named Carlos who tells you that you've been in an coma for almost five years and that the Saints have been taken out by the three new gangs of Stilwater. You then escape the prison via a boat you and Carlos have just stolen. After gunplay on the back of the boat, Carlos shows that Ultor (prevously a clothing company) has taken control as sort of a government to the city. During the second mission we see Jonny Gat, a former saint, about to be given the death penalty. Before that happens though your character frees Jonny and has to get the Saints back together. Insert Pierce, Shaundi, and Carlos. Three new members your character brings into the gang.
Gangs: Your character gives these three members different gangs to look after.
The Ronin: The Ronin are looked after by Pierce. The Ronin are a Jappenese gang controled by a young man named Shogo. His father, Akuji. later comes into the story after hearing his son is dissapointing him. The Ronin wear black and yellow colours and use samurai swords as melee weapons.
The Brotherhood: During the first mission your character and Carlos go to see the Brotherhoods leader, Maero, to make an agreement with both gangs and split Stilwater but, the Stilwater Police show up, abruptly ending the conversation. When back at the Brotherhood's base of opperations, the character and Maero have an arguement over how the deal goes when Maero tells that the Saints take 20% of Stilwater and the Brotherhood taking 80% of the rest.
The Sons Of Samedi: Samedi are a group of drug dealers with a famous product named Loa Dust. With a leader called The General, a bodyguard named Mr. Sunshine, and a deadbeat DJ named Veteran Child these guys dress in Jamacian styled clothing and uses Voo-Doo powers.
Epilogue: After the Gangs are taken out the Saints direct their attention to Ultor and try to take them out. This finale is something to look for as I can't give out any information of missions for possible spoilers.
In the end this game is hours of entertainment. I've been playing since 2012 and am still finding new stuff in it. If you still aren't sure, watch Nerdcubed's video on it. 10/10 In My Opinion

I played Kings of Kung Fu for a short period of time before I determined that, although it has some redeeming qualities, it's questionable whether or not it's your sort of game.
***KEEP IN MIND, THIS GAME IS STILL IN EARLY ACCESS***
======
CONS:
- Glitches: The music glitched and looped for quite a while, on a frequent basis.
- Hit detection: Some of the attacks and moves were not landing, even when they clearly hit the enemy.
- Story: No story, really, as the campaign only says "You are fighting for a spot on a movie as a stunt man. Go!" Not very compelling. Games like Soul Caliber and Street Fighter at least give you more than that~~~!
- Character models: They almost all look like Jackie Chan during a battle. They have very nice pictures in the selection screen, but almost all of them look like Jackie Chan in some form or another, with an oddly proportioned face/head.
- Mechanics: I couldn't get any of the moves to work, on the move list. At all. I was using an Xbox controller, so maybe it's just the support for controllers that is faulty, I'm not sure.
- VOLUME: No way of changing the volume until the game starts up, which is awful for this game, considering it blasts the music and such as soon as you start it up. It's REALLY VERY LOUD, and actually scared me, although I was prepared for the game turning on.
PROS:
- Details: Detailed enough that everything looks pretty good, considering.
- Straight forward: Though lacking a story, which is nice to have, the fighting is fairly consistent (regardless of the move list moves not working, in my case)
- Typical: Feels like a typical fighting game, although a little bit on the lean side.
======
Would I recommend "Kings of Kung Fu"?
No, sadly, I can't... yet.
If you get gifted it, it's good for a quick go.
If it's on sale for next to nothing (as it was when I purchased it), I can't say it would be a total waste, because it's not terrible.
But it's definitely not something to write home about, as of yet.
If they improve the issues, polish it up a bit more, and fine-tune it before final release, then my rating may change :) There's something here, and it's definitely salvageable~

Rising Storm 2 sadly fails to grasp the success of it's previous predecessor Red Orchestra 2, this is shown by fact that this game is beginning to have a dwindling player base that is expected to collapse in the years to come. As a Red Orchestra fan, I was dragged into the hype for RS2, sadly, this game is a massive let down to all those who enjoyed the previous Rising Storm.
Content in this game is lacking. Currently, there are only six maps to choose which suffer game breaking design issues such as the janky terrain that gets players stuck. On a more positive note, the maps look beautiful with colourful foliage, waterfalls and smoke effects however they lack the size of RO2 which allowed you to flank enemies strategically but instead we get limited maps that focus on the centre of the map. This phenomenon causes the lack of diversity in gameplay, which makes the six maps rather stale.
Weapon variety in the game is severely lacking. Players are often limited to the choice between the M4 and AK-47 due to the lack of balance for other weapons such as the shotguns and submachine guns; this is because the guns lack real use in in-game situations. Why use shotguns in open long range maps? Why use submachine guns if they lack the power to kill?
The game is plagued with very stereotypical cheesy voice acting. The Vietnamese voice actors are probably one of the worst voice actings I've heard in recent times; they especially get tiring when you hear the same voice line for like the 500th time.
However, the game still feels like a Red Orchestra game with the PTSD inducing explosions and intensity that we'll never be able to capture in other games. Newbies are expected to get destroyed with the unforgiving gameplay that Rising Storm 2 gives you. However this game wasn't enough to beat Red Orchestra in most aspects; personally, I would recommend buying Red Orchestra 2 as it provides far better gameplay than RS2 will ever achieve.
TL:DR not as good as RO2, buy RO2 instead

The game is a seemingly straightforward fantasy war-game.  Recruit troops, set formations and unit orders, move army into neighbouring provinces.  You do not control the battles themselves, you can only watch the battles to see if your orders worked or not and adjust your orders for next time.  Rinse and repeat.  Your build options are castles (allow recruitment of national troops in province – otherwise limited to the usually poor natives), temples (spread your faith – prereq to recruit holy units) and labs (prereq to mage recruitment, allow research, magic item forging and rituals in the province).
This game does not have a learning curve.  It's a learning minefield.  This charming game looks deceptively simple but it's subtleties and complexities hide underfoot ready to trip you up, especially as magic research progresses and options open up and the game shows it's true colours and depth.
There's an asymmetry to the game as the nations can play very differently, with 20+ nations in each era  (3 era's) giving lots of options of play styles.  For a new player it can be a bit daunting and it will take a while to find which nations you find fun but there should be a few in each era to suit.
A good game for single player, a great game for PBEM multi-player.  The biggest flaw in this game is the AI cannot handle all the complexities of the magic system, either to use it against you or to counter your own gambits. The controls are tight, and unlike Cave Story's Quote, Captain Yuri doesn't feel very floaty when he jumps or falls. A lot of the platforming puzzles in this game involve well-timed drops that Super Smash Bros. Brawl-styled gravity would make far too easy to perform, so this is a very good thing.

The Good
-Enjoyable portal clone
-Gameplay is quite fun
-Music is solid
-Relatively unique visual style (reminds me of Tron)
-Teaches the player controlls without holding their hand in learning gameplay mechanics
The Meh Stuff
-Sounds were hit and miss - example: jump sounds were bad and off time with visuals fairly often but sounds for the cube and polarity shift were good
-Gameplay elements were unique but there are only a few to learn
The Bad
-EXTREMELY short game - I finished the single player and bonus missions in one sitting; less than an hour and a half total
-The jump mechanics do not function very well, especially when trying to make multiple jumps in a row. This makes some levels a bit frustrating.
-EXTREMELY easy game - even the most "challenging" levels only take a couple minutes to finish. Several of the data (the things you collect each level) are in plain sight or hidden in painfully obvious hiding places. There is little to no challange in the puzzles.
Overall, I thought the game was enjoyable but definately not worth $11. I did not play the coop or vs modes, so perhaps these modes give some extra worth. I bought it on sale so it was dirt cheap.
TL;DR
BUY IT IF IT IS ON SALE, DON'T BUY IT IF IT IS NOT ON SALE
